Title: Chicken burrito bowls
Ingredients:
For the chicken:
- 2 1/2 lb boneless, skinless chicken breasts (about 5 breasts)
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 2 tsp chili powder
- 2 tsp ground cumin
- 1 1/2 tsp garlic powder
- 1 1/2 tsp smoked paprika
- 2 tsp kosher salt
- 1 tsp black pepper
- Juice of 2 limes

For the cilantro-lime rice:
- 3 cups long-grain white rice, rinsed
- 4 1/2 cups water
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp kosher salt
- 1/2 cup chopped fresh cilantro
- Juice of 2 limes

For the bowls:
- 2 cans (15 oz each) black beans, drained and rinsed
- 2 cups frozen corn kernels, thawed
- 2 bell peppers, any color
- 1 large red onion
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1/2 tsp kosher salt
- 3 cups shredded romaine lettuce
- 2 cups halved cherry tomatoes
- 2 ripe avocados
- Extra lime wedges and cilantro, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/2 cup low-sodium chicken broth
- Juice of 1 lime
- 1/3 cup sour cream (or plain Greek yogurt)
- 1-2 tsp minced chipotle in adobo
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
- Pinch of kosher salt
Steps:
1. Get the rice on first: rinsed rice, water, olive oil and salt in a lidded pot. Boil, cover, lowest heat 15 minutes, then rest 10 minutes off the heat without lifting the lid. Fluff with a fork and fold in the cilantro and lime juice.
2. Season the chicken assertively: pat the breasts bone-dry, rub with olive oil, then coat every surface with the chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, smoked paprika, salt and pepper, plus the lime juice. Rest 15 minutes at room temperature — dry, well-seasoned chicken is what sears instead of steams.
3. Char the peppers and onion: large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering, olive oil, peppers and onion in one layer with a pinch of salt. Leave them alone 2 full minutes so edges blacken, then toss and cook 3-4 minutes more — charred edges, still some bite. Out to a bowl.
4. Sear the chicken hard in the same pan — do not wipe it out; the pepper-onion fond is flavor. Lay the breasts down and do not move them for 5-6 minutes until a deep golden crust forms. Flip, 5-6 minutes more, to 165 F at the thickest point. Rest 5 minutes, then slice against the grain.
5. Beans and corn in the chicken pan: add beans, corn, 1/4 cup water and a pinch of salt to the drippings. Scrape up every browned bit as it simmers 3-4 minutes. Mash a few beans so the mix turns creamy.
6. Build the bowls: rice first, then chicken, beans and corn, charred peppers and onions, romaine and tomatoes. Slice the avocado last and fan it over the top. Finish with lime wedges and extra cilantro.
7. Storage: components keep separately up to 4 days. Reheat chicken, rice and beans with a sprinkle of water; add cold toppings and avocado fresh.

Common mistakes:
- Wet chicken: skip the paper towels and the chicken steams gray instead of crusting. Dry is non-negotiable.
- Peeking at the rice: every lid lift dumps the steam. Set a timer and walk away.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Chipotle-Lime Crema Pan Sauce — after the chicken comes out of the skillet, pour in 1/2 cup chicken broth and the juice of 1 lime and scrape the pan hard; every browned bit dissolves into the liquid. Simmer 2 minutes to reduce by a third, take the pan off the heat, and whisk in 1/3 cup sour cream (or Greek yogurt), 1-2 tsp minced chipotle in adobo, 1 tbsp cold butter and a pinch of salt until glossy. Drizzle over the chicken and rice in each bowl — smoky, tangy, rich.

Title: Chicken stir fry
Ingredients:
For the chicken (velveted):
- 2 lb boneless, skinless chicken breasts, sliced thin
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp cornstarch
- 1 tbsp vegetable oil
- 1 egg white

For the stir-fry sauce:
- 1/3 cup low-sodium soy sauce
- 2 tbsp oyster sauce
- 1 tbsp honey
- 2 tsp cornstarch
- 1/2 cup low-sodium chicken broth

For the stir fry:
- 3 cups long-grain white rice, rinsed
- 4 1/2 cups water
- 1 large head broccoli (about 1 1/2 lb)
- 2 bell peppers
- 8 oz snap peas
- 2 medium carrots
- 6 cloves garlic
- 1 piece fresh ginger, about 2 inches
- 3 tbsp vegetable oil, divided
- 1 tsp toasted sesame oil
- 1/2 tsp kosher salt
- Sesame seeds and sliced scallions, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/4 cup avocado oil
- 1/3 cup finely sliced scallions
- 2 tbsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 serrano chile, minced
- 1/2 tsp kosher salt
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp toasted sesame oil
Steps:
1. Mise en place — stir fry waits for no one: slice the chicken thin against the grain (20 minutes in the freezer makes it easy), cut the broccoli into flat-sided florets, slice the peppers and carrots on a diagonal, mince the garlic and ginger, trim the snap peas. Whisk the stir-fry sauce. Start the rice (boil, cover, lowest heat 15 minutes, rest 10).
2. Velvet the chicken: toss the strips with the soy, cornstarch, avocado oil and egg white; rest 15 minutes. Blanch in boiling water exactly 45 seconds until just opaque outside, still pink within. Drain well — this silky coat is what keeps breast meat tender in a screaming-hot wok.
3. Heat the wok until it just smokes, about 2 minutes over high heat. Add 2 tbsp avocado oil and swirl — it should shimmer instantly. (Avocado oil: neutral flavor, and it takes wok heat without smoking.)
4. Sear the chicken in a single layer, untouched for 90 seconds, until browned spots form. Toss 2 minutes more to 165 F. Out to a plate.
5. Vegetables, fiercely hot: remaining oil, broccoli and carrots with 1/4 cup water; cover 2 minutes so they steam-char. Uncover, add peppers and snap peas with the salt, and stir-fry 2-3 minutes until vivid and crisp-tender — they should still squeak.
6. Aromatics in the center: push the vegetables aside, garlic and ginger into the middle with a drizzle of oil, 30 seconds until sharp and fragrant. Do not let the garlic pass golden — it turns bitter.
7. Glaze and finish: chicken back in, sauce stirred and poured over. It bubbles into a glossy coat in 1-2 minutes. Off the heat, drizzle the sesame oil. Serve over rice with sesame seeds and scallions.

Common mistakes:
- Crowded wok: too much food drops the temperature and everything steams. Work in batches if your pan is small.
- Lukewarm wok: if the chicken does not sizzle loudly on contact, stop and heat it more.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Ginger-Scallion Oil — in a small pan, heat 1/4 cup avocado oil until shimmering. Put 1/3 cup finely sliced scallions, 2 tbsp grated ginger, 1 minced serrano and 1/2 tsp salt in a heatproof bowl and pour the hot oil over — it should sizzle violently. Stir in 1 tbsp soy sauce and 1 tsp toasted sesame oil. Spoon over each bowl of stir fry: bright, pungent, restaurant-level.

Title: Turkey chili
Ingredients:
- 2 1/2 lb ground turkey (93% lean)
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 2 large yellow onions
- 1 large bell pepper, any color
- 6 cloves garlic
- 3 tbsp chili powder
- 2 tbsp ground cumin
- 1 tbsp smoked paprika
- 2 tsp dried oregano
- 1 tsp cocoa powder, unsweetened (optional but recommended)
- 2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
- 1 tsp black pepper
- 2 cans (28 oz each) diced tomatoes
- 2 cans (15 oz each) kidney beans, drained and rinsed
- 2 cups low-sodium chicken broth
- 1 tbsp brown sugar
- Toppings: shredded cheddar, sour cream, sliced scallions, diced avocado

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 chipotle in adobo, minced, plus 1 tsp adobo sauce
- 1/2 tsp smoked paprika
- 3/4 cup sour cream
- Juice of 1/2 lime
- Pinch of kosher salt
Steps:
1. Mise en place: dice the onions and pepper, mince the garlic, and measure every spice — chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, oregano, cocoa, salt, pepper — into one bowl. Open the tomatoes; drain the beans.
2. Brown the turkey like you mean it: olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high until shimmering. Turkey in, spread flat, and leave it undisturbed 4-5 minutes until a dark crust forms on the bottom — pale, steamed turkey makes pale chili. Break it up and brown 3-4 minutes more.
3. Vegetables into the drippings: add onion and pepper with a pinch of salt; cook 5 minutes, scraping the pot, until softened and edged with brown.
4. Bloom the spices: garlic and the whole spice bowl in, stir 60 seconds until the pot smells like a campfire cookout. This toasting step is where chili gets its depth.
5. Simmer: tomatoes, beans, broth and brown sugar in. Scrape the bottom clean. Simmer gently 30-40 minutes, partially covered, stirring now and then, until thick enough that a spoon leaves a trail.
6. Taste and finish: more salt 1/2 tsp at a time until the flavors pop; a squeeze of lime if you have it wakes everything up. Rest 10 minutes — chili thickens and marries as it sits.
7. Serve with cheddar, sour cream, scallions and avocado. Leftovers keep 4 days and honestly taste better on day two.

Common mistakes:
- Rushing the browning: gray turkey = flat chili. The crust is the flavor base for the whole pot.
- Under-salting: chili needs more salt than you think. Add in stages and taste after each.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Smoky Chipotle Crema (small pan) — melt 1 tbsp butter in a small saucepan over medium heat, add 1 minced chipotle in adobo plus 1 tsp of its sauce and 1/2 tsp smoked paprika; sizzle 30 seconds until the butter turns brick red. Off the heat, whisk into 3/4 cup sour cream with the juice of 1/2 lime and a pinch of salt. Drizzle over each bowl — cool, smoky heat against the rich chili.

Title: Sheet-pan lemon herb chicken and potatoes
Ingredients:
- 3 lb bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs (about 8 thighs)
- 2 lb baby potatoes (about 1 1/2-inch size)
- 1 lb fresh green beans, trimmed
- 1/3 cup olive oil, plus 1 tbsp
- 6 cloves garlic
- 2 large lemons
- 2 tbsp fresh oregano leaves (or 2 tsp dried)
- 1 tbsp fresh thyme leaves (or 1 tsp dried)
- 2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
- 1 tsp black pepper
- 1 tsp paprika
- Lemon wedges, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- About 1/3 cup pan drippings (plus low-sodium chicken broth as needed)
- Juice of 1 lemon
- 1 tsp Dijon mustard
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
Steps:
1. Oven at 425 F, rack in the center, large rimmed sheet pan lined. Halve any big potatoes, mince the garlic, zest and halve the lemons, strip the thyme, chop the oregano, trim the beans. Pat the chicken thighs completely dry — dry skin is crisp skin.
2. Season boldly: toss the thighs with olive oil, garlic, lemon zest, oregano, thyme, paprika, 2 tsp salt and the pepper. Rub it under the skin where you can. Potatoes get olive oil, salt and pepper on the pan.
3. Roast: potatoes on first for 15 minutes alone — they need the head start. Then chicken skin-side UP on top, and roast 25-30 minutes until the skin is deep golden and crackling and the meat reads 175 F at the thigh (thighs are better cooked past 165).
4. Green beans into the drippings: pull the pan, scatter the beans around the chicken with a pinch of salt, back in for 8-10 minutes until blistered in spots and tender-crisp.
5. Rest and finish: rest the chicken 5 minutes on the pan so the juices settle into the meat, not the board. Squeeze a lemon half over everything and serve with wedges.

Common mistakes:
- Crowding the pan: overlapping pieces steam. Use two pans rather than one crowded one.
- Skin-side down: it will never crisp in the juices. Up, always.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Lemon-Butter Pan Sauce — tip the sheet pan and spoon the drippings into a small saucepan (about 1/3 cup; add chicken broth to reach it if needed). Simmer 2 minutes, then whisk in the juice of 1 lemon, 1 tsp Dijon and 2 tbsp cold butter, one piece at a time, until the sauce turns glossy and just coats a spoon. Spoon over the chicken and potatoes — all the roasted lemon-herb flavor, concentrated.

Title: Beef and broccoli
Ingredients:
For the beef (velveted):
- 2 lb flank steak
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine (or dry sherry)
- 2 tsp cornstarch
- 1 tsp vegetable oil

For the sauce:
- 1/3 cup oyster sauce
- 3 tbsp low-sodium soy sauce
- 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine
- 2 tsp sugar
- 2 tsp cornstarch
- 1/2 cup low-sodium beef or chicken broth
- 1 tsp toasted sesame oil

For the stir fry:
- 2 large heads broccoli (about 2 lb), cut into florets
- 5 cloves garlic, thinly sliced
- 1 piece fresh ginger (1 inch), peeled and julienned (julienne means cut into thin matchsticks)
- 3 tbsp vegetable oil, divided
- 3 cups long-grain white rice, rinsed
- 4 1/2 cups water
- Steamed white rice, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/4 cup avocado oil
- 1 tbsp red chile flakes
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/2 tsp Sichuan peppercorns, crushed
- Pinch of kosher salt and sugar
- 1 tsp soy sauce
Steps:
1. Mise en place: freeze the flank steak 20 minutes, then slice thin against the grain. Toss with the velvet marinade (soy, Shaoxing, cornstarch, a drizzle of avocado oil) and rest 15 minutes. Whisk the sauce. Florets cut, garlic sliced, ginger julienned. Start the rice (boil, cover, lowest heat 15, rest 10).
2. Blanch the broccoli 90 seconds in salted boiling water, drain, and spread out so it steams dry — wet broccoli kills the sear.
3. Sear the beef in a smoking wok: 1 1/2 tbsp avocado oil, half the beef in a single layer, untouched 90 seconds until charred at the edges. Toss 1 minute, out to a plate. Repeat with the rest. Hard sear, in batches — this is the whole dish.
4. Aromatics and broccoli: last of the oil, garlic and ginger 20 seconds until fragrant, then the broccoli back in for 1-2 minutes of tossing in the beefy oil.
5. Glaze: beef and all its juices back in, sauce poured around the wok's edge so it sizzles on contact. Toss 1-2 minutes until the sauce turns to a shiny lacquer. Off the heat, sesame oil over the top.
6. Serve immediately over rice, spooning the extra glaze over each bowl.

Common mistakes:
- Slicing with the grain: chewy beef no sauce can save. Cut across the lines in the meat.
- Saucing too early: the glaze needs the final 2 minutes only, or it scorches and dulls.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Chile-Garlic Crunch Oil — in a small pan, heat 1/4 cup avocado oil to shimmering. Off the heat, stir in 1 tbsp red chile flakes, 2 minced garlic cloves, 1/2 tsp Sichuan peppercorns (crushed) and a pinch of salt and sugar; it foams and blooms brick-red in 30 seconds. Cool 2 minutes, stir in 1 tsp soy sauce. Drizzle sparingly over each bowl — numbing, crunchy heat over the sweet glaze.

Title: Shrimp tacos with lime slaw
Ingredients:
For the shrimp:
- 2 lb large shrimp (21/25 count), peeled and deveined, tails off
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 2 tsp chili powder
- 1 1/2 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp garlic powder
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 1/2 tsp kosher salt
- 1/2 tsp black pepper
- Juice of 1 lime

For the lime slaw:
- 1 small head green cabbage (about 1 1/2 lb)
- 1/2 small red onion
- 1 cup plain Greek yogurt
- 1/4 cup mayonnaise
- Zest and juice of 2 limes
- 2 tbsp honey
- 1 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
- 1/2 cup chopped cilantro

For serving:
- 18 small corn tortillas
- 1/2 cup chopped cilantro
- 1/2 cup diced white onion
- Lime wedges
- Hot sauce

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/4 cup low-sodium chicken broth (or water)
- Juice of 1 lime
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
- 1-2 tsp minced chipotle in adobo
- Pinch of kosher salt
Steps:
1. Mise en place: thaw shrimp under cold water if frozen, then pat very dry. Shred the cabbage thin, dice the red onion fine, zest and juice the limes, chop the cilantro, mix the spice blend.
2. Slaw first so it can soften: whisk Greek yogurt, mayonnaise, lime zest and juice, honey and salt. Toss with cabbage, onion and cilantro. Taste — tangy, lightly sweet, well salted. Rest at least 15 minutes.
3. Season the shrimp assertively: olive oil, chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, smoked paprika, salt, pepper and lime juice, coating every shrimp.
4. Sear hot and fast: a large skillet over high heat until just smoking, a film of olive oil, shrimp in ONE layer. 90 seconds untouched until pink and charred at the edges; flip, 60 seconds more. Shrimp go from perfect to rubber in a minute — pull them the second they curl into a C and turn opaque. Work in two batches rather than crowd.
5. Char the tortillas directly over a gas flame or in a dry hot skillet, 20-30 seconds a side, until blistered in spots. Keep warm wrapped in a towel.
6. Build: slaw down first (it catches the juices), shrimp over, extra cilantro and diced onion, lime wedge and hot sauce at the table.

Common mistakes:
- Wet shrimp: they steam and never char. Paper towels, twice.
- Cold tortillas: a cold corn tortilla cracks and tastes raw. Char every one.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Chipotle-Lime Butter Pan Sauce — in the shrimp skillet over medium heat, add 1/4 cup chicken broth (or water) and the juice of 1 lime; scrape up the shrimp fond and simmer 1 minute. Off the heat, whisk in 3 tbsp cold butter, 1-2 tsp minced chipotle in adobo and a pinch of salt until the sauce turns glossy and coral. Spoon a little over the shrimp in each taco — it mingles with the slaw and tastes like a Baja fish shack.

Title: Greek chicken souvlaki bowls
Ingredients:
For the chicken:
- 2 1/2 lb boneless, skinless chicken breasts
- 1/3 cup extra-virgin olive oil
- Juice of 2 lemons
- 6 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp dried oregano
- 1 tbsp red wine vinegar
- 2 tsp kosher salt
- 1 tsp black pepper

For the tzatziki:
- 2 cups plain Greek yogurt (full-fat)
- 1 large English cucumber
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
- 1 tbsp red wine vinegar
- 1 tbsp chopped fresh dill (or 1 tsp dried)
- 1 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste

For the bowls:
- 2 1/2 cups long-grain white rice, rinsed (or 6 pita breads)
- 2 large cucumbers, diced
- 3 cups halved cherry tomatoes
- 1 large red onion, thinly sliced
- 1 cup pitted Kalamata olives
- 6 oz feta cheese, crumbled
- Lemon wedges and fresh oregano, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/2 cup low-sodium chicken broth
- Juice of 1 lemon
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
- 1 tsp dried oregano (or 1 tbsp fresh, chopped)
- Pinch of kosher salt
Steps:
1. Mise en place: grate the cucumber for the tzatziki and squeeze it dry in a towel (watery cucumber is the enemy). Mince the garlic — some for the chicken, some for the tzatziki. Juice the lemons, chop the dill, dice the bowl cucumbers, halve the tomatoes, slice the onion thin. Rinse the rice. Pat the chicken dry.
2. Marinate with intent: olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, red wine vinegar, salt and pepper whisked; chicken in for at least 30 minutes and up to 4 hours, refrigerated.
3. Tzatziki: yogurt, squeezed cucumber, garlic, olive oil, vinegar, dill and salt, stirred and chilled — it should taste bright and garlicky. Start the rice (boil, cover, lowest heat 15, rest 10, fluff).
4. Sear the chicken hard: a grill pan or large skillet over medium-high until hot, a film of olive oil. Chicken down, untouched 5-6 minutes for a deep golden crust, flip, 5-6 more to 165 F. Rest 5 minutes, then slice thick against the grain. (A grill works beautifully: medium-high, same timing, look for real char lines.)
5. Build the bowls: rice, sliced chicken, cucumber, tomatoes, red onion, olives and feta. Tzatziki generously over the top, lemon wedges alongside.

Common mistakes:
- Skipping the cucumber squeeze: tzatziki turns to soup within the hour.
- Pale chicken: souvlaki needs char. Hot pan, patience, no poking.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Warm Lemon-Oregano Pan Sauce — in the chicken skillet over medium heat, add 1/2 cup chicken broth and the juice of 1 lemon and scrape up the fond, simmering 2 minutes. Whisk in 2 tbsp cold butter and 1 tsp dried oregano (or 1 tbsp fresh), plus a pinch of salt, until just glossy. Spoon over the sliced chicken before the tzatziki goes on — hot, lemony pan juices under the cool yogurt is the whole point.

Title: Salmon with roasted asparagus and rice
Ingredients:
- 6 salmon fillets, 5 oz each, skin-on (about 2 lb total)
- 2 lb fresh asparagus
- 3 tbsp olive oil, divided
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 large lemons (1 zested and juiced, 1 cut into wedges)
- 2 tsp kosher salt, divided
- 1 tsp black pepper
- 1 tsp paprika
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter, melted
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh parsley
- 2 1/2 cups long-grain white rice, rinsed

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- 2 tbsp capers, drained
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- Juice of 1 lemon
- 1 tbsp chopped fresh parsley
- Pinch of kosher salt
Steps:
1. Oven at 425 F, sheet pan lined. Snap the woody ends off the asparagus. Pat the salmon completely dry, especially the skin — dry skin is the only route to crisp skin. Mince the garlic; zest and juice one lemon, wedge the other.
2. Rice on: rinsed rice, water and 1/2 tsp salt; boil, cover, lowest heat 15 minutes, rest 10, fluff.
3. Asparagus: toss with olive oil, half the salt and pepper on the pan; roast 8 minutes to get ahead of the fish.
4. Salmon, seasoned and roasted skin-down: rub the fillets with olive oil, paprika, remaining salt and pepper. Pull the pan, lay the salmon skin-side DOWN among the asparagus, and roast 10-12 minutes until the skin is crisp, the top is just opaque and the center flakes at a nudge — 125 F for silky, 135 F for firm. Do not flip it, ever.
5. Finish like a bistro: drizzle the melted butter mixed with the garlic, lemon zest and juice over the hot fillets, shower with parsley, and serve with lemon wedges and the pan juices spooned around.

Common mistakes:
- Wet skin: it steams and sticks instead of crisping. Pat it dry twice.
- Overcooking: salmon goes from silky to chalky in 3 minutes. Start checking at 10.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Lemon-Caper Butter Pan Sauce — in a small pan over medium heat, melt 3 tbsp butter until it foams, add 2 tbsp capers and 1 minced garlic clove and sizzle 1 minute until the butter smells nutty and the capers crisp at the edges. Off the heat: juice of 1 lemon, 1 tbsp chopped parsley, pinch of salt. Spoon over each fillet — briny, brown-buttered, bright.

Title: Turkey meatballs marinara over spaghetti
Ingredients:
For the meatballs:
- 2 1/2 lb ground turkey (93% lean)
- 1 cup Italian breadcrumbs
- 1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese, plus more for serving
- 2 large eggs, beaten
- 1/2 cup whole milk
- 6 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/2 cup chopped fresh parsley
- 2 tsp kosher salt
- 1 tsp black pepper
- 1 tsp dried oregano
- 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes

For the marinara:
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 large yellow onion, diced
- 6 cloves garlic, thinly sliced
- 2 cans (28 oz each) crushed tomatoes
- 2 tsp dried oregano
- 1 tsp sugar
- 1 1/2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
- 1/2 tsp black pepper
- 1/2 cup torn fresh basil leaves
- 1 lb spaghetti
- Fresh basil and Parmesan, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 2 cloves garlic, thinly sliced
- 1-2 tsp chopped Calabrian chiles (or 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes)
Steps:
1. Mise en place: dice the onion; mince garlic for the meatballs, slice garlic for the sauce. Chop parsley, tear the basil by hand, beat the eggs, line a sheet pan with foil and oil it lightly.
2. Panade first: stir breadcrumbs and milk into a thick paste and rest 5 minutes — these soaked crumbs are why the meatballs stay tender instead of bouncing.
3. Mix gently: turkey, panade, Parmesan, eggs, garlic, parsley, salt, pepper, oregano and red pepper flakes. Mix with your hands just until combined — overworked meatballs are dense meatballs. Roll 24 balls, about 1 1/2 inches.
4. Sear for flavor: a large skillet over medium-high, a film of olive oil, meatballs in without crowding. Brown deeply on two sides, 6-8 minutes total — they finish in the sauce. That crust is non-negotiable flavor. Out to a plate.
5. Marinara in the same pan: onion in the drippings, 5 minutes until soft and sweet; sliced garlic 30 seconds; crushed tomatoes, oregano, sugar, salt and pepper. Simmer 15 minutes, scraping the bottom.
6. Meatballs back in, nestled into the sauce. Cover and simmer gently 12-15 minutes to 165 F inside. Meanwhile boil the spaghetti in well-salted water until just shy of done; reserve a cup of pasta water.
7. Finish: basil torn into the sauce. Toss the spaghetti through the marinara with splashes of pasta water until it shines. Meatballs on top, Parmesan over everything.

Common mistakes:
- Skipping the sear: poached-in-sauce meatballs taste boiled. Brown them.
- Overmixing: mix to just-combined or the texture turns to sausage.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Calabrian Chile-Garlic Butter — in a small pan over medium heat, melt 3 tbsp butter with 1 tbsp olive oil; add 2 sliced garlic cloves and 1-2 tsp chopped Calabrian chiles (or red pepper flakes) and sizzle 60-90 seconds until the garlic is golden at the edges and the butter is brick-red. Toss half through the spaghetti before plating and spoon the rest over the meatballs — a slow, warm heat under the sweet marinara.

Title: Chicken fajitas
Ingredients:
For the fajita seasoning:
- 2 tbsp chili powder
- 1 tbsp ground cumin
- 1 tbsp smoked paprika
- 2 tsp garlic powder
- 2 tsp dried oregano
- 2 tsp kosher salt
- 1 tsp black pepper
- 1/2 tsp cayenne (optional)

For the fajitas:
- 2 1/2 lb boneless, skinless chicken breasts
- 4 bell peppers (mix of colors)
- 2 large yellow onions
- 1/3 cup olive oil, divided
- Juice of 2 limes
- 12 large flour tortillas (10-inch)

For serving:
- Sour cream, shredded cheddar, guacamole or sliced avocado, pico de gallo or salsa, lime wedges, chopped cilantro

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/3 cup low-sodium chicken broth
- Juice of 1 lime
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
- 1/2 tsp fajita seasoning (from the recipe's blend)
Steps:
1. Mise en place: slice the chicken into even 1/2-inch strips, the peppers into strips, the onions into half-moons. Mix the fajita seasoning. Juice the limes. Toppings in bowls before any heat — fajitas move fast.
2. Season the chicken hard: toss with 3 tbsp olive oil, the lime juice and 3 tbsp of the seasoning. Rest 15 minutes.
3. Sear the chicken in a ripping-hot skillet: a film of olive oil, chicken in ONE layer, untouched 3-4 minutes until deeply browned and charred at the edges. Toss, 2 minutes more, to 165 F. Out to a plate — and leave every drop of fond in the pan.
4. Vegetables in the same pan: remaining olive oil, onions first for 3 minutes until they slump and brown at the edges, then the peppers with the remaining seasoning and a pinch of salt. Cook 4-5 minutes, scraping the chicken fond up into them, until charred in spots and just tender — never limp.
5. Bring it together: chicken and its juices back in for 30 seconds of tossing. Taste for salt and lime.
6. Warm the tortillas (dry skillet or flame, 20 seconds a side) and serve the whole skillet at the table, sizzling, with sour cream, cheddar, guacamole, pico, lime and cilantro.

Common mistakes:
- Crowding the skillet: the chicken steams and the peppers go soggy. Two batches beat one sad pile.
- Slicing with the grain: strips get chewy. Cut across the fibers.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Sizzling Lime-Butter Pan Sauce — with the skillet still hot after everything comes out, pour in 1/3 cup chicken broth and the juice of 1 lime; it should boil on contact. Scrape every browned bit loose, simmer 1 minute, then whisk in 2 tbsp cold butter and 1/2 tsp of the fajita seasoning until glossy. Pour it back over the chicken and vegetables right before serving — the skillet will sizzle at the table like a restaurant fajita platter.

Title: Teriyaki salmon rice bowls
Ingredients:
For the teriyaki sauce:
- 1/2 cup low-sodium soy sauce
- 1/2 cup mirin (Japanese sweet rice wine)
- 1/4 cup sake (or dry sherry)
- 3 tbsp brown sugar
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger

For the bowls:
- 6 salmon fillets, 5 oz each (about 2 lb total), skin removed if you prefer
- 1 tbsp vegetable oil
- 1 tsp kosher salt
- 1/2 tsp black pepper
- 3 cups short-grain or jasmine rice, rinsed
- 4 1/2 cups water
- 1 1/2 lb broccoli florets (or 3 cups edamame, thawed)
- 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds
- 4 scallions, thinly sliced

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/4 cup sake (or water)
- 1 tbsp white miso paste
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
- Squeeze of lemon juice
Steps:
1. Mise en place: rinse the rice, cut the broccoli, grate the ginger, slice the scallions. Pat the salmon very dry on all sides. Stir the sauce ingredients in a small saucepan until the sugar dissolves.
2. Rice on: rinsed rice, water, 1/2 tsp salt — boil, cover, lowest heat 15 minutes, rest 10, fluff.
3. Reduce the teriyaki: boil the sauce, then simmer steadily 8-10 minutes until it coats the back of a spoon and looks like lacquer. Set aside half for glazing and half for the table.
4. Sear the salmon hard: a skillet over medium-high with a film of avocado oil until shimmering. Salmon seasoned with salt and pepper, laid down and left alone 4-5 minutes until a deep crust forms and it releases easily. Flip once, 1-2 minutes more — the center should still be slightly translucent; carryover finishes it.
5. Glaze: brush the salmon thickly with teriyaki and give it 30 seconds in the hot pan until the glaze turns shiny and sticky at the edges. Do not walk away — sugar burns fast.
6. Broccoli: steam or blanch 3-4 minutes until vivid green and crisp-tender; season with a pinch of salt.
7. Build the bowls: rice, broccoli, salmon fillet on top, the reserved teriyaki spooned over. Sesame seeds and scallions to finish.

Common mistakes:
- Moving the fish: poke at salmon early and it tears and sticks. It releases when the crust is ready.
- Thin glaze: if the teriyaki runs off the spoon like water, reduce it more — it should coat.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Miso-Butter Pan Sauce — in the salmon skillet over medium heat, add 1/4 cup sake (or water) and scrape up the fond; simmer 1 minute. Off the heat, whisk in 1 tbsp white miso and 2 tbsp cold butter until the sauce turns silky and opaque, then a squeeze of lemon. Spoon around — not over — the glazed salmon, so the teriyaki shine stays the star.

Title: Lean beef tacos
Ingredients:
For the beef:
- 2 1/2 lb ground beef (90% lean)
- 2 tbsp chili powder
- 1 tbsp ground cumin
- 2 tsp paprika
- 2 tsp garlic powder
- 1 tsp dried oregano
- 2 tsp kosher salt
- 1 tsp black pepper
- 1/2 cup water or low-sodium beef broth

For serving:
- 18 small corn tortillas
- 3 cups shredded iceberg or romaine lettuce
- 2 cups diced tomatoes
- 1 cup diced white onion
- 1 cup chopped cilantro
- 6 oz shredded Monterey Jack or cheddar cheese
- Lime wedges and your favorite salsa
- Sour cream (optional)

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/3 cup low-sodium beef broth (or water)
- Juice of 1 lime
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
- 1 tsp hot sauce
Steps:
1. Mise en place: dice tomatoes and onion, chop the cilantro, shred the lettuce, mix the spices. Cheese, salsa and limes ready — tacos wait for no one.
2. Brown the beef properly: a large skillet over medium-high, dry. Beef in, break it into small crumbles, then let it sit in contact with the pan so it actually browns — 6-8 minutes until deeply browned with crispy edges and no pink. Do not drain 90% lean fat; it carries the spices. (80/20: spoon off the excess.)
3. Bloom the spices: the whole spice mix over the beef, stir 1 minute in the hot fat until fragrant. Add the water or broth and simmer 2-3 minutes, scraping the pan, until the beef is glazed and saucy, not soupy.
4. Char the tortillas over a flame or in a dry skillet, 20-30 seconds a side, until blistered and flexible. Wrap in a towel.
5. Build: beef, lettuce, tomato, onion, cilantro, cheese. Lime and salsa at the table, sour cream if you like.

Common mistakes:
- Gray beef: stirring constantly prevents browning. Break it up, then leave it alone against the hot pan.
- Watery filling: simmer the liquid down until the beef leaves a trail when you drag a spoon.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Chile-Lime Pan Drizzle — after the beef comes out, add 1/3 cup beef broth (or water) and the juice of 1 lime to the hot skillet; scrape up every spice-crusted bit and boil 1 minute. Off the heat, whisk in 1 tbsp cold butter and 1 tsp hot sauce. Spoon a teaspoon over the beef in each taco — concentrated taco-shop flavor in every bite.

Title: Chicken tikka masala
Ingredients:
For the marinade:
- 2 1/2 lb boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
- 1 cup plain whole-milk yogurt
- 2 tbsp lemon juice
- 2 tbsp garam masala, divided
- 1 tbsp ground cumin
- 1 tbsp ground coriander
- 1 tsp turmeric
- 1 tsp paprika
- 1 tsp cayenne (use 1/2 tsp for mild)
- 4 cloves garlic, grated
- 1 tbsp grated fresh ginger
- 2 tsp kosher salt

For the sauce:
- 3 tbsp ghee or unsalted butter
- 1 large yellow onion, finely diced
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 can (28 oz) tomato passata or crushed tomatoes
- 1 tbsp tomato paste
- 1 1/2 cups heavy cream
- 1 tbsp honey or sugar
- 2 tsp garam masala (the reserved half)
- 1 tsp crushed kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) — optional but transformative
- Salt to taste
- Chopped cilantro, for serving
- Cooked basmati rice or warm naan, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter (or ghee)
- 1 tsp garam masala
- 1 clove garlic, thinly sliced
- Pinch of red chile flakes
Steps:
1. Marinate (2-8 hours ahead): whisk yogurt, lemon juice, half the garam masala, cumin, coriander, turmeric, paprika, cayenne, grated garlic and ginger, and salt. Coat the chicken pieces completely and refrigerate — the yogurt tenderizes while the spices penetrate. This marinade is the soul of the dish.
2. Char the chicken: scrape off the excess marinade and sear the pieces in a hot, lightly oiled skillet (or under a broiler) in batches, 3-4 minutes a side, until charred black at the edges. It finishes in the sauce, so aim for char, not doneness. Set aside.
3. Build the sauce in the same pan: butter or ghee over medium heat, the finely diced onion with a pinch of salt, 8-10 minutes until deep golden and sweet — browned onion is the backbone. Garlic and ginger 1 minute. Tomato paste 1 minute until brick red.
4. Simmer: passata in, scrape the pan, simmer 10 minutes until the sauce darkens and oil pearls at the edges.
5. Cream and finish: stir in the cream, honey, the reserved garam masala and kasuri methi (crush it between your palms). Simmer 2 minutes. It should taste rich, warmly spiced, and balanced — add salt until it sings.
6. Chicken and its juices back in; simmer gently 5-8 minutes to 165 F. Rest 5 minutes. Serve over basmati or with naan, cilantro over the top.

Common mistakes:
- Pale onions: five minutes is not enough. The sauce's depth comes from truly golden onions.
- Boiling the cream sauce hard after the chicken goes in: keep it at a bare simmer so it stays silky.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Brown Butter Garam Masala Tadka — in a small pan, melt 3 tbsp butter (or ghee) over medium heat and let it foam until the solids turn amber and smell nutty, 2-3 minutes. Add 1 tsp garam masala, 1 sliced garlic clove and a pinch of chile flakes; sizzle 20 seconds. Spoon the hot spiced butter over each serving at the table — it blooms in the cream and perfumes the whole bowl.

Title: Pork tenderloin with sweet potatoes and green beans
Ingredients:
- 2 pork tenderloins (about 1 1/4 lb each, 2 1/2 lb total)
- 2 lb sweet potatoes (about 4 medium)
- 1 1/2 lb fresh green beans, trimmed
- 1/4 cup olive oil, divided
- 3 tbsp Dijon mustard
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh rosemary (or 2 tsp dried)
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh thyme (or 2 tsp dried)
- 2 tsp kosher salt, divided
- 1 tsp black pepper
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tbsp honey

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/2 cup low-sodium chicken broth
- 1/4 cup dry white wine (or more broth)
- 2 tbsp Dijon mustard
- 1/3 cup heavy cream
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
- Pinch of kosher salt
Steps:
1. Oven at 425 F, sheet pan lined. Cube the sweet potatoes evenly, trim the beans, mince the garlic, chop the herbs. Trim the silverskin off the tenderloins (slide a thin knife under the shiny membrane and slice it away) and pat the pork completely dry.
2. Season assertively: rub the pork with olive oil, then the Dijon, garlic, rosemary, thyme, smoked paprika, salt and pepper — a thick, fragrant crust. Sweet potatoes tossed with olive oil, salt and pepper on the pan.
3. Sear before roasting — the step that changes everything: a skillet over medium-high with a film of olive oil, tenderloins down for 2-3 minutes a side until a deep mahogany crust forms all over. Sheet-pan-only pork is pale pork.
4. Roast: pork onto the sweet potatoes, honey drizzled over. Roast 18-22 minutes to 145 F at the thickest point — blushing, juicy pork is safe and correct at 145 with a rest.
5. Green beans into the pork drippings on the pan for the last 8-10 minutes, until blistered and tender.
6. Rest the pork a full 10 minutes tented — cut sooner and the juices flood the board. Slice into thick medallions and serve over the sweet potatoes and beans with the pan juices spooned around.

Common mistakes:
- Cooking to 160 F out of habit: tenderloin turns to chalk. 145 F plus rest is the USDA number and the juicy one.
- Skipping the sear: the oven alone will not give you that crust.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Dijon-Cream Pan Sauce — in the searing skillet over medium heat, add 1/2 cup chicken broth and 1/4 cup dry white wine (or more broth); scrape up the crusty bits and reduce by half, about 3 minutes. Whisk in 2 tbsp Dijon and 1/3 cup heavy cream; simmer 1-2 minutes until it coats a spoon. Off the heat, 1 tbsp cold butter and a pinch of salt. Spoon over the medallions — this is the classic pork tenderloin sauce for a reason.

Title: Korean beef bulgogi bowls
Ingredients:
For the marinade:
- 1 Asian pear (or 1 Bosc pear), peeled and grated
- 1/2 cup low-sodium soy sauce
- 1/4 cup brown sugar
- 3 tbsp toasted sesame oil
- 6 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 tsp black pepper

For the bowls:
- 2 1/2 lb ribeye or sirloin steak
- 2 tbsp vegetable oil, divided
- 1 large yellow onion, thinly sliced
- 3 cups jasmine or short-grain rice, rinsed
- 4 1/2 cups water
- 6 scallions, thinly sliced
- 2 tbsp toasted sesame seeds
- Kimchi and lettuce leaves, for serving (optional)

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/3 cup water
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp brown sugar
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
- 1 tsp toasted sesame oil
Steps:
1. Start 3-4 hours ahead: freeze the steak 30 minutes, then slice it paper-thin against the grain — thin is the whole identity of bulgogi. Grate the pear, mince the garlic, grate the ginger, slice the onion and scallions.
2. Marinate: whisk pear, soy, brown sugar, sesame oil, garlic, ginger and pepper; massage into the beef with your hands. Refrigerate 2-4 hours (never more than 8 — the pear enzymes turn the meat mushy).
3. Rice on: rinsed rice, water, pinch of salt — boil, cover, lowest heat 15, rest 10.
4. Sear in screaming-hot batches: a skillet or wok over the highest heat with a film of avocado oil. Beef in ONE layer, spread thin, untouched 90 seconds until the edges char and caramelize — bulgogi should taste of fire, not steam. Out, and repeat. The onion goes in for the final batch, so it picks up the beef fond and softens at the edges.
5. Bring it back together: all the beef and onion plus any accumulated juices, 30 seconds of tossing until glossy.
6. Serve over rice with scallions and sesame seeds, kimchi and lettuce leaves alongside for wrapping.

Common mistakes:
- Crowding the pan: thin beef in a pile steams in its marinade and never chars. Small batches, real heat.
- Marinating overnight: the pear keeps working and the texture goes soft. Four hours is the sweet spot.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Pear-Soy Pan Glaze — after the last batch, add 1/3 cup of the leftover marinade juices (from the bowl, not raw-meat liquid — use 1/3 cup water plus 1 tbsp soy and 1 tsp brown sugar if you prefer) to the hot pan and boil 1 minute, scraping up the char. Whisk in 1 tbsp cold butter and 1 tsp toasted sesame oil off the heat. Drizzle over the beef — the charred pan flavor, concentrated into a glaze.

Title: Chicken Caesar wraps
Ingredients:
For the chicken:
- 2 lb boneless, skinless chicken breasts
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 2 tsp garlic powder
- 2 tsp kosher salt
- 1 tsp black pepper
- Juice of 1 lemon

For the light Caesar dressing:
- 1 cup plain Greek yogurt
- 1/3 cup grated Parmesan cheese, plus more for serving
- 3 tbsp lemon juice
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 2 tsp anchovy paste (or 4 anchovy fillets, minced)
- 2 cloves garlic, grated
- 2 tsp Dijon mustard
- 1 tsp Worcestershire sauce
- 1/2 tsp black pepper
- 2-4 tbsp water, to thin

For the wraps:
- 6 large flour tortillas (12-inch burrito size)
- 3 romaine hearts, chopped
- 1 cup croutons (optional)
- Extra Parmesan, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/4 cup low-sodium chicken broth
- Juice of 1/2 lemon
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
- 1 tbsp grated Parmesan cheese
- Pinch of black pepper
Steps:
1. Mise en place: chop the romaine and dry it thoroughly — wet lettuce repels dressing. Grate the garlic and Parmesan, juice the lemons. Pound the chicken to an even 3/4 inch (between plastic wrap, with a heavy pan) — even thickness means no dry edges and raw middles. Season with olive oil, garlic powder, salt, pepper and lemon juice.
2. Caesar dressing: whisk yogurt, Parmesan, lemon juice, olive oil, anchovy paste, garlic, Dijon, Worcestershire and pepper. The anchovy is what makes it Caesar rather than garlicky yogurt — do not skip it. Thin with water to a pourable coat-the-spoon consistency; taste for salt and lemon.
3. Sear the chicken hard: a skillet over medium-high, a film of olive oil, chicken down untouched 5-6 minutes for a deep golden crust, flip, 4-5 more to 165 F. Rest 5 minutes, slice against the grain.
4. Toss the romaine with dressing until every leaf is glossed — start with 3/4 of it; you can add, you cannot subtract.
5. Build the wraps: warm tortillas, dressed romaine down the center, sliced chicken over, croutons and extra Parmesan. Roll tight, seam down, halve on a diagonal.

Common mistakes:
- Soggy wraps: undried lettuce and overdressing are the two causes. Dry leaves, dressing in stages.
- Pounding unevenly: thick ends raw, thin ends dry. Even 3/4 inch, everywhere.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Lemon-Garlic Pan Butter — in the chicken skillet over medium heat, add 1/4 cup chicken broth and the juice of 1/2 lemon; scrape up the fond and simmer 1 minute. Off the heat, whisk in 2 tbsp cold butter, 1 tbsp grated Parmesan and a pinch of black pepper until glossy. Drizzle a spoonful over the chicken inside each wrap before rolling — warm, lemony, and it ties the chicken to the dressing.

Title: Shrimp fried rice
Ingredients:
- 4 cups cooked long-grain white rice, day-old and refrigerated (from about 1 1/2 cups dry)
- 1 1/2 lb medium shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 4 large eggs, beaten
- 2 cups frozen peas and carrots, thawed
- 6 scallions
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp grated fresh ginger
- 1/4 cup low-sodium soy sauce
- 1 tbsp oyster sauce
- 2 tsp toasted sesame oil
- 1/2 tsp white pepper (or black pepper)
- 4 tbsp vegetable oil, divided
- 1 tsp kosher salt

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp avocado oil
- 1/4 cup finely minced fresh ginger
- 1/3 cup thinly sliced scallions
- 1/2 tsp kosher salt
- 2 tsp soy sauce
- 1/2 tsp toasted sesame oil
Steps:
1. Mise en place — the wok work takes 10 minutes, so everything ready: cold day-old rice with the clumps broken up by hand (fresh rice turns to mush; this is law). Eggs beaten with a pinch of salt. Scallion whites and greens sliced and kept separate. Garlic minced, ginger grated. Soy, oyster sauce and sesame oil mixed. Shrimp patted very dry.
2. Eggs first: wok over high heat until smoking, 1 tbsp avocado oil, eggs in — they should puff and sizzle. Scramble soft in 30-45 seconds, still slightly glossy. Out.
3. Sear the shrimp: fresh film of oil, shrimp in one layer, 60-90 seconds until pink with charred edges and just curled. Season with the salt. Out with the eggs.
4. Fry the rice: 2 tbsp avocado oil, scallion whites, garlic and ginger 20 seconds, then the rice spread flat against the wok. Leave it 60-90 seconds so grains crisp at the edges, then toss and repeat. You want some grains toasted and chewy — that texture is the dish.
5. Vegetables: peas and carrots in, toss 1-2 minutes until hot and bright.
6. Sauce down the wok's edge: pour the soy mixture around the sides so it sizzles and caramelizes slightly before it hits the rice. Toss until every grain is seasoned and shiny. White pepper over.
7. Finish: shrimp and eggs folded back with the scallion greens, 30 seconds to warm through. Taste for salt and serve immediately, straight from the wok.

Common mistakes:
- Fresh rice: no technique saves it. Cook the rice the day before, or spread fresh rice on a tray and refrigerate uncovered 2 hours.
- Stirring constantly: rice needs still contact with the hot wok to crisp. Press, wait, toss.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Cantonese Ginger-Scallion Sauce — in a small pan, heat 3 tbsp avocado oil until shimmering. Pour it over 1/4 cup finely minced ginger, 1/3 cup sliced scallions and 1/2 tsp salt in a heatproof bowl — it should sizzle hard. Stir in 2 tsp soy sauce and 1/2 tsp toasted sesame oil. Spoon over each serving — this is the classic poached-chicken condiment and it is electric on shrimp fried rice.

Title: Black bean and sweet potato enchiladas
Ingredients:
For the filling:
- 2 lb sweet potatoes (about 3 large), peeled and cubed
- 2 cans (15 oz each) black beans, drained and rinsed
- 1 large yellow onion, diced
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp dried oregano
- 2 tsp kosher salt
- 1/2 tsp black pepper
- 2 tbsp olive oil

For the enchilada sauce:
- 3 tbsp vegetable oil
- 3 tbsp all-purpose flour
- 1/4 cup chili powder
- 2 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp garlic powder
- 1 tsp dried oregano
- 1 can (15 oz) tomato sauce
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 tsp kosher salt
- 1 tsp sugar

For assembly:
- 18 corn tortillas
- 8 oz Monterey Jack or pepper Jack cheese, shredded
- 1/2 cup chopped cilantro
- Sour cream and lime wedges, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 chipotle in adobo, minced, plus 1 tsp adobo sauce
- 1/2 cup sour cream
- Juice of 1 lime
- Pinch of kosher salt
Steps:
1. Oven at 425 F. Cube the sweet potatoes evenly, dice the onion, mince the garlic, shred the cheese from a block (bagged shreds are starch-coated and melt poorly).
2. Roast the sweet potatoes hard: olive oil, salt and pepper, single layer, 25 minutes flipping once, until caramelized at the edges and tender — roasting concentrates their sweetness; boiled would waterlog the filling.
3. Enchilada sauce in a saucepan: olive oil over medium heat, flour whisked in for 1 minute, then the chili powder, cumin, garlic powder and oregano — toast 30 seconds until brick red and fragrant. Tomato sauce and broth in, simmer 8-10 minutes until it coats a spoon. Salt and sugar to balance.
4. Filling in a skillet: olive oil, onion 5 minutes until golden at the edges; garlic, cumin, smoked paprika and oregano 1 minute. Beans and roasted sweet potato in with a splash of water; mash a third of it roughly so the filling holds together. Salt to taste.
5. Assemble: warm the tortillas until pliable (dry skillet, 20 seconds a side). Sauce the bottom of a 9x13. Fill each tortilla with filling and a pinch of cheese, roll seam-down, pack them tight. Blanket with the remaining sauce and cheese.
6. Bake 20-25 minutes until bubbling at the edges and the cheese is browned in spots. Rest 10 minutes so they slice cleanly. Cilantro, sour cream and lime at the table.

Common mistakes:
- Cold tortillas: they crack when rolled. Warm every one.
- Skipping the spice toast in the sauce: raw chili powder tastes dusty. Thirty seconds in hot oil fixes it.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Chipotle-Lime Crema Pan Sauce — in a small pan over medium heat, warm 1 tbsp butter with 1 minced chipotle in adobo and 1 tsp adobo sauce for 30 seconds until brick red. Off the heat, whisk into 1/2 cup sour cream with the juice of 1 lime and a pinch of salt. Drizzle zigzag over the baked enchiladas — smoky and cool against the chile sauce.

Title: Thai basil chicken
Ingredients:
- 2 1/2 lb ground chicken (or chicken breast, minced)
- 2 cups packed Thai holy basil leaves (Thai basil works; see note)
- 8-10 Thai bird's eye chiles (use 4-5 for medium heat)
- 8 cloves garlic
- 3 tbsp vegetable oil
- 3 tbsp fish sauce
- 2 tbsp oyster sauce
- 1 tbsp low-sodium soy sauce
- 2 tsp sugar
- 1/4 cup low-sodium chicken broth or water
- 6 large eggs
- 3 cups jasmine rice, rinsed
- Sliced cucumber, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1 tbsp avocado oil
- 2 cloves garlic, thinly sliced
- 2-3 Thai bird's eye chiles, sliced
- 2 tbsp fish sauce
- 1 tbsp sugar
- 2 tbsp water
- Juice of 1/2 lime
Steps:
1. Rice first: 3 cups jasmine rice, water, pinch of salt — boil, cover, lowest heat 15 minutes, rest 10.
2. Mise en place: pick a mountain of basil leaves. Pound or mince the garlic and chiles together into a rough paste — this is the engine of the dish (wash your hands after; bird's eyes are fierce). Mix fish sauce, oyster sauce, soy and sugar.
3. Fry the eggs first, Thai-style: a wok or skillet over medium-high with 1 tbsp avocado oil, eggs cracked in and left alone until the whites set with lacy, crispy brown edges and the yolks stay runny, 2-3 minutes. Out to a plate.
4. Sear the chicken hard: same wok, remaining avocado oil, smoking hot. Ground chicken spread flat and left undisturbed 2-3 minutes so a crust forms, then broken up and cooked through, 5-6 minutes total, with real browned bits — pale steamed chicken makes a dull krapow.
5. Paste and sauce: garlic-chile paste in for 30 seconds until it makes you cough (a good sign). Sauce mixture around the wok's edge, broth in, toss 1-2 minutes until the chicken is glazed and the liquid nearly gone.
6. Basil off the heat: handfuls of leaves tossed through until just wilted, 30 seconds. The residual heat is enough.
7. Serve over rice with a crispy egg on top and cucumber alongside. Break the yolk and let it sauce the rice.

Common mistakes:
- Basil cooked to death: it blackens and loses its perfume. Off the heat, always.
- Timid heat: with fewer than 4 chiles this is a different, quieter dish. Adjust, but know what you are trading.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Chile-Garlic Fish Sauce Glaze — in a small pan over medium heat, warm 1 tbsp avocado oil and fry 2 sliced garlic cloves and 2-3 sliced bird's eye chiles for 30 seconds. Add 2 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp sugar and 2 tbsp water; simmer 1 minute until syrupy, then the juice of 1/2 lime off the heat. Spoon sparingly over the egg and rice — salty, hot, sour, the flavors of the dish turned up one notch.

Title: Baked cod with lemon capers and orzo
Ingredients:
- 6 cod fillets, 5 oz each (about 2 lb total), about 1 inch thick
- 1 lb orzo pasta
- 3 tbsp olive oil, divided, plus more for drizzling
- 4 cloves garlic, thinly sliced
- 1 pint cherry tomatoes, halved
- 1/2 cup dry white wine (or chicken broth)
- 3 tbsp capers, drained
- Zest and juice of 2 lemons
- 1 tsp kosher salt, divided, plus more to taste
- 1/2 tsp black pepper
- 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes
- 1/2 cup chopped fresh parsley
- 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese
- Lemon wedges, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- Juice of 1 lemon
- 1 tbsp capers, drained
- 1 tbsp chopped fresh parsley
Steps:
1. Oven at 400 F. Salted water to a boil for the orzo. Slice the garlic, halve the tomatoes, drain the capers, zest and juice the lemons, chop the parsley. Pat the cod very dry and check for pin bones with a fingertip.
2. Orzo: cook 1 minute shy of the package, reserve a cup of the starchy water, drain, toss with a drizzle of olive oil.
3. Build the base in a large oven-safe skillet: olive oil over medium heat, garlic 30 seconds, then the cherry tomatoes with a pinch of salt. Cook 4-5 minutes until they slump and burst into a sauce, crushing a few with the spoon.
4. Wine and capers in: simmer 2 minutes, scraping the pan, until the raw alcohol smell cooks off. Lemon zest, half the juice, red pepper flakes. Taste — bright, briny, alive.
5. Bake the cod in the sauce: nestle the fillets into the tomatoes, spoon sauce over the tops, drizzle with olive oil, salt and pepper. Bake 12-15 minutes until the fish flakes at a gentle press and reads 140 F — pull it there; carryover finishes it and overcooked cod is chalk.
6. Finish: orzo folded through the sauce with splashes of pasta water until glossy. Lemon juice to brighten, parsley over everything, Parmesan at the table with wedges.

Common mistakes:
- Baking to 160 F out of habit: cod dries fast. 140 F and a rest is the juicy target.
- Underseasoning the tomato base: capers and lemon need salt beneath them to read as flavor rather than noise.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Brown Butter-Lemon Pan Sauce — in a small pan, melt 3 tbsp butter over medium heat and cook until the foam subsides and the solids turn amber and nutty, 2-3 minutes. Off the heat: the juice of 1 lemon, 1 tbsp capers and 1 tbsp parsley — it will sizzle and smell like a French bistro. Spoon over each cod fillet at serving, over the tomato sauce — two lemon sauces, one bright and one brown-buttered, is not too much.

Title: Chicken parmesan (lightened)
Ingredients:
For the chicken:
- 2 1/2 lb boneless, skinless chicken breasts (about 5)
- 1 cup panko breadcrumbs
- 1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese
- 2 tsp Italian seasoning
- 1 tsp garlic powder
- 1 tsp kosher salt
- 1/2 tsp black pepper
- 2 large eggs, beaten
- 1/4 cup all-purpose flour
- Olive oil spray

For assembly:
- 3 cups marinara sauce (homemade or good jarred)
- 8 oz part-skim mozzarella cheese, shredded
- 1/4 cup grated Parmesan, for topping
- 1 lb spaghetti or 6 servings of pasta
- Chopped fresh basil, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 clove garlic, thinly sliced
- 1/4 cup torn fresh basil leaves
- Zest of 1/2 lemon
Steps:
1. Oven at 425 F; sheet pan lined, a wire rack set on it if you have one — air under the chicken keeps the bottom crisp. Pound the breasts to an even 1/2 inch and pat dry. Breading station: flour, beaten eggs, then panko mixed with Parmesan, Italian seasoning, garlic powder, salt and pepper.
2. Bread with a dry hand and a wet hand: flour, egg, then press firmly into the panko so the crust adheres in a thick, even coat. Rest the breaded chicken 10 minutes — the crust sets and will not slough off in the oven.
3. Bake 18-20 minutes until the crust is deep golden and the chicken reads 160 F. A mist of olive oil spray before baking is the lightened cook's crisping trick.
4. Sauce and cheese: spoon marinara over each breast (edges of crust left bare so they stay crisp), mozzarella and Parmesan over. Back in for 5-7 minutes until the cheese bubbles and browns in spots and the chicken hits 165 F.
5. Boil the spaghetti in well-salted water; reserve pasta water; toss with a spoonful of marinara loosened with the starchy water so it shines.
6. Serve chicken over the pasta, basil torn over everything.

Common mistakes:
- Skipping the rest after breading: the crust slides off in sheets. Ten minutes of patience.
- Drowning the crust in sauce: sauce the center, keep the edges crisp.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Garlic-Basil Brown Butter (for the pasta) — in a small pan, melt 3 tbsp butter over medium heat until amber and nutty, 2-3 minutes. Add 1 sliced garlic clove and sizzle 30 seconds; off the heat, add 1/4 cup torn basil and the zest of 1/2 lemon. Toss through the spaghetti before the marinara goes on — nutty, herby depth under the red sauce.

Title: Beef and bean burritos
Ingredients:
- 2 lb ground beef (90% lean)
- 2 cans (15 oz each) black beans, drained and rinsed (or 1 can refried beans + 1 can black beans)
- 3 cups cooked long-grain white rice (from about 1 cup dry)
- 1 large yellow onion, diced
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp chili powder
- 1 tbsp ground cumin
- 2 tsp smoked paprika
- 2 tsp dried oregano
- 2 tsp kosher salt
- 1 tsp black pepper
- 1 can (8 oz) tomato sauce
- 6 burrito-size flour tortillas (12-inch)
- 8 oz shredded cheddar or Monterey Jack cheese
- Sour cream, salsa, shredded lettuce, diced tomato, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/2 cup low-sodium chicken broth (or water)
- 2 tbsp tomato sauce
- 1-2 tsp adobo sauce (from a can of chipotles in adobo)
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
Steps:
1. Mise en place: dice the onion, mince the garlic, mix the spices. Cook the rice if needed (1 cup dry, boil, cover, lowest heat 15, rest 10). Shred the cheese from a block.
2. Brown the beef hard: a large skillet over medium-high, beef in and broken up, then left alone against the hot pan in stretches until deeply browned with crisp edges, 6-8 minutes. Gray beef makes gray burritos.
3. Aromatics and spices in the drippings: onion 4-5 minutes until golden at the edges; garlic and the whole spice mix 1 minute until fragrant.
4. Beans and tomato: black beans and tomato sauce in, scrape the pan, simmer 5 minutes until thick and cohesive. Mash a few beans to bind it. Salt until it tastes like something.
5. Warm the rice and fold it through, or keep it separate for layering — either way season it.
6. Warm the tortillas until pliable. Fill: rice, beef and beans, cheese. Fold the sides, roll tight. For the full experience, return the burritos seam-down to a hot dry skillet 1-2 minutes a side until the tortilla toasts and seals.
7. Serve with sour cream, salsa, lettuce and tomato.

Common mistakes:
- Cold tortillas: they crack and split. Warm every one.
- Wet filling: simmer it down or the burrito weeps.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Smoky Adobo Pan Sauce — after the filling comes out, add 1/2 cup chicken broth (or water) to the hot skillet and scrape up the spice-crusted fond. Stir in 2 tbsp tomato sauce and 1-2 tsp adobo sauce from a can of chipotles; simmer 2 minutes. Off the heat, whisk in 1 tbsp cold butter. Spoon inside each burrito before rolling, or over the top — concentrated burrito-shop flavor.

Title: Egg roll in a bowl
Ingredients:
- 2 lb ground pork (or ground turkey for lighter)
- 2 bags (14 oz each) coleslaw mix (shredded cabbage and carrots)
- 1 large yellow onion, diced
- 5 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp grated fresh ginger
- 4 scallions, thinly sliced
- 3 tbsp low-sodium soy sauce
- 1 tbsp oyster sauce
- 1 tbsp rice vinegar
- 2 tsp toasted sesame oil
- 1 tsp sriracha, plus more for serving
- 2 tbsp vegetable oil
- 1 tsp kosher salt
- Sesame seeds, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp avocado oil
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1-2 tsp sambal oelek (or red chile flakes)
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp honey
- 1 tsp rice vinegar
Steps:
1. Mise en place: dice the onion, mince the garlic, grate the ginger, slice the scallions. Mix soy, oyster sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil and sriracha. Open the slaw bags — this cooks in 15 minutes once the pan is hot.
2. Brown the pork with intent: 1 tbsp avocado oil in a wok or your biggest skillet over medium-high until shimmering. Pork in, broken up, then left undisturbed 3-4 minutes until a real crust forms on the bottom. Break and brown 3 minutes more. Crust is the difference between egg-roll flavor and boiled meat.
3. Onion into the drippings, 3-4 minutes until softened and edged brown. Garlic and ginger 30 seconds.
4. Slaw in two handfuls at a time with the salt, tossing 3-4 minutes until wilted but still crunchy at the core — it should taste cooked, not raw, and never soupy. If liquid pools, crank the heat and let it burn off.
5. Sauce around the pan's edge so it sizzles; toss 1 minute until everything is glossed. Scallions and sesame seeds over the top, extra sriracha at the table.

Common mistakes:
- Steaming the pork: a crowded, timid pan gives you gray crumbles. Hot pan, patience, batches if needed.
- Overcooking the cabbage to mush: pull it while it still has snap.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Chile-Garlic Drizzle — in a small pan, heat 2 tbsp avocado oil until shimmering; add 2 minced garlic cloves and 1-2 tsp sambal oelek (or chile flakes) and sizzle 30 seconds until brick red and fragrant. Off the heat: 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp honey, 1 tsp rice vinegar. Drizzle over each bowl — a hot, sweet chile lacquer over the savory pork.

Title: Chicken noodle soup
Ingredients:
- 2 1/2 lb bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs (or 1 whole 3 1/2-lb chicken)
- 10 cups water
- 3 tbsp olive oil or butter
- 2 large yellow onions, diced
- 4 large carrots, sliced into 1/4-inch coins
- 4 celery stalks, sliced 1/4 inch thick
- 5 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 bay leaves
- 1 tbsp fresh thyme leaves (or 1 tsp dried)
- 8 oz wide egg noodles
- 1/4 cup chopped fresh parsley
- 2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
- 1 tsp black pepper
- Juice of 1/2 lemon

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 tsp fresh thyme leaves
- 1 small clove garlic, minced
Steps:
1. Mise en place: dice the onions, slice carrots into coins and celery into half-moons — uniform pieces, even cooking. Mince the garlic, strip the thyme, chop the parsley. Pat the chicken dry.
2. Sear the chicken first — this is what makes it taste like soup from a real kitchen: 1 tbsp olive oil or butter in a stockpot over medium-high, thighs skin-side down 4-5 minutes until deeply golden, flip, 3 minutes more. Out to a plate.
3. Vegetables in the drippings: onion, carrot and celery with a pinch of salt, 6-8 minutes, scraping the pot, until softened and sweet at the edges. Garlic and thyme 30 seconds.
4. Simmer the broth: chicken back in with the water and bay leaves. Bare simmer 25-30 minutes — never a hard boil, which clouds the broth and toughens the meat.
5. Shred: chicken out, skin and bones discarded, meat torn into bite-size pieces. Broth skimmed of foam and excess fat.
6. Noodles: bring the broth back to a simmer, egg noodles in for the package time minus 1 minute. Chicken back in to warm through.
7. Finish: parsley, black pepper, and the lemon juice — that small squeeze is what makes people ask what your secret is. Salt to taste, generously.

Common mistakes:
- Boiling hard: the broth goes cloudy and greasy. Bare simmer, always.
- Noodles stored in the soup: they bloat overnight. Store separately if you can.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Brown Butter and Herb Drizzle — in a small pan, melt 3 tbsp butter over medium heat until amber and nutty. Add 1 tsp fresh thyme leaves and 1 small minced garlic clove; sizzle 20 seconds. Spoon a teaspoon over each bowl of soup at serving — it floats on the broth like the finish on a restaurant soup.

Title: Lentil and sausage soup
Ingredients:
- 1 lb Italian sausage (sweet or hot), casings removed
- 2 cups brown lentils, rinsed and picked over
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 large yellow onion, diced
- 3 large carrots, diced
- 3 celery stalks, diced
- 5 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 can (14 oz) diced tomatoes
- 8 cups low-sodium chicken broth
- 2 bay leaves
- 1 tsp dried thyme
- 1 tsp dried oregano
- 1 Parmesan rind (optional, but a great flavor trick)
- 4 cups baby spinach
- 2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
- 1 tsp black pepper
- Grated Parmesan and crusty bread, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/4 cup olive oil
- 3 cloves garlic, thinly sliced
- 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes
- Zest of 1/2 lemon
Steps:
1. Mise en place: rinse the lentils and pick out any stones. Dice onion, carrots and celery evenly (the soffritto), mince the garlic, squeeze the sausage from its casings.
2. Brown the sausage hard: olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high, sausage broken into crumbles and left in contact with the pot until deeply browned and crusty in spots, 6-8 minutes. Out to a plate, drippings left behind.
3. Soffritto in the drippings: onion, carrot and celery with a pinch of salt, 8 minutes, scraping, until soft and golden at the edges. Garlic, thyme and oregano 30 seconds.
4. Simmer: lentils, tomatoes, broth, bay leaves and the Parmesan rind if you have one. Bare simmer 30-35 minutes until the lentils are tender and the soup has body.
5. Sausage back in for 5 minutes. Spinach in by the handful until just wilted.
6. Finish: salt and pepper until it tastes alive, a drizzle of good olive oil and grated Parmesan on each bowl, crusty bread alongside.

Common mistakes:
- Underseasoning: lentils drink salt. Taste at the end and be generous.
- Rushing the sausage browning: the crust on the sausage flavors the whole pot.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Garlic-Chile Oil — in a small pan, warm 1/4 cup olive oil over medium heat with 3 sliced garlic cloves and 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes until the garlic turns golden at the edges, about 2 minutes — do not let it brown dark. Off the heat, add the zest of 1/2 lemon. Drizzle over each bowl with the Parmesan — a hot, garlicky slick on a rustic soup.

Title: Greek turkey burgers with tzatziki
Ingredients:
For the burgers:
- 2 1/2 lb ground turkey (93% lean)
- 4 oz feta cheese, crumbled
- 1 cup frozen chopped spinach, thawed and squeezed dry
- 1/2 cup panko breadcrumbs
- 1 large egg, beaten
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh oregano (or 2 tsp dried)
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 tsp kosher salt
- 1 tsp black pepper
- 2 tbsp olive oil, for cooking

For the tzatziki:
- 1 1/2 cups plain Greek yogurt
- 1 English cucumber, grated and squeezed dry
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tbsp red wine vinegar
- 1 tbsp chopped fresh dill
- 3/4 tsp kosher salt

For serving:
- 6 whole wheat burger buns or pita breads
- 2 large tomatoes, sliced
- 1/2 red onion, thinly sliced
- 2 cups shredded lettuce or arugula

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/3 cup low-sodium chicken broth
- Juice of 1/2 lemon
- 2 tbsp crumbled feta cheese
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
Steps:
1. Mise en place: squeeze the thawed spinach dry in a towel; grate and wring the cucumber for the tzatziki the same way — water is the enemy twice in this recipe. Mince the garlic, zest the lemon, chop the oregano and dill, slice the tomatoes and onion, beat the egg.
2. Tzatziki: yogurt, squeezed cucumber, garlic, olive oil, vinegar, dill and salt. Chill — tangy and garlicky is the goal.
3. Mix the burgers gently: turkey, feta, spinach, panko, egg, garlic, oregano, lemon zest, salt and pepper, just until combined. Form 6 patties with a thumbprint dimple in the center (it keeps them from puffing into meatballs). Chill 15 minutes if you have time — they hold together better.
4. Sear hard: olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high until shimmering. Patties down, untouched 5-6 minutes until a deep golden crust forms; flip once, 4-5 more minutes to 165 F. Turkey burgers forgive nothing — use the thermometer.
5. Toast the buns in the drippings. Build: tzatziki on both sides, burger, tomato, red onion, greens.

Common mistakes:
- Wet spinach: the patties slump and steam. Wring it until your hands are tired.
- Pressing the burgers with the spatula: you are squeezing out the juice you worked to keep.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Lemon-Feta Pan Sauce — after the burgers come out, add 1/3 cup chicken broth and the juice of 1/2 lemon to the skillet; scrape up the fond and simmer 1 minute. Off the heat, whisk in 2 tbsp crumbled feta and 1 tbsp cold butter until the sauce turns creamy and flecked. Spoon over each burger before the top bun — a warm, briny echo of the tzatziki.

Title: BBQ chicken with corn and slaw
Ingredients:
For the BBQ sauce:
- 1 can (15 oz) tomato sauce
- 1/2 cup apple cider vinegar
- 1/3 cup molasses (or packed brown sugar)
- 2 tbsp yellow mustard
- 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce
- 2 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp garlic powder
- 1 tsp onion powder
- 1 tsp kosher salt
- 1/2 tsp black pepper
- 1/4 tsp cayenne (optional)

For the chicken and sides:
- 3 lb bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs (about 8)
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 2 tsp kosher salt
- 1 tsp black pepper
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 6 ears corn, husks and silk removed
- 2 tbsp butter, melted

For the vinegar slaw:
- 1 small head cabbage, shredded
- 1 large carrot, grated
- 1/2 cup apple cider vinegar
- 2 tbsp sugar
- 1 tsp kosher salt
- 1/2 tsp black pepper
- 1/2 tsp celery seeds (optional)

For the pan sauce (optional):
- About 1/4 cup pan drippings (plus a splash of water as needed)
- 2 tbsp yellow mustard
- 1 tbsp apple cider vinegar
- 1 tbsp molasses
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
Steps:
1. Oven at 400 F, sheet pan lined. Shred the cabbage, grate the carrot. Pat the chicken thighs completely dry. Husk the corn, wiping silk away with a damp towel.
2. Slaw first: whisk vinegar, sugar, salt, pepper and celery seeds; toss with cabbage and carrot. Tangy and crunchy — it needs at least 20 minutes to relax.
3. Season the chicken assertively: olive oil, salt, pepper and smoked paprika worked over every surface, skin included.
4. Roast skin-side UP 35-40 minutes until the skin is deep golden and rendered and the thighs read 175 F. Do not sauce yet — sauce on raw chicken steams the skin you are trying to crisp.
5. Sauce while it roasts: tomato sauce, vinegar, molasses, mustard, Worcestershire, smoked paprika, garlic and onion powders, salt, pepper and cayenne, simmered 10 minutes until thick and glossy.
6. Glaze: brush the chicken thickly with sauce and roast 5 more minutes; brush again and give it 3-5 under the broiler until the edges char and the glaze sets sticky.
7. Corn: grill or roast alongside, brushed with butter, salt, until blistered in spots. Serve chicken with extra sauce, corn and slaw.

Common mistakes:
- Saucing from the start: sugared sauce burns and the skin never crisps. Sauce at the end, twice.
- Skipping the broiler finish: that sticky char is what makes it BBQ instead of baked chicken in sauce.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Carolina Mustard Pan Sauce — tip the sheet pan and pour the drippings into a small saucepan (about 1/4 cup; add a splash of water if needed). Whisk in 2 tbsp yellow mustard, 1 tbsp apple cider vinegar, 1 tbsp molasses and 1 tbsp cold butter; simmer 2 minutes until glossy. Serve as a second sauce at the table — sharp, golden, and it cuts the sweet BBQ beautifully.

Title: Shrimp and grits
Ingredients:
For the grits:
- 1 1/2 cups stone-ground grits (not instant)
- 6 cups water
- 2 cups whole milk
- 2 tsp kosher salt
- 4 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 cup shredded sharp cheddar cheese

For the shrimp:
- 2 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 6 slices bacon, chopped
- 1 large bell pepper, diced
- 1 large yellow onion, diced
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp Cajun seasoning
- 1/2 tsp kosher salt
- 1/2 tsp black pepper
- 1 tbsp all-purpose flour
- 1 cup low-sodium chicken broth
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- Juice of 1 lemon
- 4 scallions, sliced
- Hot sauce, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1/2 tsp Cajun seasoning
- 1 tsp hot sauce
Steps:
1. Mise en place: pat the shrimp very dry. Chop the bacon, dice the pepper and onion, mince the garlic, slice the scallions, shred the cheddar.
2. Grits first — they hold, shrimp do not wait: water and milk to a boil with the salt, grits whisked in a thin stream, then lowest heat 25-30 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy. Off the heat: butter and cheddar in, cover and hold. They should pour like lava; loosen with milk as needed.
3. Render the bacon in a large skillet over medium heat until crisp, 6-8 minutes. Out to a plate; the fat stays — that is the flavor base.
4. Vegetables in the bacon fat: onion and pepper with a pinch of salt, 5 minutes until softened and browned at the edges. Garlic and Cajun seasoning 30 seconds.
5. Sear the shrimp hard in the same pan, in one layer, 90 seconds a side until pink with browned edges and just curled. Out with the bacon.
6. Build the pan gravy: flour into the drippings, whisk 1 minute. Broth in slowly, whisking, simmer 2-3 minutes until it coats a spoon. Butter and lemon juice in off the heat.
7. Shrimp and bacon back for 30 seconds to gloss. Serve over the grits, scallions and hot sauce over the top.

Common mistakes:
- Lumpy grits: pour slowly and whisk like you mean it at the start; after that they are forgiving.
- Overcooked shrimp: they finish in the gravy — pull them the moment they curl.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Cajun Brown Butter — in a small pan, melt 3 tbsp butter over medium heat until amber and nutty. Add 1/2 tsp Cajun seasoning and 1 tsp hot sauce; sizzle 15 seconds. Spoon over each serving of shrimp and grits — brown butter and Cajun spice are made for each other.

Title: Cajun chicken pasta
Ingredients:
For the Cajun seasoning:
- 2 tbsp paprika
- 1 tbsp garlic powder
- 1 tbsp onion powder
- 2 tsp dried oregano
- 2 tsp dried thyme
- 2 tsp kosher salt
- 1 tsp black pepper
- 1 tsp cayenne (use 1/2 tsp for mild)

For the pasta:
- 2 lb boneless, skinless chicken breasts
- 3 tbsp olive oil, divided
- 1 lb penne pasta
- 1 large red bell pepper, sliced
- 1 large yellow bell pepper, sliced
- 1 large yellow onion, sliced
- 5 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 1/2 cups half-and-half
- 1 cup low-sodium chicken broth
- 1 cup grated Parmesan cheese
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1/2 cup sliced scallions
- Extra Cajun seasoning, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/3 cup low-sodium chicken broth
- 1/4 cup half-and-half
- 1 tsp Cajun seasoning (from the recipe's blend)
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
Steps:
1. Mise en place: slice the chicken into even strips, the peppers and onion into strips. Mince the garlic, grate the Parmesan from a block, mix the Cajun seasoning. Salted pasta water on to boil.
2. Season the chicken hard: strips tossed with 2 tbsp olive oil and 2 tbsp Cajun seasoning, every piece coated. Rest 10 minutes.
3. Blacken the chicken: a large skillet over medium-high until hot, the chicken in one layer, untouched 3-4 minutes until a dark, spiced crust forms. Toss, 2 minutes more, cooked through. Out — fond stays in the pan.
4. Vegetables in the drippings: remaining olive oil, peppers and onion with a pinch of salt, 5-6 minutes, scraping the pan, until softened and charred at the edges. Garlic 30 seconds.
5. Boil the penne 1 minute shy of done; reserve a cup of pasta water.
6. Build the sauce in the vegetable pan: half-and-half and broth in, simmer 3-4 minutes until slightly thickened. Off the heat, Parmesan and butter whisked in until silky — never boil a cheese sauce hard or it turns grainy.
7. Pasta and chicken through the sauce with splashes of pasta water until every piece is glossed. Scallions over, extra Cajun seasoning at the table.

Common mistakes:
- Boiling the finished sauce: the Parmesan splits. Off the heat for the cheese, always.
- Pale chicken: blackening is a crust, not a color of spice mix. Hot pan, no touching.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Cajun Cream Pan Sauce (for the chicken) — in the chicken skillet before the vegetables go in (or a second small pan), add 1/3 cup chicken broth and scrape up the blackened fond; simmer 1 minute. Add 1/4 cup half-and-half and 1 tsp Cajun seasoning; simmer 1 minute more. Off the heat, 1 tbsp cold butter. Spoon over the sliced chicken on top of each pasta serving instead of mixing it all in — a concentrated hit of the blackened flavor.

Title: Red beans and rice with andouille
Ingredients:
- 1 lb dried red kidney beans, soaked overnight (or 3 cans, drained)
- 1 lb andouille sausage, sliced into 1/2-inch coins
- 2 tbsp vegetable oil
- 2 large yellow onions, diced
- 1 large green bell pepper, diced
- 3 celery stalks, diced
- 6 cloves garlic, minced
- 8 cups low-sodium chicken broth (or water)
- 3 bay leaves
- 2 tsp dried thyme
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1/2 tsp cayenne
- 2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
- 1 tsp black pepper
- 3 cups long-grain white rice, rinsed
- Sliced scallions and hot sauce, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1-2 tsp hot sauce
- 1 tsp apple cider vinegar
- Pinch of smoked paprika
Steps:
1. The night before: soak the beans in cold water by 3 inches (or quick-soak: boil 2 minutes, cover, rest 1 hour, drain). Dice the onion, pepper and celery — the Holy Trinity — mince the garlic, slice the andouille into coins.
2. Brown the andouille hard: olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high, sausage coins in one layer, 3-4 minutes a side until deeply browned and the pot is coated in fond. Out to a plate.
3. Trinity in the drippings: onion, pepper and celery with a pinch of salt, 8 minutes, scraping, until soft and sweet. Garlic, thyme, smoked paprika and cayenne 1 minute.
4. Beans in: drained beans, broth, bay leaves. Bare simmer, partially covered, 1 1/2 to 2 hours until the beans are completely tender and the liquid is turning creamy. Stir now and then; add water if it gets thick before the beans are done.
5. Make it creamy: mash a cup of beans against the side of the pot and stir them back in — the traditional thickener. Sausage back in for 15 minutes.
6. Rice on (boil, cover, lowest heat 15, rest 10, fluff). Salt the beans generously at the end — they need it. Serve beans ladled over rice, scallions and hot sauce over.

Common mistakes:
- Salting too early with hard water beans: old beans take forever regardless; if they resist past 2 hours, a pinch of baking soda in the pot helps.
- Thin beans: the mash step is not optional — it is what makes the gravy.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Cayenne-Butter Pan Drizzle — in a small pan, melt 3 tbsp butter over medium heat; add 1 minced garlic clove and sizzle 30 seconds. Off the heat: 1-2 tsp hot sauce, 1 tsp apple cider vinegar and a pinch of smoked paprika. Spoon over each bowl of beans and rice — a hot, tangy butter slick, Louisiana-style.

Title: Chicken shawarma plates
Ingredients:
For the marinade:
- 2 1/2 lb boneless, skinless chicken thighs
- 1/2 cup plain whole-milk yogurt
- 1/4 cup olive oil
- Juice of 2 lemons
- 8 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp ground cumin
- 1 tbsp ground coriander
- 1 tbsp paprika
- 2 tsp turmeric
- 1 tsp cinnamon
- 1 tsp allspice
- 1/2 tsp cayenne
- 2 tsp kosher salt
- 1 tsp black pepper

For the garlic sauce:
- 1 cup plain Greek yogurt
- 1/4 cup mayonnaise
- 4 cloves garlic, grated
- 2 tbsp lemon juice
- 1 tsp kosher salt

For the plates:
- 2 1/2 cups basmati rice, rinsed (or 6 pita breads)
- 2 cups diced cucumber
- 2 cups halved cherry tomatoes
- 1 cup pickled turnips or dill pickles, sliced
- 1/2 red onion, thinly sliced
- 1 cup chopped fresh parsley
- Lemon wedges, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- About 1/3 cup pan drippings (plus low-sodium chicken broth as needed)
- Juice of 1/2 lemon
- 1/2 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
Steps:
1. Start 2-4 hours ahead: cut the thighs into 2-inch chunks. Whisk yogurt, olive oil, lemon juice, garlic and every spice; coat the chicken completely and refrigerate. Shawarma lives or dies on this marinade.
2. Garlic sauce: whisk Greek yogurt, mayonnaise, grated garlic, lemon juice and salt until it tastes boldly garlicky. Chill.
3. Rice on: rinsed basmati, water, pinch of salt — boil, cover, lowest heat 12-15 minutes, rest 10, fluff.
4. Roast the chicken hot and hard: spread the chunks on a sheet pan with space between them, 450 F for 20-25 minutes, flipping once, until the edges char black in spots and the centers hit 165 F. Crowded chicken steams into paleness — use two pans if you must. That char is the whole spit-roasted illusion.
5. Rest 5 minutes, then pile the chicken onto the rice with cucumber, tomatoes, pickles, red onion and parsley. Garlic sauce generously over, lemon wedges alongside. (Pita instead of rice is equally right.)

Common mistakes:
- Crowding the pan: char needs space and dry heat. Two pans, no regrets.
- Rushing the marinade: 30 minutes is a rumor of shawarma. Two hours minimum.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Shawarma Pan Juice Sauce — tip the roasting pan and pour the drippings into a small saucepan (about 1/3 cup; add chicken broth to reach it).
