PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Warm Sesame-Chile Oil — in a small pan, warm 3 tbsp toasted sesame oil with 1 tbsp gochugaru (Korean chile flakes) and 1 sliced garlic clove over low heat for 2 minutes — fragrant and brick-red, never smoking. Spoon a teaspoon over each bowl before mixing: warm, nutty heat threaded through the rice.

Title: Korean spicy chicken (dak bulgogi)
Ingredients:
2 1/2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
1/2 cup gochujang (Korean chili paste)
3 tablespoons soy sauce
2 tablespoons honey
2 tablespoons toasted sesame oil
6 cloves garlic, minced
1 tablespoon fresh ginger, grated
2 tablespoons rice wine (mirin) or water
1 teaspoon black pepper
2 large yellow onions, sliced into half-moons
4 scallions, cut into 2-inch pieces
1 tablespoon sesame seeds
4 1/2 cups cooked short-grain rice, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/4 cup water
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp honey
Steps:
1. Marinate (30 minutes to overnight): chicken pieces in the gochujang, soy, honey, sesame oil, garlic, ginger, rice wine and pepper. The longer it sits, the deeper the red.
2. Rice on. Onions into half-moons, scallions in 2-inch pieces.
3. Sear in batches on a screaming griddle or cast iron: chicken in one layer with space, untouched 3-4 minutes until the marinade's sugars char into dark, sticky edges; flip and cook through. Two batches minimum — a crowded pan boils the chicken in its own marinade and you get stew, not dakgalbi-style char.
4. Onions in the second batch's pan for 3-4 minutes until charred at the edges and sweet; everything back together for 1 minute to marry.
5. Scallions and sesame over. Serve over rice with the pan scrapings spooned on top — the charred marinade crust in the pan is liquid gold.

Common mistakes:
- Crowding: the char IS the dish. Batches and patience.
- Burning the honey: high heat is right, but keep the pieces moving after the flip — sugars go from charred to carbon fast.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Dak Bulgogi Pan Glaze — after the chicken and onions, add 1/4 cup water, 1 tbsp soy sauce and 1 tsp honey to the hot pan; scrape up the charred marinade and boil 1-2 minutes until syrupy. Pour over the chicken and rice — all the charred gochujang fond, collected instead of washed away.

Title: Pad thai with chicken
Ingredients:
1 pound flat rice noodles (about 1/4-inch wide)
1 1/2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken breast, sliced very thin
6 tablespoons tamarind paste (seedless)
1/3 cup fish sauce
1/3 cup palm sugar (or light brown sugar)
3 large eggs, beaten
8 ounces bean sprouts, divided
6 garlic chives or scallions, cut into 2-inch pieces
2 shallots, thinly sliced
4 tablespoons neutral oil, divided
1/2 cup roasted peanuts, crushed
Lime wedges, for serving
Chili flakes, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp tamarind paste
- 1 tbsp fish sauce
- 1 tbsp palm sugar (or light brown sugar)
- 3 tbsp water
Steps:
1. Mise en place: noodles soaked in hot tap water 20-30 minutes until pliable but still firm — never boiled. Sauce whisked: tamarind, fish sauce, palm sugar — taste it now: sour first, then salty, then sweet. Chicken sliced thin, shallots sliced, sprouts divided, chives cut.
2. Sear the chicken: a wok over high heat with 1 tbsp avocado oil, chicken in one layer, 2-3 minutes until golden at the edges and just cooked. Out.
3. Eggs: 1 tbsp oil, the beaten eggs in and scrambled in 30 seconds to soft curds. Out with the chicken.
4. The noodle fry: remaining oil, shallots 1 minute; noodles in with the sauce ladled around the edge. Toss and fold 2-3 minutes, adding splashes of water as the noodles drink the sauce, until tender and glossy and the sauce clings rather than pools. Taste a strand: it should need nothing.
5. Chicken, eggs, half the sprouts and the chives back for 30 seconds. Serve on warm plates with the remaining raw sprouts, crushed peanuts, lime wedges and chile flakes.

Common mistakes:
- Boiled noodles: mush by the time the sauce lands. Soak only.
- Sauce adjusted at the end: balance it before it hits the wok — the fry takes 3 minutes and there is no time to think.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Extra Tamarind Pan Sauce — in a small pan, simmer 2 tbsp tamarind paste, 1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp palm sugar and 3 tbsp water for 2 minutes until syrupy. Spoon over each plate for the sour-forward eaters — Bangkok stalls keep a pot of exactly this for the table.

Title: Thai green curry chicken
Ingredients:
2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken thighs, sliced into 1/2-inch strips
2 cans (14 ounces each) coconut milk (do not shake — you need the cream separated)
4 to 5 tablespoons Thai green curry paste (start with 4; add the fifth only if you like real heat)
1 tablespoon fish sauce, plus more to taste
2 teaspoons sugar (palm sugar if you have it)
1 cup low-sodium chicken broth
8 ounces bamboo shoots, drained (or 1 small zucchini, half-moons)
4 makrut lime leaves, torn (or zest of 1 lime)
2 Thai chiles, sliced (optional, for extra heat)
1 cup Thai basil leaves, packed
4 1/2 cups cooked jasmine rice, for serving
Lime wedges, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp avocado oil
- 1/2 cup Thai basil leaves
- Zest of 1 lime
Steps:
1. Mise en place: chicken in even strips. Coconut cans opened unshaken — the thick cream spooned off (about 3/4 cup). Lime leaves torn, bamboo shoots drained, basil picked, rice cooking.
2. Crack the coconut cream — the authentic first step: fry the curry paste in the thick cream over medium heat, stirring, 4-5 minutes, until the cream splits and the oil rises, red-green and fragrant. Paste fried in plain oil or thin milk never reaches this depth.
3. Chicken in, tossed 3-4 minutes until coated and just firming. Thin coconut milk, broth, fish sauce and sugar in; bare simmer 8-10 minutes.
4. Bamboo shoots and lime leaves in for 3 minutes. Taste and correct: it should be hot, salty, faintly sweet, in that order — fish sauce for salt, sugar for balance.
5. Off the heat: basil folded through until just wilted, Thai chiles over if you want the extra fire. Jasmine rice under.

Common mistakes:
- Skipping the cream crack: the curry tastes raw and one-note. The split oil is the flavor.
- Boiling after the basil: it blackens. Off the heat, fold, serve.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Thai Basil and Lime Oil — in a small pan, warm 3 tbsp avocado oil over low heat with 1/2 cup Thai basil leaves and the zest of 1 lime for 2 minutes until the oil turns green-gold and fragrant. Strain or not, your call. Spoon a teaspoon over each bowl of curry — a fresh herbal top note over the rich coconut.

Title: Peanut chicken noodles
Ingredients:
1 1/2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken thighs, sliced into thin strips
12 ounces rice noodles (flat, 1/4-inch) or lo mein noodles
3/4 cup creamy peanut butter (natural style is fine — stir it well)
1/3 cup soy sauce
3 tablespoons unseasoned rice vinegar
2 tablespoons toasted sesame oil
2 tablespoons honey
1 tablespoon sriracha (start with 2 teaspoons for mild)
1/2 cup hot water, plus more as needed
4 cloves garlic, minced
1 tablespoon fresh ginger, grated
2 tablespoons neutral oil, divided
2 cups shredded cabbage
2 carrots, julienned (thin matchsticks)
4 scallions, sliced
1/2 cup roasted peanuts, crushed
1/4 cup fresh cilantro leaves
Lime wedges, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp avocado oil
- 1 tbsp red chile flakes
- 1 tsp sesame seeds
- 1 clove garlic, minced
Steps:
1. Mise en place: chicken in thin strips. Whisk the peanut sauce (peanut butter, soy, vinegar, sesame oil, honey, sriracha, garlic, ginger, hot water) until smooth — it looks broken, then suddenly it is silk; thin to a pourable ribbons consistency. Vegetables prepped in piles.
2. Noodles: cook 1 minute shy of done, drain, rinse cold to stop them, toss with a teaspoon of sesame oil.
3. Sear the chicken: a large skillet over medium-high with 1 tbsp avocado oil, chicken in one layer, untouched 3 minutes for golden edges; toss 2 minutes to cooked through. Fond stays in the pan.
4. Vegetables in the drippings: cabbage and carrots 2-3 minutes until charred at the edges and just tender — they should keep their crunch.
5. Everything together off the heat: noodles, chicken, vegetables, the peanut sauce and splashes of hot water, tossed until every strand is coated and glossy. The residual heat warms the sauce through; boiling it makes it split and go dull.
6. Peanuts, cilantro and scallions over; lime wedges alongside.

Common mistakes:
- Cooking the peanut sauce: it breaks and turns pasty. Off the heat, tossed through.
- Sauce too thick: thin with hot water by the spoonful until it ribbons.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Chile Crisp Oil — in a small pan, heat 3 tbsp avocado oil until shimmering. Put 1 tbsp chile flakes, 1 tsp sesame seeds and 1 minced garlic clove in a heatproof bowl; pour the hot oil over and let it sizzle 1 minute. Spoon over each bowl of noodles — crunchy, fragrant heat over the creamy peanut sauce.

Title: Larb (Thai chicken salad)
Ingredients:
2 pounds ground chicken (not chicken breast — the fat keeps it juicy)
1/3 cup uncooked sticky (glutinous) rice, for the toasted rice powder
1/3 cup fresh lime juice (about 3 limes), plus wedges for serving
1/4 cup fish sauce
2 teaspoons sugar
1 teaspoon dried chili flakes, plus more to taste
1/2 red onion, very thinly sliced
4 scallions, thinly sliced
3 Thai chiles, thinly sliced (optional)
1 cup fresh mint leaves, torn
1 cup fresh cilantro leaves, roughly chopped
2 heads butter lettuce, leaves separated
3 cups cooked sticky rice or jasmine rice, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp avocado oil
- 2 cloves garlic, thinly sliced
- 1 tsp red chile flakes
Steps:
1. Toasted rice powder (khao khua) — the soul of larb: the sticky rice in a dry skillet over medium heat, stirred constantly, 5-7 minutes until deep golden and smelling like popcorn; grind to a coarse powder in a spice grinder or mortar. Do not walk away — it goes from golden to burned in the last minute.
2. Dressing whisked: lime juice, fish sauce, sugar, chile flakes — assertively sour, salty, hot. Slice the onion paper-thin, scallions thin, chiles thin; herbs torn.
3. Cook the chicken: a skillet (or wok) over medium-high with just 2 tbsp water (the traditional method — no oil), ground chicken broken fine, 5-6 minutes until just cooked and crumbly, no browning wanted here. Off the heat immediately.
4. Dress while warm: the dressing and half the rice powder over the warm chicken, tossed through — the chicken drinks it. Then the onion, scallions and chiles.
5. Herbs folded in at the very end so they stay vivid. The remaining rice powder sprinkled over. Taste: it should make your mouth water — more lime if it does not.
6. Serve in lettuce cups with sticky rice alongside.

Common mistakes:
- Browning the chicken: larb chicken is poached-tender, not seared. Water, not oil.
- Herbs cooked in: they blacken and taste muddy. Folded in off the heat.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Garlic and Chile Oil — in a small pan, heat 3 tbsp avocado oil until shimmering; add 2 sliced garlic cloves and 1 tsp chile flakes, sizzle 30 seconds until the garlic is pale gold. Drizzle just a little over each lettuce cup — a fragrant, garlicky heat slick over the sour, herbal larb.

Title: Cajun shrimp and sausage sheet pan
Ingredients:
1 1/2 pounds large shrimp (21/25 count), peeled and deveined
12 ounces andouille sausage, sliced into 1/2-inch coins
1 1/2 pounds baby potatoes, halved
3 ears corn, cut into 2-inch rounds
1 large yellow onion, cut into wedges
3 tablespoons olive oil
3 tablespoons Cajun seasoning (salt-free if your sausage is very salty)
4 cloves garlic, minced
1 lemon, cut into wedges
1/4 cup fresh parsley, chopped

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 4 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tsp Cajun seasoning
Steps:
1. Oven at 425 F. Potatoes halved (quartered if large), corn rounds, onion wedges, sausage coins, garlic minced. Shrimp peeled, deveined and patted very dry.
2. Start what takes longest: potatoes and corn tossed with 2 tbsp olive oil, half the Cajun seasoning and the garlic, single layer on the biggest sheet pan you have. Roast 20 minutes.
3. Sausage and onion on the pan for 10 minutes — the andouille renders its spicy fat over everything, which is the sheet-pan boil's whole trick.
4. Shrimp last: tossed with the remaining oil and seasoning, onto the pan in one layer for 6-8 minutes until pink and just curled. A minute too long and they go rubbery — they cook in the pan's carryover too.
5. Everything tossed on the pan with the lemon wedges squeezed over and parsley scattered. Serve straight off the pan, family style.

Common mistakes:
- Shrimp in from the start: rubber. They go on last, always.
- Wet shrimp: they steam pale. Pat them dry like the recipe depends on it — it does.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Cajun Garlic Butter — in a small pan, melt 4 tbsp butter over medium heat; add 1 minced garlic clove and 1 tsp Cajun seasoning, sizzle 30 seconds until brick red and fragrant. Pour over the whole sheet pan at the table and toss once — the boil-bag finish, without the bag.

Title: Jambalaya
Ingredients:
1 pound boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
12 ounces andouille sausage, sliced into 1/2-inch coins
3/4 pound large shrimp, peeled and deveined (optional but classic)
2 tablespoons vegetable oil
2 large yellow onions, diced (1/2-inch cubes)
1 green bell pepper, diced (see note in steps)
3 celery stalks, diced
4 cloves garlic, minced
2 cups long-grain white rice
1 can (14.5 ounces) diced tomatoes, undrained
2 tablespoons tomato paste
3 1/2 cups low-sodium chicken broth
3 tablespoons Creole or Cajun seasoning
2 bay leaves
1 teaspoon dried thyme
4 scallions, sliced, for serving
Hot sauce, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1/2 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 clove garlic, minced
Steps:
1. Mise en place: chicken in 1-inch pieces, andouille in coins, shrimp peeled and dried. The trinity diced (onion, celery, and the pepper; a poblano stands in beautifully). Garlic minced, rice measured, spices out. Gumbo rules apply: once the rice goes in, the pot wants no stirring.
2. Brown in stages: avocado oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high. Andouille first, 4-5 minutes until its edges crisp and the fat renders; out. Chicken salted and seared in the fat, 4-5 minutes untouched for a real crust; out.
3. Trinity into the drippings, 8-10 minutes, scraping, until soft and golden at the edges and the fond melts into the vegetables. Garlic and tomato paste 1 minute, until the paste darkens.
4. Rice in, stirred 1-2 minutes to toast in the fat (this keeps the grains separate). Tomatoes, broth, Cajun seasoning, bay and thyme in; the meats back. Bring to a simmer, scraping the bottom.
5. Cover, lowest heat, 18-20 minutes. NO PEEKING and NO STIRRING — the rice steams itself done. Shrimp laid on top for the final 5 minutes to steam pink.
6. Off the heat, rest 10 minutes, then fluff once with a fork. Scallions and hot sauce at the table.

Common mistakes:
- Stirring the rice: gummy, broken grains. Lid on, hands off.
- Pale chicken: sear it properly before the braise; the fond is the jambalaya's bass note.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Smoked Paprika Butter Drizzle — in a small pan, melt 3 tbsp butter over medium heat; add 1/2 tsp smoked paprika and 1 minced garlic clove, sizzle 30 seconds until deep red. Spoon over each bowl of jambalaya — a smoky butter slick that amplifies the andouille without more heat.

Title: Chicken and sausage gumbo
Ingredients:
3/4 cup all-purpose flour
3/4 cup vegetable oil
1 1/2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
12 ounces andouille sausage, sliced into 1/2-inch coins
2 large yellow onions, diced
1 green bell pepper, diced (see note in steps)
3 celery stalks, diced
6 cloves garlic, minced
6 cups low-sodium chicken broth, warmed
3 tablespoons Cajun seasoning (salt-free preferred)
1 teaspoon dried thyme
2 bay leaves
8 ounces sliced okra (optional, traditional thickener)
4 cups cooked long-grain white rice, for serving
4 scallions, sliced, for serving
Filé powder, for serving (optional)

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 clove garlic, thinly sliced
- 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper
Steps:
1. Mise en place — everything, before the roux: trinity diced (onion, celery, and the pepper; a poblano plus a minced jalapeño stands in perfectly), garlic minced, chicken cut, andouille sliced, broth warmed. Once the roux starts, you stir for 40 minutes and prep nothing.
2. Season and sear: chicken in avocado oil over medium-high, 4-5 minutes untouched for a deep crust; out. Andouille crisped in the same fat; out. Their fond is the gumbo's first layer.
3. The roux — the commitment: flour and avocado oil (equal parts — same roux, cleaner finish) in the Dutch oven over medium heat, whisked smooth, then stirred constantly with a wooden spoon, 30-45 minutes, through peanut butter, through copper, to dark chocolate. It should smell like toasted nuts and popcorn. Black specks mean it burned — start over; a burned roux cannot be saved and will not be argued with.
4. Trinity into the roux (it will hiss and stop the roux's cooking — timing is mercy), 8-10 minutes until soft. Garlic 1 minute. Warm broth in a ladle at a time, whisking, until it pours like gravy, then the rest.
5. Cajun seasoning, thyme, bay; the meats back; okra in if using. Bare simmer 1 1/2 hours, skimming fat, until the chicken is falling apart and the gumbo coats a spoon like velvet.
6. Rice mounded in bowls, gumbo ladled around, scallions over, filé and hot sauce at the table — filé goes in off the heat or it turns stringy.

Common mistakes:
- Walking away from the roux: it has exactly two states — stirring, and burning. Phone down.
- Cold broth into hot roux: it seizes into lumps. Warm broth, ladle by ladle.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Cayenne Garlic Butter — in a small pan, melt 3 tbsp butter with 1 sliced garlic clove and 1/4 tsp cayenne over medium heat, sizzling 45 seconds until the garlic is golden and the butter foams red. Spoon a little over each bowl just before serving — a hot butter finish that Louisiana cooks will recognize as pure lagniappe.

Title: Blackened chicken with dirty rice
Ingredients:
6 boneless, skinless chicken breasts (about 2 1/2 pounds total)
3 tablespoons paprika
2 tablespoons garlic powder
2 tablespoons onion powder
1 tablespoon dried thyme
1 tablespoon dried oregano
2 teaspoons cayenne pepper (use 1 teaspoon for mild)
2 teaspoons black pepper
1 tablespoon kosher salt
4 tablespoons unsalted butter, melted
For the dirty rice:
3/4 pound ground pork
2 cups long-grain white rice
3 1/2 cups low-sodium chicken broth
1 large yellow onion, finely diced
1 green bell pepper, finely diced (see note in steps)
2 celery stalks, finely diced
4 cloves garlic, minced
2 tablespoons Cajun seasoning
3 scallions, sliced
2 tablespoons fresh parsley, chopped

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/4 cup low-sodium chicken broth
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
- Juice of 1/2 lemon
Steps:
1. Mise en place: chicken pounded to even 3/4 inch. Blackening spice mixed (paprika through salt). Trinity for the rice diced fine (onion, celery, and the pepper — poblano is an excellent stand-in). Garlic minced, butter melted for brushing.
2. Dirty rice first (it holds while the chicken cooks): pork in a skillet over medium-high, broken small and browned until crisp at the edges, 6-8 minutes. Trinity into the drippings 6-8 minutes until soft and golden; garlic and Cajun seasoning 30 seconds. Rice stirred in to toast 1 minute; broth in; cover, lowest heat 18 minutes; rest 10 off the heat.
3. Blacken the chicken: brush with melted butter, press the spice mix on thick — a crust, not a dusting. A cast-iron skillet over high heat until it just begins to smoke (vent on, windows open — blackening is a smoky business). Chicken down, untouched 5-6 minutes until the crust is nearly black and crisp; flip, 4-5 minutes to 165 F.
4. Rest the chicken 5 minutes; slice thickly.
5. Fluff the rice with a fork, scallions and parsley through. Chicken fanned over the rice, pan butter spooned around.

Common mistakes:
- A timid spice coat: blackening IS the crust. Thick, pressed on, both sides.
- Lukewarm pan: the chicken steams in its own butter and the crust never forms. Smoking cast iron.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Lemon-Butter Pan Sauce — after the chicken, lower the heat and add 1/4 cup chicken broth to the cast iron; scrape up the blackened fond and simmer 1 minute. Off the heat, whisk in 2 tbsp cold butter and the juice of 1/2 lemon until glossy and dark. Spoon over the sliced chicken — the smoky crust, turned into sauce.

Title: Pulled chicken sandwiches
Ingredients:
3 pounds boneless, skinless chicken thighs
2 tablespoons brown sugar
1 tablespoon paprika
1 tablespoon garlic powder
1 tablespoon onion powder
2 teaspoons kosher salt
1 teaspoon black pepper
1 teaspoon mustard powder
1 cup low-sodium chicken broth
1 1/4 cups barbecue sauce, plus more for serving
6 brioche buns
For the slaw:
4 cups shredded green cabbage (about 1/2 head)
1/3 cup mayonnaise
2 tablespoons apple cider vinegar
1 tablespoon sugar
1/2 teaspoon kosher salt
1/4 teaspoon black pepper

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1 cup chicken braising liquid (from the recipe)
- 1/4 cup barbecue sauce
Steps:
1. Make the slaw first: dressing whisked (mayo, vinegar, sugar, salt, pepper), cabbage tossed through, refrigerated 30 minutes minimum so it softens and marries.
2. Rub the chicken thighs all over with the spice mix. Broth into a Dutch oven or slow cooker.
3. Sear before braising — the smoker-less trick: a film of avocado oil in a skillet over medium-high, thighs down 4 minutes untouched until the rubbed crust chars dark; flip, 2 minutes. This crust is what makes pulled chicken taste like it met smoke.
4. Braise: thighs and their juices into the broth, cover, bare simmer 25-30 minutes (or 3 hours on low in a slow cooker) until they shred at a fork's suggestion.
5. Shred in the pot, then — the move that matters — simmer the shredded chicken uncovered in its liquid 5 minutes to reduce, toss with the barbecue sauce, and let it drink. Dry pulled chicken is just shredded chicken.
6. Buns toasted in butter until golden. Chicken piled high, slaw on top (inside the sandwich, always), extra sauce at the table.

Common mistakes:
- Skipping the sear: boiled-tasting chicken in sauce. The char is the barbecue illusion, and it is convincing.
- Watery sauce: reduce the braising liquid into the meat before saucing.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): BBQ Pan Glaze — ladle 1 cup of the braising liquid into a small saucepan with 1/4 cup barbecue sauce; boil 5 minutes until reduced to a glossy glaze. Brush over the piled chicken on each bun — a shiny, concentrated top coat that keeps the top bites as saucy as the bottom.

Title: Oven fried chicken with green beans
Ingredients:
3 pounds bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and drumsticks
2 cups buttermilk
1 tablespoon kosher salt, plus more for the coating
1 teaspoon hot sauce
1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
1 1/2 cups panko breadcrumbs
2 tablespoons Cajun seasoning
1 teaspoon baking powder
1 teaspoon black pepper
3 tablespoons vegetable oil
For the green beans:
1 1/2 pounds fresh green beans, trimmed
2 tablespoons unsalted butter
3 cloves garlic, minced
1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice
1/2 teaspoon kosher salt

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- 2 tbsp honey
- 1/2 tsp hot sauce (or a pinch of cayenne)
Steps:
1. Brine: chicken in the buttermilk, salt and hot sauce, refrigerated 2 hours to overnight — the buttermilk tenderizes and seasons to the bone.
2. Oven at 425 F with a rack set in a rimmed sheet pan — the rack is everything; air under the chicken crisps the bottom. Coating mixed: flour, panko, Cajun seasoning, baking powder, pepper, salt.
3. Coat: chicken out of the buttermilk (let the excess drip), pressed firmly into the coating on all sides. Rest 10 minutes on the rack so the crust hydrates and sets. Brush or drizzle with the avocado oil (same crisp, better flavor).
4. Bake 35-40 minutes, flipping once at 25, until deep golden, crisp, and 165 F at the thickest piece. If a spot looks pale, another 2 minutes — color is doneness's messenger.
5. Green beans while the chicken rests: a skillet over medium-high with the butter, beans in one layer, 5-6 minutes undisturbed until blistered in spots; garlic 30 seconds; lemon juice and salt off the heat.
6. Serve chicken over or beside the beans, lemon bright against the crust.

Common mistakes:
- No rack: the bottom steams into sogginess no oven heat can rescue. Rack, always.
- Crowded coating: press it on and rest it, or it sheds in the oven.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Hot Honey Butter — in a small pan, warm 3 tbsp butter and 2 tbsp honey with 1/2 tsp hot sauce (or a pinch of cayenne) over low heat until melted together. Brush over the hot chicken — hot honey on fried chicken is a Nashville handshake, and the oven version earns it.

Title: Meatloaf with mashed potatoes
Ingredients:
2 pounds ground beef (80/20)
1 cup panko breadcrumbs
3/4 cup whole milk
2 large eggs, beaten
1 large yellow onion, finely diced
3 cloves garlic, minced
1 tablespoon olive oil
2 tablespoons Worcestershire sauce
2 tablespoons ketchup, plus 1/2 cup for the glaze
1 tablespoon Dijon mustard
1 teaspoon dried thyme
2 teaspoons kosher salt
1 teaspoon black pepper
For the glaze:
1/2 cup ketchup
2 tablespoons brown sugar
1 tablespoon apple cider vinegar
For the mashed potatoes:
3 pounds Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and cut into 1 1/2-inch chunks
6 tablespoons unsalted butter
3/4 cup whole milk, warmed
1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, plus more to taste
1/2 teaspoon black pepper

For the pan sauce (optional):
- About 1/2 cup meatloaf pan drippings (plus low-sodium beef broth as needed)
- 1 tbsp ketchup
- 1 tsp Worcestershire sauce
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
Steps:
1. Oven at 350 F. Glaze stirred (ketchup, brown sugar, vinegar) — sweet, tangy, bold. Onion sautéed in the olive oil 5-6 minutes until golden at the edges and sweet; garlic 30 seconds. (Raw onion in meatloaf stays raw — this step is not optional for good meatloaf.)
2. Mix with a light hand: beef, panko soaked in the milk (the panade — it is what keeps meatloaf tender), eggs, the sautéed onion, Worcestershire, ketchup, Dijon, thyme, salt and pepper. Mix until just combined — overworking makes a dense, bouncy loaf.
3. Shape free-form on a lined sheet pan (a loaf pan steams the sides; free-form browns them). Brush with half the glaze.
4. Bake 40 minutes; brush with the rest of the glaze; bake 15-20 more to 160 F, the glaze lacquered and caramelized at the edges.
5. Mashed potatoes while it rests: potatoes from cold salted water, simmered 15-18 minutes until completely tender; drained, returned to the hot pot 1 minute to steam dry; mashed with the butter and warm milk, salt and pepper — fluffy, never whipped to glue.
6. Rest the loaf 10 minutes, slice thick, serve over the potatoes with pan juices spooned around.

Common mistakes:
- Overmixing: meatloaf mixed like bread dough turns into a football. Just combined.
- Skipping the panade soak: dry crumb. Five minutes in the milk.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Meatloaf Pan Gravy — pour the pan drippings into a small saucepan (about 1/2 cup; add beef broth to reach it); add 1 tbsp ketchup and 1 tsp Worcestershire; simmer 2-3 minutes and whisk in 1 tbsp cold butter at the end. Spoon over the slices and potatoes — the glaze's drippings, turned into gravy.

Title: Pot roast with carrots and potatoes
Ingredients:
1 beef chuck roast, 3 1/2 pounds
2 tablespoons vegetable oil
2 teaspoons kosher salt, plus more to taste
1 teaspoon black pepper
2 large yellow onions, quartered
6 cloves garlic, smashed
2 tablespoons tomato paste
1 cup dry red wine
3 cups low-sodium beef broth
2 bay leaves
4 sprigs fresh thyme (or 1 teaspoon dried)
2 sprigs fresh rosemary (or 1/2 teaspoon dried)
1 1/2 pounds carrots, cut into 2-inch pieces
2 pounds Yukon Gold or red potatoes, cut into 1 1/2-inch chunks

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter, plus 1 tbsp more (cold) to finish
- 8 oz mushrooms, sliced
- 1 cup pot roast braising liquid (from the recipe)
Steps:
1. Oven at 300 F. Chuck roast out 30 minutes ahead, patted completely dry, salted and peppered all over. Vegetables cut big — 2-inch pieces survive a braise. Wine and broth measured.
2. Sear the roast like it matters (it does): avocado oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high until shimmering, roast down 5-6 minutes untouched per side until a deep mahogany crust forms on every face including the ends. This crust is the difference between pot roast and boiled beef.
3. Roast out; onions into the drippings 5 minutes, scraping, until golden at the edges; garlic and tomato paste 2 minutes until the paste darkens. Wine in, scraping every browned bit loose, reduced by half.
4. Braise: broth, bay, thyme and rosemary in; roast back with its juices. Cover, into the oven 2 hours.
5. Carrots and potatoes nestled in around the roast; back for 1 to 1 1/2 hours until the vegetables are tender and the meat surrenders to a fork.
6. Rest the roast 15 minutes in its liquid. Serve in thick slices (or pulled in chunks, pot-roast style) with the vegetables and braising liquid spooned over — the liquid IS the sauce; reduce it 5 minutes on the stove if you want it thicker.

Common mistakes:
- A pale sear: gray meat, weak gravy. Dry meat, hot pan, patience.
- Vegetables in from the start: they dissolve. Two hours in, not four.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Mushroom Pan Sauce — while the roast rests, sauté 8 oz sliced mushrooms in 1 tbsp butter in a small pan over medium-high until deeply browned, 5-6 minutes. Add 1 cup of the braising liquid and simmer 2 minutes; off the heat, 1 tbsp cold butter whisked in. Spoon over the sliced roast — an extra layer of savory on a Sunday classic.

Title: Beef stew
Ingredients:
2 1/2 pounds beef chuck roast, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
1/3 cup all-purpose flour
2 teaspoons kosher salt, divided, plus more to taste
1 teaspoon black pepper
3 tablespoons vegetable oil, divided
1 large yellow onion, diced
3 carrots, sliced into 1/2-inch rounds (for the base)
3 celery stalks, sliced
4 cloves garlic, minced
2 tablespoons tomato paste
1 cup dry red wine
4 cups low-sodium beef broth
2 bay leaves
1 teaspoon dried thyme
1 1/2 pounds Yukon Gold potatoes, cut into 1-inch chunks
3 carrots, cut into 1-inch chunks (added later)
1 cup frozen peas

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 tbsp prepared horseradish
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh parsley
- Pinch of kosher salt
Steps:
1. Mise en place: beef in 1 1/2-inch cubes (bigger than you think — small cubes dry out), tossed with the flour, 1 tsp salt and pepper. Vegetables prepped in two waves: the base carrots and celery sliced for the pot; the potatoes and late carrots chunked for later.
2. Brown the beef in batches: avocado oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high, beef in one layer, 3-4 minutes untouched per batch until every piece wears a deep crust. Three batches, no shortcuts — this fond is the stew.
3. Onion, base carrots and celery into the drippings 6-8 minutes, scraping, until golden at the edges; garlic and tomato paste 2 minutes until darkened.
4. Wine in, scraping, reduced by half. Broth, bay and thyme in; beef and its juices back. Bare simmer, partially covered, 1 1/2 hours.
5. Potatoes and late carrots in for 30-40 minutes until tender and the beef gives at a fork's press. Peas in for the final 3 minutes — bright green or don't bother.
6. Salt boldly, pepper, and let it stand 10 minutes; stews thicken and marry as they rest.

Common mistakes:
- One crowded batch of beef: steamed, gray, and the stew never recovers. Batches.
- Peas in early: khaki peas. Three minutes at the end.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Parsley-Horseradish Butter — in a small pan, melt 3 tbsp butter over medium heat until foaming; off the heat, stir in 1 tbsp prepared horseradish, 2 tbsp chopped parsley and a pinch of salt. Spoon a little over each bowl of stew — a bright, peppery butter melting into the rich beef, the way Alpine kitchens finish a goulash.

Title: Lighter chicken pot pie
Ingredients:
1 1/2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken breasts
2 tablespoons unsalted butter
1 large yellow onion, diced (1/4-inch cubes)
3 carrots, diced (1/4-inch cubes)
3 celery stalks, diced (1/4-inch cubes)
1/3 cup all-purpose flour
2 1/2 cups low-sodium chicken broth
1 cup 2% milk
1 1/2 cups frozen peas
1 teaspoon dried thyme
1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, plus more to taste
1/2 teaspoon black pepper
2 tablespoons fresh parsley, chopped
For the biscuit topping:
2 cups all-purpose flour
1 tablespoon baking powder
1/2 teaspoon baking soda
1 teaspoon sugar
1 teaspoon kosher salt
6 tablespoons cold unsalted butter, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
3/4 cup cold buttermilk, plus more as needed

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 tsp fresh thyme leaves
- 1/2 cup heavy cream
- Kosher salt and black pepper to taste
Steps:
1. Oven at 425 F. Biscuit butter cubed and kept cold — cold butter is flaky biscuits, full stop. Vegetables in even 1/4-inch dice.
2. Poach the chicken gently: salted water at a bare simmer, breasts 14-16 minutes to 165 F; out, rested, diced. Never boiled — poached chicken stays silky in the filling.
3. Build the filling: butter in a Dutch oven, onion, carrot and celery 8-10 minutes until soft and sweet. Flour stirred in 2 minutes (a pale roux). Broth and milk in a stream, whisking, simmered 3-4 minutes until it coats a spoon. Chicken, peas, thyme, salt, pepper, parsley through. It should taste like the finished pie — season it now, confidently.
4. Biscuits: flour, baking powder, soda, sugar and salt whisked; cold butter cut in to pea-size; cold buttermilk stirred in just until a shaggy dough forms. Pat out and cut 8 rounds, or drop in rustic mounds — do not overwork it.
5. Filling into a 9x13 (or keep it in the Dutch oven), biscuits laid on top with a little space to puff. Bake 18-22 minutes until the biscuits are deep golden and the filling bubbles at the edges.
6. Rest 10 minutes — the filling sets from lava to gravy.

Common mistakes:
- Warm butter in the biscuits: they bake up tough and flat. Cold butter, cold buttermilk, hot oven.
- Thin filling: the roux needs its simmer. It thickens more in the oven, but only a little.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Herb Cream Pan Sauce — in a small pan, melt 1 tbsp butter with 1 tsp fresh thyme leaves for 30 seconds; add 1/2 cup heavy cream and simmer 2-3 minutes until slightly thickened; salt and pepper. Spoon over each serving of pot pie — a little extra gravy richness for the biscuit to soak up.

Title: Turkey sloppy joes
Ingredients:
- 2 lb 93% lean ground turkey
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 2 medium yellow onions, diced (about 2 cups)
- 1 large green bell pepper, diced (about 1 1/2 cups)
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 can (15 oz) tomato sauce
- 1/2 cup ketchup
- 3 tbsp Worcestershire sauce
- 3 tbsp brown sugar, packed
- 2 tbsp yellow mustard
- 1 tbsp chili powder
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 1/2 tsp kosher salt (start with this; add more to taste at the end)
- 1 tsp black pepper
- 6 whole wheat hamburger buns, split

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 tbsp yellow mustard
- 2 tbsp dill pickle juice
- 1/4 tsp smoked paprika
Steps:
1. Mise en place: onions and the pepper diced to 1/4 inch, garlic minced to a paste. Sauce ingredients measured — sloppy joes move fast once the pan is hot. Buns split.
2. Brown the turkey in two waves: olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high, half the turkey spread flat and left untouched 4 minutes until a dark crust forms; break up and remove. Repeat. Gray, steamed turkey is why people think sloppy joes are bland.
3. Onion and pepper into the drippings, 6-8 minutes until golden at the edges and sweet — they should take on real color. Garlic 30 seconds.
4. Sauce: tomato sauce, ketchup, Worcestershire, brown sugar, mustard, chili powder and smoked paprika in; scrape the pan. Turkey back. Simmer 8-10 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick enough that a spoon leaves a trail. Salt in stages — the sauces bring their own.
5. Toast the buns in a dry skillet or under the broiler until golden — a toasted bun survives the sauce; a soft one disintegrates.
6. Pile the mixture high, top bun on, pickles alongside if you have them.

Common mistakes:
- One crowded batch of turkey: it steams in its juices and never browns. Two waves.
- Serving on raw buns: mush by the third bite. Toast them.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Smoky Mustard Pan Sauce — in a small pan, melt 1 tbsp butter; whisk in 1 tbsp yellow mustard, 2 tbsp pickle juice and 1/4 tsp smoked paprika; simmer 30 seconds. Drizzle over the sloppy joe filling on each bun — a tangy, smoky top note that cuts the sweetness.

Title: Cheeseburger bowls
Ingredients:
- 2 lb 90% lean ground beef
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 large yellow onion, diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp Worcestershire sauce
- 1 tbsp yellow mustard
- 2 tsp kosher salt
- 1 tsp black pepper
- 1 tsp garlic powder
- 1 tsp onion powder
- 6 cups chopped romaine lettuce (about 2 hearts)
- 3 cups cherry tomatoes, halved
- 1 1/2 cups shredded sharp cheddar cheese (6 oz)
- 1 1/2 cups diced dill pickles
- 1/2 red onion, thinly sliced
- 1/2 cup light mayonnaise
- 1/4 cup ketchup
- 2 tbsp yellow mustard
- 2 tbsp dill pickle juice
- 1 tsp paprika

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/4 cup dill pickle juice
- 1 tsp Worcestershire sauce
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
Steps:
1. Mise en place: lettuce chopped and dried, tomatoes halved, pickles diced, red onion sliced paper-thin, cheddar shredded. Burger sauce whisked (mayo, ketchup, mustard, pickle juice, paprika) and refrigerated — it should taste like the drive-thru sauce of memory.
2. Brown the beef hard: olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high, beef in one layer, untouched 4-5 minutes until a dark crust forms; then break into bite-size crumbles and finish. Drain the excess fat, leaving a spoonful.
3. Season in the pan: Worcestershire, mustard, salt, pepper, garlic and onion powders tossed through over the heat for 1 minute — the beef should taste like a smashed burger patty, seasoned boldly.
4. Build the bowls: romaine, beef, cheddar (it melts slightly against the hot beef — that is the point), tomatoes, pickles, red onion.
5. Burger sauce drizzled generously over. Serve with extra pickles — there are never enough.

Common mistakes:
- Underseasoned beef: a bowl has no bun to hide behind. Season like a burger, because it is one.
- Wet lettuce: the sauce slides off and pools. Dry it properly.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Pickle-Brined Beef Pan Drizzle — after the beef, add 1/4 cup pickle juice and 1 tsp Worcestershire to the skillet; scrape up the crust and boil 1 minute. Off the heat, whisk in 1 tbsp cold butter until glossy and dark. Spoon over the beef in each bowl — the skillet's burger crust, poured back on.

Title: Buffalo chicken stuffed sweet potatoes
Ingredients:
- 6 medium sweet potatoes (about 2 1/2 lb), scrubbed
- 2 lb boneless, skinless chicken breasts
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp garlic powder
- 1 tsp onion powder
- 1 tsp kosher salt
- 1/2 tsp black pepper
- 3/4 cup Frank's RedHot or other cayenne hot sauce
- 3 tbsp butter, melted
- 1 tbsp white vinegar
- 1/2 cup light ranch dressing
- 3 stalks celery, diced small
- 1/4 cup crumbled blue cheese (1 oz)
- 2 scallions, thinly sliced

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 2 tbsp crumbled blue cheese
- 1 tsp hot sauce (such as Frank's RedHot)
Steps:
1. Oven at 400 F. Sweet potatoes scrubbed, poked 4-5 times each, rubbed lightly with oil and salted; onto a lined pan for 45-55 minutes until they slump and a knife slides in like butter.
2. Buffalo sauce: hot sauce, melted butter and vinegar whisked — taste it; it should be hot first, buttery second.
3. Poach the chicken gently: breasts in simmering water (or broth) 14-16 minutes to 165 F; rest and shred with two forks into strands. (Or sear and shred for more flavor — both work; poached shreds finer.)
4. Toss the warm shredded chicken through the buffalo sauce until every strand is coated and glossy. It should be saucy, not soupy.
5. Split the sweet potatoes, fluff the flesh with a fork and a pinch of salt, and pile the buffalo chicken in high.
6. Ranch drizzled over, celery and blue cheese scattered, scallions on top. The cold-crisp toppings against the hot chicken are the whole design.

Common mistakes:
- Undercooked sweet potatoes: they should slump. A firm center ruins the scoop.
- Cold chicken into cold sauce: toss them together warm so the shreds drink the sauce.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Blue Cheese Butter — in a small pan, melt 2 tbsp butter over low heat; add 2 tbsp crumbled blue cheese and 1 tsp hot sauce, whisking until just melted into a pourable sauce — do not boil. Drizzle over the stuffed potatoes: buffalo wings' two sauces, finally in one place.

Title: Chicken and broccoli rice casserole
Ingredients:
- 2 lb boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut in 3/4-inch cubes
- 1 1/2 cups long-grain white rice, uncooked
- 6 cups broccoli florets (about 1 1/2 lb), cut small
- 2 tbsp butter
- 1 tbsp olive oil (for the panko topping)
- 1 medium yellow onion, diced
- 8 oz mushrooms, sliced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/3 cup all-purpose flour
- 3 cups 2% milk
- 2 cups low-sodium chicken broth
- 2 cups shredded sharp cheddar cheese (8 oz), divided
- 1 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
- 1 tsp black pepper
- 1 tsp garlic powder
- 1 tsp onion powder
- 1 tsp paprika
- 1/2 cup panko breadcrumbs

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1/4 cup 2% milk
- 1/2 cup shredded sharp cheddar cheese
- Pinch of paprika
Steps:
1. Oven at 375 F; 9x13 dish greased. Chicken in even 3/4-inch cubes, broccoli in small florets, onion diced, mushrooms sliced, garlic minced, cheese shredded.
2. Rice cooked and spread in the dish — or use the par-cook method: it finishes in the casserole's sauce.
3. Sear the chicken: butter in a large skillet over medium-high, chicken in one layer, untouched 3-4 minutes for golden edges; toss to just cooked. Out — it finishes in the oven and must not dry.
4. Mushrooms in the drippings 4-5 minutes until deeply browned (crowd them and they steam — space or batches); onion in 4 minutes until golden; garlic 30 seconds. Flour stirred in 1 minute; milk and broth in a stream, simmered 3 minutes to a proper sauce. Half the cheddar melted through; salt, pepper and the spices in.
5. Broccoli blanched 2 minutes in the rice water or microwaved until bright — raw broccoli stays raw in a casserole.
6. Assemble: rice, chicken and sauce folded together in the dish; remaining cheddar and the oiled panko scattered over. Bake 20-25 minutes until bubbling and the top is crisp and golden. Rest 5 minutes.

Common mistakes:
- Raw broccoli in: crunchy, sulfurous florets in a creamy casserole. Blanch first.
- Overcooked chicken: sear to just-done; the oven adds 25 minutes of heat.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Cheddar Cream Pan Sauce — in a small pan, melt 1 tbsp butter; add 1/4 cup milk and bring to a bare simmer; off the heat, whisk in 1/2 cup shredded cheddar a handful at a time until smooth, with a pinch of paprika. Spoon over each serving for anyone who wants the casserole extra saucy.

Title: Shepherd's pie
Ingredients:
- 2 lb ground lamb
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 2 medium yellow onions, diced
- 3 carrots, peeled and diced small
- 2 stalks celery, diced small
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 3 tbsp tomato paste
- 2 tbsp Worcestershire sauce
- 2 cups beef or lamb broth
- 1 1/2 cups frozen peas
- 2 tsp dried thyme
- 1 tsp dried rosemary, crushed
- 2 bay leaves
- 3 lb Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and quartered
- 4 tbsp butter
- 1/2 cup 2% milk, warmed
- 1/2 cup grated parmesan cheese (2 oz)
- 2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste, divided
- 1 tsp black pepper

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/2 cup dry red wine
- 1 cup low-sodium beef broth
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
Steps:
1. Oven at 400 F. Potatoes peeled and quartered, into cold salted water. Mirepoix (onion, carrot, celery) diced small, garlic minced.
2. Potatoes: bring to a boil, simmer 15-18 minutes until completely tender. Drain, steam dry 1 minute in the hot pot, mash with the butter and warm milk, salt and pepper — fluffy, not whipped.
3. Brown the lamb hard: olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high, lamb in one layer, untouched 4-5 minutes for a deep crust; break up and brown through. Spoon off the excess fat — lamb gives plenty.
4. Mirepoix into the drippings 6-8 minutes until golden at the edges; garlic 30 seconds; tomato paste 1 minute until darkened. Broth and Worcestershire in, scraping; thyme, rosemary and bay in. Simmer 12-15 minutes until thick enough to hold a spoon's trail. Peas in at the end.
5. Filling into a 9x13; mash spread over in an even blanket, ruffled with a fork (the ruffles brown). Parmesan scattered over.
6. Bake 20-25 minutes until the top is golden in the ruffles and the filling bubbles at the edges. Rest 10 minutes before serving.

Common mistakes:
- A thin filling: it must be thick before the mash goes on, or the pie slumps into soup.
- Gluey mash: never whip potatoes with a mixer; mash and stop.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Red Wine Pan Gravy — after the lamb, add 1/2 cup dry red wine to the skillet; scrape the crust loose and reduce by half. Add 1 cup beef broth, simmer 3 minutes; off the heat, 1 tbsp cold butter whisked in. Spoon around each serving of pie — pub gravy, for a pub classic.

Title: Oven fish and chips
Ingredients:
- 2 1/2 lb cod fillets (or haddock), cut into 6 portions, patted very dry
- 3 lb russet potatoes, cut into 1/2-inch thick chips
- 3 tbsp olive oil, divided
- 1/2 cup all-purpose flour, for dredging
- 1 cup all-purpose flour, for the batter
- 1 tsp baking powder
- 2 tsp kosher salt, divided, plus more to taste
- 1 tsp black pepper
- 1 tsp paprika
- 1 tsp garlic powder
- 1 cup ice-cold sparkling water
- 1/2 cup light mayonnaise
- 1/4 cup dill pickles, diced fine
- 1 tbsp capers, chopped
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- Malt vinegar and lemon wedges, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 tbsp capers, drained
- 1 tsp lemon juice
Steps:
1. Oven at 425 F with two sheet pans inside — hot pans are half the crisp. Chips cut thick (1/2 inch, the British way), soaked in cold water 20 minutes to pull starch, then dried completely. Fish patted very dry. Tartar sauce stirred (mayo, pickles, capers, lemon) and refrigerated.
2. Chips: tossed with 2 tbsp olive oil and salt, onto the screaming pans in one layer. Roast 25-30 minutes, flipping once, until golden and crisp at the edges.
3. Batter at the last moment: flour, baking powder, salt, pepper, paprika and garlic powder whisked; the ice-cold sparkling water stirred in just until combined — lumps are fine, overmixing kills the bubbles that make the crust light. Cold batter, hot oven.
4. Fish: dredged in flour, shaken off, dipped in the batter, and laid on the second hot pan brushed with the remaining oil. Bake 14-16 minutes, flipping once, until deep golden and the fish flakes.
5. Serve on warm plates with the chips, tartar, lemon wedges and malt vinegar shaken over the chips — the vinegar is not optional in any house that respects the dish.

Common mistakes:
- Warm batter or warm fish: the crust goes heavy. Everything cold until the oven.
- Wet chips: dried properly or they steam. Twenty minutes of soak, then towels.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Brown Butter and Caper Sauce — in a small pan, melt 3 tbsp butter over medium heat until amber and nutty; add 1 tbsp capers and 1 tsp lemon juice — it will sputter. Spoon over the fish: a French-leaning finish that loves crisp batter and cod.

Title: Japanese chicken curry
Ingredients:
- 2 lb boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut in 1 1/2-inch chunks
- 2 tbsp neutral oil (vegetable or canola)
- 2 large yellow onions, cut in wedges
- 3 carrots, peeled and cut in 1-inch chunks
- 2 lb Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and cut in 1 1/2-inch cubes
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 5 cups low-sodium chicken broth
- 1 box (7 oz) Japanese curry roux (S&B Golden Curry or Vermont Curry), medium heat
- 1 tbsp honey
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp ketchup
- 1/2 apple, grated
- 3 cups Japanese short-grain rice, uncooked
- Scallions, thinly sliced, and pickled ginger, for serving (optional)

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp honey
Steps:
1. Mise en place: chicken in 1 1/2-inch chunks, onions in wedges, carrots and potatoes in large even chunks, garlic minced, ginger and apple grated. Roux blocks broken apart. Rice on (short-grain, per its method).
2. Sear the chicken: avocado oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high, chicken in one layer, untouched 3-4 minutes for golden crust. Out. Japanese curry is often made without this step; with it, the curry tastes roasted instead of boiled.
3. Onions into the drippings, 6-8 minutes, scraping, until golden and sweet at the edges — caramelized onion is Japanese curry's quiet foundation. Carrots and potatoes in for 2 minutes; garlic and ginger 30 seconds.
4. Broth in; bare simmer 15-18 minutes until the potatoes are just tender. Chicken back for the last 5.
5. The roux, off the boil: take the pot off the heat, stir the roux blocks in until completely melted (roux into boiling liquid clumps). Back over low heat, simmer gently 5 minutes until the curry turns glossy and thick. Honey, soy, ketchup and the grated apple stirred in — the sweet-savory depth that makes it taste like a Tokyo curry house.
6. Rest 10 minutes (curry is better after a short rest, and better still tomorrow). Scallions and pickled ginger at the table.

Common mistakes:
- Roux into a rolling boil: lumps that never fully melt. Off the heat, melted, then simmered.
- Undercooked potato: check before the roux goes in — it will not soften further in the thickened curry.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Butter-Soy Pan Glaze — in a small pan, melt 2 tbsp butter over medium heat until foaming; add 1 tbsp soy sauce and 1 tsp honey and swirl 30 seconds until syrupy and dark. Drizzle a little over each bowl of curry and rice — a steakhouse-style finish the curry houses keep quiet about.

Title: Lamb kofta with yogurt sauce
Ingredients:
- 2 lb ground lamb (not lean — 80/20 is ideal)
- 1 large yellow onion, grated on the large holes and squeezed dry
- 5 cloves garlic, minced to a paste
- 1/2 cup fresh flat-leaf parsley, finely chopped
- 1/4 cup fresh mint, finely chopped
- 2 tsp ground cumin
- 2 tsp paprika
- 1 tsp pul biber (Aleppo-style chili flakes) or regular chili flakes
- 1 tsp ground coriander
- 1/2 tsp cinnamon
- 2 tsp kosher salt
- 1 tsp black pepper
- 1/3 cup plain breadcrumbs
- 1 large egg, beaten
- 2 tbsp olive oil, for cooking
- 2 cups plain 2% Greek yogurt
- 1 cucumber, grated and squeezed very dry
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp lemon juice
- 2 tbsp olive oil (for the sauce)
- 2 tbsp fresh dill, chopped
- 6 pita breads
- 3 cups shredded lettuce, 2 tomatoes diced, 1/2 red onion sliced

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 cup crushed tomatoes
- 1/2 tsp paprika
- Pinch of kosher salt
Steps:
1. Mise en place: onion grated and squeezed bone-dry in a towel (wet onion makes kofta that fall apart). Garlic minced to a paste. Herbs chopped. Yogurt sauce: yogurt, cucumber grated and squeezed very dry, garlic, lemon, olive oil, dill, salt — refrigerated so the flavors marry.
2. Mix the kofta with a light but thorough hand: lamb, squeezed onion, garlic paste, parsley, mint, cumin, paprika, pul biber, coriander, cinnamon, salt, pepper, breadcrumbs and egg. Chill 30 minutes — cold kofta hold their shape and sear better.
3. Shape into 12 oval torpedoes, slightly flattened — the classic kofta silhouette cooks evenly.
4. Sear: a large skillet over medium-high with the olive oil, kofta in with space, 3-4 minutes untouched until a deep crust forms; turn and brown the other faces, 8-10 minutes total, to 160 F. Rest 5 minutes.
5. Warm the pitas. Build: pita, lettuce, tomato, red onion, kofta, yogurt sauce spooned generously over.

Common mistakes:
- Wet onion or wet cucumber: one ruins the kofta, the other ruins the sauce. Squeeze both like you mean it.
- Skipping the chill: warm kofta slump and stick. Thirty minutes.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Iskender Tomato-Butter Sauce — in a small pan, melt 2 tbsp butter over medium heat; add 1 cup crushed tomatoes, 1/2 tsp paprika and a pinch of salt; simmer 4-5 minutes until glossy. Spoon hot over the kofta in their pitas with the yogurt sauce — the Iskender kebab treatment: tomato butter and cool yogurt in the same bite.

Title: Shakshuka with feta
Ingredients:
- 3 tbsp olive oil, plus more for drizzling
- 2 medium yellow onions, diced
- 2 bell peppers (1 red, 1 green), diced
- 1 jalapeño, seeded and minced (leave seeds in for more heat)
- 5 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp tomato paste
- 2 tbsp harissa paste
- 2 cans (28 oz each) crushed tomatoes
- 2 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp ground coriander
- 1 tsp caraway seeds, lightly crushed
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
- 1 tsp black pepper
- 1 tsp sugar
- 9 large eggs
- 6 oz feta cheese, crumbled
- 1/2 cup fresh cilantro or parsley, chopped
- 6 pita breads or thick slices of crusty bread, warmed

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tbsp harissa paste
- 1 clove garlic, thinly sliced
Steps:
1. Mise en place: onions and the peppers (the recipe's peppers can be swapped for 3 poblanos plus an extra jalapeño if you keep a no-sweet-pepper house) diced, jalapeño minced, garlic minced, caraway lightly crushed. Feta crumbled, herbs chopped, bread ready to warm.
2. Build the base with patience: olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat, onions and peppers 8-10 minutes until soft, sweet and golden at the edges — a rushed base makes a thin shakshuka.
3. Garlic, tomato paste, harissa, cumin, coriander, caraway and smoked paprika in; stir 2 minutes until the paste darkens and the spices bloom in the oil.
4. Tomatoes, salt, pepper and sugar in; simmer 10-12 minutes until thick enough that a spoon leaves a trail and the oil pearls red at the edges. Taste — it should be bold, smoky, hot enough to notice.
5. Eggs: wells pressed into the sauce, an egg in each; lid on, 5-8 minutes at a bare simmer until the whites are just set and the yolks still run. Feta scattered over for the last 2 minutes.
6. Herbs over, a thread of olive oil, bread for swiping. Eat from the pan if the table allows it.

Common mistakes:
- Thin sauce: the eggs poach in soup instead of nestling in sauce. Reduce until a spoon leaves a trail.
- Overcooked yolks: watch from minute 5 — the lid traps heat and they set fast.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Harissa Oil — in a small pan, warm 3 tbsp olive oil with 1 tbsp harissa paste and 1 sliced garlic clove over low heat for 2 minutes until brick-red and fragrant — do not fry it hard. Drizzle over the finished shakshuka: a hot, red slick over the eggs and feta.

Title: Stuffed bell peppers
Ingredients:
- 6 large bell peppers (any color), tops cut off and seeded
- 1 1/2 lb 93% lean ground turkey
- 1 1/2 cups cooked long-grain white rice (from 3/4 cup dry)
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 medium yellow onion, diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 can (15 oz) tomato sauce, divided
- 1 can (14.5 oz) diced tomatoes, drained
- 2 tsp Italian seasoning
- 1 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
- 1 tsp black pepper
- 1 tsp garlic powder
- 1 1/2 cups shredded part-skim mozzarella cheese (6 oz), divided
- 1/4 cup grated parmesan cheese (1 oz)

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 cup tomato sauce
- 1/2 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
Steps:
1. Oven at 375 F. The peppers prepped (tops off, seeds and bitter ribs out, a sliver shaved off the bottoms so they stand). Rice cooked. A thin layer of tomato sauce spread in the baking dish so the peppers sit in sauce, not on dry glass.
2. Brown the turkey hard: olive oil in a skillet over medium-high, turkey spread flat, untouched 4 minutes for a real crust; break up and finish. Onion into the drippings 5 minutes until golden; garlic and Italian seasoning 30 seconds.
3. Filling: rice, half the tomato sauce, the drained diced tomatoes, salt, pepper and garlic powder folded through the turkey; half the mozzarella stirred in. Taste it — the filling should be seasoned like it is the whole meal, because it is.
4. Fill the peppers generously, mounding slightly. The remaining sauce spooned over, a splash of water in the dish, covered with foil.
5. Bake 30 minutes covered (the peppers steam tender), then uncovered with the remaining mozzarella and the Parmesan over, 12-15 more minutes until bubbling and browned in spots.
6. Rest 5 minutes — they are molten inside.

Common mistakes:
- Crunchy peppers: the covered steam-bake is what tenderizes them. Do not skip the foil.
- Bland filling: the pepper contributes almost no seasoning. The filling must stand alone.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Smoky Tomato Pan Sauce — in a small pan, warm 1 tbsp olive oil with 1 minced garlic clove for 30 seconds; add 1 cup tomato sauce and 1/2 tsp smoked paprika; simmer 4 minutes. Off the heat, 1 tbsp cold butter whisked in. Spoon around the peppers in their dish — extra sauce is never wrong with stuffed peppers.

Title: Chicken quesadillas
Ingredients:
- 2 lb boneless, skinless chicken breasts
- 1 tbsp olive oil, plus more for the pan
- 2 tsp chili powder
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp garlic powder
- 1 tsp onion powder
- 1 tsp kosher salt
- 1/2 tsp black pepper
- 1 medium yellow onion, diced
- 1 bell pepper, diced
- 1 can (4 oz) diced green chiles, drained
- 3 cups shredded Monterey Jack cheese (12 oz)
- 6 large (10-inch) flour tortillas
- 1/2 cup light sour cream, for serving
- 1 cup salsa, for serving
- 2 avocados, mashed with lime juice and salt, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 jalapeño, minced
- 1/2 cup sour cream
- Juice of 1 lime
- Pinch of kosher salt
Steps:
1. Mise en place: chicken in thin strips, tossed with chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, onion powder, salt and pepper. Onion and the pepper diced; green chiles drained; cheese shredded from a block (pre-shredded cheese is coated in starch and melts like plastic — this matters here more than anywhere).
2. Sear the chicken: a large skillet over medium-high with the olive oil, chicken in one layer, untouched 3 minutes for golden crust; toss 2 minutes to cooked through. Out — with its juices.
3. Onion and pepper into the drippings 4-5 minutes until charred at the edges and sweet. Green chiles through. Chicken and juices back for 30 seconds.
4. Build: tortillas laid out, cheese on the whole surface first (cheese is the glue), filling on one half, more cheese on top of the filling — cheese both sides or it falls apart.
5. Cook in a dry or lightly oiled skillet over medium heat, 2-3 minutes a side, pressing gently, until deep golden and crisp and the cheese pulls. Rest 1 minute before cutting or the filling floods out.
6. Cut in wedges; sour cream, salsa and the lime-mashed avocado alongside.

Common mistakes:
- Pre-shredded cheese: it never melts properly. Shred a block; it takes one minute.
- Overfilling: a quesadilla is a crisp, thin thing. Restraint keeps it crisp.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Jalapeño-Lime Crema Pan Sauce — in a small pan, melt 1 tbsp butter; add 1 minced jalapeño and sizzle 45 seconds. Off the heat, whisk into 1/2 cup sour cream with the juice of 1 lime and a pinch of salt. Drizzle over the cut quesadillas — cool, green heat against the crisp tortilla.

Title: Breakfast burritos
Ingredients:
- 12 large eggs
- 1 lb pork breakfast sausage
- 3 cups frozen shredded hash browns
- 1 tbsp butter
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 bell pepper, diced
- 1/2 yellow onion, diced
- 1 can (4 oz) diced green chiles, drained
- 1 1/2 cups shredded sharp cheddar cheese (6 oz)
- 6 large (12-inch) flour tortillas
- 1 tsp kosher salt, divided
- 1/2 tsp black pepper
- 1 cup salsa, for serving
- 1/2 cup light sour cream, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter
- 2 oz diced green chiles (about 1/2 small can)
- 1/4 cup 2% milk
- 3/4 cup shredded sharp cheddar cheese
Steps:
1. Mise en place: the pepper and onion diced to 1/4 inch, eggs beaten with the salt, pepper and 2 tbsp water. Green chiles drained, cheese shredded. Tortillas at room temperature so they roll without cracking.
2. Brown the sausage: a large skillet over medium-high, sausage broken into crumbles and left until deeply browned and crisp at the edges, 6-8 minutes. Out, leaving the drippings.
3. Hash browns in the drippings (butter if the pan is dry), spread flat and untouched 4-5 minutes until a golden crust forms on the bottom; flip in sections and crisp 3 more minutes. Pepper and onion in for the last 3 minutes.
4. Eggs, low and slow: heat down, eggs in, pushed gently with a spatula 2-3 minutes to soft, glossy curds — pull them shy of done; they finish in the burritos.
5. Build: tortilla, eggs, sausage, hash browns, green chiles, cheese. Fold the sides in, roll tight.
6. Seam-seal: the rolled burritos seam-side down in the hot dry skillet 1-2 minutes until the tortilla crisps and seals — this is what makes it a burrito and not a wrap. Salsa and sour cream alongside.

Common mistakes:
- Dry eggs: scramble them soft and pull early. Rubbery eggs cannot be rescued.
- Unsealed burritos: they unroll in the hand. The seam-sear is structural.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Green Chile Queso Pan Sauce — in a small pan, melt 1 tbsp butter; add the remaining half can of green chiles (about 2 oz) and 1/4 cup milk; simmer 1 minute. Off the heat, whisk in 3/4 cup shredded cheddar a handful at a time until smooth. Spoon over the burritos or serve as a dip — breakfast burritos with queso need no defense.

Title: Protein pancakes with berries
Ingredients:
- 2 cups white whole wheat flour
- 3 scoops (90g) vanilla protein powder
- 2 tbsp sugar
- 1 tbsp baking powder
- 1 tsp cinnamon
- 1/2 tsp kosher salt
- 2 cups 2% milk
- 3 large eggs
- 3 tbsp butter, melted, plus more for the pan
- 2 tsp vanilla extract
- 2 cups blueberries
- 1 cup strawberries, hulled and sliced
- 1/2 cup pure maple syrup, warmed, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1/4 cup pure maple syrup
- Pinch of kosher salt
Steps:
1. Mise en place: strawberries hulled and sliced, butter melted, maple syrup warmed in a small pot — warm syrup on hot pancakes is a small luxury worth 30 seconds.
2. Batter: dry ingredients whisked (flour, protein powder, sugar, baking powder, cinnamon, salt). Milk, eggs, melted butter and vanilla whisked in a second bowl. Wet into dry, stirred until JUST combined — lumps are correct; overmixed pancakes are tough pancakes. Rest 5 minutes so the protein powder hydrates (it drinks more than flour does).
3. Griddle over medium heat, buttered lightly. 1/3 cup batter per pancake; a few blueberries pressed into each while wet.
4. Flip when the edges look set and bubbles hold their shape on the surface, about 2-3 minutes; 1-2 minutes more. Golden, not pale — a pale pancake is an undercooked one.
5. Serve in stacks with the strawberries, more blueberries, and the warm maple syrup.

Common mistakes:
- Overmixing: ten stirs, then stop. Gluten is the enemy of fluff.
- Pressing the pancakes with the spatula: you are squeezing out the rise. Never.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Brown Butter Maple Sauce — in a small pan, melt 3 tbsp butter over medium heat until amber and nutty; off the heat, whisk in 1/4 cup warm maple syrup and a pinch of salt. Pour over the stacks instead of plain syrup — brown butter turns pancake syrup into something you would pay for.

Title: Overnight oats with Greek yogurt
Ingredients:
- 3 cups old-fashioned rolled oats (not quick oats)
- 3 cups plain 2% Greek yogurt
- 1 1/2 cups 2% milk
- 1 cup apple juice
- 3 sweet apples (Gala or Pink Lady), unpeeled
- 3 tbsp honey, plus more for drizzling
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tsp cinnamon
- 1/2 cup sliced almonds
- 1/2 cup raisins
- 2 cups mixed berries, for topping

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 tbsp honey
- 1/4 tsp ground cinnamon
Steps:
1. Grate the unpeeled apples on the large holes of a box grater — the skin adds color and fiber, and grating (not chopping) is the traditional Swiss Bircher method. Lemon juiced.
2. Combine: oats, yogurt, milk, apple juice, grated apple, honey, lemon juice and cinnamon stirred together in a large bowl until completely mixed. The lemon keeps the apple from browning and brightens everything.
3. Cover and refrigerate at least 4 hours, overnight if you can — the oats drink the liquid and turn creamy, not gummy, given real time.
4. In the morning: stir, and loosen with a splash of milk if it set too thick. Taste for sweetness — cold dulls it; a drizzle more honey is usually right.
5. Spoon into bowls; berries over, almonds and raisins scattered. (For warm oats on a cold morning: 60-90 seconds in the microwave takes the chill off without cooking them.)

Common mistakes:
- Two hours and calling it done: the oats stay chewy-raw in the center. Four hours minimum.
- Quick oats: they dissolve to paste overnight. Rolled oats only.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Warm Cinnamon-Honey Butter — in a small pan, melt 2 tbsp butter with 1 tbsp honey and 1/4 tsp cinnamon over low heat until just combined and fragrant. Drizzle a spoonful over each bowl of cold oats — the warm, spiced butter melting into the cold Bircher is a contrast worth waking for.

Title: Egg and veggie muffin cups
Ingredients:
- 12 large eggs
- 1/2 cup 2% milk
- 1 red bell pepper, diced small
- 8 oz mushrooms, diced small
- 2 cups fresh spinach, chopped
- 1/2 yellow onion, diced small
- 3/4 cup crumbled feta cheese (3 oz)
- 1 tsp kosher salt
- 1/2 tsp black pepper
- 1/2 tsp garlic powder
- Olive oil spray, for the pan

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- 1 tbsp chopped fresh parsley
- Pinch of kosher salt
Steps:
1. Oven at 350 F. Muffin tin sprayed very generously with olive oil spray, sides included — egg sticks to everything. Vegetables diced small (the pepper, mushrooms, onion), spinach chopped, feta crumbled.
2. Sauté the vegetables first (the step that makes these good instead of spongy): a skillet over medium-high with a drizzle of olive oil, mushrooms 3-4 minutes until they give up their water and brown; onion and the pepper 3 minutes; spinach 1 minute until wilted and its water cooks off. Cool slightly.
3. Eggs whisked with the milk, salt, pepper and garlic powder until the yolks are fully broken and the mix is uniform.
4. Vegetables and feta divided among the cups; the egg mixture poured over to just below the rim.
5. Bake 18-22 minutes until puffed, set in the center, and just golden at the edges. Cool 5 minutes in the tin — they release cleanly once the steam settles; run a thin knife around any stubborn ones.
6. Eat warm, or refrigerate up to 4 days and reheat 30 seconds in the microwave.

Common mistakes:
- Raw vegetables in: they weep water into the eggs and the cups bake up spongy. Sauté and dry them first.
- Under-sprayed tin: you will chisel them out. Generous spray.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Lemon Butter Pan Sauce — in a small pan, melt 2 tbsp butter over medium heat until foaming; off the heat, whisk in 1 tbsp lemon juice and 1 tbsp chopped parsley with a pinch of salt. Spoon a little over the warm muffin cups — a hollandaise-adjacent brightness for meal-prep eggs.

Title: Greek yogurt parfaits
Ingredients:
- 6 cups plain 2% Greek yogurt
- 3 cups granola
- 2 cups blueberries
- 1 cup strawberries, hulled and sliced
- 3 tbsp honey
- 1/4 cup sliced almonds, toasted

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 cup strawberries, hulled and sliced
- 1 tbsp honey
- 1 tsp lemon juice
Steps:
1. Toast the almonds in a dry skillet over medium heat 3-4 minutes until golden and fragrant — you will smell them the moment they are done; nuts go from toasted to burnt in under a minute. Cool.
2. Sweeten the yogurt: honey stirred through until smooth. Taste — lightly sweet, not dessert-sweet; the granola brings its own sugar.
3. Berries: strawberries hulled and sliced; blueberries left whole.
4. Layer in glasses or jars, in this order, twice: yogurt, granola, berries. The granola layer in the middle stays crisp longest; a final small spoon of yogurt on top seals it.
5. Almonds scattered over just before serving (they go soft if they sit in the yogurt). If prepping ahead, keep granola and almonds separate until the moment of eating — a parfait's crunch is perishable.

Common mistakes:
- Assembling hours ahead with the granola in: it turns to wet cardboard. Layer at serving.
- Unsweetened tang: straight Greek yogurt can pucker. The honey is structural, not decorative.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Warm Strawberry-Lemon Pan Sauce — in a small pan, melt 1 tbsp butter; add 1 cup sliced strawberries, 1 tbsp honey and 1 tsp lemon juice; simmer 3-4 minutes until the berries slump and the sauce turns rosy and syrupy. Spoon warm over the parfaits: warm berries over cold yogurt is the whole argument for making the sauce.

Title: Steak and eggs with potatoes
Ingredients:
- 2 lb sirloin steak, about 1 1/4 inches thick
- 12 large eggs
- 2 1/2 lb Yukon Gold potatoes, cut in 3/4-inch cubes
- 3 tbsp olive oil, divided
- 1 medium yellow onion, diced
- 1 bell pepper, diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp garlic powder
- 2 tsp kosher salt, divided, plus more to taste
- 1 tsp black pepper, divided
- 2 tbsp butter, divided
- Hot sauce and sliced scallions, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/4 cup low-sodium beef broth
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp chopped fresh parsley
Steps:
1. Mise en place: steak out 30 minutes ahead, patted dry, seasoned generously. Potatoes in even 3/4-inch cubes; onion and the pepper diced; garlic minced.
2. Crisp the potatoes: 2 tbsp olive oil in a large cast iron over medium-high, potatoes in one layer, untouched 5 minutes until a golden crust forms on the underside; toss and crisp 8-10 minutes more, until tender inside. Onion and pepper in for the last 5 minutes; garlic, smoked paprika and garlic powder for the last minute. Out and kept warm.
3. Sear the steak in the same iron: heat high until it just smokes, the remaining oil in, steak down untouched 4-5 minutes for a deep crust; flip, butter in to baste, 3-4 minutes more for medium-rare (130 F). Rest a full 10 minutes — steak and eggs waits for the steak.
4. Eggs in the steak's pan drippings (and the second butter if needed): fried sunny or over-easy, edges crisped in the beef fat, yolks runny — the yolk is the sauce the potatoes are waiting for.
5. Steak sliced against the grain, fanned over the potatoes; eggs on top; scallions and hot sauce at the table.

Common mistakes:
- Crowded potatoes: they steam into mash. One layer, or two pans.
- Slicing with the grain: chewy steak over perfect potatoes. Across the fibers.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Steakhouse Herb Butter Pan Sauce — after the eggs, add 1/4 cup beef broth to the hot steak pan; scrape up the fond and reduce 1 minute. Off the heat, whisk in 2 tbsp cold butter, 1 minced garlic clove and 1 tbsp chopped parsley until glossy. Spoon over the sliced steak — the diner classic, done the steakhouse way.

Title: Turkey sausage and egg hash
Ingredients:
- 1 1/2 lb turkey breakfast sausage, casings removed
- 12 large eggs
- 2 1/2 lb russet potatoes, cut in 1/2-inch dice
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 medium yellow onion, diced
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- 1 green bell pepper, diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 2 tsp kosher salt
- 1 tsp black pepper
- 4 scallions, sliced

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1/2 tsp ground cumin
- Juice of 1 lime
- Pinch of kosher salt
Steps:
1. Mise en place: potatoes in small 1/2-inch dice (big chunks stay raw inside — smaller than you think). Onion and both peppers diced, garlic minced, scallions sliced. Sausage squeezed from its casings and broken up.
2. Crisp the potatoes first (they take longest): olive oil in a large cast iron over medium-high, potatoes in one layer, untouched 5 minutes for a crust; toss and cook 10-12 minutes until crisp-edged and tender. Out.
3. Brown the sausage in the same pan, broken into crumbles and left until deeply browned with crisp edges, 6-8 minutes.
4. Onion and peppers into the drippings 5 minutes until golden at the edges; garlic, smoked paprika and cumin 30 seconds. Potatoes back; everything tossed and salted boldly.
5. Wells pressed into the hash; an egg in each. Lid on, 4-6 minutes at low heat until the whites are set and the yolks still run — or scramble them through if your table prefers.
6. Scallions over, hot sauce at the table.

Common mistakes:
- Everything in at once: the potatoes never crisp under a pile of sausage and veg. Stages.
- Eggs overcooked under the lid: check at 4 minutes; carryover is real.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Cumin-Lime Butter — in a small pan, melt 3 tbsp butter over medium heat; add 1/2 tsp ground cumin and sizzle 20 seconds until fragrant. Off the heat: the juice of 1 lime and a pinch of salt. Spoon over the hash and eggs — a bright, earthy butter that ties the Southwest spices together.

Title: Smoked salmon bagels
Ingredients:
- 6 bagels (plain, everything, or sesame)
- 12 oz smoked salmon (lox), thinly sliced
- 3/4 cup light cream cheese, softened
- 1/2 red onion, sliced paper-thin
- 2 tomatoes, sliced
- 1 cucumber, sliced thin
- 2 tbsp capers, drained
- 1 lemon, cut in wedges
- 2 tbsp fresh dill, chopped

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 tbsp capers, drained
- 1 tsp lemon juice
- 1 tsp chopped fresh dill
Steps:
1. Mise en place: red onion sliced paper-thin (soak it 10 minutes in cold water if you want it gentler), tomatoes and cucumber sliced, capers drained, dill chopped, lemon wedged. Cream cheese out 15 minutes so it spreads without tearing.
2. Toast the split bagels until golden and crisp at the edges — a proper bagel has structure; a soft one collapses under the toppings.
3. Schmear generously, edge to edge — a thin scrape of cream cheese is a missed opportunity.
4. Build in order: tomato, cucumber, a tumble of lox folded in ribbons (never laid flat like a slice of cheese), red onion, capers scattered, dill over.
5. Lemon squeezed over at the table, black pepper if you like. Eat open-face if the lox pile is generous — it should be.

Common mistakes:
- Cold cream cheese: it tears the bagel into crumbs. Room temperature, always.
- Flat lox: ribbons and folds trap the toppings and eat like a deli made them.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Warm Caper-Lemon Butter — in a small pan, melt 2 tbsp butter over medium heat until foaming; add 1 tbsp capers and sizzle 30 seconds; off the heat, 1 tsp lemon juice and 1 tsp chopped dill. Spoon just a little over the lox — a warm, briny butter over cold smoked salmon is a Scandinavian open-sandwich trick that works beautifully here.

Title: Banana oat protein muffins
Ingredients:
- 2 cups old-fashioned rolled oats, blended into flour
- 2 scoops (60g) vanilla protein powder
- 3 very ripe bananas, mashed (about 1 1/2 cups)
- 3 large eggs
- 1/2 cup plain 2% Greek yogurt
- 1/3 cup honey
- 1/4 cup butter, melted and cooled slightly
- 2 tsp baking powder
- 1 tsp baking soda
- 1 tsp cinnamon
- 1/2 tsp kosher salt
- 2 tsp vanilla extract
- 1/2 cup walnuts, chopped

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 tbsp honey
- 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1/2 tsp vanilla extract
Steps:
1. Oven at 350 F; a 12-cup muffin tin lined or greased. The bananas must be very ripe — heavily speckled, soft, fragrant; under-ripe bananas make bland, dry muffins, full stop. Oats blended to a coarse flour, walnuts chopped, butter melted and cooled 2 minutes.
2. Mash the bananas until almost liquid. Whisk in the eggs, yogurt, honey, cooled butter and vanilla until smooth.
3. Dry over wet: oat flour, protein powder, baking powder, soda, cinnamon and salt folded in until just combined — streaks of flour are fine; overmixed oat muffins bake up gummy.
4. Walnuts folded through. Batter divided among the cups, filled to the top — these do not rise dramatically.
5. Bake 16-19 minutes until the tops spring back and a tester comes out with moist crumbs, not batter. Cool 10 minutes in the tin, then out to a rack.
6. Good for 3 days in a tin, a week in the fridge; 20 seconds in the microwave returns them to fresh-baked softness.

Common mistakes:
- Green bananas: no sugar, no moisture, no flavor. Wait for the speckles.
- Overmixing: oat flour plus protein powder turns to paste fast. Fold and stop.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Cinnamon Butter Glaze — in a small pan, melt 2 tbsp butter with 1 tbsp honey, 1/2 tsp cinnamon and 1/2 tsp vanilla over low heat until combined and glossy. Brush over the warm muffins — a bakery-case shine with a spiced butter heart.

Title: Cobb salad
Ingredients:
- 2 lb boneless, skinless chicken breasts
- 12 cups chopped romaine lettuce (about 2 hearts)
- 8 slices bacon
- 6 large eggs
- 3 avocados, diced
- 3 cups cherry tomatoes, halved
- 1 1/2 cups crumbled blue cheese (6 oz)
- 1/2 red onion, thinly sliced
- 1/2 cup olive oil
- 1/4 cup red wine vinegar
- 2 tbsp Dijon mustard
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tsp honey
- 1 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
- 1/2 tsp black pepper

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp bacon fat (from the recipe's bacon; or olive oil)
- 1 shallot, minced
- 2 tbsp red wine vinegar
- 1 tsp Dijon mustard
- Pinch of sugar
Steps:
1. Mise en place: romaine chopped, washed and dried thoroughly (wet lettuce dilutes everything). Eggs hard-boiled: cold water, bring to a boil, off the heat covered 10 minutes, ice bath, peel. Tomatoes halved, red onion sliced thin, blue cheese crumbled, avocados diced last.
2. Bacon: in a cold skillet, then medium heat, rendered until crisp, 8-10 minutes; chop. Keep a spoonful of the bacon fat if you make the pan sauce below.
3. Sear the chicken: breasts pounded even, seasoned boldly, olive oil in a skillet over medium-high, 5-6 minutes a side untouched for a golden crust, to 165 F. Rest 5 minutes, slice.
4. Dressing whisked: olive oil, red wine vinegar, Dijon, garlic, honey, salt and pepper — sharp and mustardy; it has bacon and blue cheese to stand up to.
5. Build in rows over the romaine, diner-style: chicken, bacon, egg quarters, avocado, tomatoes, onion, blue cheese. Dressing at the table — a composed Cobb is dressed by its eater.

Common mistakes:
- Dressing the whole salad at once: the rows collapse into a tossed salad. Cobb is composed.
- Boiled-gray eggs: the ice bath and the 10-minute rest give you clean whites and golden yolks.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Warm Bacon Vinaigrette — in the bacon skillet over low heat, warm 2 tbsp of the bacon fat (or olive oil) with 1 minced shallot for 1 minute. Off the heat, whisk in 2 tbsp red wine vinegar, 1 tsp Dijon and a pinch of sugar. Spoon warm over the rows — a steakhouse wedge-salad finish that makes the Cobb taste like it came from a chophouse.

Title: Chicken Caesar salad
Ingredients:
- 2 lb boneless, skinless chicken breasts
- 12 cups romaine hearts, chopped (about 3 hearts)
- 2 large eggs, for coddling
- 3/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus 3 tbsp for croutons
