- 1/4 cup fresh lime juice (about 2 limes)
- 6 anchovy fillets in oil, minced to a paste
- 3 cloves garlic, minced to a paste
- 2 tbsp Dijon mustard
- 2 tsp Worcestershire sauce
- 1/2 cup finely grated parmesan cheese (2 oz), plus 1/2 cup shaved for serving
- 4 cups cubed sourdough or rustic bread (about 8 oz)
- 1 tsp garlic powder
- 1 1/2 tsp kosher salt, divided
- 1 tsp black pepper, plus more for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 anchovy fillet, minced
- 1/4 cup low-sodium chicken broth
- Juice of 1/2 lime
Steps:
1. Mise en place: romaine washed, dried completely and refrigerated — cold, crisp lettuce is Caesar law. Bread cubed; anchovies and garlic minced to a paste; limes juiced; Parmesan grated fine.
2. Croutons: bread tossed with the olive oil, garlic powder and salt, toasted in a skillet or 375 F oven 10-12 minutes, tossing once, until golden and crisp at the edges.
3. Sear the chicken: breasts seasoned, a skillet over medium-high, 5-6 minutes a side untouched for a deep golden crust, to 165 F. Rest 5, slice.
4. The dressing, Tijuana-style (this is the original Caesar, born in Tijuana — hence the lime): coddled eggs (1 minute in just-boiled water), whisked with the anchovy-garlic paste, Dijon and Worcestershire; the olive oil streamed in slowly, whisking constantly, until it emulsifies thick and pale; lime juice and the grated Parmesan folded in. It should taste garlicky, bright and boldly savory.
5. Toss the romaine with dressing to coat every leaf; chicken fanned over; shaved Parmesan and the croutons on top. Extra black pepper, always.

Common mistakes:
- Oil dumped in at once: the dressing breaks into grease. A slow stream and constant whisking.
- Wet lettuce: the dressing slides off. Dry it like the salad depends on it.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Warm Lemon-Anchovy Pan Sauce — in the chicken skillet over medium heat, melt 1 tbsp butter; add 1 minced anchovy fillet and stir 20 seconds until it melts. Add 1/4 cup chicken broth and the juice of 1/2 lime; scrape the fond and reduce 1 minute. Spoon over the sliced chicken on each salad — the Caesar dressing's flavors, warm and concentrated.

Title: Asian sesame chicken salad
Ingredients:
- 2 lb boneless, skinless chicken breasts
- 8 cups mixed salad greens
- 3 cups shredded red cabbage
- 2 cups shredded carrots
- 1 red bell pepper, thinly sliced
- 1 cup shelled edamame, thawed
- 1 cup mandarin orange segments, drained
- 4 scallions, sliced
- 1/2 cup sliced almonds, toasted
- 1 cup crispy wonton strips
- 1/3 cup rice vinegar
- 1/4 cup low-sodium soy sauce
- 2 tbsp honey
- 2 tbsp toasted sesame oil
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/4 cup neutral oil (avocado or vegetable)
- 1 tbsp sesame seeds

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp avocado oil
- 1 tbsp toasted sesame oil
- 1 tbsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 clove garlic, thinly sliced
Steps:
1. Mise en place: cabbage shredded thin, carrots shredded, the pepper sliced thin, scallions sliced, almonds toasted in a dry skillet 3-4 minutes. Edamame thawed, mandarins drained.
2. Sear the chicken: breasts marinated briefly in a spoonful of the dressing (or just salted), then a skillet over medium-high with a film of avocado oil, 5-6 minutes a side untouched for a golden crust, to 165 F. Rest 5, slice thin.
3. The dressing whisked until the honey dissolves: rice vinegar, soy, honey, sesame oil, ginger, garlic, the avocado oil (in place of the neutral oil — cleaner flavor) and sesame seeds. Shake or whisk it hard; it separates as it sits.
4. Build: greens, cabbage, carrots, pepper, edamame, mandarin segments, chicken slices.
5. Dress at the table (the greens wilt fast under vinegar), almonds and wonton strips over at the last second so they stay crisp.

Common mistakes:
- Dressing ahead: limp greens and soggy wontons. Dress, scatter, serve, in that order.
- Steamed chicken: dry it, hot pan, untouched. The crust is the salad's hot element.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Warm Ginger-Sesame Oil — in a small pan, warm 2 tbsp avocado oil and 1 tbsp toasted sesame oil with 1 tbsp grated ginger and 1 sliced garlic clove over low heat for 2 minutes until fragrant. Spoon a teaspoon over the chicken on each salad — warm sesame against the cold crunch is the restaurant trick.

Title: Southwest chicken salad
Ingredients:
- 2 lb boneless, skinless chicken breasts
- 8 cups chopped romaine lettuce
- 2 cans (15 oz) black beans, drained and rinsed
- 2 cups corn kernels (frozen, thawed, or fresh)
- 2 cups cherry tomatoes, halved
- 2 avocados, diced
- 1 cup shredded sharp cheddar cheese (4 oz)
- 1/2 red onion, diced
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 cup tortilla strips
- 1/2 cup light sour cream
- 1/4 cup salsa
- 2 tbsp lime juice
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp chili powder
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 2 tsp kosher salt, divided
- 1 tsp black pepper

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/4 cup low-sodium chicken broth
- Juice of 1 lime
- 1/2 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
Steps:
1. Mise en place: romaine washed, dried, chopped. Beans rinsed, corn thawed, tomatoes halved, onion diced, cilantro chopped, cheddar shredded, avocados diced last.
2. Char the corn: a dry cast iron over high heat, corn in one layer, untouched 3-4 minutes until blackened in spots; toss, 2 minutes more. Charred corn is a different vegetable from boiled corn.
3. Sear the chicken: breasts rubbed with olive oil, salt, pepper, half the cumin and half the chili powder; a hot skillet, 5-6 minutes a side untouched for a dark crust, to 165 F. Rest 5, slice.
4. Dressing: sour cream, salsa, lime juice and the remaining cumin whisked — cool, tangy, pink. Taste for salt.
5. Build: romaine, beans, corn, tomatoes, chicken, cheddar, onion, avocado, cilantro. Dressing drizzled, tortilla strips over at the last second.

Common mistakes:
- Plain boiled corn: five minutes of dry charring is the whole Southwest note.
- Dressing the avocado early: it browns and smears. Dice it last, dress the bowl, not the avocado.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Cumin-Lime Pan Sauce — in the chicken skillet over medium heat, add 1/4 cup chicken broth, the juice of 1 lime and 1/2 tsp ground cumin; scrape up the spiced fond and reduce 1 minute. Off the heat, 1 tbsp cold butter whisked in. Spoon over the sliced chicken — all the rub's flavor, collected from the pan.

Title: Tuna and white bean salad
Ingredients:
- 3 cans (5 oz each) Italian tuna in olive oil, drained
- 3 cans (15 oz each) cannellini beans, drained and rinsed
- 1 red onion, sliced paper-thin
- 2 stalks celery, diced small
- 1 cup cherry tomatoes, halved
- 2 tbsp capers, drained
- 1/2 cup fresh flat-leaf parsley, chopped
- 1/3 cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
- 3 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tbsp red wine vinegar
- 1 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
- 1/2 tsp black pepper
- 6 cups baby arugula

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tbsp capers, drained
- Zest of 1 lemon
Steps:
1. Mise en place: beans drained, rinsed and left to drain a full 5 minutes (wet beans make a watery salad). Onion sliced paper-thin, celery diced small, tomatoes halved, parsley chopped, capers drained.
2. Tame the onion: ice water with a splash of the vinegar, 10 minutes, then drained and patted dry — the bite mellows, the crunch stays.
3. Flake the tuna in large chunks — never mash it to cat food; Italian tuna is meant to be seen. Fold with the beans, onion, celery, tomatoes and capers.
4. Dress: olive oil, lemon juice, vinegar, salt and plenty of black pepper whisked and folded through. Taste — it should be bright and olive-oily. Rest 10 minutes so the beans drink the dressing.
5. Serve over the arugula with another thread of your best olive oil.

Common mistakes:
- Over-mixed tuna: flakes, folded, not stirred to paste.
- Under-dressed beans: they are sponges. Dress them first and let them sit.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Warm Lemon-Caper Oil — in a small pan, warm 3 tbsp olive oil with 1 tbsp capers and the zest of 1 lemon over low heat for 2 minutes until fragrant and the capers sizzle gently. Spoon over the salad at the table — a warm, briny slick that wakes the cold beans and tuna right up.

Title: Steak salad with blue cheese
Ingredients:
- 2 lb sirloin steak, about 1 1/4 inches thick
- 8 cups mixed salad greens
- 2 cups cherry tomatoes, halved
- 1 cucumber, sliced
- 1/2 red onion, thinly sliced
- 1 cup crumbled blue cheese (4 oz)
- 1/2 cup walnuts, toasted and chopped
- 1/3 cup olive oil
- 3 tbsp balsamic vinegar
- 1 tbsp Dijon mustard
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 2 tsp kosher salt, divided
- 1 tsp black pepper, divided

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp balsamic vinegar
- 1/4 cup low-sodium beef broth
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
Steps:
1. Mise en place: steak out 30 minutes ahead, patted completely dry. Greens washed and dried, tomatoes halved, cucumber and onion sliced, walnuts toasted 3-4 minutes in a dry skillet and chopped, blue cheese crumbled.
2. Sear the steak like a steakhouse: a cast iron over the highest heat until just smoking, a film of avocado oil, the steak seasoned generously and laid down — untouched 4-5 minutes for a deep crust; flip, 3-4 minutes to medium-rare (130 F), basting with its juices at the end.
3. Rest a full 10 minutes. Slice thin against the grain.
4. Dressing whisked: olive oil, balsamic, Dijon, garlic, salt and pepper — sharp enough to cut blue cheese and beef fat.
5. Build: greens, tomatoes, cucumber, onion; steak fanned over while still warm so the blue cheese softens against it; walnuts scattered. Dressing at the table.

Common mistakes:
- Slicing with the grain: across the fibers, always, or the best crust in the world still chews.
- Cold steak on cold greens: warm slices make the blue cheese go creamy. Time it so the steak lands warm.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Warm Balsamic Pan Sauce — in the steak skillet over medium heat, add 2 tbsp balsamic vinegar and 1/4 cup beef broth; scrape up the crust and reduce 2 minutes until syrupy. Off the heat, 1 tbsp cold butter whisked in. Spoon over the steak slices — the pan's crust, sharpened and poured back.

Title: Quinoa and black bean salad
Ingredients:
- 2 cups quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cans (15 oz) black beans, drained and rinsed
- 2 cups corn kernels
- 2 cups cherry tomatoes, halved
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- 1/2 red onion, diced
- 2 avocados, diced
- 1/2 cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1/3 cup olive oil
- 1/3 cup fresh lime juice (about 3 limes)
- 2 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp chili powder
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 2 tsp kosher salt

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 clove garlic, thinly sliced
- Juice of 1 lime
Steps:
1. Mise en place: quinoa rinsed 30 seconds (its saponin coating tastes soapy if you skip). Beans rinsed, corn ready, tomatoes halved, the pepper and onion diced, cilantro chopped, limes juiced, avocado diced last.
2. Cook the quinoa the fluffy way: quinoa and salted water (2 cups quinoa to 3 1/2 cups water), boil, cover, lowest heat 15 minutes, rest 10 off the heat, fluff with a fork. Spread on a tray to cool 10 minutes — warm quinoa wilts the herbs and melts the avocado.
3. Dressing whisked: olive oil, lime juice, cumin, chili powder, garlic, salt — bold and bright.
4. Fold quinoa, beans, corn, tomatoes, pepper and onion through the dressing. Rest 10 minutes so the quinoa drinks it.
5. Cilantro folded in, avocado placed on top (not folded — it smears), extra lime at the table.

Common mistakes:
- Hot quinoa into the bowl: herbs blacken, avocado melts. Cool it first.
- Unrinsed quinoa: bitter and soapy. Thirty seconds under the tap.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Warm Cumin-Lime Oil — in a small pan, warm 3 tbsp olive oil with 1 tsp ground cumin and 1 sliced garlic clove over low heat for 2 minutes until fragrant. Off the heat, the juice of 1 lime. Drizzle over the finished salad — the dressing's flavors, warmed and deepened, threaded through the quinoa.

Title: Salmon nicoise salad
Ingredients:
- 2 lb salmon fillet, skin on, cut into 6 portions
- 12 large eggs
- 2 lb small potatoes, halved
- 1 lb green beans, trimmed
- 8 cups mixed salad greens
- 3 cups cherry tomatoes, halved
- 1 cucumber, sliced
- 1 cup nicoise or kalamata olives
- 12 anchovy fillets in oil, drained
- 1/2 cup olive oil
- 1/4 cup red wine vinegar
- 2 tbsp Dijon mustard
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp capers, drained
- 2 tbsp olive oil, for the salmon
- 2 tsp kosher salt, divided, plus more to taste
- 1 tsp black pepper
- 1/4 cup fresh basil leaves, torn

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp olive oil
- 2 anchovy fillets, minced
- 1 tsp capers, drained
Steps:
1. Mise en place: salmon in 6 even portions. Eggs at room temperature. Potatoes halved, beans trimmed, greens washed and dried, tomatoes halved, cucumber sliced.
2. Eggs: covered with cold water, brought to a boil, off the heat covered 9 minutes, ice bath — jammy-golden yolks, the modern nicoise standard. Peel and halve.
3. Potatoes: simmered in salted water 12-15 minutes until tender, drained and dressed warm with a spoonful of the vinaigrette (warm potatoes drink dressing). Beans blanched 3 minutes in the same water — bright green, snappy.
4. Sear the salmon: olive oil in a skillet over medium-high, salmon skin-side down and untouched 5-6 minutes until the skin crisps and releases; flip for 60 seconds. Center silky, 125 F.
5. Vinaigrette whisked: olive oil, red wine vinegar, Dijon, garlic, capers, salt and pepper.
6. Compose on a platter, bistro-style: greens, potatoes, beans, tomatoes, cucumber, olives, anchovies laid over, salmon in the center, egg halves around, basil torn over. Dressing spooned, not dumped.

Common mistakes:
- Flabby salmon skin: dry fish, hot pan, no touching. It releases when the skin is crisp.
- Hard, chalky eggs: the 9-minute method or nothing.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Warm Anchovy-Olive Oil — in a small pan, warm 3 tbsp olive oil with 2 minced anchovy fillets and 1 tsp capers over low heat for 2 minutes until the anchovy melts into the oil. Spoon over the salmon and potatoes — the nicoise's Mediterranean soul, warmed and concentrated.

Title: Split pea soup with ham
Ingredients:
- 1 lb dried green split peas (2 cups), rinsed and picked over
- 1 lb ham, diced (or 1 meaty ham hock)
- 2 tbsp butter
- 2 medium yellow onions, diced
- 4 carrots, peeled and diced
- 3 stalks celery, diced
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 bay leaves
- 1 tsp dried thyme
- 8 cups low-sodium chicken broth
- 1 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
- 1 tsp black pepper

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1/4 cup finely diced ham
- 1 clove garlic, thinly sliced
Steps:
1. Mise en place: split peas rinsed and picked over (60 seconds that saves a cracked tooth). Ham diced, onions, carrots and celery diced, garlic minced.
2. Sweat the vegetables: butter in a Dutch oven over medium heat, onion, carrot and celery with the salt, 8-10 minutes until soft and sweet and golden at the edges.
3. Garlic 30 seconds. Peas, ham (and the hock if you have one), bay, thyme and broth in.
4. Bare simmer, partially covered, 1 to 1 1/4 hours, stirring every 20 minutes (the peas settle and scorch if ignored), until the peas have completely collapsed into a thick, creamy puree and the ham is tender. Add water if it thickens too far — it should pour like heavy cream.
5. Fish out the bay and the hock (shred its meat back in). Salt carefully — the ham brings plenty — and plenty of black pepper.
6. Serve with crusty bread. A thread of olive oil over each bowl is not a garnish; it is seasoning.

Common mistakes:
- A rolling boil: it scorches the settled peas onto the pot's bottom. Bare simmer, occasional stir.
- Salting early: ham varies wildly. Salt at the end.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Crispy Ham and Garlic Butter — in a small pan, melt 2 tbsp butter over medium heat; add 1/4 cup finely diced ham and 1 sliced garlic clove; fry 2-3 minutes until the ham crisps at the edges. Spoon over each bowl of soup — a little crisp, salty crunch on the creamy peas.

Title: Beef and barley soup
Ingredients:
- 1 1/2 lb beef chuck, cut in 3/4-inch cubes
- 1 cup pearled barley, rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 2 medium yellow onions, diced
- 4 carrots, peeled and diced
- 3 stalks celery, diced
- 8 oz mushrooms, sliced
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp tomato paste
- 8 cups low-sodium beef broth
- 2 bay leaves
- 1 tsp dried thyme
- 2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
- 1 tsp black pepper
- 1/4 cup fresh parsley, chopped

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 tsp fresh thyme leaves
- 1 clove garlic, thinly sliced
Steps:
1. Mise en place: beef in even 3/4-inch cubes, patted very dry, seasoned. Onions, carrots and celery diced, mushrooms sliced, garlic minced, barley rinsed.
2. Brown the beef in batches: olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high, beef in one layer, 3-4 minutes untouched per batch until deeply crusted. The fond is this soup's entire depth — do not crowd it away.
3. Mushrooms in the drippings 4-5 minutes until deeply browned; then onion, carrot and celery 6-8 minutes until golden at the edges; garlic and tomato paste 2 minutes until darkened.
4. Broth in, scraping the pot clean; barley, bay and thyme in; beef and juices back. Bare simmer 45-55 minutes until the barley is tender with a pleasant chew and the beef gives easily.
5. Salt boldly — barley drinks salt — and pepper. Parsley over each bowl.

Common mistakes:
- Gray beef: batch it and let the crust form. It is the soup.
- Mushy barley: check at 40 minutes; it goes from chewy to blown-out quickly.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Thyme-Garlic Brown Butter — in a small pan, melt 3 tbsp butter over medium heat until amber and nutty; add 1 tsp fresh thyme leaves and 1 sliced garlic clove, sizzle 30 seconds. Spoon over each bowl — brown butter over beef and barley tastes like a mountain lodge kitchen.

Title: White chicken chili
Ingredients:
- 2 lb boneless, skinless chicken breasts
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 2 medium yellow onions, diced
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 3 cans (4 oz each) diced green chiles
- 2 cans (15 oz) cannellini beans, drained and rinsed
- 1 can (15 oz) corn, drained
- 4 cups low-sodium chicken broth
- 2 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp dried oregano
- 1 tsp chili powder
- 1/2 tsp cayenne pepper
- 8 oz cream cheese, cubed and softened
- 1/2 cup heavy cream
- 2 limes, juiced
- 1/2 cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 1/2 cups shredded Monterey Jack cheese (6 oz), for serving
- 1/2 cup light sour cream, for serving
- 1 avocado, diced, for serving
- 2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
- 1 tsp black pepper

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 jalapeño, minced
- 1/3 cup sour cream
- Pinch of kosher salt and a squeeze of lime
Steps:
1. Mise en place: onions diced, garlic minced, beans rinsed, corn drained, cream cheese cubed and left out — cold cream cheese never melts smooth. Limes juiced, cilantro chopped. Chicken seasoned.
2. Sear the chicken: olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high, breasts down 5-6 minutes untouched for a golden crust; flip 4-5 minutes to 165 F. Out, rested, shredded coarse. The fond stays for the chili.
3. Onion into the drippings 6-8 minutes until golden at the edges, scraping; garlic, cumin, oregano, chili powder and cayenne 1 minute until fragrant.
4. Green chiles, beans, corn and broth in; bare simmer 15 minutes. Mash a cup of the beans against the side and stir back — body without flour.
5. Cream cheese in off a rolling boil, whisked until completely melted; the cream in. Chicken back for 5 minutes to heat through.
6. Lime juice and cilantro off the heat — acid last, always. Serve with Monterey Jack, sour cream and avocado.

Common mistakes:
- Boiling the cream cheese: it can turn grainy. Melt it at a bare simmer, whisking.
- Lime cooked in: flat. At the end, off the heat.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Jalapeño Crema Pan Sauce — in a small pan, melt 1 tbsp butter; add 1 minced jalapeño and sizzle 45 seconds. Off the heat, whisk into 1/3 cup sour cream with a pinch of salt and a squeeze of lime. Drizzle over each bowl — cool, green heat over the creamy chili.

Title: Tomato basil soup with turkey grilled cheese
Ingredients:
- 3 tbsp olive oil
- 2 medium yellow onions, diced
- 6 cloves garlic, minced
- 3 cans (28 oz each) crushed tomatoes
- 2 cups low-sodium chicken broth
- 1 tsp sugar
- 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes
- 1 cup fresh basil leaves, packed, plus more for serving
- 3/4 cup heavy cream
- 1/2 cup grated parmesan cheese (2 oz)
- 2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
- 1 tsp black pepper
- 12 slices sourdough bread
- 12 oz sliced deli turkey breast
- 6 oz sliced sharp cheddar cheese
- 6 oz sliced mozzarella cheese
- 3 tbsp butter, softened

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp olive oil
- 1 clove garlic, thinly sliced
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh basil
Steps:
1. Mise en place: onions diced, garlic minced, basil chiffonaded (stack, roll, slice thin), Parmesan grated, butter softened for the sandwiches.
2. Soup base: olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat, onions with the salt 8-10 minutes until soft, sweet and golden at the edges. Garlic and red pepper flakes 30 seconds.
3. Tomatoes and broth in; bare simmer 20 minutes until the tomatoes taste cooked and sweet. Sugar in if your tomatoes are sharp.
4. Blend until completely smooth (an immersion blender in the pot). Cream and Parmesan in; simmer 2 minutes — never a hard boil after the cream. Basil folded in off the heat so it stays vivid.
5. Grilled cheese, the diner way: butter on the outsides of the sourdough, turkey and both cheeses inside; a skillet over medium heat, 3-4 minutes a side, pressed gently, until deep golden and the cheese pulls. (Mayo on the outside instead of butter is the other diner secret — either works, butter is classic.)
6. Soup in warm bowls, sandwiches halved on the diagonal, basil over the soup.

Common mistakes:
- Basil cooked in the soup for 20 minutes: it turns black and dull. Folded in at the end.
- A rushed onion: the soup's sweetness is built here. Eight minutes minimum.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Garlic-Basil Oil — in a small pan, warm 3 tbsp olive oil with 1 sliced garlic clove over low heat for 2 minutes until fragrant; off the heat, stir in 2 tbsp chopped basil. Drizzle over each bowl of soup — a green, garlicky slick over the cream-swirled tomato.

Title: Hamburger veggie soup
Ingredients:
- 1 1/2 lb 90% lean ground beef
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 2 medium yellow onions, diced
- 4 carrots, peeled and diced
- 3 stalks celery, diced
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 cans (14.5 oz each) diced tomatoes
- 1 can (15 oz) tomato sauce
- 6 cups low-sodium beef broth
- 2 cups green beans, cut in 1-inch pieces
- 2 cups corn kernels
- 2 cups russet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 2 bay leaves
- 2 tsp Italian seasoning
- 2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
- 1 tsp black pepper

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 clove garlic, thinly sliced
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh parsley
- Pinch of kosher salt
Steps:
1. Mise en place: all vegetables in uniform 1/2-inch dice (even pieces, even cooking), green beans in 1-inch pieces, garlic minced, cans opened.
2. Brown the beef hard: olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high, beef in chunks, untouched 4 minutes until a dark crust forms, then crumbled and finished. Drain the excess fat.
3. Onion, carrots and celery into the drippings 6-8 minutes until golden at the edges; garlic 30 seconds.
4. Tomatoes, tomato sauce and broth in, scraping; potatoes, bay and Italian seasoning in. Bare simmer 20 minutes.
5. Green beans and corn in for the last 8-10 minutes — they should stay bright and keep their bite; an hour in the pot turns them khaki.
6. Salt boldly, pepper, rest 5 minutes. It is better the second day, like all its kind.

Common mistakes:
- Vegetables in all at once: the green beans dissolve while the potatoes firm up. Stages by cooking time.
- Steamed beef: the undisturbed crust is the soup's meaty depth.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Parsley-Garlic Butter — in a small pan, melt 3 tbsp butter over medium heat until foaming; add 1 sliced garlic clove, sizzle 30 seconds; off the heat, 2 tbsp chopped parsley and a pinch of salt. Spoon a little over each bowl — garlic butter melting into a hamburger soup tastes like the best diner in town.

Title: Chicken and dumplings
Ingredients:
- 2 lb boneless, skinless chicken thighs
- 2 tbsp butter
- 2 medium yellow onions, diced
- 4 carrots, peeled and diced
- 3 stalks celery, diced
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/3 cup all-purpose flour
- 8 cups low-sodium chicken broth
- 2 bay leaves
- 1 tsp dried thyme
- 1 1/2 cups frozen peas
- 1/2 cup heavy cream
- 2 cups all-purpose flour (for dumplings)
- 1 tbsp baking powder
- 1 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
- 1/2 tsp black pepper
- 4 tbsp cold butter, cubed (for dumplings)
- 1 cup cold 2% milk
- 2 tbsp fresh chives, snipped

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 tbsp snipped fresh chives
- Pinch of kosher salt
Steps:
1. Mise en place: vegetables in 1/2-inch dice, garlic minced. Dumpling butter cubed and kept cold in the fridge — cold butter is fluffy dumplings. Chicken seasoned.
2. Brown the chicken: butter foaming in a Dutch oven over medium-high, thighs down 4-5 minutes untouched for a deep golden crust; flip 3 minutes. Out — they finish in the stew.
3. Onion, carrots and celery into the drippings 8-10 minutes until soft and golden at the edges; garlic 30 seconds. Flour stirred in 2 minutes (a pale roux).
4. Broth in a stream, whisking; bay and thyme in. Bare simmer 15 minutes. Chicken back in chunks, peas and cream in, 5 minutes. The stew should coat a spoon — this is the dumplings' landing pad, and a thin stew drowns them.
5. Dumplings: flour, baking powder, salt whisked; cold butter cut in to pea-size; cold milk stirred in to a shaggy, just-combined dough. Drop in golf-ball spoonfuls over the simmering stew. Lid on, 15 minutes, NO PEEKING — they steam, and peeking lets the steam out and the dumplings turn to lead.
6. Chives over. Serve in deep bowls, stew ladled around the dumplings.

Common mistakes:
- Lifting the lid: leaden dumplings, every time. Fifteen minutes of faith.
- Warm butter in the dumpling dough: they bake dense. Cold, cold.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Brown Butter and Chive Sauce — in a small pan, melt 2 tbsp butter over medium heat until amber and nutty; off the heat, stir in 1 tbsp snipped chives and a pinch of salt. Spoon over the dumplings in each bowl — brown butter on a steamed dumpling is a small revelation.

Title: Teriyaki chicken and pineapple skewers
Ingredients:
- 2 1/2 lb boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut in 1 1/2-inch chunks
- 1 fresh pineapple, cut in 1 1/2-inch chunks (about 4 cups)
- 2 red bell peppers, cut in 1 1/2-inch squares
- 1 red onion, cut in 1 1/2-inch wedges
- 3/4 cup low-sodium soy sauce
- 1/2 cup brown sugar, packed
- 1/4 cup honey
- 1/4 cup rice vinegar
- 2 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 5 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp cornstarch
- 1/4 cup water
- 1 tbsp neutral oil, for the grill
- 1 1/2 cups long-grain white rice, uncooked
- 3 scallions, sliced, and 1 tbsp sesame seeds, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/4 cup low-sodium soy sauce
- 2 tbsp brown sugar
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
Steps:
1. Mise en place: chicken and pineapple in even 1 1/2-inch chunks; the pepper and onion in matching squares and wedges (a poblano swaps in beautifully if you want heat instead of sweet). Wooden skewers soaked 30 minutes. Rice on.
2. Teriyaki sauce: soy, brown sugar, honey, rice vinegar, ginger and garlic simmered 3 minutes; the cornstarch slurry in until glossy and thick enough to coat a spoon. Half is marinade and glaze, half stays clean for serving.
3. Marinate the chicken 20-30 minutes in half the sauce (no longer — the sugar and acid work fast).
4. Thread skewers: chicken, pineapple, pepper, onion, alternating, with a little space between pieces — crowded skewers steam instead of charring.
5. Grill (or a screaming cast iron) over medium-high, oiled: 10-12 minutes, turning every 3, until the chicken is cooked through and the pineapple caramelizes at the edges. Brush with the reserved sauce in the last 2 minutes only — earlier and the sugar burns.
6. Rest 3 minutes. Scallions and sesame over; the remaining clean sauce at the table; rice under.

Common mistakes:
- Glazing from the start: burnt sugar, raw chicken. Last 2 minutes.
- Using the marinade as serving sauce: it held raw chicken. The reserved half is the serving half.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Extra Teriyaki Glaze — in a small pan, simmer 1/4 cup soy sauce, 2 tbsp brown sugar and 1 tsp grated ginger for 3-4 minutes until reduced to a syrup (no cornstarch needed at this concentration). Brush over the skewers at serving for a second lacquered shine.

Title: Honey garlic shrimp and broccoli
Ingredients:
- 2 1/2 lb large shrimp (21/25), peeled and deveined, tails on
- 2 tbsp cornstarch
- 1 tsp kosher salt
- 1/2 tsp white pepper
- 2 tbsp neutral oil, divided
- 8 cups broccoli florets, cut small
- 6 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, minced
- 1/2 cup honey
- 1/3 cup low-sodium soy sauce
- 2 tbsp rice vinegar
- 1 tbsp oyster sauce
- 1 tsp toasted sesame oil
- 1 tbsp cornstarch (for the sauce)
- 1/3 cup water
- 2 tsp sesame seeds
- 4 scallions, sliced
- 1 1/2 cups long-grain white rice, uncooked

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp avocado oil
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1/2 tsp red chile flakes
Steps:
1. Mise en place: shrimp patted VERY dry (dry shrimp sear; wet shrimp steam), tossed with the cornstarch, salt and white pepper — the velvet coat. Broccoli in small florets. Garlic and ginger minced. Sauce whisked: honey, soy, vinegar, oyster sauce, sesame oil, cornstarch, water. Rice on.
2. Char the broccoli first: 1 tbsp avocado oil in a wok over high heat, broccoli in one layer, untouched 2 minutes until charred at the edges; toss 1 minute to crisp-tender. Out.
3. Sear the shrimp in one layer, 90 seconds a side, until pink with golden edges. Out immediately — they finish in the sauce for seconds, not minutes.
4. Sauce into the wok with the garlic and ginger; simmer 1 minute until glossy and thickened.
5. Shrimp and broccoli back for 30-60 seconds, tossed until everything shines. Sesame seeds and scallions over. Rice under.

Common mistakes:
- Shrimp cooked through in the sear: they turn to rubber in the sauce. Pull them pink-but-translucent in the middle.
- Waterlogged broccoli: small florets, high heat, one layer.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Chile-Ginger Oil — in a small pan, heat 2 tbsp avocado oil until shimmering; off the heat, stir in 1 tsp grated ginger and 1/2 tsp chile flakes; bloom 1 minute. Spoon over each serving — a fragrant heat slick over the sweet honey garlic.

Title: Tofu and veggie stir fry with cashews
Ingredients:
- 3 blocks (14 oz each) extra-firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 1/2 cup cornstarch
- 4 tbsp neutral oil, divided
- 1 red bell pepper, cut in 1-inch squares
- 1 yellow bell pepper, cut in 1-inch squares
- 8 oz sugar snap peas, strings removed
- 8 oz mushrooms, sliced
- 2 cups broccoli florets, cut small
- 1 cup shredded carrots
- 6 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, minced
- 1 cup roasted cashews
- 1/2 cup low-sodium soy sauce
- 1/4 cup hoisin sauce
- 2 tbsp rice vinegar
- 1 tbsp honey
- 2 tsp toasted sesame oil
- 1 tbsp cornstarch (for the sauce)
- 1/2 cup water
- 4 scallions, sliced
- 1 1/2 cups long-grain white rice, uncooked
- 2 tsp kosher salt, divided

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp hoisin sauce
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp rice vinegar
- 2 tbsp water
Steps:
1. Press the tofu — the whole dish depends on it: blocks wrapped in towels, a heavy pan on top, 20-30 minutes. Then 1-inch cubes, tossed in the cornstarch and salt until coated.
2. Crisp the tofu in batches: 2 tbsp avocado oil in a wok over medium-high, tofu in one layer, untouched 3-4 minutes until a golden crust forms on the underside; turn and crisp 2-3 more faces. Out. Pale, soft tofu is pressed tofu's betrayal — give it time and space.
3. Vegetables in stages in the remaining oil: mushrooms first, 3-4 minutes until browned; broccoli 2 minutes; the peppers and snap peas 2 minutes until charred at the edges and still snappy; carrots through. Garlic and ginger 30 seconds.
4. Sauce in (soy, hoisin, vinegar, honey, sesame oil, cornstarch, water); simmer 1 minute until glossy.
5. Tofu back for 30 seconds to coat. Cashews and scallions over at the very end — cashews in the sauce go soft; on top they crunch.
6. Rice under, immediately.

Common mistakes:
- Unpressed tofu: it steams, sheds its coating, and never crisps. Twenty minutes under weight.
- Cashews cooked in: soft nuts, sad finish. On top, at the table.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Extra Hoisin Glaze — in a small pan, simmer 3 tbsp hoisin sauce, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp rice vinegar and 2 tbsp water for 1-2 minutes until glossy. Spoon over the stir fry for anyone who likes theirs saucier — the wok sauce, doubled down.

Title: Chicken gyros with tzatziki
Ingredients:
- 2 1/2 lb boneless, skinless chicken thighs
- 1/3 cup extra-virgin olive oil
- 1/4 cup fresh lemon juice (about 2 lemons)
- 5 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp red wine vinegar
- 1 tbsp dried oregano
- 2 tsp ground cumin
- 2 tsp paprika
- 2 tsp kosher salt, divided
- 1 tsp black pepper
- 2 cups plain 2% Greek yogurt
- 1 cucumber, grated
- 3 cloves garlic, minced (for tzatziki)
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice (for tzatziki)
- 2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil (for tzatziki)
- 2 tbsp fresh dill, chopped
- 6 pita breads
- 3 tomatoes, diced
- 1/2 red onion, thinly sliced
- 3 cups shredded lettuce
- 4 oz feta cheese, crumbled

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/4 cup low-sodium chicken broth
- Juice of 1/2 lemon
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
- 1/2 tsp dried oregano
Steps:
1. Tzatziki first: cucumber grated and squeezed bone-dry in a towel; folded into the yogurt with garlic, lemon, olive oil and dill; salt. Refrigerated — it should taste bright and garlicky.
2. Marinate the chicken (30 minutes to overnight): olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, red wine vinegar, oregano, cumin, paprika, salt and pepper. This marinade is the gyro.
3. Sear the chicken thighs whole: a cast iron or grill over medium-high, 5-6 minutes a side untouched, until deeply charred at the edges and cooked through (175 F for thighs is juicier than 165). Rest 5 minutes, slice into strips — slicing after cooking keeps the crust on every piece, the gyro-shop way.
4. Warm the pitas (directly over a flame or in the dry skillet) until pliable and blistered in spots.
5. Build: pita, lettuce, tomato, red onion, chicken strips piled high, tzatziki generously, feta over.

Common mistakes:
- Watery tzatziki: squeeze the cucumber until your hands ache. There is always more water.
- Slicing raw chicken into strips before cooking: it dries out. Whole thighs, sliced after, stay juicy.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Lemon-Oregano Pan Sauce — in the chicken skillet over medium heat, add 1/4 cup chicken broth and the juice of 1/2 lemon; scrape up the charred fond and reduce 1 minute. Off the heat, 1 tbsp cold butter and 1/2 tsp dried oregano whisked in. Spoon over the sliced chicken in each pita — the souvlaki stand's pan juices, put to work.

Title: Beef and black bean chili mac
Ingredients:
- 1 1/2 lb 90% lean ground beef
- 12 oz elbow macaroni, uncooked
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 medium yellow onion, diced
- 1 bell pepper, diced
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 cans (15 oz) black beans, drained and rinsed
- 1 can (14.5 oz) diced tomatoes
- 1 can (15 oz) tomato sauce
- 2 tbsp chili powder
- 2 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp dried oregano
- 2 cups low-sodium beef broth
- 2 cups shredded sharp cheddar cheese (8 oz)
- 4 scallions, sliced
- 1/2 cup light sour cream, for serving
- 2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
- 1 tsp black pepper

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- 2 scallions, thinly sliced
- Juice of 1/2 lime
Steps:
1. Mise en place: onion and the pepper diced, garlic minced, beans rinsed, spices in one bowl, cheese shredded, scallions sliced.
2. Brown the beef hard: olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high, beef in chunks, untouched 4 minutes for a dark crust; crumble and finish. Drain the fat.
3. Onion and pepper into the drippings 5-6 minutes until golden at the edges; garlic, chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika and oregano 1 minute, toasting in the fat.
4. Beans, tomatoes, tomato sauce and broth in, scraping. Macaroni in dry — it cooks in the chili and its starch thickens the pot, the chili-mac bargain. Bare simmer 10-12 minutes, stirring twice, until the pasta is just tender.
5. Off the heat: half the cheddar stirred through until melted and glossy; the rest over the top, lid on 2 minutes to melt in sheets.
6. Scallions over; sour cream at the table. Salt in stages — the cheese brings its own.

Common mistakes:
- Pasta cooked separately: you lose the starch that thickens the chili and gain a pot to wash. In the pot.
- A hard boil: the pasta blows out and the bottom scorches. Bare simmer, stir twice.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Scallion-Lime Butter — in a small pan, melt 3 tbsp butter over medium heat until foaming; add 2 sliced scallions and sizzle 30 seconds. Off the heat, the juice of 1/2 lime. Spoon over each bowl of chili mac — a bright green butter over all that cheddar and smoke.

Title: Jerk chicken with rice and peas
Ingredients:
- 3 lb bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs (about 12)
- 6 scallions, roughly chopped
- 1 medium yellow onion, quartered
- 5 cloves garlic
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, roughly chopped
- 2 scotch bonnet peppers, stemmed (see note)
- 2 tbsp fresh thyme leaves
- 3 tbsp brown sugar, packed
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 1/4 cup fresh lime juice (about 2 limes)
- 3 tbsp neutral oil
- 1 tbsp ground allspice
- 1 tsp cinnamon
- 1 tsp nutmeg
- 2 tsp kosher salt, plus more for the rice
- 2 1/2 cups long-grain white rice
- 2 cans (15 oz) kidney beans, with their liquid
- 1 can (13.5 oz) full-fat coconut milk
- 4 scallions, sliced
- 3 cloves garlic, smashed
- 4 sprigs fresh thyme
- 1 whole scotch bonnet pepper
- Lime wedges, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/2 cup coconut milk
- Juice of 1 lime
- Pinch of kosher salt
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
Steps:
1. Jerk marinade: scallions, onion, garlic, ginger, scotch bonnets, thyme, brown sugar, soy, lime juice, avocado oil (in place of the neutral oil), allspice, cinnamon, nutmeg and salt blended smooth. Gloves for the bonnets — they are seriously hot, and the heat lingers on skin.
2. Marinate the chicken 4 hours to overnight, scored lightly so the paste penetrates. Overnight is not a suggestion for jerk; it is the recipe.
3. Rice and peas: rice rinsed; kidney beans WITH their liquid, coconut milk, water to cover by an inch, the smashed garlic, thyme sprigs and the whole bonnet (unbroken — it perfumes without detonating). Boil, cover, lowest heat 18 minutes, rest 10. Fish the bonnet and thyme out.
4. Grill or roast the chicken: over medium heat (or a 425 F oven), skin-side down first, 30-40 minutes turning every 10, until the skin is charred in spots, the marinade has set into a dark crust, and the thickest thigh hits 175 F. The sugar chars fast near the end — watch the last 10 minutes.
5. Rest 10 minutes. Lime wedges and the sliced scallions over; rice and peas under.

Common mistakes:
- A 30-minute marinade: jerk paste needs hours to penetrate. Overnight or accept a lesser chicken.
- Breaking the whole bonnet in the rice: the peas become a weapon. Whole and unbroken, or seeded and minced on purpose.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Coconut-Lime Pan Sauce — in a small pan, simmer 1/2 cup coconut milk with the juice of 1 lime and a pinch of salt for 3 minutes until slightly thickened; off the heat, 1 tbsp cold butter whisked in. Spoon over the jerk chicken and rice — cool coconut against the bonnet heat is the island's own balance.

Title: Basque Garlic Chicken & Potatoes
Ingredients:
3 lb bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs (about 8)
2 lb baby potatoes (such as Yukon Gold or red), halved
1 whole head of garlic, cloves separated and peeled (10-12 cloves)
1 large yellow onion, halved and sliced into thin half-moons
1 large red bell pepper, stemmed, seeded, and sliced into thin strips
1/2 cup dry white wine
1/2 cup low-sodium chicken broth
3 tbsp olive oil
2 tsp smoked paprika (pimenton)
1 1/2 tsp kosher salt
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper
2 bay leaves
1 tbsp sherry vinegar
1/4 cup fresh flat-leaf parsley, chopped

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1 cup Basque chicken braising liquid (from the recipe)
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
Steps:
1. Mise en place: a whole head of garlic peeled (10-12 cloves), potatoes halved, onion in half-moons, the pepper in strips (a poblano swaps in if you want warmth instead). Wine, broth and vinegar measured.
2. Sear the chicken: thighs patted completely dry, salted and peppered, olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high; skin-side down 6-7 minutes untouched until the skin is deep golden and crisp; flip 2 minutes. Out — under-seared skin goes rubbery in the braise, so earn the crust now.
3. Potatoes and aromatics into the drippings: potatoes cut-side down 4-5 minutes until golden at the edges; onion and the pepper 5 minutes until soft; the whole garlic cloves and smoked paprika in for 1 minute — the garlic will melt into the sauce.
4. Wine in, scraping the pot; broth and bay in; chicken back skin-up (skin above the liquid stays crisper). Cover, bare simmer 30-35 minutes until the chicken is tender and the potatoes creamy.
5. Finish: sherry vinegar stirred in at the end — it wakes the whole pot. Parsley over. Serve with the garlicky pan juices spooned around and bread for them.

Common mistakes:
- Wet chicken skin: it steams gray. Dry, hot, untouched.
- Vinegar at the start: it dulls in the braise. Last, off the boil.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Sherry-Butter Pan Sauce — ladle 1 cup of the braising liquid into a small saucepan; boil 3-4 minutes until reduced by a third. Off the heat, whisk in 2 tbsp cold butter until glossy. Spoon over the chicken and potatoes — the Basque braise, concentrated and buttered.

Title: BBQ Chicken Naan Pizzas
Ingredients:
6 (8-inch) plain naan breads
3 cups shredded rotisserie chicken (about 12 oz meat)
3/4 cup BBQ sauce, plus 2 tbsp extra for drizzling
12 oz shredded low-moisture mozzarella
1 medium red onion, halved and sliced paper-thin
1/4 cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped
2 tbsp olive oil
1 jalapeno, thinly sliced into rings (optional)

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1/4 cup barbecue sauce
- 1/2 tsp smoked paprika
Steps:
1. Oven at 450 F, racks in the top and bottom thirds, sheet pans inside heating. Rotisserie chicken shredded, red onion sliced paper-thin, jalapeño in rings, cilantro chopped.
2. Chicken tossed with 3/4 cup BBQ sauce until every shred is coated — dry chicken on pizza is a missed opportunity.
3. Crisp the naan bases first: brushed with olive oil, 3-4 minutes on the hot pans until the bottoms firm and the edges just color. A floppy base makes a floppy pizza.
4. Build: sauced chicken spread to the edges, mozzarella in a full blanket, red onion and jalapeño over.
5. Bake 6-8 minutes (swap the pans halfway) until the cheese bubbles and browns in spots and the edges crisp.
6. The extra BBQ sauce drizzled in lines, cilantro over. Slice and serve hot.

Common mistakes:
- Topping a cold naan: soggy middle, guaranteed. The pre-crisp is the recipe.
- Cold shredded chicken straight from the fridge: warm it in its sauce for 2 minutes so the pizza bakes evenly.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Smoky BBQ Butter Sauce — in a small pan, melt 2 tbsp butter with 1/4 cup BBQ sauce and 1/2 tsp smoked paprika over low heat until combined and glossy. Drizzle over the finished pizzas instead of (or with) the plain sauce — a buttery, smoky lacquer over the cheese.

Title: Beef Bourguignon-Style Potatoes
Ingredients:
1 1/2 lb beef chuck roast, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
2 lb Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and cut into 1 1/2-inch chunks
6 slices thick-cut bacon (about 6 oz), chopped into 1-inch pieces
2 cups dry red wine (such as Pinot Noir or Cotes du Rhone)
1 cup low-sodium beef broth
2 tbsp tomato paste
2 tbsp all-purpose flour
2 tbsp olive oil
1 large yellow onion, diced
3 carrots, peeled and sliced into 1/2-inch rounds
8 oz cremini mushrooms, quartered
2 cups frozen pearl onions (about 10 oz)
3 garlic cloves, minced
2 bay leaves
3 sprigs fresh thyme (or 1 tsp dried thyme)
1 1/2 tsp kosher salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper
2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1 1/2 cups bourguignon braising liquid (from the recipe)
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
Steps:
1. Oven at 325 F. Beef in 1 1/2-inch cubes, patted completely dry. Bacon chopped, onion diced, carrots in rounds, mushrooms quartered, pearl onions ready, potatoes chunked.
2. Render the bacon in a Dutch oven over medium heat until crisp, 6-8 minutes; out, fat stays. Sear the beef in the bacon fat in batches, 3-4 minutes untouched per batch, deep mahogany crusts. Out.
3. Onion and carrots into the drippings 6-8 minutes until golden at the edges; garlic and tomato paste 2 minutes until darkened. Flour stirred in 1 minute.
4. Wine in, scraping every bit of fond; reduce 3 minutes. Broth, bay and thyme in; beef and bacon back. Cover, into the oven 1 1/2 hours.
5. Potatoes and mushrooms in for 45 minutes; pearl onions for the last 20, until everything is tender and the sauce has turned to gravy.
6. Rest 10 minutes; parsley over. Salt at the end — the bacon and reduction concentrate it.

Common mistakes:
- Crowded beef: steamed gray cubes in wine. Batches, always.
- Potatoes from the start: they disintegrate into the gravy. Ninety minutes in, not at zero.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Red Wine Pan Gravy — ladle 1 1/2 cups of the braising liquid into a small saucepan; boil 5-6 minutes until reduced by half and syrupy. Off the heat, 1 tbsp cold butter whisked in. Spoon over each serving — the bourguignon sauce, doubled down.

Title: Beef Daube with Carrots & Potatoes
Ingredients:
2 1/2 lb beef chuck roast, cut into 2-inch cubes
2 lb small Yukon Gold potatoes, halved (or large potatoes cut into 2-inch chunks)
1 1/2 cups dry red wine (such as Cotes du Rhone)
1 1/2 cups low-sodium beef broth
4 (3-inch) strips orange zest, white pith scraped off
2 large yellow onions, quartered
4 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1-inch pieces
4 garlic cloves, minced
2 tbsp tomato paste
3/4 cup pitted black olives (Nicoise or Kalamata)
1/4 cup olive oil
4 sprigs fresh thyme (or 1 tsp dried thyme)
2 bay leaves
1 1/2 tsp kosher salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper
2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1 cup daube braising liquid (from the recipe)
- 1 strip fresh orange zest
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
- 1 tbsp chopped fresh parsley
Steps:
1. Marinate if you can (2 hours to overnight): beef cubes in the wine with the orange zest strips and thyme — daube is a Provençal wine marinade by birth. Even 2 hours changes it.
2. Oven at 300 F. Beef drained (wine saved) and patted dry — wet beef will not brown. Onions quartered, carrots in 1-inch pieces, garlic minced.
3. Sear the beef in batches in olive oil over medium-high, 3-4 minutes untouched per batch, until every cube wears a dark crust. Out.
4. Onions and carrots into the drippings 6-8 minutes until golden at the edges; garlic and tomato paste 2 minutes. The reserved wine in, scraping, reduced by a third; broth in.
5. Beef, zest, thyme and bay back; cover, into the oven 2 hours. Potatoes nestled in for the last hour; olives stirred in for the final 15 minutes so they warm without going mushy.
6. Rest 10 minutes. The sauce should be dark, winey and just thick enough to coat. Parsley over.

Common mistakes:
- Skipping the dry-off after the marinade: the sear never happens. Towels, thoroughly.
- Olives from the start: they turn soft and harsh. Fifteen minutes at the end.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Orange and Herb Pan Sauce — ladle 1 cup of the braising liquid into a small saucepan with a fresh strip of orange zest; boil 4 minutes until reduced by a third. Off the heat, 1 tbsp cold butter and 1 tbsp chopped parsley whisked in. Spoon over the beef — Provence in a spoonful: wine, orange, herbs.

Title: Beef Empanada-Style Rice Bowls
Ingredients:
2 lb ground beef (90/10)
2 cups long-grain white rice
3 1/2 cups water
2 large yellow onions, diced
1 large red bell pepper, diced
4 garlic cloves, minced
2 tbsp olive oil
2 tbsp sweet smoked paprika (pimenton dulce)
1 tbsp ground cumin
2 tsp dried oregano
1/2 tsp red pepper flakes
1/2 cup green olives, sliced
4 large eggs, hard-boiled and chopped
1/2 cup sliced scallions
1 1/2 tsp kosher salt
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper
Fresh cilantro or parsley, chopped (optional, for serving)
Lime wedges (optional, for serving)

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/4 cup water
- Juice of 1 lime
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
- 1/2 tsp smoked paprika (pimentón)
Steps:
1. Eggs hard-boiled first: cold water, boil, off the heat covered 11 minutes, cooled, peeled, chopped. Rice on (boil, cover, lowest heat 15, rest 10).
2. Brown the beef hard: olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high, beef in one layer, untouched 4-5 minutes until a dark crust forms; break up and finish. Drain the excess fat.
3. Onion and the pepper into the drippings 6-8 minutes until golden and sweet; garlic 30 seconds. Paprika, cumin, oregano and red pepper flakes in for 30 seconds, toasting — Argentine picadillo seasoning lives on smoked paprika.
4. Olives through; simmer 2 minutes so the brine seasons the beef. Salt in stages.
5. Off the heat: the chopped eggs folded in gently (they are the empanada's signature — do not mash them).
6. Serve over the rice, scallions over, lime wedges and herbs at the table.

Common mistakes:
- Gray beef: the crust is what makes this taste like an empanada filling instead of taco meat. Untouched, hot, one layer.
- Eggs cooked in the beef: they turn rubbery and gray. Folded in at the end.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Paprika-Lime Butter Pan Sauce — after the beef, add 1/4 cup water and the juice of 1 lime to the skillet; scrape up the spiced fond and reduce 1 minute. Off the heat, whisk in 2 tbsp cold butter and 1/2 tsp smoked paprika. Spoon over each bowl — the skillet's paprika crust, poured back over the beef and rice.

Title: Beef Kofta with Tomato Orzo
Ingredients:
2 lb ground beef (85/15)
1 large yellow onion, grated
4 garlic cloves, minced
1 cup fresh flat-leaf parsley, finely chopped
1/4 cup fresh mint leaves, finely chopped
1 large egg
2 tsp ground cumin
2 tsp sweet paprika
1 tsp ground coriander
1/2 tsp ground cinnamon
2 tsp kosher salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper
2 tbsp olive oil, divided
For the tomato orzo:
1 1/2 cups dry orzo
1 1/2 tbsp butter
1 small yellow onion, diced
3 garlic cloves, minced
1 can (14.5 oz) crushed tomatoes
2 1/2 cups low-sodium chicken broth
1 tsp sweet paprika
1/2 tsp dried oregano
3/4 tsp kosher salt
For the yogurt sauce:
1 cup plain Greek yogurt
1 garlic clove, minced
1 tbsp lemon juice
2 tbsp fresh mint, chopped
1/4 tsp kosher salt

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 tsp Aleppo pepper (pul biber)
- 1/2 tsp sweet paprika
Steps:
1. Yogurt sauce first: yogurt, garlic, lemon, mint and salt stirred and refrigerated. Onion grated for the kofta; herbs chopped fine.
2. Kofta mix: beef, grated onion (with a spoon of its juice), garlic, parsley, mint, egg, cumin, paprika, coriander, cinnamon, salt and pepper — mixed thoroughly but not packed. Chill 20 minutes.
3. Tomato orzo base: butter in a large pot, the diced onion 5-6 minutes until golden; garlic 30 seconds. Orzo stirred in and toasted 2 minutes until it smells nutty. Crushed tomatoes, broth, paprika, oregano and salt in; simmer 10-12 minutes, stirring often, until the orzo is tender and saucy.
4. Sear the kofta: shaped into 12 ovals, olive oil in a skillet over medium-high, 3-4 minutes untouched per side until deeply crusted, to 160 F. Rest 5 minutes; the crust is where kofta flavor lives.
5. Serve kofta over the tomato orzo, yogurt sauce spooned over both.

Common mistakes:
- Unstirred orzo: it welds to the pot's bottom. Stir it like a risotto's lazier cousin.
- Pale kofta: give them the full untouched sear. Color is flavor here.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Aleppo Butter Drizzle — in a small pan, melt 3 tbsp butter over medium heat until foaming; add 1 tsp Aleppo pepper (or pul biber) and 1/2 tsp sweet paprika; sizzle 20 seconds until brick red. Spoon over the kofta and orzo — the Turkish butter drizzle that finishes half the dishes in Istanbul.

Title: Beef Parmesan Risotto
Ingredients:
1 3/4 lb beef sirloin or strip steak, cut into 1/2-inch-thick strips
2 cups arborio or carnaroli rice (risotto rice)
6 cups low-sodium beef broth
1 large yellow onion, finely diced
3/4 cup dry white wine
4 oz Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese, finely grated (about 1 1/2 cups)
5 tbsp unsalted butter, divided
4 tbsp olive oil, divided
2 garlic cloves, minced
1 tbsp fresh rosemary, finely chopped
1 1/2 tsp kosher salt, divided
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper
Fresh parsley, chopped (for serving)

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 tsp finely chopped fresh rosemary
Steps:
1. Broth at a bare simmer in its own pot the whole time — warm broth is risotto law. Onion diced fine, garlic minced, rosemary chopped, Parmigiano grated.
2. Sear the beef first: strips patted dry, salted; 2 tbsp olive oil in a wide pan over medium-high, beef in one layer, untouched 2-3 minutes until deeply seared; toss 1 minute. Out with its juices — it returns at the end, medium-rare at heart.
3. The risotto: remaining oil and 2 tbsp butter, onion 5-6 minutes until soft and sweet; garlic and rosemary 30 seconds. Rice in, stirred 2 minutes until the grains turn translucent at the edges (the tostatura).
4. Wine in, stirred until absorbed. Then the broth a ladle at a time, stirring often, each addition absorbed before the next — 18-20 minutes until the rice is al dente and flows like lava.
5. Off the heat: the remaining butter and the Parmigiano beaten in (the mantecatura), then the beef and its juices folded through for 1 minute to warm. It should ripple when the pan shakes.
6. Parsley over, more Parmigiano at the table.

Common mistakes:
- Cold broth: the risotto stalls and cooks unevenly. Bare simmer, always.
- Beef cooked in the risotto from raw: gray strips and thin flavor. Sear first, fold in last.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Rosemary Brown Butter — in a small pan, melt 3 tbsp butter over medium heat until amber and nutty; add 1 tsp finely chopped rosemary and sizzle 20 seconds. Spoon over each serving of risotto — a Tuscan finish that makes the beef taste even beefier.

Title: Beef Picadillo Rice Bowls
Ingredients:
2 lb ground beef (85/15)
2 cups long-grain white rice
3 1/2 cups water
1 large yellow onion, diced
1 green bell pepper, diced
5 garlic cloves, minced
2 tbsp olive oil
1 can (15 oz) tomato sauce
2 tbsp tomato paste
1/3 cup raisins
2/3 cup pitted green olives, sliced
2 tbsp capers, drained
1 tbsp ground cumin
2 tsp dried oregano
1/2 tsp ground cinnamon
2 bay leaves
1 tbsp apple cider vinegar (or dry white wine)
1 1/2 tsp kosher salt
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper
2 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped (for serving)

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tbsp capers, drained
- 2 tbsp sliced green olives
Steps:
1. Rice on first (boil, cover, lowest heat 15, rest 10). Sofrito prepped: onion and the pepper diced, garlic minced, olives sliced, capers drained.
2. Brown the beef hard: olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high, beef in one layer, untouched 4-5 minutes for a dark crust; break up and finish. Drain the fat.
3. Sofrito into the drippings 6-8 minutes until golden and sweet; garlic 30 seconds. Tomato paste 1 minute until darkened; cumin, oregano and cinnamon 30 seconds.
4. Tomato sauce in, scraping; simmer 8-10 minutes until thick and cohesive. Raisins, olives and capers in for the last 3 minutes — the sweet-salty-briny triangle that IS picadillo.
5. Vinegar at the very end, off the heat — it brightens without cooking dull. Salt in stages; the olives and capers bring plenty.
6. Over the rice, cilantro over.

Common mistakes:
- Vinegar early: it flattens in the simmer. Last, off the heat.
- Pale beef: empanada-grade picadillo starts with a crust. Untouched and hot.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Warm Olive and Caper Oil — in a small pan, warm 3 tbsp olive oil with 1 tbsp capers and 2 tbsp sliced green olives over low heat for 2 minutes until fragrant and the capers sizzle gently. Spoon over each bowl of picadillo and rice — the dish's briny soul, warmed and doubled.

Title: Beef Picadinho with Potatoes
Ingredients:
2 lb beef chuck roast, cut into small 3/4-inch cubes
2 lb russet or Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and cut into 1-inch cubes
2 tbsp olive oil
1 large yellow onion, diced
4 garlic cloves, minced
3 ripe tomatoes, diced (or 1 can / 14.5 oz diced tomatoes)
2 tbsp tomato paste
2 tbsp Worcestershire sauce
2 tsp sweet paprika (colorau)
1 tsp ground cumin
1 bay leaf
3 cups low-sodium beef broth
1 cup frozen green peas
1 1/2 tsp kosher salt
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper
1/4 cup fresh parsley, chopped
Cooked white rice, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/4 cup low-sodium beef broth
- Juice of 1 lime
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
Steps:
1. Mise en place: beef in small 3/4-inch cubes — small is the whole point of picadinho. Potatoes in 1-inch cubes, held in cold water. Onion diced, garlic minced, tomatoes diced.
2. Brown the beef in batches: olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high, beef in one layer, 3 minutes untouched per batch until every cube is crusted. Out.
3. Onion into the drippings 6-8 minutes until golden; garlic and tomato paste 2 minutes until darkened. Paprika (colorau — it paints the stew red) and cumin 30 seconds.
4. Tomatoes and broth in, scraping; beef back. Bare simmer 30 minutes.
5. Potatoes in for 20-25 minutes until tender and the stew has thickened around them. Worcestershire through at the end. Peas in for the final 3 minutes, bright green.
6. Parsley over; white rice alongside, always.

Common mistakes:
- One big batch of beef: it boils in its own juice. Small cubes still need batches.
- Peas from the start: khaki. Three minutes at the end.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Lime-Butter Pan Sauce — after the beef sears, add 1/4 cup beef broth and the juice of 1 lime to the pot; scrape up the fond and boil 1 minute. Off the heat, whisk in 2 tbsp cold butter. Stir this back into the finished stew — a bright, buttery lift for a dark, beefy pot.

Title: Beef Sukiyaki-Style Rice Bowls
Ingredients:
2 lb beef ribeye or sirloin, sliced paper-thin (shabu-shabu / sukiyaki cut)
2 cups Japanese short-grain rice
2 1/4 cups water, plus 1 cup for the sauce
2 large yellow onions, sliced into thin half-moons
8 oz fresh shiitake mushrooms, stemmed and sliced
14 oz firm tofu, cut into 1-inch cubes
For the sukiyaki sauce:
1/2 cup soy sauce (shoyu)
1/4 cup sake
1/4 cup mirin
3 tbsp granulated sugar
1 tsp instant dashi powder dissolved in 1 cup hot water
1 tbsp neutral oil (such as canola)
For serving:
3 scallions, thinly sliced
1/4 cup pickled red ginger (beni shoga), optional
Shichimi togarashi (Japanese seven-spice), optional

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/4 cup soy sauce
- 2 tbsp mirin
- 1 tbsp sake
- 1 tbsp sugar
Steps:
1. Rice on (rinsed short-grain; boil, cover, lowest heat 15, rest 10). Beef sliced paper-thin against the grain (45 minutes semi-frozen makes it easy). Onions in half-moons, shiitakes sliced, tofu cubed gently.
2. Sukiyaki sauce whisked: soy, sake, mirin, sugar and the dashi water — it should taste sweet-salty and deep.
3. Sear the beef first, sukiyaki-shop style: the avocado oil in a wide skillet over high heat, a third of the beef laid in, 60-90 seconds until just browned at the edges; out. Repeat. (Restaurants sear in rendered fat and sugar; the quick sear is the home version of that caramelization.)
4. Onions in the drippings 3-4 minutes until soft and golden at the edges; shiitakes 2 minutes.
5. Sauce in, simmering; tofu slid in for 2 minutes to drink it; the beef back for 30 seconds only — it is already cooked and the sauce just warms it.
6. Over the rice with scallions, beni shoga and a shake of shichimi togarashi.

Common mistakes:
- Boiling the beef in the sauce from raw: it toughens and grays. Sear, then a 30-second reunion.
- Drowning the rice: spoon the beef and vegetables on with a slotted spoon, sauce at the table.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Extra Sukiyaki Glaze — in a small pan, simmer 1/4 cup soy sauce, 2 tbsp mirin, 1 tbsp sake and 1 tbsp sugar for 3-4 minutes until reduced to a glossy syrup. Spoon over the bowls — the sweet-salty lacquer, concentrated for the beef.

Title: Beef & Zucchini Bolognese
Ingredients:
1 1/2 lb 90% lean ground beef
4 oz pancetta, cut into 1/4-inch cubes (or 4 slices thick-cut bacon, chopped)
2 tbsp olive oil
1 medium yellow onion
1 medium carrot, peeled
1 celery stalk
2 medium zucchini (about 1 lb total)
2 cloves garlic
2 tbsp tomato paste
1 can (28 oz) crushed tomatoes
1 cup dry white wine (something you would drink)
1 cup whole milk
1 lb spaghetti
3/4 cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese, plus more for serving
2 1/2 tsp kosher salt, divided
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper
1/4 tsp ground nutmeg

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 2 tbsp finely diced pancetta
Steps:
1. Soffritto in fine 1/4-inch dice (onion, carrot, celery), garlic minced, pancetta cubed, zucchini grated on the large holes and squeezed lightly.
2. Render the pancetta in the olive oil over medium heat until crisp and its fat runs, 5-6 minutes. Beef in, spread flat, untouched 4-5 minutes for a deep crust; break up and brown through. This double-meat browning is the ragù's foundation.
3. Soffritto into the drippings 8-10 minutes until soft, sweet and golden at the edges; garlic 30 seconds; tomato paste 2 minutes until brick red.
4. Wine in, scraping, reduced by half. Crushed tomatoes and the grated zucchini in (it melts invisibly into the sauce — the zucchini trick); nutmeg and salt in. Bare simmer 45-60 minutes until thick and glossy; the milk stirred in for the last 10 minutes to round it.
5. Spaghetti in well-salted water, 1 minute shy of done; a cup of pasta water reserved.
6. Pasta through the ragù with splashes of pasta water until glossed. Parmesan at the table.

Common mistakes:
- A 15-minute ragù: the zucchini needs the simmer to disappear and the flavors to marry. Forty-five minutes.
- Skipping the pancetta render: it is half the depth. Crisp first, beef second.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Crispy Pancetta Butter — in a small pan, melt 2 tbsp butter over medium heat; add 2 tbsp finely diced pancetta and fry 2-3 minutes until crisp. Spoon over each bowl of spaghetti — the ragù's first ingredient, echoed as a crunchy finish.

Title: Blackened Trout & Roasted Potatoes
Ingredients:
2 lb baby potatoes (about 24)
3 tbsp olive oil, divided
1 1/2 tsp kosher salt, divided
1 lb fresh green beans
4 tbsp unsalted butter, melted, plus 1 tbsp for the pan
1 1/2 lb trout fillets (about 6 fillets), patted very dry
1 1/2 tbsp sweet paprika
1 tsp garlic powder
1 tsp onion powder
1 tsp dried thyme
1/2 tsp dried oregano
1 tsp cayenne pepper (use 1/2 tsp for mild)
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper
1 lemon, cut into wedges

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- Juice of 1/2 lemon
- Pinch of kosher salt
Steps:
1. Oven at 425 F. Potatoes halved, oiled and salted, cut-side down on a sheet pan; roast 25-30 minutes until crisp and golden on the cut faces. Green beans ready. Blackening spice mixed; melted butter ready for brushing.
2. Beans: blanched 3 minutes in salted water, or roasted alongside for the last 12 — bright and snappy either way.
3. Blacken the trout: fillets patted very dry, brushed with melted butter, the spice blend pressed on thick. A cast iron over high heat with the tablespoon of butter until it just smokes; fillets down (skin-side up if skinless) untouched 3-4 minutes until the crust is nearly black; flip 1-2 minutes. Vent on — blackening is smoky work.
4. Rest 2 minutes. Lemon wedges squeezed over at the table.
5. Serve over or beside the potatoes and beans, pan butter spooned around.

Common mistakes:
- A dusting of spice: blackening is a crust, pressed on thick. Timid spice makes spicy fish, not blackened fish.
- Wet fillets: they steam and the crust slides. Towels, thoroughly.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Brown Butter and Lemon — in a small pan, melt 3 tbsp butter over medium heat until amber and nutty; off the heat, the juice of 1/2 lemon and a pinch of salt — it will foam. Spoon over the trout: brown butter is blackened fish's oldest friend.

Title: Black Pepper Beef & Broccoli
Ingredients:
1 1/2 lb flank steak
2 tbsp low-sodium soy sauce, plus 1 tbsp more
2 tbsp cornstarch, divided
1 tbsp Shaoxing rice wine (or dry sherry)
2 tsp sugar
1 tbsp oyster sauce
2 tsp coarsely cracked black pepper (freshly ground is essential)
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp avocado oil or other neutral oil, divided
1 medium yellow onion
4 cloves garlic
1-inch piece fresh ginger
1 1/2 lb broccoli (about 2 large heads), cut into florets
1/2 cup low-sodium chicken broth
1 1/2 cups dry jasmine rice
2 1/4 cups water

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp oyster sauce
- 1 tsp sugar
- 1 tsp coarsely cracked black pepper
Steps:
1. Beef sliced thin against the grain (20 minutes frozen firms it), tossed with 2 tbsp soy, 1 tbsp cornstarch and the Shaoxing; rest 15 minutes. Sauce whisked: remaining soy, oyster sauce, sugar and the cracked black pepper — cracked coarse, never powder; the pepper is the headline. Rice on.
2. Char the broccoli: 2 tsp avocado oil in a wok over high heat, broccoli in one layer, untouched 2 minutes until charred at the edges; a splash of broth to steam 1 minute to crisp-tender. Out.
3. Sear the beef in two batches in the remaining oil, one layer, untouched 90 seconds per batch until dark at the edges. After the beef, the onion wedges go in for 2 minutes until charred at the edges; garlic and ginger 20 seconds.
4. Beef and broccoli back; the sauce and broth in; toss 1 minute until glossy and the pepper blooms in the heat. Taste — it should be boldly peppery with a sweet-salty base.
5. Over the jasmine rice immediately.

Common mistakes:
- Fine pepper powder: it vanishes. Coarse-cracked peppercorns give the dish its slow bloom of heat.
- Crowded beef: two batches or gray meat.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Extra Black Pepper Glaze — in a small pan, simmer 3 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp oyster sauce, 1 tsp sugar and 1 tsp coarsely cracked black pepper for 1-2 minutes until syrupy. Spoon over the beef and broccoli for the pepper-maximalists at the table.

Title: Brazilian Beef, Rice & Peas
Ingredients:
2 tbsp olive oil, divided
1 large yellow onion, finely diced
3 cloves garlic, minced
1 1/2 cups long-grain white rice
3 cups water
1 1/2 tsp kosher salt, divided
1 1/2 lb 93% lean ground beef
1 tbsp sweet paprika (pimentao doce)
1/2 tsp ground cumin
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper
2 medium tomatoes, diced
1 cup frozen peas (no need to thaw)
3 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped
Lime wedges and hot sauce, for serving (optional)

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/4 cup water
- Juice of 1 lime
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
- 1 clove garlic, minced
Steps:
1. Start the Brazilian rice (arroz branco): 1 tbsp olive oil in a pot over medium heat, half the onion and half the garlic 3-4 minutes until golden at the edges; the rice stirred in and toasted 2 minutes until it smells nutty; water and salt in; boil, cover, lowest heat 15, rest 10, fluff. Toasted rice is the Brazilian signature.
2. Brown the beef hard: the remaining oil in a large skillet over medium-high, beef in one layer, untouched 4-5 minutes for a dark crust; break up and finish. The remaining onion in for 4 minutes until golden; garlic, paprika, cumin and pepper 30 seconds.
3. Tomatoes in, simmered 5-6 minutes until they break down into a light sauce that coats the beef.
4. Peas through for 2 minutes — bright green.
5. Serve the beef over the toasted rice, parsley over, lime wedges and hot sauce at the table.

Common mistakes:
- Untoasted rice: it tastes like plain rice next to seasoned beef. The 2-minute toast in onion and oil is the dish's base note.
- Pale beef: one layer, untouched, hot pan.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Garlic-Lime Pan Sauce — after the beef, add 1/4 cup water and the juice of 1 lime to the skillet; scrape the paprika-dark fond and reduce 1 minute. Off the heat, 1 tbsp cold butter whisked in with 1 minced garlic clove rested in it for 30 seconds. Spoon over the beef and rice.

Title: Bulgogi Chicken Rice Bowls
Ingredients:
1 3/4 lb boneless, skinless chicken breast
1/2 cup low-sodium soy sauce
1/2 Asian pear, peeled and grated on the fine holes (or 1/2 sweet apple)
2 tbsp packed brown sugar
1 tbsp toasted sesame oil
4 cloves garlic, minced
1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
1 tbsp rice vinegar
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper
1 1/2 cups dry short-grain rice
2 cups water
1 English cucumber
1 tbsp rice vinegar, plus 1/2 tsp sugar
4 green onions
1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds
1 tbsp neutral oil, for the pan

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/4 cup soy sauce
- 1 tbsp brown sugar
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 tsp toasted sesame oil
Steps:
1. Marinate (30 minutes to 4 hours): chicken strips in the soy, grated pear, brown sugar, sesame oil, garlic, ginger, rice vinegar and pepper. The pear is the bulgogi secret — it tenderizes and sweetens at once.
2. Cucumber quick-pickled in the vinegar and sugar while you cook. Rice on (short-grain; boil, cover, lowest heat 15, rest 10).
3. Sear the chicken in batches: a film of avocado oil in a skillet over high heat, chicken lifted from the marinade and in one layer, untouched 2-3 minutes until the pear sugars char into dark, sticky edges; toss to finish. Batches — the marinade weeps, and a crowded pan boils the chicken instead of charring it.
4. All the chicken back for 30 seconds with a spoonful of the marinade to gloss it.
5. Bowls: rice, chicken, drained cucumber, green onions and sesame seeds over.

Common mistakes:
- Crowding: no char, no bulgogi. Two batches minimum.
- Marinade in the pan from the start: it burns before the chicken cooks. A spoonful at the end, as a gloss.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Extra Bulgogi Glaze — in a small pan, simmer 1/4 cup soy sauce, 1 tbsp brown sugar, 1 tsp grated ginger and 1 tsp sesame oil for 2-3 minutes until syrupy. Spoon over the chicken bowls — the marinade, concentrated into a lacquer.

Title: Caramel Pork with Cucumber Rice
Ingredients:
1 1/2 lb pork tenderloin
3 tbsp brown sugar
2 tbsp water
1 tbsp avocado oil
1 shallot, minced
2 cloves garlic, minced
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper
3 tbsp fish sauce
1 cup coconut water (or plain water)
1 English cucumber
1 tbsp rice vinegar
1/2 tsp sugar
1 1/2 cups dry jasmine rice
2 1/4 cups water
2 green onions, thinly sliced, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/4 cup coconut water (or water)
- 1 tbsp fish sauce
- 1 tbsp brown sugar
- 1/2 tsp coarsely cracked black pepper
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
Steps:
1. Pork in 1-inch cubes, silverskin trimmed. Cucumber sliced into half-moons and tossed with the rice vinegar and 1/2 tsp sugar; set aside. Rice on (jasmine; boil, cover, lowest heat 15, rest 10).
2. The caramel — watch it like a hawk: brown sugar and water in a heavy skillet over medium heat, swirled (not stirred) until it melts and turns deep amber, 3-4 minutes. It goes from amber to burned in 20 seconds.
3. Pork in immediately (it stops the caramel cooking), tossed to coat; the avocado oil, shallot and garlic in. The caramel will seize into threads, then melt again into the braise — this is correct.
4. Fish sauce, coconut water and the black pepper in; bare simmer 15-18 minutes, turning the pork now and then, until the sauce reduces to a dark, glossy lacquer and the pork is tender. It should taste salty, sweet and peppery in waves.
5. Serve over the rice with the pickled cucumber alongside (its crunch and acid are structural, not garnish) and the green onions over.

Common mistakes:
- Stirring the caramel: it crystallizes. Swirl the pan only.
- A pale caramel: timid caramel means sweet pork with no depth. Deep amber — one breath before burned.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Black Pepper Caramel Sauce — in a small pan, simmer 1/4 cup coconut water, 1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp brown sugar and 1/2 tsp cracked black pepper for 3 minutes until syrupy; off the heat, 1 tbsp cold butter whisked in. Spoon over the pork for a second, glossier coat of the caramel.

Title: Chicken Chile Verde Rice Bowls
Ingredients:
1 1/2 lb tomatillos, husks removed and rinsed
3 poblano peppers
1 jalapeno
1 medium yellow onion, half cut into wedges, half diced
3 cloves garlic, unpeeled
2 tbsp neutral oil, divided
1 3/4 lb boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 tsp ground cumin
1 tsp dried Mexican oregano (or regular oregano)
1 cup low-sodium chicken broth
1/2 cup fresh cilantro leaves, roughly chopped, plus more for serving
1 1/2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
1 lime, cut into wedges
1 1/2 cups dry long-grain white rice
2 1/4 cups water

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
- Juice of 1/2 lime
- Pinch of kosher salt
Steps:
1. Broiler on high, rack 4 inches below it. Tomatillos husked and rinsed, poblanos whole, jalapeño whole, the onion wedges and the unpeeled garlic on a sheet pan.
2. Char everything: broil 8-10 minutes, turning once, until the tomatillos slump and the poblanos blacken in patches. Garlic squeezed from its skins; poblanos stemmed and seeded. Blend it all with the cilantro and salt to a bright green sauce — it should taste tart, roasted and alive.
3. Sear the chicken: pieces salted, avocado oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high, 3-4 minutes untouched for golden crust. Cumin and oregano over for 30 seconds.
4. The verde sauce and broth in, scraping; bare simmer 15-18 minutes until the chicken is tender and the sauce has thickened slightly.
5. Rice under (boil, cover, lowest heat 15, rest 10), chicken and sauce over, cilantro and lime at the table.

Common mistakes:
- Skipping the char: raw-blended tomatillo sauce tastes grassy and thin. The broiler is the recipe.
- Under-salted verde: tomatillos are tart; the sauce needs salt until the tartness turns bright instead of sharp.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Cilantro-Lime Butter — in a small pan, melt 3 tbsp butter over medium heat until foaming; off the heat, stir in 2 tbsp chopped cilantro, the juice of 1/2 lime and a pinch of salt. Spoon over the chicken and rice — a green butter that softens the verde's tart edge in the best bites.

Title: Chicken & Chorizo-Style Paella
Ingredients:
4 cups low-sodium chicken broth
1/2 tsp saffron threads (about 1 generous pinch)
1 1/2 lb boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
1 1/2 tsp kosher salt, divided
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper
6 oz Spanish cured chorizo, sliced into 1/4-inch coins
3 tbsp olive oil
1 medium yellow onion, finely diced
1 red bell pepper, cut into 1/4-inch strips
3 cloves garlic, minced
2 tsp smoked paprika (pimenton)
1 can (14.5 oz) diced tomatoes, drained
1 1/2 cups bomba rice (or arborio as a substitute)
1 cup frozen peas
1 lemon, cut into wedges

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- Pinch of saffron threads
- Juice of 1/2 lemon
Steps:
1. Saffron bloomed in the warm broth (crumble the threads in and let it stand — saffron needs the soak). Chorizo in coins, chicken in 1 1/2-inch pieces seasoned, onion diced fine, the pepper in strips (a poblano stands in well), garlic minced, tomatoes drained.
2. Render and sear: olive oil in the widest skillet or paella pan you have, chorizo 3-4 minutes until its red fat runs; out. Chicken in the fat, one layer, untouched 4-5 minutes for a deep crust; out.
3. Sofrito: onion and the pepper strips in the drippings, 8-10 minutes, slow, until completely soft and sweet; garlic and smoked paprika 30 seconds; tomatoes in 5 minutes until dark and thick. This base is the paella.
4. Rice in, stirred 1 minute to coat in the sofrito. The saffron broth poured over evenly. Arrange the chicken and chorizo across the top. From here: DO NOT STIR. Bare simmer 18-20 minutes, rotating the pan once for even cooking.
5. Peas scattered over for the last 5 minutes. Then the socarrat: heat up for 60-90 seconds at the end until you hear the rice crackle and smell toast — the crispy bottom is the prize.
6. Rest 5 minutes off the heat, covered with a cloth. Lemon wedges at the table.

Common mistakes:
- Stirring: you get risotto, not paella, and no socarrat. Hands off after the broth.
- A timid sofrito: 10 slow minutes, no shortcuts; it is the whole flavor base.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Saffron-Lemon Butter — in a small pan, melt 3 tbsp butter over low heat with a pinch of saffron threads (or 1/4 tsp of the saffron broth) for 1 minute until golden; off the heat, the juice of 1/2 lemon. Spoon lightly over the paella at serving — a buttery saffron gloss over the socarrat's crunch.

Title: Chicken Dijon Risotto
Ingredients:
1 1/2 lb boneless, skinless chicken breast
1 1/2 tsp kosher salt, divided
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper
1 tbsp olive oil
1 large shallot, finely minced
1 1/2 cups arborio rice (do not substitute long-grain rice)
1/2 cup dry white wine
5 cups low-sodium chicken broth
3 tbsp Dijon mustard
1/4 cup heavy cream
3 tbsp cold unsalted butter, cut into small cubes
1/2 cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese
3 tbsp fresh tarragon leaves, chopped (or 1 tbsp fresh thyme leaves)

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 tsp Dijon mustard
- 1/4 cup heavy cream
- 1 tbsp chopped fresh tarragon
Steps:
1. Broth at a bare simmer the whole time. Shallot minced fine, tarragon chopped, Parmesan grated, the Dijon and cream whisked together, the cold butter cubed and kept cold.
2. Sear the chicken first: breasts salted and peppered, the olive oil in a wide pan over medium-high, 5-6 minutes a side untouched for a golden crust, to 165 F. Out to rest; sliced at the end. (Chicken cooked on top of finished risotto stays juicy; chicken cooked in it does not.)
3. Risotto: shallot in the chicken drippings 3-4 minutes until soft and sweet. Rice in, stirred 2 minutes until translucent at the edges. Wine in, absorbed.
4. Broth a ladle at a time, stirring often, each absorbed before the next, 18-20 minutes to al dente and flowing.
5. Off the heat: the Dijon-cream whisked in, then the cold butter and Parmesan beaten in until glossy (the mantecatura). Tarragon folded through.
6. Risotto in warm bowls, the sliced chicken fanned over.

Common mistakes:
- Dijon at the start: its bite cooks off. It goes in at the end, with the cream.
- Cold butter warmed up: it must be cold to emulsify the risotto glossy. Fridge to pan.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Tarragon Cream Pan Sauce — in a small pan, melt 1 tbsp butter with 1 tsp Dijon over low heat; add 1/4 cup heavy cream and 1 tbsp chopped tarragon; simmer 1-2 minutes until slightly thickened. Spoon over the chicken on each bowl — the risotto's flavors, echoed as a sauce for the meat.

Title: Chicken Fajita Potatoes with Jalapeños
Ingredients:
2 lb Yukon Gold potatoes
3 tbsp olive oil, divided
1 1/2 tsp kosher salt, divided
1 1/2 lb boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into 1/2-inch strips
