2 tbsp chili powder
2 tsp ground cumin
2 tsp smoked paprika
2 tsp garlic powder
1 tsp onion powder
1 tsp dried oregano
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper
1/4 tsp cayenne pepper (use 1/2 tsp for extra heat)
3 bell peppers (mixed colors), cut into 1/2-inch strips
1 large yellow onion, cut into 1/2-inch strips
3 jalapenos, sliced into 1/4-inch rings (seeds in for heat, out for mild)
1 lime, cut into wedges
3/4 cup plain Greek yogurt, for serving
1/4 cup fresh cilantro, chopped, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1/2 tsp smoked paprika
- Juice of 1 lime
Steps:
1. Oven at 425 F. Potatoes in 3/4-inch cubes, tossed with 1 tbsp olive oil and salt, one layer on the biggest sheet pan; roast 25-30 minutes, flipping once, until crisp and golden. Chicken in strips, coated in the fajita spice mix (chili powder through cayenne).
2. Sear the chicken: a large skillet over medium-high with 1 tbsp olive oil, chicken in one layer, untouched 3 minutes for charred edges; toss 2 minutes to cooked through. Out.
3. The peppers and onion into the drippings with the remaining oil, one layer, untouched 3-4 minutes until charred at the edges and just tender — fajita vegetables keep their snap. Jalapeño rings through for the last minute.
4. Chicken back for 30 seconds to marry with the vegetables and their juices.
5. Serve over the crispy potatoes (not rice — the potatoes are the point), the Greek yogurt dolloped over, cilantro scattered, lime wedges alongside.

Common mistakes:
- Crowded peppers: they steam into strips of mush. One layer, real char.
- Soggy potatoes: the chicken goes over them at the table, not in the pan, so the crisp survives.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Smoked Paprika and Lime Butter — after the chicken, melt 2 tbsp butter in the hot skillet with 1/2 tsp smoked paprika for 20 seconds; off the heat, the juice of 1 lime. Spoon over the chicken and potatoes — the fajita pan's charred spices, buttered and poured back.

Title: Chicken Fried Rice
Ingredients:
1 3/4 lb boneless, skinless chicken breast
6 cups cooked long-grain white rice, cooked the day before and refrigerated uncovered (from about 2 cups dry rice)
4 large eggs
1 1/2 cups frozen peas and carrots (no need to thaw)
6 green onions
3 garlic cloves
4 tbsp low-sodium soy sauce, divided
1 tbsp toasted sesame oil
2 tbsp avocado oil (or another neutral high-heat oil), divided
1 tsp kosher salt, divided
1/2 tsp ground white pepper (black pepper works too)

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1/2 tsp ground white pepper
Steps:
1. Mise en place — all of it, before heat: chicken in 1/2-inch dice, patted dry; the day-old cold rice broken up by hand (cold, dry rice fries; warm rice steams — this is fried rice's first law). Eggs beaten, green onions sliced, garlic minced, peas and carrots ready.
2. Eggs first: 1 tbsp avocado oil in a wok over medium-high, eggs in, scrambled in 30 seconds to soft ribbons. Out.
3. Sear the chicken: remaining oil, chicken in one layer, untouched 2-3 minutes until golden at the edges; toss with half the soy, the salt and white pepper to cooked through. Out.
4. The rice: wok at its hottest, the rice in, spread flat and left 60 seconds to crisp on the bottom; toss and repeat once. Peas and carrots through for 1 minute. Garlic 20 seconds.
5. Everything back: chicken, eggs, the remaining soy around the wok's edge so it sizzles, tossed hard for 1 minute. Sesame oil and green onions off the heat.
6. Taste for salt and serve immediately — fried rice waits for no one.

Common mistakes:
- Fresh rice: a gummy clump that no wok skill can fix. Day-old and cold, or spread fresh rice on a tray in the fridge for an hour.
- Sauce in the middle of the pan: it steams instead of sizzling. Around the edge.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): White Pepper Butter Sauce — in a small pan, melt 2 tbsp butter over medium heat; add 1 tbsp soy sauce and 1/2 tsp white pepper, swirl 30 seconds until combined and fragrant. Spoon over each serving of fried rice — a silky, peppery finish the takeout places do not offer.

Title: Chicken Katsu-Style Rice Bowls
Ingredients:
2 lb boneless, skinless chicken breast (4 large breasts)
2 cups short-grain white rice (sushi rice)
2 cups panko breadcrumbs (Japanese-style coarse crumbs)
2 large eggs
1/2 cup all-purpose flour
3 cups finely shredded green cabbage (about 1/2 small head)
1/3 cup tonkatsu sauce (store-bought; Bull-Dog brand is the classic)
1 cup neutral oil for frying (vegetable, canola, or avocado), plus 1 tsp for the cabbage
1 1/2 tsp kosher salt, divided
1/2 tsp black pepper
Lemon wedges, for serving (optional)

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 3 tbsp tonkatsu sauce
Steps:
1. Rice on (rinsed short-grain; boil, cover, lowest heat 15, rest 10). Cabbage shredded fine. Breading station: flour, beaten eggs, panko.
2. Chicken butterflied or pounded to an even 1/2 inch, seasoned. Bread: flour (excess shaken off), egg, panko pressed firmly. Rest 10 minutes so the crust sets.
3. Fry: 1/2 inch of avocado oil in a heavy skillet at 350 F, two cutlets at a time, 3-4 minutes a side, deep golden and crisp, to 165 F. Drain on a rack, salt immediately — never paper towels, which steam the crust.
4. Rest 3 minutes; slice into strips pressing straight down.
5. Bowls: rice, a bed of cabbage (tossed with the teaspoon of oil and a pinch of salt), the sliced katsu over, tonkatsu sauce in lines, lemon wedges alongside.

Common mistakes:
- Crust sliding off: dry chicken, excess flour off, the 10-minute rest, and hands off in the first minute of frying.
- Oil below 350 F: the panko drinks oil and goes greasy. Small batches hold the temperature.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Tonkatsu Butter Glaze — in a small pan, melt 2 tbsp butter over low heat; whisk in 3 tbsp tonkatsu sauce until glossy and combined. Drizzle over the sliced katsu — the classic sauce, warmed and buttered, clinging instead of pooling.

Title: Chicken Marsala-Style Orzo
Ingredients:
2 lb boneless, skinless chicken breast
1/4 cup all-purpose flour, for dredging
2 cups orzo pasta (about 12 oz)
12 oz cremini mushrooms (baby bella)
1 shallot
3/4 cup dry Marsala wine (NOT sweet -- the bottle should say "dry" or "secco"; Marsala is a fortified wine from Sicily)
3 1/2 cups low-sodium chicken broth
2 tbsp unsalted butter
2 tbsp olive oil, divided
1/4 cup chopped fresh parsley
1 1/2 tsp kosher salt, divided
1/2 tsp black pepper

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/2 cup dry Marsala wine
- 1/4 cup low-sodium chicken broth
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
Steps:
1. Chicken sliced into 1/2-inch cutlets, seasoned, dredged lightly in flour with ALL the excess shaken off. Mushrooms sliced, shallot minced.
2. Sear the cutlets: olive oil and butter in a large skillet over medium-high, cutlets in one layer, untouched 3-4 minutes until deeply golden; flip 2-3 minutes to cooked through. Out — the fond is the Marsala's base.
3. Mushrooms in the drippings in one layer, untouched 3 minutes until deeply browned; shallot in for 2 minutes. (Crowded mushrooms steam; browned mushrooms are half this dish.)
4. Marsala in, scraping every browned bit; reduce by half, 3 minutes, until the raw alcohol smell is gone. Broth in.
5. Orzo in the broth; bare simmer 9-11 minutes, stirring now and then, until tender and the liquid has turned to a glossy sauce around it.
6. Chicken back on top for 2 minutes to warm through and drink a little sauce. Parsley over.

Common mistakes:
- Sweet Marsala: the bottle must say dry or secco. Sweet Marsala makes dessert chicken.
- Mushrooms stirred constantly: they never brown. Untouched, one layer.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Extra Marsala Pan Sauce — in a small pan, simmer 1/2 cup dry Marsala until reduced by half; add 1/4 cup chicken broth, simmer 1 minute; off the heat, whisk in 1 tbsp cold butter. Spoon over the chicken on each plate — a double measure of the dish's winey, mushroom-dark soul.

Title: Chicken Milanesa with Parmesan Potatoes
Ingredients:
2 lb boneless, skinless chicken breast (4 large breasts)
1/4 cup all-purpose flour
3 large eggs
3 garlic cloves
3 tbsp chopped fresh parsley, plus more for serving
1 1/2 cups plain fine breadcrumbs (pan rallado style -- not Italian-seasoned)
1/2 cup finely grated Parmesan cheese, divided
2 lb Yukon Gold potatoes (about 4 medium)
3 tbsp olive oil, divided
1 lemon, cut into wedges
2 tsp kosher salt, divided, plus more for the potatoes
1 tsp black pepper

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/4 cup low-sodium chicken broth (or water)
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
- 1 tbsp chopped fresh parsley
- Squeeze of lemon juice
Steps:
1. Oven at 425 F with a sheet pan inside heating. Potatoes in wedges, oiled and salted, onto the hot pan cut-side down; roast 30-35 minutes, flipping once, until crisp and golden. Garlic minced, parsley chopped, Parmesan grated, lemon wedged.
2. Chicken butterflied or pounded to an even 1/2 inch, seasoned. Breading: flour, eggs beaten with the garlic and parsley (the Argentine way — the egg wash is seasoned, not the crumbs), then the fine breadcrumbs mixed with half the Parmesan, pressed on firmly. Rest 10 minutes.
3. Cook the milanesa: olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high, cutlets 3-4 minutes a side until deep golden and crisp, to 165 F — or bake them on a rack at 425 F for 15-18 minutes, flipping once. Drain on a rack.
4. Potatoes finished with the remaining Parmesan tossed over while hot so it clings.
5. Lemon squeezed over the milanesa at the table — non-negotiable — parsley over everything.

Common mistakes:
- Unseasoned egg wash: bland crust. Garlic and parsley in the egg is the Buenos Aires way.
- Thick, uneven chicken: dry edges, raw middle. Even 1/2 inch or nothing.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Lemon-Parsley Butter Pan Sauce — after the cutlets, add 1/4 cup chicken broth (or water) to the skillet; scrape up the crumbs and fond, simmer 1 minute. Off the heat, whisk in 2 tbsp cold butter, 1 tbsp chopped parsley and a squeeze of lemon. Spoon around the milanesa — crisp crust, warm lemon butter at the edges.

Title: Chicken Moqueca-Style Rice
Ingredients:
2 lb boneless, skinless chicken breast
2 limes (1 juiced, 1 cut into wedges for serving)
4 garlic cloves, divided
2 tsp kosher salt, divided
2 cups long-grain white rice
2 tbsp olive oil, divided
1 large yellow onion
1 large red bell pepper
1 can (14.5 oz) diced tomatoes, drained
1 can (13.5 oz) full-fat coconut milk (shake the can well first)
1 tbsp achiote oil -- the home substitute for dende (red palm oil): warm 1 tbsp avocado oil with 1 tsp annatto seeds over low heat 3 minutes until the oil turns deep orange, then strain out the seeds. (Or use 1 tbsp olive oil plus 1/2 tsp sweet paprika.)
2 tsp sweet paprika
1/2 cup chopped fresh cilantro, plus whole leaves for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1/2 tsp sweet paprika
Steps:
1. Marinate the chicken 15 minutes: lime juice, half the garlic, 1 tsp salt (the quick lime marinade is classic Bahian seasoning). Onion and the pepper sliced, remaining garlic minced, tomatoes drained, achiote oil made (avocado oil warmed with annatto seeds and strained, or olive oil plus paprika).
2. Rice on (boil, cover, lowest heat 15, rest 10).
3. Sear the chicken: 1 tbsp olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high, chicken lifted from the marinade and in one layer, untouched 3 minutes until golden at the edges. Out.
4. Onion and the pepper into the drippings 6-8 minutes until soft and sweet; garlic and sweet paprika 30 seconds.
5. Tomatoes and coconut milk in, scraping; bare simmer 5 minutes. Chicken back, simmer gently 8-10 minutes until cooked through — coconut milk at a hard boil can split; gentle heat keeps it silky.
6. The achiote oil drizzled over at serving (its orange-gold is the dendê look), cilantro over, lime wedges alongside.

Common mistakes:
- Boiling the coconut milk hard: it splits and turns greasy. Bare simmer once it is in.
- Skipping the sear: the moqueca tastes steamed instead of roasted at the edges. Three untouched minutes.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Achiote Butter Drizzle — in a small pan, melt 2 tbsp butter over low heat with 1/2 tsp sweet paprika (or a pinch of annatto) for 1 minute until deep orange-gold. Spoon over the chicken and rice — the dendê richness, finished with butter.

Title: Chicken, Olive & Tomato Orzo
Ingredients:
2 lb boneless, skinless chicken breast
2 tsp dried oregano, divided
2 cups orzo pasta (about 12 oz)
4 cups low-sodium chicken broth
1 1/2 pints cherry tomatoes (about 3 cups)
3/4 cup pitted Kalamata olives, halved
3 garlic cloves
2 tbsp olive oil
1/2 cup crumbled feta cheese
1 lemon
1 1/2 tsp kosher salt, divided
1/2 tsp black pepper

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1/2 tsp dried oregano
- Juice of 1/2 lemon
Steps:
1. Chicken in 1-inch chunks, tossed with oregano, salt and pepper. Tomatoes and olives halved, garlic minced, feta crumbled, lemon halved.
2. Sear the chicken: olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high, chicken in one layer, untouched 3-4 minutes for golden crust; toss to just cooked. Out — it returns to warm through, and overcooked chicken in orzo is chalk.
3. Orzo in the drippings, stirred 2 minutes to toast until it smells nutty. Garlic 30 seconds. Broth in, scraping; bare simmer 8-10 minutes, stirring often, until the orzo is tender and the broth has become a light sauce.
4. Tomatoes and olives in for 2 minutes until the tomatoes slump slightly.
5. Chicken back, lemon juice squeezed over, 1 minute to marry. Feta scattered on top off the heat so it softens without melting away.

Common mistakes:
- Unstirred orzo: it sets on the bottom. Stir like you mean it, every minute or so.
- Feta cooked in: it disappears into saltiness. On top, at the end.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Oregano-Lemon Pan Butter — in a small pan, melt 2 tbsp butter over medium heat; add 1/2 tsp dried oregano and sizzle 20 seconds. Off the heat: the juice of 1/2 lemon. Spoon over each serving — a warm, herbal butter that loves feta and olives.

Title: Chicken Parmesan Risotto
Ingredients:
2 lb boneless, skinless chicken breast (4 large breasts)
2 tbsp olive oil
2 cups arborio rice (risotto rice -- do not substitute long-grain rice)
1 yellow onion
6 cups low-sodium chicken broth
3/4 cup finely grated Parmesan cheese, plus more for serving
2 tbsp unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
1 1/2 cups marinara sauce (store-bought is fine)
1 cup shredded part-skim mozzarella
1/4 cup chopped fresh basil
1 1/2 tsp kosher salt, divided
1/2 tsp black pepper

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter, plus 1 tbsp more (cold) to finish
- 1/2 cup marinara sauce
- 1 tbsp chopped fresh basil
Steps:
1. Broth at a bare simmer throughout. Onion diced, Parmesan grated, basil chopped, butter cubed and kept cold.
2. Sear the chicken: breasts in the olive oil over medium-high, 5-6 minutes a side untouched for a golden crust, to 165 F. Rest, then slice. Cooked separately, it stays juicy; cooked in the risotto, it would chalk.
3. Risotto in the same pot: onion in the drippings 5-6 minutes until soft and sweet. Rice in, stirred 2 minutes until translucent at the edges. (No wine in this one — the marinara brings the acid.)
4. Broth a ladle at a time, stirring often, absorbed before the next, 18-20 minutes to al dente and flowing.
5. Marinara stirred through for the last 2 minutes so the risotto turns rosy. Off the heat: cold butter and Parmesan beaten in until glossy.
6. Risotto in bowls, sliced chicken over, mozzarella scattered so it melts in strands over the hot rice, basil on top.

Common mistakes:
- Marinara from the start: its acid toughens the rice's cooking. Last 2 minutes.
- Sliced chicken served cold on top: rest it tented and slice it last so it lands warm.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Tomato-Basil Butter — in a small pan, melt 1 tbsp butter; add 1/2 cup marinara and simmer 2 minutes until glossy. Off the heat, 1 tbsp cold butter and 1 tbsp chopped basil whisked in. Spoon over the chicken on each bowl — chicken parm's red sauce, buttered and finished like a pan sauce.

Title: Chicken Parm Pasta Bake
Ingredients:
2 lb boneless, skinless chicken breast
16 oz penne pasta (1 standard box)
3 cups marinara sauce (one 24-oz jar plus a little, or 3 cups homemade)
1 1/2 cups shredded part-skim mozzarella, divided
1/2 cup finely grated Parmesan cheese, divided
3/4 cup panko breadcrumbs
2 tsp Italian seasoning
2 tbsp olive oil
1 1/2 tsp kosher salt, divided, plus 1 tbsp for the pasta water

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1/2 cup heavy cream
- 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese
Steps:
1. Oven at 400 F. Pasta water boiling and salted like the sea. Chicken in 1-inch cubes, tossed with the Italian seasoning and salt.
2. Sear the chicken: olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high, chicken in one layer, untouched 3-4 minutes for golden crust; toss to just cooked. Out.
3. Penne 2 minutes shy of the package time; drain, reserving a cup of pasta water.
4. Pasta, chicken and marinara folded together with splashes of pasta water until everything is glossed; half the mozzarella and Parmesan stirred through.
5. Into a 9x13; the remaining cheeses over; the panko tossed with a drizzle of olive oil and scattered on top.
6. Bake 15-18 minutes until bubbling and the panko is deep golden. Rest 5 minutes.

Common mistakes:
- Fully cooked pasta before the bake: mush. Two minutes shy, always.
- Pale panko: it needs the oil toss and the full bake. Golden is the goal, not beige.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Garlic-Parmesan Cream Sauce — in a small pan, melt 1 tbsp butter with 1 minced garlic clove for 30 seconds; add 1/2 cup heavy cream, simmer 2 minutes; off the heat, whisk in 1/4 cup grated Parmesan until smooth. Spoon over each serving of the bake — a white-sauce ribbon through the red.

Title: Chicken Pesto Orzo with Broccoli
Ingredients:
2 lb boneless, skinless chicken breast
2 cups orzo pasta (about 12 oz)
1 1/2 lb broccoli florets (about 2 large heads, cut into bite-size pieces)
1/3 cup finely grated Parmesan cheese, plus more for serving
1 lemon
2 tbsp olive oil
1 tsp kosher salt, divided, plus 1 tbsp for the pasta water
1/2 tsp black pepper
For the fresh pesto Genovese (makes about 3/4 cup):
2 cups packed fresh basil leaves (about 2 large bunches -- leaves only, no thick stems)
1/4 cup pine nuts
1/3 cup finely grated Parmigiano-Reggiano
2 tbsp finely grated pecorino Romano (Parmesan works if you cannot find it)
1/3 cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more if needed
1 small garlic clove
1/2 tsp kosher salt

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp olive oil
- 2 tbsp pesto (from the recipe)
- Squeeze of lemon juice
Steps:
1. Pesto first: pine nuts toasted in a dry skillet 3-4 minutes until golden. Basil leaves dry. Pulse the garlic and pine nuts coarse; basil in with the olive oil pulsed to a rough, vivid paste; the cheeses and salt folded in by hand. Bright, loose, almost too salty.
2. Chicken in 1-inch cubes, seasoned. Pasta water on, salted like the sea. Broccoli in small florets, lemon zested and juiced.
3. Sear the chicken: olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high, chicken in one layer, untouched 3-4 minutes for a golden crust; toss to cooked through. Out.
4. Orzo in the boiling water; broccoli in for the last 3 minutes. Reserve a cup of pasta water; drain.
5. Off the heat: orzo and broccoli back in the pot, pesto and chicken over, lemon zest and juice in, splashes of pasta water tossed through until everything is glossed green — residual heat only; cooking pesto turns it army-green.
6. Parmesan at the table.

Common mistakes:
- Blending the pesto to a smoothie: pulse to a rough paste; texture is Genovese.
- Pesto over direct heat: dull color, flat flavor. Off the heat, always.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Warm Pesto Oil — in a small pan, warm 3 tbsp olive oil with 2 tbsp of the pesto and a squeeze of lemon over low heat for 1 minute — just warmed, never fried. Drizzle over each bowl: a warm, green slick that makes the pesto taste freshly made all over again.

Title: Chicken with Tomato Olive Salsa
Ingredients:
2 lb boneless, skinless chicken breast (4 large breasts)
1 1/2 cups pearled farro (quick-cooking kind if you can find it)
1 1/2 pints cherry tomatoes (about 3 cups)
1/2 cup Castelvetrano olives, pitted and roughly chopped (the bright-green Sicilian olives; Kalamata work in a pinch)
2 tbsp capers, drained and roughly chopped
1 shallot
1/4 cup chopped fresh basil, plus whole leaves for serving
3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, divided
2 tbsp red wine vinegar
1 1/2 tsp kosher salt, divided, plus 1 tbsp for the farro water
1/2 tsp black pepper

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/4 cup dry white wine (or low-sodium chicken broth)
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
- 1 tsp capers, chopped
Steps:
1. Farro on: salted boiling water, 25-30 minutes until tender with a pleasant chew; drain. Tomatoes quartered, olives and capers chopped coarse, shallot minced; the salsa folded together with the basil, 2 tbsp olive oil and the vinegar, and left to marinate so its juices become the dressing.
2. Sear the chicken: breasts patted dry and seasoned, the remaining olive oil in a skillet over medium-high, 5-6 minutes a side untouched for a deep golden crust, to 165 F. Rest 5 minutes, slice.
3. Spoon half the salsa (with its juices) over the warm farro and toss — the grains drink the tomato-olive liquor.
4. Farro in bowls, chicken fanned over, the remaining salsa spooned across, whole basil leaves on top.

Common mistakes:
- Salsa made and served instantly: it needs 15 minutes for the tomatoes to give up their juice. Make it first.
- Undercooked farro: it should chew pleasantly, not crunch. Taste at 25 minutes.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Caper Pan Sauce — in the chicken skillet over medium heat, add 1/4 cup dry white wine (or broth); scrape up the fond and reduce by half. Off the heat, whisk in 2 tbsp cold butter and 1 tsp chopped capers. Spoon over the sliced chicken — a briny butter that bridges the salsa and the meat.

Title: Chili Garlic Shrimp with Bok Choy
Ingredients:
2 1/4 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined, tails off
2 1/4 cups jasmine rice
3 cups water
1 1/2 lb baby bok choy
6 cloves garlic
1 tablespoon fresh ginger
3 green onions
3 tablespoons chili garlic sauce
3 tablespoons low-sodium soy sauce
2 tablespoons rice vinegar
1 tablespoon honey
2 tablespoons avocado oil, divided
1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, plus more for the rice

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp chili garlic sauce
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp honey
- 2 tbsp water
Steps:
1. Rice on (jasmine; boil, cover, lowest heat 15, rest 10). Shrimp patted VERY dry and seasoned. Bok choy halved, garlic and ginger minced, green onions sliced. Sauce whisked: chili garlic sauce, soy, vinegar, honey.
2. Char the bok choy: 1 tbsp avocado oil in a wok over high heat, bok choy cut-side down, untouched 2 minutes until charred at the edges; toss 1 minute to just wilted. Out.
3. Sear the shrimp in one layer, 90 seconds a side, until pink with seared edges. Out immediately.
4. Garlic and ginger in the remaining oil 20 seconds; the sauce in, simmered 30 seconds until glossy.
5. Shrimp and bok choy back for 30 seconds, tossed until lacquered. Green onions over; rice under.

Common mistakes:
- Wet shrimp: they steam pale and shed the sauce. Towels, thoroughly.
- Sauce reduced too far: it turns harsh and salty. Thirty seconds of simmer, no more.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Extra Chili Garlic Glaze — in a small pan, simmer 2 tbsp chili garlic sauce, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp honey and 2 tbsp water for 1-2 minutes until syrupy. Spoon over the shrimp for the heat-seekers — the wok sauce, concentrated.

Title: Chili Lime Shrimp Noodle Bowls
Ingredients:
2 1/4 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
12 oz dried flat rice noodles
3 limes
3 tablespoons fish sauce
2 tablespoons sweet chili sauce
1 tablespoon granulated sugar
2 cloves garlic
1 teaspoon red pepper flakes (start with 1/2 teaspoon if you are heat-shy)
1 1/2 English cucumbers
3 medium carrots
1/3 cup roasted peanuts
3/4 cup fresh cilantro leaves
1 tablespoon avocado oil
1/2 teaspoon kosher salt

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 2 tbsp sweet chili sauce
- Juice of 1/2 lime
Steps:
1. Noodles soaked in hot water 20-30 minutes until pliable but firm; drained. Dressing whisked: lime juice, fish sauce, sweet chili sauce, sugar, garlic, chile flakes — sour, salty, sweet, hot, in that order. Cucumber and carrots in matchsticks, peanuts crushed, cilantro picked. Shrimp patted dry and salted.
2. Sear the shrimp: the avocado oil in a skillet over high heat, shrimp in one layer, 90 seconds a side until pink with charred edges. Out to cool slightly — warm shrimp on a cold noodle salad wilt it; 5 minutes of cooling is right.
3. Toss the noodles with half the dressing and let them drink it for 5 minutes (noodles absorb dressing as they stand; this is the salad's secret).
4. Cucumber, carrots and cilantro folded through; shrimp arranged over; the remaining dressing spooned across; peanuts on top at the last second so they stay crunchy.
5. Lime wedges at the table.

Common mistakes:
- All the dressing at once on hot noodles: they go gummy. Half to drink, half to finish.
- Boiled noodles: mush. Soak only.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Sweet Chile Butter — in a small pan, melt 2 tbsp butter over medium heat; whisk in 2 tbsp sweet chili sauce and the juice of 1/2 lime until glossy. Spoon warm over the shrimp on each bowl — a hot, buttery sweet-heat against the cold, sour noodles.

Title: Chipotle Beef & Black Bean Rice
Ingredients:
2 lb 93% lean ground beef
2 1/4 cups long-grain white rice
3 3/4 cups water, plus more as needed
2 (15-ounce) cans black beans
1 (28-ounce) can diced tomatoes
3 chipotle peppers in adobo sauce
2 tablespoons adobo sauce (from the can)
1 large yellow onion
3 cloves garlic
1 1/2 teaspoons ground cumin
1 teaspoon dried oregano
2 limes
1/3 cup chopped fresh cilantro
1 tablespoon avocado oil
1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, divided, plus more to taste
1/2 teaspoon black pepper

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 tbsp adobo sauce (from the can of chipotles)
- Pinch of kosher salt
Steps:
1. Rice on (boil, cover, lowest heat 18, rest 10). Onion diced, garlic and chipotles minced fine (wash your hands after — chipotle oil burns eyes), beans rinsed.
2. Brown the beef hard: avocado oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high, beef in one layer, untouched 4-5 minutes for a dark crust; break up and finish. Drain the fat.
3. Onion into the drippings 5-6 minutes until golden; garlic, cumin and oregano 30 seconds. Chipotles and adobo sauce in — this is the dish's smoke and fire.
4. Tomatoes and beans in, scraping; bare simmer 10 minutes until thick.
5. Serve over the rice — or fold some rice through, diner-style. Cilantro and lime over; salt to taste at the end.

Common mistakes:
- Timid chipotle: this dish is supposed to be smoky-hot. Three peppers is the recipe, not the ceiling — but taste before adding a fourth.
- Pale beef: the crust carries the whole pot's depth.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Adobo Butter Sauce — in a small pan, melt 3 tbsp butter over medium heat; whisk in 1 tbsp adobo sauce (from the chipotle can) and a pinch of salt until brick red and glossy. Spoon over each bowl — smoky butter over smoky beef is not too much; it is exactly enough.

Title: Cod & Tomato Orzo Skillet
Ingredients:
2 1/4 lb cod fillets (about 1 inch thick), skinless
2 1/4 cups orzo
1 (28-ounce) can diced tomatoes
3 1/2 cups low-sodium chicken broth
3 cloves garlic
1 tablespoon tomato paste
1 1/2 teaspoons dried oregano
3 cups baby spinach
1/3 cup crumbled feta cheese
2 tablespoons olive oil, divided
1 lemon
1 teaspoon kosher salt, divided, plus more to taste
1/2 teaspoon black pepper

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1/2 tsp dried oregano
- Juice of 1/2 lemon
Steps:
1. Cod patted dry and seasoned. Garlic minced, lemon halved (half for juice, half in wedges).
2. Toast the orzo: 1 tbsp olive oil in a deep skillet over medium heat, orzo stirred 2-3 minutes until golden and nutty. Garlic and tomato paste 1 minute until darkened.
3. Tomatoes and broth in, scraping; oregano in. Bare simmer 8 minutes, stirring often.
4. Cod nestled into the orzo, lid on, 6-8 minutes at a bare simmer until the fish flakes at a touch. Spinach folded through in the last 2 minutes until wilted.
5. Lemon juice over, feta scattered off the heat so it softens in blobs. Rest 3 minutes before serving.

Common mistakes:
- Boiling the cod: it shatters into the orzo. Bare simmer, lid on, patience.
- Unstirred orzo before the fish goes in: it sets on the bottom. Stir often in stage one.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Lemon-Oregano Butter — in a small pan, melt 2 tbsp butter over medium heat; add 1/2 tsp dried oregano and sizzle 20 seconds. Off the heat: the juice of 1/2 lemon. Spoon over the cod — a warm Greek butter for a Greek skillet.

Title: Cod with Tomato Olive Couscous
Ingredients:
2 1/4 lb cod fillets (about 1 inch thick), skinless
2 1/4 cups dry couscous
2 1/4 cups low-sodium chicken broth
1 1/2 pints cherry tomatoes
1/2 cup pitted green olives
1/2 red onion
4 cloves garlic
1 1/2 teaspoons ground cumin
1 1/2 teaspoons sweet paprika
1/2 teaspoon ground turmeric
3 tablespoons olive oil, divided
2 lemons
3 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley
3 tablespoons chopped fresh cilantro
1 teaspoon kosher salt, divided, plus more to taste
1/2 teaspoon black pepper

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1-2 tsp harissa paste
Steps:
1. Couscous: broth to a boil, couscous and a pinch of salt in, off the heat covered 5 minutes, fluffed with a fork and a drizzle of olive oil. Cod patted dry and rubbed with the spice mix (cumin, paprika, turmeric, salt, pepper). Tomatoes halved, olives halved, onion diced, herbs chopped, one lemon juiced, one wedged.
2. Vegetables first: 2 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high, onion 4 minutes until golden at the edges; tomatoes in, untouched 2 minutes until they blister and slump; garlic 30 seconds. Out.
3. Sear the cod: remaining oil, the spiced fillets in one layer, untouched 3-4 minutes until a golden crust forms; flip gently, 2-3 minutes until just flaking — cod breaks if you fuss with it, so one flip, decisively.
4. Vegetables back around the fish for 1 minute. Lemon juice over everything.
5. Serve over the couscous, herbs scattered generously — parsley AND cilantro, the Moroccan way.

Common mistakes:
- Moving the cod early: the crust sticks and the fillet tears. It releases when it is ready.
- Dry couscous: fluff it with the fork and the oil, and let it steam the full 5 minutes.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Harissa Butter — in a small pan, melt 3 tbsp butter over medium heat; whisk in 1-2 tsp harissa paste until brick red and fragrant, 30 seconds. Spoon over the cod — Moroccan spices, buttered, for the fish that can take it.

Title: Crab & Parmesan Orzo Bake
Ingredients:
1 1/2 lb lump crab meat
2 1/4 cups orzo
4 cups low-sodium chicken broth
1/2 cup heavy cream
1/2 cup dry white wine (such as Pinot Grigio)
3 cloves garlic
1 1/2 cups frozen peas
3/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese, divided
3/4 cup panko breadcrumbs
2 tablespoons butter
2 tablespoons olive oil
1 lemon
2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley
1 teaspoon kosher salt, divided
1/2 teaspoon black pepper

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- 1 tbsp chopped fresh parsley
Steps:
1. Oven at 400 F. Crab picked through for shell (even good lump crab hides pieces), peas thawed, garlic minced, lemon zested and juiced.
2. Toast the orzo: olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat, garlic 30 seconds, orzo stirred 2 minutes until golden. Wine in, reduced by half.
3. Broth in; bare simmer 9-11 minutes, stirring often, until the orzo is tender and has drunk most of the liquid.
4. Cream and half the Parmesan in; peas through. Crab folded in gently — lump crab is folded, never stirred hard, or the lumps vanish. Two minutes to warm through.
5. Into a baking dish; the buttered panko (panko tossed with the melted butter) and remaining Parmesan over.
6. Bake 10-12 minutes until the top is deep golden and the edges bubble. Lemon juice and parsley over; rest 5 minutes.

Common mistakes:
- Shredding the crab: fold it in big, proud lumps at the end.
- Dry panko: it needs its butter toss or it bakes pale and dusty.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Lemon-Parsley Butter — in a small pan, melt 3 tbsp butter over medium heat until foaming; off the heat, 1 tbsp lemon juice and 1 tbsp chopped parsley. Spoon over each serving of the bake — crab and lemon butter are one of cooking's oldest agreements.

Title: Creamy Tuscan Chicken Pasta
Ingredients:
2 1/4 lb boneless, skinless chicken breasts
18 oz penne pasta
3/4 cup oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes, drained
4 1/2 cups baby spinach (about 5 oz)
5 cloves garlic
1 1/2 cups low-sodium chicken broth
3/4 cup heavy cream
1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese
1 1/2 teaspoons Italian seasoning
1/2 teaspoon red pepper flakes
2 tablespoons olive oil
1 tablespoon butter
1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, divided
1/2 teaspoon black pepper

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter
- 2 tbsp finely chopped sun-dried tomatoes
- 1/4 cup heavy cream
Steps:
1. Pasta water on, salted like the sea. Chicken in strips, garlic minced, sun-dried tomatoes sliced thin.
2. Sear the chicken: olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high, chicken in one layer, untouched 3-4 minutes for golden crust; toss to cooked through. Out.
3. Butter in the drippings; garlic, the Italian seasoning and red pepper flakes 30 seconds; sun-dried tomatoes 1 minute until their oil turns the butter orange.
4. Broth in, scraping; cream in; bare simmer 3-4 minutes until slightly thickened. Parmesan whisked in until melted.
5. Penne 1 minute shy of done, straight into the sauce with splashes of pasta water; spinach in by the handful until wilted; chicken back for 1 minute. Everything glossed and clinging.
6. Salt to taste; more Parmesan at the table.

Common mistakes:
- Boiling the cream sauce hard: it can split and turn greasy. Bare simmer.
- Spinach in early: it goes khaki and stringy. Last, by the handful.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Sun-Dried Tomato Cream — in a small pan, melt 1 tbsp butter; add 2 tbsp finely chopped sun-dried tomatoes and sizzle 30 seconds. Add 1/4 cup heavy cream; simmer 2 minutes until rosy and slightly thick. Spoon over each serving — the Tuscan sauce, concentrated for the top of the bowl.

Title: Dakgalbi-Style Chicken & Rice
Ingredients:
2 1/4 lb boneless, skinless chicken thighs
2 1/4 cups short-grain white rice
2 3/4 cups water, plus 1/2 cup more as needed
3 tablespoons gochujang (Korean chili paste)
1 1/2 tablespoons gochugaru (Korean chili flakes)
3 tablespoons low-sodium soy sauce
2 tablespoons honey
1 teaspoon Korean curry powder
5 cloves garlic
1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger
2 medium sweet potatoes (about 1 lb total)
3/4 head green cabbage (about 6 cups chopped)
1 large yellow onion
4 green onions
2 tablespoons avocado oil
1 teaspoon toasted sesame oil
1 teaspoon kosher salt

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp gochujang (Korean chili paste)
- 1 tbsp honey
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 2 tbsp water
Steps:
1. Marinade: gochujang, gochugaru, soy, honey, curry powder, garlic, ginger and salt stirred to a thick red paste; chicken pieces worked through it by hand. Rest 20 minutes minimum. Rice on (short-grain; boil, cover, lowest heat 15, rest 10). Sweet potatoes in 1/2-inch cubes, cabbage chopped coarse, onion wedged, green onions sliced.
2. The dakgalbi sizzle: avocado oil in the widest skillet or a griddle over medium-high; the chicken spread out with its marinade, untouched 4-5 minutes until the sugars char dark at the edges — this char is dakgalbi's signature, not an accident.
3. Sweet potatoes and onion in around the chicken; toss and cook 8-10 minutes, scraping, until the potatoes are tender. Cabbage in for the last 3-4 minutes until wilted but still snappy.
4. Sesame oil off the heat, green onions over. Serve straight from the pan over the rice, Chuncheon-style.

Common mistakes:
- A crowded, wet pan: the chicken stews instead of charring. The widest pan you own, or two batches.
- Cabbage from the start: it drowns the pan in liquid and kills the char. Last minutes only.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Extra Gochujang Glaze — in a small pan, simmer 2 tbsp gochujang, 1 tbsp honey, 1 tbsp soy sauce and 2 tbsp water for 2 minutes until glossy. Spoon over the dakgalbi for anyone who wants the heat and shine turned up.

Title: Dijon Pork with Parmesan Potatoes
Ingredients:
2 1/4 lb pork tenderloin
2 1/4 lb baby potatoes
1 1/2 lb green beans, trimmed
3 tablespoons Dijon mustard
1 1/2 tablespoons honey
3 cloves garlic
1 teaspoon dried thyme
1/3 cup grated Parmesan cheese
3 tablespoons olive oil, divided
1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, divided
3/4 teaspoon black pepper, divided

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/4 cup low-sodium chicken broth
- 2 tbsp heavy cream
- 1 tsp Dijon mustard
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
Steps:
1. Oven at 425 F. Potatoes halved, oiled and salted, cut-side down on a sheet pan. Green beans ready. Dijon glaze whisked (mustard, honey, garlic, thyme). Pork patted completely dry, silverskin trimmed, seasoned.
2. Roast the potatoes 25-30 minutes until crisp on the cut faces. Beans on a second pan (or alongside) for the last 12 minutes until blistered in spots.
3. Sear the pork: olive oil in a skillet over medium-high, tenderloin turned every 2-3 minutes until every side wears a deep golden crust — 8-10 minutes of turning is the whole technique. Brush with half the Dijon glaze; into the oven (or the hot pan into the oven) 8-10 minutes to 145 F.
4. Rest a full 10 minutes — tenderloin dries if sliced hot and impatient. Slice into medallions; the remaining glaze warmed and brushed over.
5. Potatoes finished with the Parmesan tossed over while hot. Everything on warm plates.

Common mistakes:
- Glaze from the start: the honey burns before the pork cooks. Sear first, glaze in the oven.
- Pork past 145 F: tenderloin has no fat to forgive you. Pull at 145, rest, slice.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Dijon Cream Pan Sauce — in the pork skillet over medium heat, add 1/4 cup chicken broth; scrape up the fond and reduce 1 minute. Off the heat, whisk in 2 tbsp heavy cream, 1 tsp Dijon and 1 tbsp cold butter until glossy. Spoon over the medallions — the glaze, turned into a proper French pan sauce.

Title: Garlic Beef & Green Onion Rice
Ingredients:
2 lb flank steak
2 1/4 cups jasmine rice
3 cups water
12 green onions
7 cloves garlic
1 tablespoon fresh ginger
4 tablespoons low-sodium soy sauce, divided
1 1/2 tablespoons oyster sauce
1 1/2 tablespoons cornstarch
1 teaspoon granulated sugar
2 tablespoons avocado oil, divided
1 teaspoon toasted sesame oil
1/2 teaspoon white pepper (or black pepper)

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/4 cup low-sodium chicken broth
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp oyster sauce
Steps:
1. Rice on (jasmine; boil, cover, lowest heat 15, rest 10). Beef sliced thin against the grain, tossed with 1 tbsp soy, the cornstarch and sugar; rest 15 minutes. Green onions in 2-inch pieces (whites and greens separated), garlic sliced, ginger minced — a mountain of garlic is the point of this dish.
2. Sear the beef in two batches: 1 tbsp avocado oil in a wok over high heat until smoking, beef in one layer, untouched 90 seconds until dark at the edges; toss 1 minute. Out.
3. Garlic and ginger in the remaining oil 20 seconds until fragrant — do not let the garlic brown past gold. Green onion whites 30 seconds.
4. Beef back; the remaining soy, oyster sauce and sesame oil in; white pepper over. Toss 1 minute until glossy.
5. Green onion greens through at the very end. Over the rice immediately.

Common mistakes:
- Burned garlic: it turns bitter and ruins the dish's whole premise. Gold, then move.
- Green onions cooked to death: the greens go in at the end, raw-crisp.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Beef Pan Glaze — after the beef, add 1/4 cup chicken broth, 1 tbsp soy sauce and 1 tsp oyster sauce to the wok; scrape up the seared fond and boil 1 minute until syrupy. Pour over the beef and rice — the wok's crust, collected.

Title: Garlic Butter Chicken & Orzo
Ingredients:
- 2 lb boneless, skinless chicken breasts (about 3 large)
- 1 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
- 1/2 tsp black pepper
- 1 tsp garlic powder
- 1 tsp Italian seasoning
- 1 lb (about 2 3/4 cups) dry orzo
- 5 tbsp unsalted butter, divided
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 6 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice (about 1 lemon)
- 1 1/2 cups chicken broth
- 1/2 cup heavy cream
- 1/2 cup freshly grated Parmesan, plus more for serving
- 5 oz baby spinach (about 5 packed cups)
- 1/4 cup chopped fresh parsley

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 clove garlic, thinly sliced
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
Steps:
1. Chicken evened out (pound to 3/4 inch), seasoned with salt, pepper, garlic powder and Italian seasoning. Garlic minced, Parmesan grated, lemon juiced, spinach rinsed.
2. Sear the chicken: olive oil and 1 tbsp butter in a large deep skillet over medium-high, chicken down untouched 5-6 minutes until deeply golden; flip 4-5 minutes to 165 F. Out — the fond is the sauce's base.
3. Orzo in the drippings, stirred 2 minutes to toast. Garlic in for 30 seconds.
4. Broth in, scraping; bare simmer 8-10 minutes, stirring often, until the orzo is tender. Cream and the remaining butter in; Parmesan melted through.
5. Spinach in by the handful until just wilted. Chicken back (sliced) on top, lemon juice over everything — add it last so it stays bright.
6. Parsley over; more Parmesan at the table.

Common mistakes:
- Lemon in early: it dulls in the simmer. Over the finished dish.
- Unstirred orzo: welded to the pan. Stir it often.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Extra Lemon-Garlic Butter — in a small pan, melt 2 tbsp butter over medium heat with 1 sliced garlic clove until foaming and fragrant, 1 minute; off the heat, 1 tbsp lemon juice. Spoon over the chicken on each plate — because garlic butter chicken can, in fact, have more garlic butter.

Title: Garlic Butter Lobster Rice
Ingredients:
- 3 cups long-grain white rice
- 4 1/2 cups seafood stock or chicken broth
- 1 1/2 lb cooked lobster meat, cut into 1-inch chunks (look for claw and tail meat near the fish counter)
- 8 tbsp (1 stick) unsalted butter
- 8 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/4 cup dry sherry
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice, plus lemon wedges for serving
- 1 tsp lemon zest (the thin yellow outer peel, grated — stop before the white pith, which is bitter)
- 3 tbsp chopped fresh chives
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh parsley
- 1/2 tsp sweet paprika
- 1 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- 2 tbsp dry sherry
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- Pinch of kosher salt
Steps:
1. Rice rinsed and cooked in the seafood stock (boil, cover, lowest heat 15, rest 10) — stock-cooked rice is this dish's quiet luxury. Lobster in 1-inch chunks, garlic minced, lemon zested and juiced, herbs chopped.
2. Garlic butter: the butter melted in a large skillet over medium heat, garlic in for 1 minute until fragrant and just golden — never brown.
3. Sherry in, simmered 1 minute until the sharp smell cooks off.
4. Lobster in for 2-3 minutes ONLY, tossed until just warmed through and glossy — cooked lobster reheated hard turns to rubber bands; it was already cooked, and your only job is to warm it in butter.
5. Lemon juice and zest in off the heat. Fold through the hot rice (or serve the lobster and its butter spooned over rice in bowls).
6. Chives, parsley and paprika over.

Common mistakes:
- Cooking the lobster: it is already cooked. Warm, glossy, out.
- Browned garlic in the butter: bitterness in every bite. One minute, golden, go.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Sherry-Lemon Butter — in a small pan, melt 3 tbsp butter over medium heat; add 2 tbsp dry sherry and simmer 1 minute; off the heat, 1 tbsp lemon juice and a pinch of salt. Spoon over each bowl — an extra measure of the dish's own sauce, for the rice at the bottom.

Title: Garlic Butter Shrimp Orzo
Ingredients:
- 2 lb large shrimp (21/25 count), peeled and deveined
- 12 oz (about 2 cups) dry orzo
- 1 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
- 1/2 tsp black pepper
- 6 tbsp unsalted butter, divided
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 6 cloves garlic, thinly sliced
- 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes
- 1 cup chicken broth
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice (about 1 lemon)
- 1/4 cup freshly grated Parmesan
- 8 oz cherry tomatoes, halved
- 1/4 cup chopped fresh parsley

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- 1 tbsp grated Parmesan cheese
Steps:
1. Shrimp patted completely dry and seasoned. Garlic sliced into coins, tomatoes halved, parsley chopped, lemon juiced.
2. Sear the shrimp: olive oil and 1 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium-high, shrimp in one layer, 90 seconds untouched until pink with seared edges; flip 30 seconds. Out immediately.
3. Orzo in the drippings, stirred 2 minutes to toast. Garlic coins and red pepper flakes in for 30 seconds (coins, not mince — they toast without burning).
4. Broth in, scraping; bare simmer 8-10 minutes, stirring often, until tender.
5. Remaining butter and the Parmesan in; tomatoes through for 1 minute until they just slump. Shrimp back for 30 seconds. Lemon juice over off the heat.
6. Parsley over, more Parmesan at the table.

Common mistakes:
- Shrimp finishing in the orzo: rubber. Sear, out, back for 30 seconds.
- Minced garlic here: it burns in the time the coins toast. Slice, don't mince.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Lemon-Parmesan Butter — in a small pan, melt 2 tbsp butter over medium heat until foaming; off the heat, whisk in 1 tbsp lemon juice and 1 tbsp grated Parmesan until glossy. Spoon over the shrimp and orzo — a bright, cheesy butter finish.

Title: Garlic Chicken & Bok Choy
Ingredients:
For the velveting marinade:
- 1 3/4 lb boneless, skinless chicken breasts, sliced 1/4-inch thick
- 1 tbsp light soy sauce
- 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine (or dry sherry)
- 1 tbsp cornstarch
- 1 tbsp water
- 1 tbsp vegetable oil

For the stir-fry sauce:
- 1/4 cup chicken broth
- 2 tbsp oyster sauce
- 1 tbsp light soy sauce
- 1 tsp sugar
- 1 tbsp cornstarch
- 2 tbsp water

For the stir-fry:
- 2 lb baby bok choy
- 3 tbsp vegetable oil, divided
- 8 cloves garlic, roughly chopped
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, minced
- 2 tsp toasted sesame oil
- 3 scallions, sliced

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp low-sodium chicken broth
- 1 tbsp oyster sauce
- 1 tsp soy sauce
- 1/2 tsp sugar
- 1/2 tsp cornstarch
Steps:
1. Velvet the chicken: slices tossed with the soy, Shaoxing, cornstarch, water and oil; rest 15 minutes. This coating is why Chinese-restaurant chicken is silky. Bok choy halved and rinsed of grit; garlic chopped chunky (8 cloves is the point), ginger minced. Sauce whisked: broth, oyster sauce, soy, sugar, cornstarch, water.
2. Blanch or steam the bok choy 2 minutes until bright; drain dry — wet bok choy floods the wok later.
3. Sear the chicken: 2 tbsp avocado oil in a wok over high heat, chicken in one layer, untouched 90 seconds until golden at the edges; toss 2 minutes to cooked through. Out.
4. Garlic and ginger in the remaining oil 20 seconds until fragrant — the garlic should sizzle, not brown. Bok choy in for 1 minute to coat in the garlic oil.
5. Chicken back; the sauce in; toss 1 minute until glossy and clinging. Sesame oil and scallions off the heat.
6. Rice under, immediately.

Common mistakes:
- Skipping the velvet: ordinary stir-fry chicken, fine but not silky. Fifteen minutes changes the texture completely.
- Wet bok choy: drain it like the sauce depends on it.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Extra Garlic Sauce Glaze — in a small pan, simmer the sauce mix (3 tbsp chicken broth, 1 tbsp oyster sauce, 1 tsp soy sauce, 1/2 tsp sugar, 1/2 tsp cornstarch) for 1 minute until glossy. Spoon over the chicken for anyone who likes theirs extra sauced.

Title: Garlic Cod & Potato Stew
Ingredients:
- 2 lb cod fillets (about 1 1/2 inches thick), cut into 2-inch chunks
- 2 lb Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and sliced 1/4-inch thick
- 2 medium yellow onions, thinly sliced
- 3 large ripe tomatoes, sliced 1/4-inch thick
- 1 red bell pepper, sliced into strips
- 1 green bell pepper, sliced into strips
- 6 cloves garlic, thinly sliced
- 6 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
- 1 cup dry white wine
- 1 cup fish stock, chicken broth, or water
- 2 bay leaves
- 1 tsp sweet paprika
- 1 1/2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
- 1/2 tsp black pepper
- 1/4 cup chopped fresh parsley or cilantro
- Crusty bread, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/4 cup olive oil
- 2 cloves garlic, thinly sliced
- 1 tsp sweet paprika
- 1/2 tsp red chile flakes
Steps:
1. A caldeirada is built in layers — potatoes sliced 1/4 inch, onions and tomatoes sliced, the peppers in strips (poblanos swap in beautifully), garlic sliced thin, cod in 2-inch chunks patted dry and seasoned.
2. Layer the pot: a drizzle of olive oil; half the onions, tomatoes and peppers; all the potatoes (they take longest, so they go low, near the heat); the cod on top of the potatoes; the remaining vegetables over the fish. Garlic, paprika, bay, salt and pepper scattered between the layers; the rest of the olive oil poured over.
3. Wine and stock poured down the side (do not stir — the layers are the method). Lid on, bare simmer 25-30 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the cod flakes. Shake the pot gently once or twice instead of stirring.
4. Rest 5 minutes off the heat. Serve in deep bowls with the layers intact, the broth ladled over, parsley or cilantro scattered.
5. Crusty bread for the broth — mandatory.

Common mistakes:
- Stirring: you get fish soup with broken cod. Layers, a gentle shake, faith.
- Boiling hard: the cod shatters. Bare simmer only.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Piri-Piri Garlic Oil — in a small pan, warm 1/4 cup olive oil with 2 sliced garlic cloves, 1 tsp sweet paprika and 1/2 tsp chile flakes over low heat for 2-3 minutes until deep red and fragrant. Spoon over each bowl — Portugal's table oil, and the caldeirada's perfect finish.

Title: Garlic Lime Chicken Rice Bowls
Ingredients:
For the chicken:
- 2 lb boneless, skinless chicken thighs
- 6 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/4 cup fresh lime juice (about 3 limes)
- 2 tsp lime zest
- 1/4 cup olive oil
- 2 tsp ground cumin
- 2 tsp dried oregano
- 1 tsp chili powder
- 1 1/2 tsp kosher salt

For the bowls:
- 3 cups long-grain white rice
- 1 (15-oz) can black beans, drained and rinsed
- 1 1/2 cups frozen corn
- 2 medium tomatoes, diced
- 1/2 small red onion, diced
- 1 jalapeño, minced (remove the seeds for less heat)
- 1/4 cup chopped fresh cilantro, plus more for serving
- 1 large avocado, diced
- 2 oz cotija cheese, crumbled
- Lime wedges, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/4 cup low-sodium chicken broth
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
- Juice of 1/2 lime
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
Steps:
1. Marinate the chicken (30 minutes to 4 hours): garlic, lime juice and zest, olive oil, cumin, oregano, chili powder and salt. Rice rinsed and on. Beans drained, corn ready, tomatoes and onion diced, jalapeño minced, avocado diced last.
2. Sear the thighs whole: a cast iron over medium-high, chicken lifted from the marinade, 5-6 minutes a side untouched until deeply charred at the edges, to 175 F. Rest 5 minutes, slice — slicing after keeps every piece juicy and crusted.
3. Beans and corn warmed through in the chicken pan with a splash of water, scraping up the fond — they come out seasoned by the pan itself.
4. Bowls: rice, beans and corn, sliced chicken, tomatoes, onion, jalapeño, avocado, cotija. Cilantro over, lime wedges at the table.

Common mistakes:
- Slicing the chicken before cooking: it dries and loses its crust. Whole, then sliced.
- Marinating past 4 hours: the lime starts to cure the surface chalky. Four is the ceiling.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Cilantro-Lime Pan Sauce — in the chicken skillet over medium heat, add 1/4 cup chicken broth; scrape up the charred fond and reduce 1 minute. Off the heat, whisk in 1 tbsp cold butter, the juice of 1/2 lime and 2 tbsp chopped cilantro. Spoon over the sliced chicken in each bowl.

Title: Garlic Pork Tenderloin Risotto
Ingredients:
- 1 3/4 lb pork tenderloin, trimmed of silverskin
- 2 cups arborio rice
- 7 cups chicken stock
- 1/2 cup dry white wine
- 6 tbsp unsalted butter, cold, cut into pieces and divided
- 1 cup freshly grated Parmesan, plus more for serving
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 large shallot (or 1 small onion), minced
- 6 cloves garlic, minced, divided
- 8 oz cremini mushrooms, sliced
- 2 tsp fresh thyme leaves (or 1/2 tsp dried)
- 1 1/2 tsp kosher salt, divided
- 1/2 tsp black pepper

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 tsp fresh thyme leaves
Steps:
1. Stock at a bare simmer throughout. Pork trimmed of silverskin and cut into medallions; shallot and garlic minced; mushrooms sliced; Parmesan grated.
2. Sear the pork: olive oil and 1 tbsp butter in a wide pan over medium-high, medallions in one layer, untouched 2-3 minutes per side until deeply golden (130 F inside — they finish at serving). Out.
3. Mushrooms in the drippings in one layer, untouched 3-4 minutes until deeply browned; shallot and half the garlic 1 minute.
4. Risotto in the same pan: rice stirred 2 minutes until translucent at the edges; wine in, absorbed; then stock a ladle at a time, stirring often, 18-20 minutes to al dente and flowing. Thyme through.
5. Off the heat: the cold butter and Parmesan beaten in until glossy (the mantecatura); the pork and its juices laid over for 2 minutes to warm through.
6. More Parmesan at the table.

Common mistakes:
- Pork cooked to 165 in the sear: dry medallions in a creamy risotto. Pull at 130-135 and let the risotto's heat finish them.
- Mushrooms crowded: they steam. One layer, untouched.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Thyme Brown Butter — in a small pan, melt 3 tbsp butter over medium heat until amber and nutty; add 1 tsp fresh thyme leaves, sizzle 20 seconds. Spoon over the pork on each bowl — brown butter and pork tenderloin are old friends.

Title: Garlic Salmon Pasta Primavera
Ingredients:
- 2 lb salmon fillets (about 1 1/2 inches thick), cut into 6 portions, skin removed
- 1 lb fettuccine or linguine
- 3 tbsp olive oil, divided
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 6 cloves garlic, thinly sliced
- 1/2 cup dry white wine
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice (about 1 lemon)
- 12 oz cherry tomatoes, halved
- 8 oz asparagus, tough ends snapped off, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
- 1 medium zucchini, halved lengthwise and sliced into half-moons
- 1 cup frozen peas
- 1/2 cup freshly grated Parmesan, plus more for serving
- 1/4 cup chopped fresh basil or parsley
- 1 1/2 tsp kosher salt, plus more for the pasta water

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/3 cup dry white wine
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
- 1 tsp lemon juice
- Pinch of kosher salt
Steps:
1. Pasta water on, salted like the sea. Salmon in portions, patted very dry and seasoned. Garlic sliced into coins, tomatoes halved, asparagus and zucchini cut, basil chopped, Parmesan grated.
2. Sear the salmon: 2 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high, salmon down untouched 4-5 minutes until a crust forms; flip 1-2 minutes to silky, 125 F. Out.
3. Fettuccine 1 minute shy of done; peas in for the last minute; reserve a cup of pasta water.
4. Vegetables in the salmon drippings with the butter: asparagus 2 minutes, zucchini 2 minutes until golden at the edges; garlic coins 30 seconds; tomatoes in until they slump, 2 minutes. Wine in, scraping, simmered 1 minute.
5. Pasta into the pan with splashes of pasta water, tossed until glossy. Lemon juice off the heat. Salmon laid over in its portions (or flaked in large pieces — both are done).
6. Basil and Parmesan over.

Common mistakes:
- The salmon cooked in the sauce: it overcooks and breaks. Sear, rest, lay over.
- Garlic mince instead of coins: it burns while the vegetables cook. Coins toast gently.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): White Wine Butter Sauce — in a small pan, simmer 1/3 cup dry white wine until reduced by half; off the heat, whisk in 3 tbsp cold butter a cube at a time until glossy, then 1 tsp lemon juice and a pinch of salt. Spoon over the salmon — a simple beurre blanc that makes primavera feel like a bistro dish.

Title: Garlic Shrimp & Tomato Rice
Ingredients:
- 2 lb large shell-on shrimp
- 2 1/2 cups long-grain white rice
- 1/4 cup olive oil
- 1 large yellow onion, diced
- 8 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- 2 medium ripe tomatoes, diced
- 1 (28-oz) can crushed tomatoes
- 1/2 cup dry white wine
- 2 bay leaves
- 1 tsp sweet paprika
- 1/2 tsp piri-piri or red pepper flakes
- 1 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
- 1/4 cup chopped fresh cilantro

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1/2 tsp piri-piri (or red chile flakes)
- 1 clove garlic, thinly sliced
- Squeeze of lemon juice
Steps:
1. Shell stock — the dish's secret: shells and heads simmered in 4 cups water 15 minutes, strained. (Fifteen minutes of shells is worth more than any seasoning in this recipe.) Shrimp peeled and dried; onion, the pepper and tomatoes diced; garlic minced.
2. Refogado: olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat, onion and the pepper 8-10 minutes until soft and sweet; garlic and paprika 1 minute; the fresh tomatoes 5 minutes until they break down.
3. Rice in, stirred 2 minutes to toast in the refogado. Crushed tomatoes, 3 cups of the shell stock and the wine in; bay in. Bare simmer 15 minutes, covered.
4. Shrimp laid over the rice for the last 4-5 minutes, lid on, until just pink — they steam in the tomato rice's perfume.
5. Piri-piri (or chile flakes) to taste, salt checked. Cilantro over. The rice should be loose and brothy — arroz de camarão is a wet rice, almost a soup; add stock if it tightens.

Common mistakes:
- Throwing the shells away: you threw away the dish. Fifteen minutes of simmering is the whole depth.
- Shrimp in from the start: rubber in tomato sauce. Last 5 minutes, steamed on top.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Piri-Piri Butter — in a small pan, melt 3 tbsp butter over medium heat; add 1/2 tsp piri-piri (or chile flakes) and 1 sliced garlic clove, sizzle 30 seconds. Off the heat, a squeeze of lemon. Spoon over the shrimp and rice — hot butter over shellfish rice, Lisbon-style.

Title: Garlic Shrimp Bibimbap Bowls
Ingredients:
For the shrimp:
- 1 1/2 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp toasted sesame oil
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp sugar

For the vegetables (namul):
- 10 oz baby spinach
- 12 oz bean sprouts
- 2 medium carrots, julienned (cut into thin matchsticks)
- 1 medium zucchini, julienned
- 6 oz shiitake mushrooms, sliced
- 3 tbsp toasted sesame oil, divided
- 2 tsp kosher salt, divided
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds

For the gochujang sauce:
- 6 tbsp gochujang (Korean chili paste)
- 2 tbsp sugar
- 2 tbsp rice vinegar
- 1 tbsp toasted sesame oil
- 2 tbsp water
- 1 clove garlic, grated

For assembly:
- 2 cups short-grain white rice (makes about 6 cups cooked)
- 6 large eggs
- 2 tbsp vegetable oil

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp gochujang (Korean chili paste)
- 1 tbsp honey
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp toasted sesame oil
Steps:
1. Rice on (short-grain; boil, cover, lowest heat 15, rest 10). Gochujang sauce whisked. Shrimp marinated 10 minutes in the soy, sesame oil, garlic and sugar. Each namul prepped separately: spinach, sprouts, carrots, zucchini, shiitakes.
2. Namul, one at a time in a lightly oiled skillet (with avocado oil): spinach wilted 1 minute; sprouts blanched 1 minute and drained dry; carrots 2 minutes; zucchini 2 minutes; shiitakes 4-5 minutes until deeply browned. Each seasoned with sesame oil, salt and garlic as it comes out, piled separately.
3. Sear the shrimp: the skillet at high heat, shrimp in one layer, 90 seconds a side until charred at the edges and just pink.
4. Eggs fried with lacy edges and runny yolks — the yolk is a second sauce.
5. Bowls: rice, the namul in wedges, shrimp in the center, egg on top, sesame seeds over. Gochujang sauce at the table; mix violently before eating.

Common mistakes:
- All the vegetables in one pan: a brown pile instead of a rainbow. Separately, in piles.
- Wet sprouts: they flood the rice. Drained and squeezed.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Gochujang-Sesame Glaze — in a small pan, simmer 2 tbsp gochujang, 1 tbsp honey, 1 tbsp soy sauce and 1 tsp toasted sesame oil for 1-2 minutes until glossy. Spoon over the shrimp in each bowl — a second, hotter layer over the table sauce.

Title: Garlic Shrimp Chimichurri Couscous
Ingredients:
- 1½ lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined (tails on or off)

For the chimichurri:
- 1 cup packed fresh flat-leaf parsley leaves (about 1 large bunch)
- 6 large garlic cloves, minced
- 1 tbsp dried oregano
- 1 tsp crushed red pepper flakes
- 1/3 cup red wine vinegar
- 1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil
- 1 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste — taste before serving and add up to 1/2 tsp more

For the couscous and shrimp:
- 2¼ cups dry couscous (about 13 oz)
- 2¼ cups water or chicken broth
- 2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, divided
- 6 large garlic cloves, thinly sliced
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice (about 1 lemon), plus wedges for serving
- 1/2 tsp kosher salt
- 1/4 tsp freshly ground black pepper

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 clove garlic, thinly sliced
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
Steps:
1. Chimichurri by hand (a processor turns it pesto): parsley and garlic chopped fine, folded with the oregano, chile flakes, vinegar, olive oil and salt; rested 15 minutes minimum so the flavors marry. Couscous ready: boiling water or broth over, covered 5 minutes, fluffed with the lemon juice and a drizzle of olive oil.
2. Shrimp patted very dry and seasoned with the salt, pepper and cumin.
3. Sear hard: 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over high heat until smoking, shrimp in one layer, untouched 90 seconds until charred at the edges; flip 30-60 seconds. Out immediately.
4. Garlic coins in the drippings 30 seconds until pale gold; the pan off the heat, shrimp back for 15 seconds to coat in the garlic oil.
5. Couscous in bowls, shrimp over, chimichurri spooned generously across — it should pool a little. Lemon wedges alongside.

Common mistakes:
- Blended chimichurri: bruised and dull. Hand-chopped, rested, bright.
- Shrimp past pink: they cook in the pan's carryover. Pull them a breath early.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Garlic-Lemon Butter — in a small pan, melt 2 tbsp butter over medium heat; add 1 sliced garlic clove, sizzle 30 seconds; off the heat, 1 tbsp lemon juice. Spoon over the shrimp before the chimichurri — butter under the sharp herbs is a beautiful layering.

Title: Garlic Shrimp Couscous
Ingredients:
- 1½ lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 2½ cups dry couscous
- 2½ cups hot chicken broth
- 3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, divided
- 1 large yellow onion, diced
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- 4 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 large tomato, diced
- 1½ tsp ground cumin
- 1½ tsp sweet paprika
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon
- Big pinch of saffron threads (optional)
- 1 cup frozen peas
- 1/4 cup chopped fresh parsley
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice (about 1 lemon)
- 1 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste — taste before serving and add up to 1/2 tsp more

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1/2 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
Steps:
1. Couscous: hot broth over, covered 5 minutes, fluffed with a fork and a drizzle of olive oil. Onion and the pepper diced (a poblano swaps in for warmth), tomato diced, garlic minced, spices in one bowl (cumin, paprika, turmeric, cinnamon, saffron).
2. Base: 2 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat, onion and the pepper 6-8 minutes until soft and golden at the edges; garlic and the spice mix 1 minute until the pan smells like a Marrakech spice stall.
3. Tomato in, simmered 3 minutes until it melts into a light sauce. Peas through for 1 minute.
4. Shrimp seasoned, in one layer over the base, 2 minutes a side until just pink and curled — they finish in the sauce's heat.
5. Couscous folded through (or the shrimp and sauce spooned over couscous in bowls). Lemon juice over, parsley scattered.

Common mistakes:
- Spices added with the shrimp: they taste raw. Bloomed in the oil with the onion, they perfume everything.
- Shrimp simmered: 2 minutes a side, then the pan's heat does the rest.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Cumin-Lemon Butter — in a small pan, melt 3 tbsp butter over medium heat; add 1/2 tsp ground cumin and sizzle 20 seconds. Off the heat: 1 tbsp lemon juice. Spoon over the shrimp and couscous — spiced butter is the Moroccan finish the dish is quietly asking for.

Title: Garlic Shrimp Paella
Ingredients:
- 1½ lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 2½ cups short-grain paella rice (bomba or arborio)
- 5 cups fish or seafood stock
- 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil
- 1 large yellow onion, finely diced
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- 6 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 cup grated fresh tomato (about 2 large tomatoes, grated on a box grater)
- 2 tsp sweet smoked paprika
- 1/2 tsp saffron threads
- 1 cup frozen peas
- 1/2 cup dry white wine
- 2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
- Lemon wedges and chopped fresh parsley, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1/2 tsp smoked paprika
- Squeeze of lemon juice
Steps:
1. Stock warmed with the saffron crumbled in (15 minutes to bloom golden). Onion diced fine, the pepper diced (a poblano stands in), garlic minced, tomatoes grated to a pulp, skins discarded.
2. Sofrito: olive oil in the widest pan you have, onion and the pepper 8-10 minutes slow until completely soft and sweet; garlic and smoked paprika 30 seconds; the grated tomato in, cooked 6-8 minutes until dark, thick and sweet — this is the paella's soul.
3. Rice in, stirred 1 minute to coat. The saffron stock and wine poured over evenly. DO NOT STIR from here. Bare simmer 16-18 minutes, rotating the pan once.
4. Shrimp pressed lightly into the rice for the last 5-6 minutes; peas scattered over. Then the socarrat: heat up 60-90 seconds until the bottom crackles and smells toasty.
5. Rest 5 minutes covered with a cloth. Lemon wedges and parsley at the table.

Common mistakes:
- Stirring: risotto, not paella, and no socarrat. Hands off.
- Shrimp from the start: rubber by the time the rice is done. Last 5 minutes.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Smoked Paprika and Lemon Butter — in a small pan, melt 3 tbsp butter over medium heat; add 1/2 tsp smoked paprika, sizzle 20 seconds until brick red. Off the heat, a squeeze of lemon. Spoon lightly over the paella — a buttery gloss that loves the socarrat.

Title: Garlic Shrimp Rice Bowls
Ingredients:
- 1½ lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined, tails on (shell-on, deveined shrimp are the most authentic shrimp-truck style; peeled is easier to eat)
- 3 tbsp rice flour (or mochiko)
- 1 tbsp cornstarch
- 1 tbsp paprika
- 2 tsp kosher salt
- 1/2 tsp cayenne pepper (optional, for heat)
- 1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 6 tbsp unsalted butter
- 2 tbsp olive oil, divided
- 1/3 cup minced garlic (about 12 cloves)
- 1 lemon, cut into wedges
- 4 green onions, thinly sliced
- 2½ cups dry long-grain white rice (about 7½ cups cooked), cooked and kept hot

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- 2 tbsp minced garlic
Steps:
1. Rice on first (rinsed; boil, cover, lowest heat 15, rest 10, fluffed and kept hot). Garlic minced — a full 1/3 cup; this is a garlic dish with shrimp in it, not the reverse. Green onions sliced.
2. Dredge: shrimp patted dry, tossed in the rice flour, cornstarch, paprika, salt, cayenne and pepper until coated. The rice flour is the North Shore truck secret — it fries shatter-crisp.
3. Fry: butter and olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high until foaming; shrimp in one layer, untouched 2 minutes until golden-crisp; flip 1-2 minutes. Out.
4. The garlic butter: heat down, the remaining butter in, the garlic stirred 1-2 minutes until golden and fragrant — watch it; garlic goes from gold to bitter in seconds.
5. Shrimp back for 30 seconds, tossed in the garlic butter until every piece is glossy. Over the hot rice, green onions over, lemon wedges at the table, the pan butter spooned around — every drop.

Common mistakes:
- Garlic in with the shrimp from the start: it burns while they crisp. Shrimp first, garlic butter second.
- Wheat flour instead of rice flour: good, not great. The rice flour crunch is the truck's signature.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Crispy Garlic Butter — in a small pan, melt 3 tbsp butter over medium heat; add 2 tbsp minced garlic and fry 1-2 minutes, stirring, until the garlic crisps gold. Spoon over the shrimp and rice — a double measure of the dish's whole reason to exist.

Title: Garlic Shrimp Yakimeshi
Ingredients:
- 1¼ lb medium shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 6 cups cooked day-old short-grain white rice (from about 2½ cups dry), chilled
- 3 large eggs, beaten
- 3 tbsp neutral oil (canola or vegetable), divided
- 1 tsp toasted sesame oil
- 3 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp mirin
- 1 tbsp sake
- 6 garlic cloves, thinly sliced
- 1 tbsp grated fresh ginger
- 4 green onions, thinly sliced (whites and greens separated)
- 1/2 cup frozen peas
- 1 tsp kosher salt
- 1/2 tsp white pepper

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
Steps:
1. Rice must be day-old and cold — non-negotiable (spread fresh rice on a tray in the fridge an hour if you forgot). Garlic sliced into coins, ginger grated, green onions separated into whites and greens, eggs beaten, shrimp patted dry.
2. Eggs: 1 tbsp avocado oil in a wok over medium-high, eggs scrambled to soft ribbons in 30 seconds. Out.
3. Shrimp: remaining oil, shrimp in one layer, 90 seconds until just pink with seared edges. Out.
4. Garlic coins and ginger in the wok 20 seconds until fragrant (coins, so they toast without burning). The cold rice in, spread flat 60 seconds to crisp; toss; peas through.
5. Soy, mirin and sake around the wok's edge; toss hard 1-2 minutes. Shrimp and eggs back; sesame oil and green onion greens off the heat; white pepper over.

Common mistakes:
- Warm fresh rice: mush. Cold and day-old, or the tray trick.
- Garlic mince: it burns in a screaming wok. Coins.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Garlic Butter Soy Sauce — in a small pan, melt 2 tbsp butter; add 1 tbsp soy sauce and swirl 30 seconds until combined and glossy. Spoon over the yakimeshi — butter in fried rice sounds wrong until the first bite.

Title: Ginger Beef & Edamame Rice
Ingredients:
- 1¼ lb flank steak
- 2 cups frozen shelled edamame, thawed
- 2½ cups dry short-grain white rice

For the ginger marinade:
- 3 tbsp soy sauce
- 2 tbsp mirin
- 2 tbsp sake
- 2 tbsp grated fresh ginger (about a 2-inch piece)
- 3 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 tbsp brown sugar

To finish:
- 1 tbsp neutral oil (canola or vegetable)
- 1 tsp toasted sesame oil
- 4 green onions, thinly sliced
- 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp mirin
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 tsp brown sugar
Steps:
1. Rice on (rinsed short-grain; boil, cover, lowest heat 15, rest 10). Beef sliced thin against the grain; marinade whisked (soy, mirin, sake, ginger, garlic, brown sugar); beef in for 15-30 minutes. Edamame thawed.
2. Sear the beef in two batches: the avocado oil (in place of the neutral oil) in a wok over high heat until smoking, beef lifted from the marinade and in one layer, untouched 90 seconds until charred at the edges; toss 1 minute. The marinade's sugars caramelize fast — watch the second batch.
3. Edamame in for 1-2 minutes until hot and lightly blistered.
4. A spoonful of the marinade in to gloss everything for 30 seconds. Sesame oil off the heat.
5. Over the rice; green onions and sesame seeds over.

Common mistakes:
- Crowding: the marinade floods the wok and the beef boils. Batches.
- Marinade in early: it burns before the beef cooks. A spoonful at the end.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Extra Ginger-Soy Glaze — in a small pan, simmer 3 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp mirin, 1 tsp grated ginger and 1 tsp brown sugar for 2-3 minutes until syrupy. Spoon over the beef bowls — the marinade's best self.

Title: Ginger Chicken & Bok Choy Rice
Ingredients:
- 1½ lb boneless, skinless chicken breasts
- 1½ lb baby bok choy
- 2½ cups dry jasmine rice
- 6 cups chicken broth
- 1/4 cup sliced fresh ginger (about a 3-inch piece, cut into coins)
- 6 scallions, cut into 3-inch pieces, plus more sliced for garnish

For the ginger-scallion oil:
- 1/2 cup neutral oil (canola or vegetable)
- 6 scallions, finely minced
- 3 tbsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 tsp kosher salt
- 1 tsp sugar
- 1 tsp rice vinegar

To serve:
- 1 cucumber, thinly sliced
- Soy sauce (optional)

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp avocado oil
- 1 tsp toasted sesame oil
- 1 tsp red chile flakes
Steps:
1. Poach the chicken and cook the rice in its broth, Hainanese-style: chicken breasts into the broth with the ginger coins and scallion lengths at a bare simmer, 16-18 minutes to 165 F — never boiled. Lift out; the rice cooked in that same broth (rinsed jasmine, broth measured to the rice's ratio), covered, lowest heat 15, rest 10. Bok choy blanched 2 minutes in the broth at the end.
2. Slice the chicken into thick, juicy slabs.
3. Ginger-scallion oil — made with avocado oil in place of the neutral oil: the minced scallions, grated ginger, salt and sugar in a heatproof bowl; the oil heated until shimmering and poured over — it sizzles and turns jade-green and fragrant. The rice vinegar stirred in. This oil is the dish's crown; make it generously.
4. Serve: the broth-kissed rice, chicken over, bok choy alongside, cucumber slices, and the ginger-scallion oil spooned over everything. Soy at the table for those who want it.

Common mistakes:
- Boiling the chicken: poached silk or nothing. Bare simmer.
- Cold oil for the sauce: it must shimmer so the scallions bloom. Pour, sizzle, stir.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Sesame-Chile Oil — in a small pan, heat 2 tbsp avocado oil until shimmering; off the heat, stir in 1 tsp toasted sesame oil and 1 tsp chile flakes; bloom 1 minute. Spoon a little over the chicken alongside the ginger-scallion oil — Singapore's stalls keep a chile sauce by the plate for exactly this.

Title: Ginger Pork Donburi
Ingredients:
- 1¼ lb pork tenderloin
- 2½ cups dry short-grain white rice

For the donburi sauce:
- 2 cups water
- 2 tsp instant dashi granules
- 1/4 cup soy sauce
- 3 tbsp mirin
- 2 tbsp sake
- 2 tbsp sugar
- 2 tbsp grated fresh ginger

For the topping:
- 1 large yellow onion, thinly sliced
- 4 large eggs, lightly beaten
- 1 tbsp neutral oil (canola or vegetable)
- 2 green onions, thinly sliced
- 1 tsp toasted sesame seeds
- Beni shoga (pickled red ginger), optional, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/4 cup donburi sauce mix (water, dashi, soy, mirin, sake, sugar and ginger in the recipe's proportions)
Steps:
1. Rice on (rinsed short-grain; boil, cover, lowest heat 15, rest 10). Pork in medallions, then strips. Donburi sauce simmered together (water, dashi, soy, mirin, sake, sugar, ginger) — taste: sweet-salty with a ginger hum.
2. Sear the pork first: the avocado oil in a large skillet over medium-high, pork in one layer, untouched 2-3 minutes until golden at the edges. (Classic oyako-style donburi simmers raw pork in the sauce; the sear is the upgrade — keep it.)
3. Onion over the pork; the sauce poured in; bare simmer 4-5 minutes until the onion is silky and the pork cooked through.
4. Eggs drizzled over in a spiral; lid on, 1-2 minutes at the lowest heat until just set and glossy — donburi eggs should look like custard, not scramble.
5. Slide a portion over each bowl of rice with plenty of sauce. Green onions, sesame and beni shoga over.

Common mistakes:
- Eggs cooked hard: they should barely set, glossy and trembling. Lid on, low heat, watch.
- Raw-simmered pork: fine, but the sear is what makes this taste like a restaurant don. Two minutes well spent.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Extra Donburi Glaze — in a small pan, simmer 1/4 cup of the donburi sauce (dashi, soy, mirin, sake, sugar, ginger — mixed fresh in the same proportions) for 2-3 minutes until slightly syrupy. Spoon over the bowls for a glossier, sweeter finish.

Title: Gochujang Beef Bowls
Ingredients:
- 1¼ lb 93% lean ground beef
- 2½ cups dry jasmine rice

For the gochujang sauce:
- 1/4 cup gochujang (Korean fermented chili paste)
- 3 tbsp soy sauce
- 2 tbsp honey
- 1 tbsp brown sugar
- 1 tbsp rice vinegar
- 2 tsp toasted sesame oil
- 4 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 tbsp grated fresh ginger

For the bowls:
- 1 tbsp neutral oil (canola or vegetable)
- 1 cup shredded carrots
- 1 cucumber, thinly sliced
- 6 large eggs
- 4 green onions, thinly sliced
- 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp gochujang (Korean chili paste)
- 1 tbsp honey
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp toasted sesame oil
Steps:
1. Rice on (rinsed jasmine; boil, cover, lowest heat 15, rest 10). Sauce whisked (gochujang, soy, honey, brown sugar, vinegar, sesame oil, garlic, ginger). Carrots shredded, cucumber sliced, eggs ready.
2. Brown the beef hard: the avocado oil in a large skillet over medium-high, beef in one layer, untouched 4 minutes until a dark crust forms; break into crumbles and finish, crisp at the edges. Drain the fat.
3. Sauce in, simmered 2-3 minutes, stirring, until it thickens and lacquers the beef.
4. Eggs fried separately with lacy edges and runny yolks.
5. Bowls: rice, beef, carrots, cucumber, the fried egg on top, green onions and sesame over. Extra sauce at the table for the mix.

Common mistakes:
- Steamed beef: one layer and patience. The crust plus the glaze is the whole dish.
- Sauce reduced to tar: 2-3 minutes to glossy, no further.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Sesame-Gochujang Glaze — in a small pan, simmer 2 tbsp gochujang, 1 tbsp honey, 1 tbsp soy sauce and 1 tsp toasted sesame oil for 1-2 minutes until glossy. Spoon over the beef bowls for a second lacquer.

Title: Gochujang Salmon Rice Bowls
Ingredients:
- 1½ lb salmon fillet, skin removed, cut into 6 portions
- 2½ cups dry jasmine rice

For the gochujang glaze:
- 1/4 cup gochujang (Korean fermented chili paste)
- 2 tbsp honey
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp toasted sesame oil
- 1 tbsp rice vinegar
- 3 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 tbsp grated fresh ginger

For the bowls:
- 1 tbsp neutral oil (canola or vegetable)
- 1 ripe avocado, sliced
- 1 cucumber, thinly sliced
- 4 green onions, thinly sliced
- 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds
- Lime wedges

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 tbsp gochujang (Korean chili paste)
- 1 tsp honey
Steps:
1. Rice on (rinsed jasmine; boil, cover, lowest heat 15, rest 10). Glaze whisked (gochujang, honey, soy, sesame oil, vinegar, garlic, ginger); 3 tbsp set aside clean for serving. Salmon in portions, patted dry.
2. Sear the salmon: the avocado oil in a skillet over medium-high, salmon down untouched 4-5 minutes until a crust forms and the flesh turns opaque halfway up.
3. Flip; brush the glaze generously over the top; 1-2 minutes more until the glaze caramelizes and the center is silky, 125 F. Watch it — honey and gochujang sugars go from lacquer to burn in a breath.
4. Bowls: rice, salmon, avocado slices, cucumber, green onions and sesame over. The reserved clean glaze drizzled; lime wedges alongside.
