Common mistakes:
- Glazing from the start: burned sugars, raw center. Glaze after the flip.
- Using the marinade-side glaze for serving: the reserved 3 tbsp is the serving sauce. Keep them separate.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Gochujang Butter — in a small pan, melt 2 tbsp butter over medium heat; whisk in 1 tbsp gochujang and 1 tsp honey until glossy and brick red, 30 seconds. Spoon over the salmon — Korean heat with a French finish, and it loves salmon fat.

Title: Grilled Steak with Tomato Chimichurri Rice
Ingredients:
- 2 1/2 lb sirloin steak, about 1 1/2 inches thick
- 1 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
- 1/2 tsp black pepper
- 1 tbsp olive oil (for the grill)

For the tomato rice:
- 2 1/2 cups long-grain white rice
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 small yellow onion, finely diced
- 2 tbsp tomato paste
- 3 3/4 cups chicken broth
- 1 tsp kosher salt

For the tomato chimichurri:
- 1 pint cherry tomatoes (about 12 oz)
- 1 1/2 cups packed fresh flat-leaf parsley leaves (about 2 bunches)
- 4 garlic cloves, minced
- 2 tsp dried oregano
- 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes
- 3 tbsp red wine vinegar
- 1/3 cup extra-virgin olive oil
- 1 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste - taste the sauce before serving and add up to 1/2 tsp more

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- 2 tbsp tomato chimichurri (from the recipe)
Steps:
1. Tomato rice: olive oil in a pot, the onion 5-6 minutes until golden; tomato paste 2 minutes until darkened; rice stirred in and toasted 2 minutes; broth and salt in; boil, cover, lowest heat 15, rest 10, fluff.
2. Steak out 30 minutes ahead, patted completely dry, salted and peppered generously.
3. Tomato chimichurri: tomatoes diced, parsley and garlic chopped fine by hand; folded with the oregano, chile flakes, vinegar, olive oil and salt; rested 15 minutes so the tomatoes juice into the herbs.
4. Grill or sear the steak at maximum heat: 5-6 minutes a side for medium-rare (130 F), a deep crust all over. Rest a full 10 minutes.
5. Slice against the grain; serve over the tomato rice with the chimichurri and its juices spooned generously across.

Common mistakes:
- Slicing with the grain: chewy ribbons. Across the fibers.
- Untoasted rice: the tomato paste toast is what makes the rice taste cooked-in, not stirred-in.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Chimichurri Butter — in a small pan, melt 3 tbsp butter over medium heat until foaming; off the heat, stir in 2 tbsp of the tomato chimichurri. Spoon over the sliced steak — the chimichurri's brightness, warmed and buttered, over the crust.

Title: Herbes de Provence Chicken & Potatoes
Ingredients:
- 1 whole chicken, about 4 1/2 lb, giblets removed
- 2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
- 1 tsp black pepper

For the herb butter:
- 6 tbsp unsalted butter, softened at room temperature
- 2 tbsp herbes de Provence
- 4 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 tsp lemon zest (about 1 lemon)

- 1 lemon, quartered
- 3 lb Yukon Gold potatoes, cut into 1 1/2-inch chunks
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 4 sprigs fresh thyme (optional)

For the pan sauce (optional):
- About 3/4 cup chicken roasting drippings, fat skimmed
- 1/4 cup dry white wine
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
Steps:
1. Chicken out 45 minutes ahead, patted VERY dry inside and out — dry skin is crisp skin. Herb butter mashed (softened butter, herbes de Provence, garlic, lemon zest). Potatoes in 1 1/2-inch chunks, oiled and salted.
2. Oven at 425 F. Butter worked under the chicken's skin and over it; salt and pepper everywhere; the lemon quarters in the cavity; legs tied if you like.
3. Potatoes in a roasting pan as the chicken's bed (they baste in the drippings — the Provençal way), chicken on top, thyme sprigs scattered.
4. Roast 50-60 minutes, rotating the pan once, until the skin is deep golden and crisp and the thigh hits 165 F at the joint. If the skin races ahead, tent loosely with foil for the last stretch.
5. Rest a full 15 minutes — a rested roast carves juicy; a rushed one bleeds onto the board. Carve over the potatoes so the juices land where they belong.

Common mistakes:
- Wet skin: it steams pale in its own juices. Towels, thoroughly, and the 45-minute air rest helps.
- Carving immediately: 15 minutes of rest is the difference between juicy slices and a puddle.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Provençal Pan Jus — tip the roasting pan and pour the drippings into a small saucepan (about 3/4 cup; skim the fat). Add 1/4 cup dry white wine; boil 3 minutes. Off the heat, whisk in 2 tbsp cold butter until glossy. Spoon over the carved chicken and potatoes — the roast's own juices, finished like a sauce.

Title: Korean Beef & Potato Bowls
Ingredients:
- 3 cups long-grain white rice (for serving)
- 2 lb Yukon Gold or russet potatoes, peeled and cut into 1-inch cubes
- 1 lb ground beef (90% lean)
- 4 green onions, thinly sliced (white and green parts separated)
- 6 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 jalapeño, thinly sliced (optional, for heat)
- 1/2 cup soy sauce
- 3 tbsp sugar
- 1 tbsp toasted sesame oil
- 1 1/2 cups water
- 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/4 cup soy sauce
- 1 tbsp sugar
- 1 tsp toasted sesame oil
Steps:
1. Rice on. Potatoes in 1-inch cubes; garlic minced; green onions separated (whites and greens); jalapeño sliced.
2. Potatoes first: simmered in salted water 10-12 minutes until just tender; drained. (They finish in the sauce — par-cooking keeps them from drinking it all.)
3. Brown the beef hard: a large skillet over medium-high (a film of avocado oil if your beef is lean), beef in one layer, untouched 4 minutes for a dark crust; break up and finish. Green onion whites and garlic in for 1 minute.
4. Soy, sugar, sesame oil and water in; the potatoes folded through; simmer 5-6 minutes until the sauce glosses the potatoes and reduces slightly.
5. Jalapeño and green onion greens over; sesame seeds scattered. Serve over the rice with the pan sauce spooned around.

Common mistakes:
- Raw potatoes into the sauce: they drink it dry before they tenderize. Par-cook first.
- Gray beef: the crust is the dish's depth against the sweet soy.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Extra Soy-Sesame Glaze — in a small pan, simmer 1/4 cup soy sauce, 1 tbsp sugar and 1 tsp toasted sesame oil for 2-3 minutes until syrupy. Spoon over the bowls — the gamja jorim glaze, concentrated.

Title: Lemon Chicken Couscous Bowls
Ingredients:
- 2 1/2 lb boneless, skinless chicken thighs
- 2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
- 1 tsp black pepper
- 2 tbsp olive oil

For the tagine:
- 1 large yellow onion, thinly sliced
- 4 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 tbsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- 1 1/2 cups chicken broth
- 1 large preserved lemon, pulp removed and rind thinly sliced (about 2 oz; find them in the Middle Eastern aisle, or substitute 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice plus 1 tsp zest)
- 3/4 cup pitted green olives (such as Castelvetrano)
- 1/2 cup chopped fresh cilantro, plus more for serving
- 1/4 cup chopped fresh parsley

For the couscous:
- 2 1/2 cups dry couscous
- 2 1/2 cups boiling water or chicken broth
- 2 tbsp olive oil or butter
- 1 tsp kosher salt

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1/2 cup tagine braising liquid (from the recipe)
- 1 tbsp finely sliced preserved lemon rind
Steps:
1. Couscous at the end: boiling water or broth over, covered 5 minutes, fluffed with the olive oil (or butter) and salt. Chicken patted dry and seasoned; onion sliced thin; preserved lemon rind in strips (pulp scooped out and discarded).
2. Sear the thighs: olive oil in a Dutch oven or tagine over medium-high, chicken in one layer, untouched 4-5 minutes until deeply golden; flip 3 minutes. Out.
3. Onion into the drippings 8-10 minutes until soft, sweet and golden; garlic, ginger, turmeric, cumin, cinnamon and cayenne 1 minute until the pot smells like a Marrakech evening.
4. Broth in, scraping; chicken back; bare simmer 20-25 minutes until tender. Preserved lemon and olives in for the last 5 minutes (they are seasoning, not vegetables — they need only to warm and perfume).
5. Cilantro and parsley over. Serve over the couscous with the braising juices spooned around.

Common mistakes:
- Preserved lemon from the start: its funk dominates after a long braise. Last 5 minutes.
- Pale chicken: the sear's fond is half the tagine's depth.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Preserved Lemon Butter Sauce — in a small pan, melt 2 tbsp butter over medium heat; add 1/2 cup of the tagine's braising liquid and 1 tbsp finely sliced preserved lemon rind; simmer 2 minutes. Spoon over the chicken — the tagine's perfume, buttered and brightened.

Title: Lemon Garlic Salmon Risotto
Ingredients:
- 1 1/2 lb salmon fillet, skin on, cut into 6 portions
- 1 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
- 1/2 tsp black pepper
- 2 tbsp olive oil

For the risotto:
- 6 to 7 cups chicken broth, kept hot
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 medium yellow onion, finely diced
- 4 garlic cloves, minced
- 2 cups arborio rice (do not rinse)
- 1/2 cup dry white wine (such as Pinot Grigio)
- 1 tbsp lemon zest (about 2 lemons)
- 3 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 4 tbsp cold unsalted butter, cubed
- 3/4 cup grated Parmesan, plus more for serving
- 1/4 cup chopped fresh parsley

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/3 cup dry white wine
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
- 1 tsp lemon juice
Steps:
1. Broth at a bare simmer the whole time. Onion diced fine, garlic minced, lemons zested and juiced, cold butter cubed, Parmesan grated. Salmon patted dry and seasoned.
2. Sear the salmon: olive oil in a skillet over medium-high, salmon skin-side down untouched 5-6 minutes until the skin crisps and the flesh turns opaque two-thirds up; flip 60 seconds. Out — silky centers, 125 F.
3. Risotto: olive oil in a wide pot, onion 5-6 minutes until soft and sweet; garlic 30 seconds; rice stirred 2 minutes until translucent at the edges. Wine in, absorbed.
4. Broth a ladle at a time, stirring often, 18-20 minutes to al dente and flowing.
5. Off the heat: lemon zest and juice, the cold butter and Parmesan beaten in until glossy. It should ripple.
6. Risotto in warm bowls, salmon laid over, parsley scattered.

Common mistakes:
- Lemon juice cooked in the risotto: it dulls. Zest and juice at the end, off the heat.
- Salmon flipped early: the skin sticks and tears. It releases when crisp.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): White Wine and Lemon Pan Sauce — in the salmon skillet over medium heat, add 1/3 cup dry white wine; scrape up the fond and reduce by half. Off the heat, whisk in 2 tbsp cold butter and 1 tsp lemon juice. Spoon around the salmon on each bowl — the bistro finish.

Title: Lemon Salmon & Olive Potatoes
Ingredients:
- 3 lb Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and cut into wedges
- 1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil
- 1/2 cup fresh lemon juice (about 3 lemons)
- 1 cup water or chicken broth
- 4 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 tbsp dried oregano, plus more for serving
- 2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
- 1 tsp black pepper
- 1 cup Kalamata olives, pitted
- 2 lb salmon fillet, cut into 6 portions
- Lemon wedges and chopped fresh parsley, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/2 cup lemon roasting liquid (from the recipe's pan)
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
- Pinch of dried oregano
Steps:
1. Oven at 400 F. Potato wedges in the roasting pan with the olive oil, lemon juice, water, garlic, oregano, salt and pepper tossed through — this lemony bath is the Greek way (the potatoes cook IN the sauce, not beside it).
2. Roast the potatoes 40-45 minutes, turning once, until tender, golden at the edges, and the liquid has reduced to a glossy lemon-oil sauce in the pan.
3. Olives scattered over for the last 10 minutes.
4. Salmon laid on top of the potatoes for the final 10-12 minutes: it roasts gently in the lemony steam and comes out silky. (For crisper skin, sear it separately skin-down in a skillet 5 minutes and lay it over at serving — both are done in Greece.)
5. Lemon wedges and parsley at the table. Spoon the pan's lemon sauce over everything — do not leave it in the pan.

Common mistakes:
- Skimpy liquid: the potatoes need the bath to turn creamy inside. The full measure.
- Salmon in from the start: chalky fish on perfect potatoes. Last 10-12 minutes.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Lemon-Oregano Pan Butter — spoon 1/2 cup of the roasting pan's lemon liquid into a small saucepan; boil 2 minutes. Off the heat, whisk in 2 tbsp cold butter and a pinch of dried oregano. Spoon over the salmon and potatoes — the Greek lemon sauce, finished with butter.

Title: Lemongrass Chicken Rice Bowls
Ingredients:
- 3 cups jasmine rice (for serving)
- 2 1/2 lb boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces

For the marinade:
- 4 stalks lemongrass, tough outer layers removed, finely minced (about 1/2 cup)
- 4 garlic cloves, minced
- 2 Thai bird chiles, thinly sliced (or 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes)
- 3 tbsp fish sauce
- 2 tbsp sugar
- 1 tbsp neutral oil (such as avocado oil)

For the bowls:
- 3 tbsp neutral oil, divided
- 1/2 cup water
- 1 cucumber, thinly sliced
- 1/2 cup fresh cilantro leaves
- 4 green onions, thinly sliced
- Lime wedges, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp fish sauce
- 2 tbsp sugar
- 1 tbsp water
- 1 tsp finely minced lemongrass
- Juice of 1/2 lime
Steps:
1. Marinate (30 minutes to 2 hours): chicken pieces in the lemongrass (tender core only, minced very fine — woody chunks are unpleasant), garlic, bird chiles, fish sauce, sugar and oil. Rice on (jasmine; boil, cover, lowest heat 15, rest 10).
2. Sear in batches: the avocado or neutral oil (avocado preferred) in a wok over high heat, chicken in one layer, untouched 2-3 minutes until the sugars char into caramelized edges; toss to finish. Batches — lemongrass chicken weeps, and a crowded wok stews it.
3. Everything back with the water; simmer 2-3 minutes, scraping, until the pan sauce turns glossy and coats the chicken.
4. Bowls: rice, chicken with its sauce, cucumber slices, cilantro, green onions. Lime wedges at the table.

Common mistakes:
- Woody lemongrass: only the pale tender core, minced fine. The tough outer layers go in the compost, not the chicken.
- One big batch: stewed chicken, no char. Two batches.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Lemongrass Glaze — in a small pan, simmer 3 tbsp fish sauce, 2 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp water and 1 tsp minced lemongrass for 2-3 minutes until syrupy; off the heat, the juice of 1/2 lime. Spoon over the chicken — a caramel-fish-sauce lacquer in the Vietnamese style.

Title: Lemongrass Pork Rice Plates
Ingredients:
- 3 cups jasmine rice (broken rice if you can find it at an Asian market - that is the Saigon original)
- 2 1/2 lb boneless pork chops, about 3/4 inch thick

For the marinade:
- 3 stalks lemongrass, tough outer layers removed, finely minced
- 4 garlic cloves, minced
- 1/4 cup fish sauce
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 1/4 cup sugar
- 2 tbsp neutral oil (such as avocado oil)

For the nuoc cham (dipping sauce):
- 1/4 cup fish sauce
- 1/4 cup water
- 3 tbsp sugar
- 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 garlic clove, minced
- 1 Thai chile, thinly sliced

For the quick pickles:
- 1 cup julienned carrot
- 1 cup julienned daikon radish (or use all carrot)
- 1/2 cup rice vinegar
- 1/2 cup water
- 2 tbsp sugar
- 1 tsp kosher salt

For serving:
- 1/4 cup neutral oil
- 6 green onions, thinly sliced
- 1 cucumber, thinly sliced
- Fresh cilantro sprigs

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp fish sauce
- 2 tbsp sugar
- 2 tbsp water
- Squeeze of lime juice
Steps:
1. Pickles first (30 minutes minimum): carrot and daikon in the vinegar, water, sugar and salt. Nuoc cham whisked (fish sauce, water, sugar, lime, garlic, chile) — sweet, sour, salty, hot, in balance. Rice on (broken rice if you have it — the Saigon original).
2. Marinate the pork (30 minutes to overnight): lemongrass (tender core, minced fine), garlic, fish sauce, soy, sugar and oil.
3. Scallion oil: the neutral oil (avocado) heated in a small pan until shimmering, poured over the sliced green onions with a pinch of salt — they sizzle and turn jade. Set aside.
4. Grill or sear the chops at maximum heat: a cast iron or grill screaming hot, chops down 4-5 minutes a side until deeply charred at the edges and just cooked through (145 F). The sugar in the marinade chars fast — watch the last minutes. Rest 5, slice.
5. Plates: rice, sliced pork, drained pickles, cucumber, cilantro. The scallion oil spooned over the rice and pork; nuoc cham at the table.

Common mistakes:
- Low heat: lemongrass pork wants violent heat and char. Anything less is a pork chop with ideas.
- Skipping the rest: sliced hot, the juices run out onto the board instead of staying in the meat.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Caramel Fish Sauce Glaze — in a small pan, simmer 3 tbsp fish sauce, 2 tbsp sugar and 2 tbsp water for 3-4 minutes until reduced to a dark syrup; off the heat, a squeeze of lime. Brush over the sliced pork — com tam's lacquered shine, doubled.

Title: Miso Butter Cod & Bok Choy
Ingredients:
- 2 1/2 cups jasmine rice (for serving)
- 2 1/2 lb cod fillets, 1 to 1 1/2 inches thick, cut into 6 portions
- 1 tsp kosher salt

For the miso butter glaze:
- 1/3 cup white miso paste
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter, softened
- 2 tbsp mirin (sweet Japanese rice wine)
- 1 tbsp sugar

For the bok choy:
- 2 lb baby bok choy, halved lengthwise
- 1 tbsp neutral oil (such as avocado oil)
- 3 garlic cloves, thinly sliced
- 2 tbsp water
- 1 tsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp toasted sesame seeds (optional)

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 tbsp white miso paste
- 1 tbsp mirin
Steps:
1. Oven at 400 F, pan foil-lined (miso burns onto bare pans). Rice on. Cod patted very dry and salted lightly. Miso butter whisked smooth (miso, softened butter, mirin, sugar). Bok choy halved, garlic sliced.
2. Spread the miso butter thickly over the tops of the cod portions — a full coat, not a glaze.
3. Roast 10-13 minutes until the miso butter caramelizes into deep golden patches and the cod just flakes. No flipping; the bottom steams in its juices while the top lacquers.
4. Bok choy while the cod rests: the avocado oil in a wok over high heat, cut sides down 2 minutes until charred at the edges; garlic in; the water and soy to steam 1 minute until just wilted.
5. Cod over the rice, bok choy alongside, sesame over.

Common mistakes:
- A thin miso coat: it should be a blanket. Thin coats dry; thick coats lacquer.
- Overcooked cod: pull it when it just flakes — carryover finishes it on the plate.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Extra Miso Butter Glaze — in a small pan, melt 1 tbsp butter with 1 tbsp white miso and 1 tbsp mirin over low heat, whisking until glossy (do not boil). Spoon over the cod at serving — a second lacquer for the miso maximalists.

Title: Miso Chicken & Zucchini Rice
Ingredients:
- 3 cups jasmine rice (for serving)
- 2 lb boneless, skinless chicken breasts

For the miso glaze:
- 1/4 cup white miso paste
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter, softened
- 1 tbsp mirin (sweet Japanese rice wine)
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger

- 1 1/2 lb zucchini, halved lengthwise and cut into 1/2-inch half-moons
- 1 tbsp neutral oil (such as avocado oil)
- 1 tsp toasted sesame oil (optional, for finishing)
- 2 green onions, thinly sliced
- 1 tsp toasted sesame seeds

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp white miso paste
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 tbsp mirin
- 1 tbsp water
Steps:
1. Rice on (jasmine; boil, cover, lowest heat 15, rest 10). Miso glaze whisked (miso, softened butter, mirin, soy, ginger). Chicken pounded to even 3/4 inch. Zucchini in half-moons.
2. Sear the chicken: the avocado oil in a skillet over medium-high, chicken down untouched 5 minutes until deeply golden; flip 4-5 minutes to 165 F. Rest 5 minutes.
3. Glaze at the end: the miso glaze brushed thickly over the hot chicken and left 2 minutes off the heat to set into a lacquer (miso burns under direct high heat — it glazes, it does not sear).
4. Zucchini in the chicken drippings over high heat, one layer, untouched 2 minutes until charred at the edges; toss 1 minute to just tender.
5. Chicken sliced, over the rice with the zucchini; sesame oil and seeds over if you like; green onions scattered.

Common mistakes:
- Glaze on raw chicken in a hot pan: scorched miso. Sear first, glaze warm at the end.
- Soggy zucchini: high heat, one layer, brief.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Warm Miso Glaze — in a small pan, whisk 2 tbsp white miso, 1 tbsp butter, 1 tbsp mirin and 1 tbsp water over low heat until glossy and just combined (never boil). Spoon over the sliced chicken — extra lacquer, warm from the pan.

Title: Orange-Ginger Chicken & Broccoli
Ingredients:
- 1 3/4 lb boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces

For the velveting marinade:
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine (or dry sherry)
- 1 tbsp cornstarch
- 1 tbsp water

For the orange-ginger sauce:
- 1 cup fresh orange juice (about 3 large oranges)
- 1 tbsp orange zest (from 1 large orange)
- 1/4 cup soy sauce
- 3 tbsp honey
- 2 tbsp rice vinegar
- 1 tbsp cornstarch
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated (about a 1-inch piece)
- 2 garlic cloves, minced
- 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes

For cooking and serving:
- 1 1/2 lb broccoli florets (about 8 cups)
- 1 1/2 cups jasmine rice, dry
- 3 tbsp neutral oil (such as avocado or canola), divided
- 2 tsp toasted sesame oil
- 1 tsp sesame seeds
- 2 green onions, thinly sliced
- 1 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste - taste the sauce before serving and add up to 1/2 tsp more

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/2 cup fresh orange juice
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
Steps:
1. Velvet the chicken: pieces tossed with the soy, Shaoxing and cornstarch; rest 15 minutes. Orange sauce whisked (juice, zest, soy, honey, vinegar, cornstarch, ginger, garlic, chile flakes). Broccoli in florets. Rice on (jasmine; boil, cover, lowest heat 15, rest 10).
2. Char the broccoli: 1 tbsp avocado oil in a wok over high heat, broccoli in one layer, untouched 2 minutes until charred at the edges; a splash of water to steam 1 minute to crisp-tender. Out.
3. Sear the chicken in two batches in the remaining oil, one layer, untouched 2 minutes per batch until golden at the edges and just cooked.
4. Sauce in; simmer 1 minute until glossy and thickened enough to coat. Chicken and broccoli back for 30 seconds, tossed until everything shines.
5. Sesame oil off the heat; sesame seeds and green onions over. Rice under.

Common mistakes:
- Dull orange flavor: fresh juice AND zest, both — bottled juice alone tastes flat.
- One crowded batch of chicken: steamed, pale, sauce sliding off. Two batches.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Ginger-Orange Butter Glaze — in a small pan, simmer 1/2 cup fresh orange juice with 1 tsp grated ginger for 3 minutes until reduced by half; off the heat, whisk in 1 tbsp cold butter. Spoon over the chicken — a bright, buttery second coat of orange.

Title: Parmesan Cod & Pea Risotto
Ingredients:
- 1 3/4 lb cod fillets, cut into 2-inch chunks (about 12 pieces)
- 2 cups Arborio rice (do not rinse it - the starch on the grains is what makes risotto creamy)
- 7 cups chicken stock (or light fish stock)
- 1/2 cup dry white wine
- 1 large yellow onion, finely diced (cut into small 1/4-inch cubes)
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 2 cups frozen peas
- 1 cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese (about 3 1/2 oz)
- 3 tbsp cold unsalted butter, cut into small cubes
- 1 tsp lemon zest
- 2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 1/2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste - taste before serving and add up to 1/2 tsp more
- 1/2 tsp black pepper

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- 1 tbsp chopped fresh parsley
Steps:
1. Stock at a bare simmer throughout. Onion diced fine. Cod in 2-inch chunks, patted very dry and seasoned (dry cod sears; the sear is this risotto's upgrade).
2. Sear the cod: olive oil in a skillet over medium-high, cod in one layer, untouched 2-3 minutes until a golden crust forms; flip gently 1 minute. Out — it finishes on the risotto.
3. Risotto: the butter in a wide pot, onion 5-6 minutes until soft and sweet. Rice stirred 2 minutes until translucent at the edges. Wine in, absorbed.
4. Stock a ladle at a time, stirring often, 18-20 minutes to al dente and flowing. Peas in for the last 3 minutes.
5. Off the heat: the cold butter, Parmesan and lemon zest beaten in until glossy. The cod laid over for 2 minutes to warm through in the risotto's steam.
6. Lemon juice and parsley over.

Common mistakes:
- Cod stirred into the risotto: it shreds to nothing. Laid over, warmed, served in chunks.
- Wet cod in the sear pan: it steams and falls apart. Towels, thoroughly.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Lemon-Herb Butter — in a small pan, melt 2 tbsp butter over medium heat until foaming; off the heat, 1 tbsp lemon juice and 1 tbsp chopped parsley. Spoon over the cod on each bowl — lemon butter is cod's oldest friend.

Title: Parmesan Trout with Pea Orzo
Ingredients:
- 6 skin-on trout fillets, about 5-6 oz each
- 12 oz orzo pasta, dry
- 1 1/2 cups frozen peas
- 3/4 cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese (about 2 1/2 oz)
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- 2 tbsp olive oil, divided
- 3 garlic cloves, minced (chopped into tiny pieces)
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice (about 1 lemon)
- 2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped
- 1 1/2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste - taste the orzo before serving and add up to 1/2 tsp more
- 1/2 tsp black pepper

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp grated Parmesan cheese
Steps:
1. Pasta water on, salted like the sea. Trout patted very dry (dry skin crisps), seasoned. Garlic minced, parsley chopped, Parmesan grated, lemon juiced.
2. Orzo 1 minute shy of done; peas in for the last 2 minutes. Reserve a cup of pasta water; drain.
3. Crisp the trout: olive oil in a skillet over medium-high, fillets skin-side down and untouched 4-5 minutes until the skin is crisp and releases; flip 60 seconds. Out.
4. Orzo back in the pot with the butter, garlic (30 seconds in the melting butter — no more), Parmesan and splashes of pasta water, tossed until it turns glossy and creamy.
5. Lemon juice and parsley through. Trout laid over each serving, skin up so it stays crisp.

Common mistakes:
- Skin-down trout moved early: it tears the skin off. It releases when crisp — patience.
- Garlic cooked to brown: bitter. Thirty seconds in the butter at the end.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Garlic-Parmesan Butter — in a small pan, melt 2 tbsp butter over medium heat with 1 minced garlic clove for 30 seconds; off the heat, whisk in 1 tbsp grated Parmesan until glossy. Spoon over the trout and orzo.

Title: Patagonian Trout with Crispy Potatoes
Ingredients:
- 6 skin-on trout fillets, about 6 oz each
- 2 1/2 lb small Yukon Gold potatoes, scrubbed and halved (quartered if large)
- 1/4 cup olive oil, divided
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 large lemon, half cut into wedges and half juiced
- 3 garlic cloves, thinly sliced (cut into thin coins)
- 2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped
- 1 tsp smoked paprika (optional, for the potatoes)
- 2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste - taste a potato before serving and add up to 1/2 tsp more
- 1/2 tsp black pepper

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1/2 tsp smoked paprika
Steps:
1. Oven at 425 F with a sheet pan inside heating. Potatoes halved, oiled and salted, onto the screaming pan cut-side down; roast 25-30 minutes until the cut faces are deep golden and crisp. Garlic sliced into coins, parsley chopped, lemon halved (half juiced, half wedged).
2. Crisp the trout: olive oil in a skillet over medium-high, fillets skin-side down untouched 4-5 minutes until the skin crisps and releases; flip 60 seconds. Out.
3. The butter and garlic coins in the trout pan 30 seconds until fragrant; lemon juice in off the heat.
4. Trout over the crispy potatoes, the garlic butter spooned around, parsley over, lemon wedges alongside. Smoked paprika dusted over the potatoes if you like.
5. Serve immediately — crisp skin waits for no one.

Common mistakes:
- Potatoes on a cold pan: they stick and steam. The preheated pan is the trick.
- Trout flipped and fussed: one flip, at the end, briefly.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Smoked Paprika Butter — in a small pan, melt 2 tbsp butter over medium heat; add 1/2 tsp smoked paprika and sizzle 20 seconds until brick red. Spoon over the trout and potatoes — Patagonia meets the paprika tin, beautifully.

Title: Picanha-Style Steak Rice Bowls
Ingredients:
- 2 1/2 lb picanha (top sirloin cap) with the fat cap intact
- 2 tbsp coarse kosher salt (or coarse sea salt)
- 1 1/2 cups long-grain white rice, dry

For the vinagrete (Brazilian tomato-onion relish):
- 2 medium tomatoes, diced (cut into 1/2-inch cubes)
- 1/2 small red onion, finely diced
- 1/2 green bell pepper, finely diced
- 1/4 cup olive oil
- 3 tbsp red wine vinegar
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro or flat-leaf parsley, chopped
- 1 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste - taste before serving and add up to 1/2 tsp more

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 clove garlic, minced
Steps:
1. Picanha out 30-40 minutes ahead. Fat cap scored in a crosshatch (cut through the fat, not the meat). Vinagrete made: tomatoes, onion and the pepper finely diced, folded with the olive oil, vinegar, cilantro or parsley and salt; rested 20 minutes so the juices become the dressing. Rice on.
2. Salt the picanha with the coarse salt — generously, all over, like a churrasco. Nothing else; the fat cap is the seasoning.
3. Grill or sear fat-side down first over medium-high, 8-10 minutes, until the fat renders and crisps deep golden; flip and sear the lean side 6-8 minutes to medium-rare (130 F). The fat cap bastes the meat as it renders — this is picanha's whole genius.
4. Rest a full 10 minutes. Slice against the grain into thick slabs, then across into pieces — the Brazilian way is slices with a ribbon of crisp fat on each.
5. Over the rice, the vinagrete and its juices spooned over. Extra coarse salt at the table.

Common mistakes:
- Trimming the fat cap: you have made a sirloin roast and lost the point. The cap stays; it is scored, rendered and eaten.
- Slicing with the grain: across, always.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Coarse Garlic Butter — in a small pan, melt 3 tbsp butter over medium heat with 1 minced garlic clove until foaming and fragrant, 1 minute. Spoon over the sliced picanha — garlic butter on churrasco beef is a São Paulo steakhouse habit worth importing.

Title: Pork & Broccoli Garlic Rice
Ingredients:
- 1 3/4 lb pork tenderloin, sliced into thin 1/4-inch medallions
- 1 1/4 lb broccoli florets (about 6 cups)

For the velveting marinade:
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine (or dry sherry)
- 1 tbsp cornstarch

For the garlic rice:
- 2 cups jasmine rice, dry
- 6 garlic cloves, thinly sliced (cut into thin coins)
- 2 tbsp neutral oil (such as avocado or canola)

For the stir-fry sauce and finish:
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 2 tbsp oyster sauce
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated (about a 1-inch piece)
- 1 tsp toasted sesame oil
- 3 green onions, sliced into 1-inch pieces
- 1 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste - taste before serving and add up to 1/2 tsp more

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp avocado oil
- 2 cloves garlic, thinly sliced
Steps:
1. Velvet the pork: medallions (freezer 20 minutes makes them slice clean) tossed with the soy, Shaoxing and cornstarch; rest 15 minutes. Broccoli in florets. Garlic sliced into coins. Sauce whisked (soy, oyster sauce, ginger).
2. Garlic rice: the avocado oil in a pot over medium heat, the garlic coins fried 1-2 minutes until golden and crisp at the edges — pull half out for garnish. The rice stirred in and toasted 2 minutes in the garlic oil; water per the rice's ratio; boil, cover, lowest heat 15, rest 10.
3. Char the broccoli: a wok over high heat with a film of avocado oil, broccoli one layer, untouched 2 minutes until charred at the edges; a splash of water to steam 1 minute. Out.
4. Sear the pork in one layer, 90 seconds a side, until golden and just cooked. Broccoli back; the sauce in; toss 1 minute until glossy. Sesame oil off the heat.
5. Over the garlic rice; green onions and the reserved crispy garlic over.

Common mistakes:
- Garlic coins burned: bitter rice, whole pot. Golden, then half come out.
- Pork past just-cooked: tenderloin medallions dry in a breath. Ninety seconds a side.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Crispy Garlic Oil — in a small pan, heat 3 tbsp avocado oil with 2 sliced garlic cloves over medium heat for 2 minutes until the garlic turns golden and crisp. Spoon the oil and its garlic crisps over the pork and rice — the garlic rice's garnish, doubled.

Title: Pork & Jalapeño Tacos
Ingredients:
- 1 3/4 lb ground pork
- 12 corn tortillas (6-inch)
- 3 jalapenos, sliced into thin rings (remove the seeds and white ribs for milder heat)
- 1 large yellow onion, diced (cut into small 1/4-inch cubes)
- 1 tbsp neutral oil (such as avocado or canola)
- 1 tbsp chili powder
- 2 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp dried oregano (Mexican oregano if you can find it)
- 1 tsp garlic powder
- 2 limes, cut into wedges
- 1/2 cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste - taste the pork before serving and add up to 1/2 tsp more

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 jalapeño, thinly sliced
- Squeeze of lime juice
Steps:
1. Spice mix ready (chili powder, cumin, oregano, garlic powder, salt). Onion diced, jalapeños in rings, limes wedged, cilantro chopped. Tortillas wrapped in a towel to warm later.
2. Brown the pork hard: the avocado oil in a large skillet over medium-high, pork in one layer, untouched 4-5 minutes until a dark crust forms; break into crumbles and finish with crisp edges. Drain the fat.
3. Onion into the drippings 5 minutes until golden; the spice mix in for 1 minute, toasting in the fat. Jalapeño rings through for the last minute.
4. Warm the tortillas directly over a flame or in a dry skillet until pliable and blistered in spots.
5. Tacos: pork piled in, onion and cilantro over, lime squeezed at the table. Salt checked — the pork should be boldly seasoned.

Common mistakes:
- Steamed pork: one layer, untouched, dark crust. Ground pork especially needs the time.
- Cold, stiff tortillas: they crack and the taco dies in the hand. Warm and blistered.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Jalapeño Butter — in a small pan, melt 3 tbsp butter over medium heat; add 1 sliced jalapeño and sizzle 45 seconds until the butter turns faintly green and fragrant. Off the heat, a squeeze of lime. Spoon over the tacos — hot butter on tacos sounds wrong and tastes like a taqueria secret.

Title: Pork Albondigas with Saffron Rice
Ingredients:
For the albondigas (Spanish meatballs):
- 1 1/2 lb ground pork
- 1 large egg, lightly beaten
- 1/2 cup plain breadcrumbs
- 1/4 cup whole milk
- 1/2 small yellow onion, very finely minced
- 2 garlic cloves, minced (chopped into tiny pieces)
- 1/4 cup fresh parsley, chopped
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1/2 tsp ground cumin
- 1 1/2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste - taste the sauce before serving and add up to 1/2 tsp more
- 1/2 tsp black pepper

For the tomato sauce:
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 large yellow onion, diced (cut into small 1/4-inch cubes)
- 3 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 can (28 oz) crushed tomatoes
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 bay leaf
- 1/2 tsp sugar

For the saffron rice:
- 1 1/2 cups long-grain white rice, dry
- 1/2 tsp saffron threads
- 3 cups chicken stock, warmed
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 small yellow onion, finely diced
- 1/2 tsp kosher salt

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1 cup tomato sauce (from the recipe)
- 2 tbsp dry sherry (or dry white wine)
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
Steps:
1. Saffron rice: the saffron threads steeped in the warmed stock 10 minutes. Panade soaking (breadcrumbs and milk, 5 minutes). Meatballs mixed: pork, panade, egg, minced onion, garlic, parsley, smoked paprika, cumin, salt and pepper — thorough but gentle. Rolled into 1 1/2-inch balls; chill 15 minutes.
2. Sear the albondigas: olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high, meatballs in batches, turned every 2 minutes until browned on most faces, 6-8 minutes. Out — they finish in the sauce.
3. Tomato sauce: the diced onion in the drippings 6-8 minutes until golden; garlic and smoked paprika 30 seconds; crushed tomatoes, bay and sugar in; bare simmer 10 minutes.
4. Meatballs back, simmered gently 12-15 minutes until cooked through and the sauce has thickened around them.
5. Rice: olive oil in a pot, the small onion 4 minutes until golden; the rice toasted 2 minutes; the saffron stock in; boil, cover, lowest heat 15, rest 10.
6. Meatballs and sauce over the saffron rice.

Common mistakes:
- Meatballs simmered from raw: pale and soft. The sear gives them a crust the sauce can cling to.
- Saffron in cold stock: it barely blooms. Warm stock, 10 minutes.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Sherry-Tomato Pan Sauce — in a small pan, simmer 1 cup of the tomato sauce with 2 tbsp dry sherry for 3 minutes; off the heat, whisk in 1 tbsp cold butter. Spoon over the albondigas — a little bodega richness over the saffron rice.

Title: Pork Carnitas Potato Bowls
Ingredients:
For the carnitas:
- 2 1/2 lb boneless pork shoulder (Boston butt), cut into 3-inch chunks
- 1 large orange, halved
- 1 large white onion, quartered
- 6 garlic cloves, smashed (press flat with the side of a knife)
- 2 bay leaves
- 1 tbsp kosher salt, plus more to taste - taste the shredded pork before serving and add up to 1 tsp more
- 2 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp dried oregano
- 2 cups chicken broth

For the crispy potatoes:
- 2 lb Yukon Gold potatoes, cut into 1-inch cubes
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp kosher salt
- 1/2 tsp black pepper

For crisping and serving:
- 3 tbsp neutral oil (such as avocado or canola)
- 1/2 cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1/2 white onion, finely diced
- 2 limes, cut into wedges

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1 cup carnitas cooking liquid (from the recipe)
- Juice of 1 lime
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
Steps:
1. Carnitas: pork chunks into a Dutch oven with the orange halves (squeezed in, rinds too), onion, smashed garlic, bay, salt, cumin, oregano and broth to barely cover. Bare simmer, covered, 2 to 2 1/2 hours until the pork shreds at a fork's press and the liquid has mostly cooked down to its fat.
2. Potatoes: 1-inch cubes, oiled and salted, roasted at 425 F for 30-35 minutes, flipping once, until crisp and golden.
3. Crisp the carnitas — the step that IS carnitas: shred the pork coarse; a large skillet over medium-high with a film of the avocado oil (or a spoon of the cooking fat), pork spread flat and untouched 4-5 minutes until the edges crisp dark and lacy; toss and crisp 2 more minutes in spots. A splash of the cooking liquid over to keep the centers juicy.
4. Bowls: crispy potatoes, carnitas piled over, the finely diced white onion and cilantro scattered, lime wedges alongside.

Common mistakes:
- Skipping the crisp: braised pork is not carnitas. The lacy edges are the dish.
- Shredding too fine: fine shreds dry out in the crisping. Coarse chunks, crisp faces, juicy middles.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Orange-Lime Pan Sauce — ladle 1 cup of the carnitas cooking liquid into a small saucepan; boil 5 minutes until reduced by half. Off the heat: the juice of 1 lime and 1 tbsp cold butter whisked in. Spoon over the bowls — the braise's citrus soul, concentrated.

Title: Pork Chops with Garlic Lyonnaise Potatoes
Ingredients:
- 6 boneless pork chops, about 8 oz each and 1 inch thick
- 2 1/2 lb Yukon Gold or russet potatoes, peeled
- 2 large yellow onions, halved and thinly sliced (cut into thin half-moons)
- 5 tbsp unsalted butter, divided
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 4 garlic cloves, minced (chopped into tiny pieces)
- 1/4 cup fresh parsley, chopped
- 2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste - taste the potatoes before serving and add up to 1/2 tsp more
- 1 tsp black pepper
- 1 tsp dried thyme (optional)

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/3 cup low-sodium chicken broth
- 1 tsp Dijon mustard
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
Steps:
1. Potatoes parboiled whole in salted water 10 minutes, drained, cooled slightly, then sliced 1/4 inch. Onions in half-moons, garlic minced, parsley chopped. Chops out 20-30 minutes ahead, patted very dry and seasoned.
2. Lyonnaise potatoes: 3 tbsp butter and the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat, the onion half-moons 12-15 minutes, slow, until deeply golden and sweet — Lyonnaise means the onions are nearly caramelized, not merely soft. Potato slices in, spread flat, untouched 4-5 minutes until crisp on the underside; toss and crisp 5 more. Garlic and thyme for the last minute.
3. Sear the chops: a second skillet (or the potatoes held warm) over medium-high with a film of olive oil, chops down untouched 4-5 minutes until a deep crust forms; flip, remaining butter in to baste, 3-4 minutes to 145 F.
4. Rest the chops 5 minutes. Potatoes finished with parsley and salt.
5. Chops over or beside the potatoes, pan butter spooned around.

Common mistakes:
- Rushed onions: pale onions make this ordinary potatoes. Twelve slow minutes to gold.
- Chops past 145 F: they dry on the plate. Pull, baste, rest.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Dijon Pan Sauce — in the chop skillet over medium heat, add 1/3 cup chicken broth; scrape up the fond and reduce 1 minute. Off the heat, whisk in 1 tsp Dijon and 1 tbsp cold butter until glossy. Spoon over the chops — the Lyonnaise bistro finish.

Title: Pork Chops with Salsa Criolla Rice
Ingredients:
2 lb boneless pork chops, 1-inch thick (about 6 chops)
1 tbsp kosher salt, divided (start with 1 tbsp; add more to taste at the end)
1 tsp black pepper, freshly ground
2 tbsp olive oil, for searing
2 cups long-grain white rice, uncooked
3 cups water, for the rice
1 large red bell pepper, finely diced (dice = cut into small even cubes about 1/2 inch)
1 large white onion, finely diced
2 large tomatoes, seeded and finely diced
4 cloves garlic, minced (mince = chop very fine)
1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil, for the salsa
1/3 cup red wine vinegar, for the salsa
1/2 cup water, for the salsa
1 tsp dried oregano
1/2 tsp crushed red pepper flakes (start with 1/2 tsp; add up to 1 tsp for more heat)
1/4 cup fresh parsley, chopped

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh parsley
- 1 tsp red wine vinegar
- Pinch of red chile flakes
Steps:
1. Salsa criolla first (it needs 20 minutes to pickle): the pepper, white onion and tomatoes finely diced, folded with the olive oil, vinegar, water, oregano, chile flakes and salt; rested so the onion mellows into the dressing. Rice on (boil, cover, lowest heat 15, rest 10).
2. Sear the chops: patted very dry, seasoned with the salt and pepper; the olive oil in a skillet over medium-high until shimmering; chops down untouched 4-5 minutes until a deep crust forms; flip, 3-4 minutes to 145 F, basting with the pan oil at the end.
3. Rest 5 minutes — non-negotiable for pork.
4. Chops over the rice, the salsa criolla and all its juices spooned generously across, parsley over.

Common mistakes:
- Salsa served instantly: the onion is raw and harsh. Twenty minutes of pickling is the recipe.
- Chops at 165 F out of habit: dry. 145 and a rest is juicy and safe.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Chimichurri Butter — in a small pan, melt 3 tbsp butter over medium heat until foaming; off the heat, stir in 2 tbsp chopped parsley, 1 tsp red wine vinegar and a pinch of chile flakes. Spoon over the chops — Argentina's two steakhouse finishes in one bite.

Title: Pork Egg Fried Rice
Ingredients:
6 cups cooked long-grain rice, day-old and cold (from 2 cups uncooked rice)
1 lb pork loin or tenderloin, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
6 large eggs, beaten in a bowl
1 cup frozen peas, thawed
1 cup frozen corn kernels, thawed
4 green onions, thinly sliced (slice = cut into thin flat pieces), white and green parts kept separate
3 tbsp neutral oil (vegetable or canola), divided
3 tbsp light soy sauce (start with 3 tbsp; add up to 4 tbsp to taste)
1 tbsp Shaoxing wine or dry sherry, optional
1 tsp kosher salt, divided (start with 1 tsp; adjust at the end)
1/2 tsp black pepper

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1/2 tsp black pepper
Steps:
1. Mise en place — everything, before the wok: eggs beaten, pork in 1/2-inch cubes, green onions separated, peas and corn thawed, the cold day-old rice at hand (cold rice fries; warm rice clumps — fried rice's first law).
2. Eggs: 1 tbsp avocado oil in a wok over medium-high, eggs scrambled to soft ribbons in 30 seconds. Out.
3. Sear the pork: remaining oil, pork in one layer, untouched 2-3 minutes until golden and crisp at the edges; the Shaoxing in to sizzle. Out.
4. Green onion whites 20 seconds. The rice in, spread flat 60 seconds to crisp on the bottom; toss; peas and corn through 1 minute.
5. Pork and eggs back; the soy around the wok's edge so it sizzles; tossed hard 1 minute. Salt and pepper checked; green onion greens off the heat.

Common mistakes:
- Fresh warm rice: gummy. Day-old and cold, or the tray-in-the-fridge trick.
- Soy poured in the center: it steams. Around the hot edge.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Soy Butter Sauce — in a small pan, melt 2 tbsp butter over medium heat; add 1 tbsp soy sauce and 1/2 tsp black pepper, swirl 30 seconds until glossy. Spoon over the fried rice — a rich, savory finish the diners of Osaka would approve.

Title: Pork Kofta Rice Bowls
Ingredients:
2 lb ground pork (85 percent lean)
1 large egg
1/2 cup plain breadcrumbs
1 medium onion, grated on a box grater (keep the juice)
4 cloves garlic, minced (mince = chop very fine)
1/2 cup fresh parsley, finely chopped
2 tbsp ground cumin
1 tbsp sweet paprika
1 tbsp dried mint
2 tsp ground coriander
2 tsp dried oregano
2 tsp kosher salt, divided (start with 2 tsp; adjust at the end)
1 tsp black pepper
2 cups long-grain rice, uncooked
3 cups water, for the rice
2 tbsp olive oil, for cooking
1 cup plain Greek yogurt
2 tbsp lemon juice
1 large cucumber, diced (dice = cut into small even cubes about 1/2 inch)
2 large tomatoes, diced
1/2 red onion, thinly sliced (slice = cut into thin flat pieces)

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 tsp sweet paprika
- 1/2 tsp ground cumin
Steps:
1. Rice on (boil, cover, lowest heat 15, rest 10). Yogurt sauce: yogurt, lemon and a pinch of salt, refrigerated with the diced cucumber, tomatoes and red onion ready as the salad.
2. Kofta mix: pork, egg, breadcrumbs, grated onion WITH its juice (it keeps these moist), garlic, parsley, cumin, paprika, mint, coriander, oregano, salt and pepper. Chill 20 minutes.
3. Shape into 12 ovals. Sear: olive oil in a skillet over medium-high, kofta in with space, 3-4 minutes untouched until a deep crust forms; turn and brown all faces, 8-10 minutes total, to 160 F. Rest 5 minutes.
4. Bowls: rice, the cucumber-tomato-onion salad, kofta over, yogurt sauce spooned generously.

Common mistakes:
- Squeezing the onion dry for these: pork kofta wants the juice — that is what the breadcrumbs are for. (Beef kofta rules differ; here, juicy wins.)
- Skipping the chill: warm kofta slump and stick. Twenty minutes.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Paprika Butter Drizzle — in a small pan, melt 3 tbsp butter over medium heat; add 1 tsp sweet paprika and 1/2 tsp ground cumin, sizzle 20 seconds until brick red. Spoon over the kofta and rice — the Istanbul finish.

Title: Pork Meatballs with Parmesan Orzo
Ingredients:
2 lb ground pork
1 large egg
1 cup plain breadcrumbs
1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese, for the meatballs, plus 1/2 cup for the orzo
1/2 cup fresh parsley, finely chopped
4 cloves garlic, minced (mince = chop very fine), divided
1 tsp dried oregano
1 tsp dried basil
2 tsp kosher salt, divided (start with 2 tsp; adjust at the end)
1 tsp black pepper
2 tbsp olive oil, for the sauce
1 medium onion, diced (dice = cut into small even cubes about 1/2 inch)
1 can (28 oz) crushed tomatoes
2 1/2 cups orzo pasta, uncooked
3 tbsp butter
2 tbsp lemon juice (from 1 lemon)
1/4 cup fresh basil leaves, torn

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- 1 tbsp torn fresh basil
Steps:
1. Oven at 425 F. Meatballs mixed: pork, egg, breadcrumbs, Parmesan, parsley, half the garlic, oregano, basil, salt and pepper — gentle hands. Rolled into 1 1/2-inch balls.
2. Brown the meatballs: a rack in the oven 15-18 minutes until deeply browned (or seared in a skillet in batches — the oven is easier and the fond-less trade is fine here since the sauce is tomato).
3. Tomato sauce: olive oil in a Dutch oven, the onion 6-8 minutes until golden; remaining garlic 30 seconds; crushed tomatoes in; bare simmer 10 minutes.
4. Orzo in the sauce with 2 cups water; simmer 9-11 minutes, stirring often, until tender and the sauce has turned glossy around it.
5. Meatballs folded through; the butter and lemon juice in off the heat (the lemon is this dish's quiet surprise — do not skip it). Basil torn over.

Common mistakes:
- Unstirred orzo in tomato sauce: it scorches on the bottom fast. Stir it like a risotto's cousin.
- Skipping the lemon: the dish reads heavy without it. It is two tablespoons and it changes everything.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Lemon-Basil Butter — in a small pan, melt 2 tbsp butter over medium heat until foaming; off the heat, 1 tbsp lemon juice and 1 tbsp torn basil. Spoon over the meatballs — the dish's lemon note, doubled at the finish.

Title: Pork Ragu with Parmesan Polenta
Ingredients:
2 1/2 lb pork shoulder, cut into 2-inch chunks (trim very large fat caps but leave some)
2 tbsp olive oil
2 tsp kosher salt, divided (start with 2 tsp; adjust at the end)
1 tsp black pepper
1 large onion, diced (dice = cut into small even cubes about 1/2 inch)
2 medium carrots, diced
2 ribs celery, diced
4 cloves garlic, minced (mince = chop very fine)
1 cup dry white wine
2 tbsp tomato paste
1 can (28 oz) crushed tomatoes
2 bay leaves
1 cup whole milk, for the ragu
2 cups coarse polenta (cornmeal), dry
4 cups water, for the polenta
2 cups whole milk, for the polenta
4 tbsp butter
1 cup grated Parmesan cheese
2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 tsp chopped fresh rosemary
- 1 clove garlic, thinly sliced
Steps:
1. Pork in 2-inch chunks, patted dry and seasoned. Soffritto (onion, carrot, celery) diced, garlic minced.
2. Sear the pork in batches: olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high, pork in one layer, 3-4 minutes untouched per batch until every chunk is deeply crusted. Out.
3. Soffritto into the drippings 8-10 minutes until soft, sweet and golden; garlic 30 seconds; tomato paste 2 minutes until darkened. Wine in, scraping, reduced by half.
4. Crushed tomatoes and bay in; pork back. Bare simmer, partially covered, 1 1/2 to 2 hours until the pork shreds at a fork. The milk stirred in for the last 15 minutes — ragù's rounding secret.
5. Polenta: water and milk to a boil, the polenta rained in whisking constantly; lowest heat 30-35 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until it pulls from the sides. Butter and Parmesan beaten in off the heat; salt boldly.
6. Pork pulled into coarse shreds in its sauce; served over the polenta in deep bowls, parsley over.

Common mistakes:
- Polenta dumped in at once: lumps that never leave. Rain it in, whisking.
- A fast ragù simmer: it turns harsh. Lazy bubbles for two hours.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Rosemary-Garlic Butter — in a small pan, melt 3 tbsp butter over medium heat; add 1 tsp chopped rosemary and 1 sliced garlic clove, sizzle 30 seconds until fragrant. Spoon over the ragù and polenta — a Tuscan finish for a Tuscan pot.

Title: Pork Tenderloin with Lime Potatoes
Ingredients:
3 lb pork tenderloin (about 2 tenderloins)
1 cup fresh orange juice (about 3 oranges)
1/3 cup fresh lime juice (about 3 limes), plus 1 lime cut into wedges
8 cloves garlic, smashed (hit once with the flat of the knife so each clove breaks open)
1 tsp ground cumin
1 tsp dried oregano
1/3 cup olive oil, for the marinade, plus a glug for searing
2 tsp kosher salt, divided (start with 2 tsp; adjust at the end)
1 tsp black pepper
3 lb baby potatoes, halved
1/4 cup fresh cilantro, chopped

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/2 cup reserved mojo marinade (from the recipe; boiled in the sauce, see steps)
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
Steps:
1. Mojo marinade: orange juice, lime juice, smashed garlic, cumin, oregano, olive oil, salt and pepper whisked; tenderloins in for 1-4 hours refrigerated (citrus marinades work fast — past 4 hours the surface goes chalky). Oven at 425 F. Potatoes halved.
2. Potatoes on a sheet pan with a glug of olive oil and salt, cut-side down; roast 25-30 minutes until crisp on the faces.
3. Sear the tenderloins: lifted from the marinade (marinade saved) and patted dry; a skillet over medium-high with a film of olive oil, tenderloins turned every 2-3 minutes until every side is deeply crusted, 12-15 minutes total to 145 F. Rest a full 10 minutes.
4. Potatoes finished with the lime wedges' juice squeezed over and tossed — lime potatoes earn their name at the end, not in the oven.
5. Slice the pork thick; cilantro over; the potatoes alongside. The pan juices from resting poured over the slices.

Common mistakes:
- Marinade left on for the sear: wet pork steams. Pat dry; the flavor is already in.
- Slicing at 165 thinking: tenderloin at 145 plus a 10-minute rest is juicy and safe. At 165 it is chalk.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Mojo Pan Sauce — in the searing skillet over medium heat, add 1/2 cup of the reserved marinade (it must boil, since it held raw pork — a full 2-minute boil makes it safe); reduce by half. Off the heat, whisk in 2 tbsp cold butter until glossy. Spoon over the pork — the mojo, concentrated and buttered.

Title: Provencal Cod with Tomato & Olives
Ingredients:
2 1/2 lb cod fillets, about 1 1/2 inches thick
3 tbsp olive oil, divided
1 large onion, sliced into thin half-rounds (slice = cut into thin flat pieces)
4 cloves garlic, minced (mince = chop very fine)
2 cans (14.5 oz each) diced tomatoes
1 cup kalamata olives, halved
2 tbsp capers, drained
1 tsp herbes de Provence
1/2 tsp crushed red pepper flakes (start with 1/2 tsp; add up to 1 tsp for more heat)
2 tsp kosher salt, divided (start with 2 tsp; adjust at the end)
1 tsp black pepper
2 tbsp lemon juice
1/4 cup fresh parsley, chopped

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/2 cup dry white wine
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
- 1 tbsp chopped fresh parsley
Steps:
1. Onion in half-rounds, garlic minced, olives halved, parsley chopped, lemon juiced. Cod patted very dry and seasoned.
2. The Provençal base: 2 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat, onion 8-10 minutes until soft, sweet and golden at the edges; garlic, herbes de Provence and chile flakes 30 seconds.
3. Tomatoes, olives and capers in; bare simmer 10-12 minutes until the sauce thickens and turns brick-red and glossy. Salt carefully — olives and capers bring plenty.
4. Cod nestled into the sauce, lid on, bare simmer 7-9 minutes until it just flakes. (For a crisper top, sear the cod 2 minutes in a separate hot pan first and lay it over — optional, both are honest.)
5. Lemon juice and the remaining olive oil over off the heat; parsley scattered. Crusty bread for the sauce.

Common mistakes:
- Boiling the cod: it breaks into the sauce. Bare simmer, lid on.
- Undercooked base: the onion needs its 10 minutes or the sauce tastes raw under the fish.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): White Wine Pan Sauce — in a small pan, simmer 1/2 cup dry white wine until reduced by half; off the heat, whisk in 2 tbsp cold butter and 1 tbsp chopped parsley. Spoon over the cod — a little Nice bistro polish on a rustic dish.

Title: Salmon Couscous with Cucumber & Olives
Ingredients:
2 lb salmon fillets, skin-on, cut into 6 portions
2 tsp kosher salt, divided (start with 2 tsp; adjust at the end)
1 tsp black pepper
1 tsp dried oregano
2 tbsp olive oil, divided
2 cups couscous, uncooked
2 cups chicken or vegetable broth
1 large cucumber, diced (dice = cut into small even cubes about 1/2 inch)
1 pint cherry tomatoes, halved
1 cup kalamata olives, halved
1/2 red onion, thinly sliced (slice = cut into thin flat pieces)
4 oz feta cheese, crumbled
1/4 cup olive oil, for the dressing
3 tbsp lemon juice
1/4 cup fresh dill, chopped (or 1 tbsp dried dill)

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1/2 tsp dried oregano
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
Steps:
1. Couscous: broth to a boil, couscous in, off the heat covered 5 minutes, fluffed with a fork and a drizzle of olive oil. Cucumber diced, tomatoes and olives halved, onion sliced thin, feta crumbled, dill chopped. Dressing whisked: olive oil, lemon juice, salt, pepper, half the dill.
2. Sear the salmon: olive oil in a skillet over medium-high, fillets skin-side down untouched 5-6 minutes until the skin crisps and releases; flip 60 seconds. Silky center, 125 F.
3. Couscous folded with the cucumber, tomatoes, olives, onion and half the dressing while the grains are warm (they drink it).
4. Salmon over the couscous, feta scattered, the remaining dressing spooned over, dill on top.

Common mistakes:
- Dressing cold couscous: it sits on the surface. Fold it in warm.
- Flabby salmon skin: dry fillets, hot pan, no touching for 5 minutes.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Oregano-Lemon Butter — in a small pan, melt 2 tbsp butter over medium heat; add 1/2 tsp dried oregano, sizzle 20 seconds; off the heat, 1 tbsp lemon juice. Spoon over the salmon — a warm Greek butter over the cold, bright couscous.

Title: Salmon Teriyaki with Bok Choy
Ingredients:
2 lb salmon fillets, cut into 6 portions
1/2 cup low-sodium soy sauce
1/2 cup mirin (sweet Japanese cooking wine)
1/4 cup packed brown sugar
1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
2 cloves garlic, minced (mince = chop very fine)
1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 1 tbsp cold water (stir until smooth -- a smooth slurry keeps the sauce from lumping)
2 lb baby bok choy, halved lengthwise
1 tbsp toasted sesame oil
1 tbsp neutral oil (vegetable or canola)
2 cups long-grain rice, uncooked
3 cups water, for the rice
2 tbsp sesame seeds, toasted, for garnish
3 green onions, thinly sliced (slice = cut into thin flat pieces)

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/4 cup soy sauce
- 1/4 cup mirin
- 2 tbsp brown sugar
Steps:
1. Rice on. Teriyaki sauce simmered (soy, mirin, brown sugar, ginger, garlic) 3 minutes; the cornstarch slurry in until glossy. Half reserved clean for serving. Salmon patted dry; bok choy halved.
2. Sear the salmon: the avocado oil (in place of the neutral oil) in a skillet over medium-high, fillets down untouched 4-5 minutes until a crust forms; flip, brush with teriyaki, 1-2 minutes until lacquered and silky at 125 F. The sugar burns fast after the glaze lands — watch it.
3. Bok choy: the sesame oil in a wok over high heat, cut sides down 2 minutes until charred at the edges; a splash of water and the lid for 1 minute to steam tender.
4. Salmon over the rice, bok choy alongside, the reserved teriyaki spooned over, sesame and green onions scattered.

Common mistakes:
- Glaze from the start: scorched sugar, raw fish. Sear, flip, glaze, out.
- Serving the pan's glaze if the fish sat in it raw-side: the reserved clean half is the serving half.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Extra Teriyaki Glaze — in a small pan, simmer 1/4 cup soy sauce, 1/4 cup mirin and 2 tbsp brown sugar for 3-4 minutes until reduced to a syrup (no slurry needed at this concentration). Spoon over the salmon for a second lacquer.

Title: Salmon with Lemon Butter Orzo
Ingredients:
2 lb salmon fillets, cut into 6 portions
2 tsp kosher salt, divided (start with 2 tsp; adjust at the end)
1 tsp black pepper
2 tbsp olive oil, divided
2 cups orzo pasta, uncooked
6 tbsp butter (3/4 stick)
4 cloves garlic, minced (mince = chop very fine)
1/4 cup lemon juice (about 2 lemons), plus lemon wedges for serving
1 tsp lemon zest
1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese
1 bunch asparagus, tough ends trimmed, cut into 2-inch pieces
1/4 cup fresh parsley, chopped

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- 1 tbsp chopped fresh parsley
Steps:
1. Orzo on: a large pot of salted water, orzo 1 minute shy of done; asparagus in for the last 2 minutes. Reserve a cup of pasta water; drain. Salmon patted dry and seasoned; garlic minced; lemons zested and juiced; Parmesan grated.
2. Sear the salmon: olive oil in a skillet over medium-high, fillets down untouched 4-5 minutes until crusted; flip 1-2 minutes to silky, 125 F. Out.
3. Lemon butter orzo: butter melted in the pot, garlic 30 seconds; orzo and asparagus back with the lemon juice, zest, Parmesan and splashes of pasta water, tossed until glossy and creamy.
4. Salmon over the orzo (or flaked through in large pieces). Parsley over, lemon wedges alongside.

Common mistakes:
- The orzo waiting on the salmon: it clumps and dries. Salmon rests fine — finish the orzo while it does.
- Garlic browned in the butter: 30 seconds, then the pasta goes in.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Garlic-Lemon Butter — in a small pan, melt 2 tbsp butter over medium heat with 1 minced garlic clove for 30 seconds; off the heat, 1 tbsp lemon juice and 1 tbsp chopped parsley. Spoon over the salmon — a second, brighter lemon butter for the fish.

Title: Salmon with Rice, Peas & Garlic
Ingredients:
2 lb salmon fillets, cut into 6 portions
2 tsp kosher salt, divided (start with 2 tsp; adjust at the end)
1 tsp black pepper
2 tbsp olive oil
2 cups long-grain rice, uncooked
3 cups water, for the rice
2 cups frozen peas, thawed (run under warm water first)
6 cloves garlic, minced (mince = chop very fine)
3 tbsp butter
2 tbsp lemon juice
1/4 cup fresh parsley, chopped
Lemon wedges, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 tbsp chopped fresh parsley
- Zest of 1/2 lemon
- Pinch of kosher salt
Steps:
1. Rice cooked and kept warm. Peas thawed, garlic minced, parsley chopped, lemon juiced. Salmon patted dry and seasoned.
2. Sear the salmon: the olive oil in a skillet over medium-high, fillets down untouched 4-5 minutes until a deep crust forms; flip 1-2 minutes to silky, 125 F. Out.
3. Garlic butter peas: butter in the salmon pan, garlic 30 seconds until fragrant; peas in for 2 minutes until hot and glossed in the butter (they cook in the salmon's drippings — that is the recipe's quiet genius).
4. Peas folded through the rice with the lemon juice and parsley.
5. Salmon over the rice, lemon wedges alongside, the pan's remaining butter spooned around.

Common mistakes:
- Peas cooked to khaki: 2 minutes in the hot butter, bright green, done.
- Salmon flipped early and often: once, at the end, briefly.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Herb Butter — in a small pan, melt 2 tbsp butter over medium heat until foaming; off the heat, stir in 1 tbsp chopped parsley, the zest of 1/2 lemon and a pinch of salt. Spoon over the salmon — a simple green butter for a simple, good plate.

Title: Salsa Verde Cod Tacos
Ingredients:
2 lb cod fillets, skinless, cut into strips about 3 inches long and 1 inch wide, patted very dry
1.5 cups all-purpose flour, divided (1 cup for the batter, 0.5 cup for dredging)
0.5 cup cornstarch
1 tbsp baking powder
2 tsp kosher salt, divided
1 tsp ground cumin
1 tsp smoked paprika
1 cup cold Mexican lager beer (keep it ice cold; do not open until batter time)
1 large egg, lightly beaten
5 cups avocado oil, for frying (about 2 inches deep in a heavy skillet)
18 small corn tortillas (6-inch)
4 cups shredded green cabbage
0.5 cup Mexican crema (or sour cream)
0.25 cup mayonnaise
1 tbsp fresh lime juice, plus extra lime wedges for serving
1.5 cups salsa verde (tomatillo salsa)
0.75 cup crumbled cotija cheese
0.5 cup chopped fresh cilantro

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1/3 cup Mexican crema (or sour cream)
- 1 tbsp lime juice
- 1 chipotle in adobo, minced
- Pinch of kosher salt
Steps:
1. Mise en place before heat: cod in strips, patted very dry. Cabbage shredded, cilantro chopped. Crema stirred (crema, mayo, lime juice) and refrigerated. Salsa verde ready. Tortillas to be warmed later. The beer kept ICE cold and unopened until batter time — cold batter is crisp batter.
2. Batter at the last moment: flour, cornstarch, baking powder, salt, cumin and smoked paprika whisked; the cold beer and egg stirred in just until combined — lumps are fine.
3. Fry: 2 inches of avocado oil at 375 F in a heavy skillet. Cod dredged in flour, dipped in batter, laid in away from you; 3-4 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and crisp. Drain on a rack, salt immediately. Small batches — the oil temperature is the whole game.
4. Tortillas warmed directly over a flame or in a dry skillet until pliable and blistered.
5. Tacos: two tortillas if they are thin, cabbage, cod, salsa verde spooned over, crema in lines, cotija and cilantro scattered, lime at the table.

Common mistakes:
- Warm beer: heavy, greasy batter. Ice cold, opened at the last second.
- Crowded frying: the temperature crashes and the fish steams in oil. Batches, with the oil recovering between.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Baja Crema Pan Sauce — in a small pan, melt 1 tbsp butter over low heat; whisk in 1/3 cup Mexican crema (or sour cream), 1 tbsp lime juice, 1 minced chipotle in adobo and a pinch of salt until just warm and pourable — never boil it. Drizzle over the tacos: a warm, smoky crema over the crisp fish.

Title: Scallop Tomato Risotto
Ingredients:
1.5 cups arborio rice
2 lb large dry sea scallops (U-15/U-20), side muscle removed, patted very dry
6 cups low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth
1.5 cups crushed tomatoes
1 large yellow onion, diced (cut into small even cubes about 1/2 inch)
4 garlic cloves, minced (chopped very fine)
0.5 cup dry white wine, such as pinot grigio or sauvignon blanc
4 tbsp unsalted butter, divided
3 tbsp olive oil, divided
1 cup finely grated Parmesan cheese
0.5 cup chopped fresh basil or flat-leaf parsley
1 tbsp fresh lemon juice, plus the zest of 1 lemon
1.5 tsp kosher salt, divided, plus more as needed
0.75 tsp black pepper, divided

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- Pinch of kosher salt
Steps:
1. Broth at a bare simmer. Onion diced, garlic minced, Parmesan grated, basil or parsley chopped, lemon zested and juiced. Scallops: side muscles pulled off, patted VERY dry, seasoned — dry scallops are the entire sear.
2. Sear the scallops first: olive oil in a skillet over high heat until smoking, scallops in with space, untouched 90 seconds until a deep golden crust forms; flip, butter in, 30-60 seconds basting. Out immediately — they wait, tented, while the risotto cooks, and they are better for the rest.
3. Risotto: remaining oil and butter in a wide pot, onion 5-6 minutes until soft and sweet; garlic 30 seconds; rice stirred 2 minutes until translucent at the edges. Wine in, absorbed.
4. Crushed tomatoes in, then the broth a ladle at a time, stirring often, 18-20 minutes to al dente and flowing.
5. Off the heat: Parmesan beaten in until glossy; lemon zest and juice folded through.
6. Risotto in warm bowls, scallops laid over with their butter, basil or parsley scattered.

Common mistakes:
- Wet scallops: they steam white and never crust. Towels, then more towels.
- Scallops cooked in the risotto: rubber erasers in a lovely sauce. Sear separately, lay over.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Lemon Brown Butter — in a small pan, melt 3 tbsp butter over medium heat until amber and nutty; off the heat, 1 tbsp lemon juice and a pinch of salt — it will foam. Spoon over the scallops: brown butter and scallops are a first principle of good cooking.

Title: Seared Trout with Tomato Olive Rice
Ingredients:
2 lb rainbow trout fillets (6 fillets, about 5 to 6 oz each), skin on or off
2 cups long-grain white rice
1 can (14.5 oz) diced tomatoes with their juices
1 cup pitted Kalamata olives, halved (slice = cut into thin flat pieces)
1 large yellow onion, diced (cut into small even cubes about 1/2 inch)
4 garlic cloves, minced (chopped very fine)
3 cups low-sodium chicken broth
4 tbsp olive oil, divided
1.5 tsp smoked paprika (pimenton dulce), divided
0.25 tsp saffron threads, crumbled (optional; or 0.5 tsp turmeric for color)
1 lemon, cut into wedges
0.5 cup chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley
1.75 tsp kosher salt, divided
0.75 tsp black pepper

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/4 cup olive oil
- 2 cloves garlic, thinly sliced
- 1/2 tsp smoked paprika
Steps:
1. Tomato-olive rice: 2 tbsp olive oil in a pot, onion 6-8 minutes until golden; garlic and half the smoked paprika 30 seconds; rice stirred in and toasted 2 minutes; tomatoes with their juices, broth and saffron (or turmeric) in; boil, cover, lowest heat 15, rest 10. Olives folded through at the end so they stay firm.
2. Trout checked for pin bones, patted very dry, seasoned with the remaining paprika, salt and pepper.
3. Sear the trout: remaining olive oil in a skillet over medium-high, fillets skin-side down untouched 4-5 minutes until the skin crisps and releases; flip 60 seconds.
4. Trout over the rice, parsley over, lemon wedges at the table. A thread of good olive oil over each plate.

Common mistakes:
- Olives cooked in the rice from the start: they go soft and harsh. Folded in at the end.
- Trout skin steamed: dry fish, hot pan, no touching.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Pil-Pil Style Garlic Oil — in a small pan, warm 1/4 cup olive oil with 2 sliced garlic cloves and 1/2 tsp smoked paprika over medium heat for 2 minutes until the garlic is golden and the oil deep red. Spoon over the trout and rice — the Basque pil-pil spirit in a drizzle.

Title: Sesame-Free Tuna Poke Bowls
Ingredients:
2 lb sushi-grade ahi tuna, cut into 3/4-inch cubes
3 cups short-grain white rice, rinsed well
3 cups water, for cooking rice
1 tsp kosher salt, for the rice water
0.5 cup low-sodium soy sauce
2 tbsp rice vinegar
1 tbsp honey
1 tbsp avocado oil (this recipe is sesame-free; we skip sesame oil and sesame seeds entirely)
1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
4 green onions, thinly sliced (slice = cut into thin flat pieces)
1 tsp crushed red pepper flakes (start with 0.5 tsp if you like it mild)
2 ripe avocados, diced
2 cups diced fresh mango
1 English cucumber, thinly sliced
0.5 cup roasted macadamia nuts, coarsely crushed
4 cups shredded red cabbage
0.25 cup chopped fresh cilantro
1 lime, cut into wedges

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp avocado oil
- 1 tbsp grated fresh ginger
- Juice of 1/2 lime
Steps:
1. Food safety first: sushi-grade tuna, kept cold until the moment of cubing, clean board and knife. Rice cooked and seasoned warm (salt in its water; or fold in a pinch of sugar and vinegar, sushi-style), cooled to just warm.
2. Dressing whisked: soy, rice vinegar, honey, avocado oil (this bowl is sesame-free by design — the avocado oil and macadamia carry the richness), ginger and chile flakes.
3. Tuna cubed cleanly, folded through the dressing with the green onions — 10 minutes maximum before serving, so the acid does not cook the fish's edges.
4. Bowls: rice, cabbage, tuna and its dressing, mango, cucumber, avocado. Macadamia nuts crushed over (they replace the sesame crunch entirely), cilantro scattered, lime wedges alongside.
5. Serve immediately, cold fish on warm rice.

Common mistakes:
- Tuna sitting in the dressing for an hour: ceviche edges, chalky texture. Ten minutes.
- Room-temperature tuna: keep it cold until the knife work.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Warm Ginger-Lime Oil — in a small pan, warm 3 tbsp avocado oil with 1 tbsp grated ginger over low heat for 2 minutes until fragrant; off the heat, the juice of 1/2 lime. Spoon a teaspoon over the tuna in each bowl — a warm, bright gloss, sesame-free as the bowl demands.

Title: Shaking Beef Tomato Rice
Ingredients:
2.5 lb top sirloin, cut into 1-inch cubes
3 tbsp oyster sauce
2 tbsp fish sauce
2 tbsp low-sodium soy sauce
1 tbsp granulated sugar
5 garlic cloves, minced (chopped very fine), divided
1 tsp black pepper
3 tbsp avocado oil (or another neutral high-heat oil), divided
2 tbsp unsalted butter, divided
1 large red onion, cut into thin wedges (slice = cut into thin flat pieces)
5 cups cooked jasmine rice, day-old and chilled (start with about 1.75 cups dry rice)
2 tbsp tomato paste
1 tbsp fish sauce (for the rice)
2 tsp chicken bouillon powder (or 1 crumbled bouillon cube)
2 large eggs, beaten
1 bunch watercress (or 4 cups mixed salad greens)
2 ripe tomatoes, cut into wedges
1 cucumber, thinly sliced (slice = cut into thin flat pieces)
2 tbsp fresh lime juice (about 2 limes)
1 tsp kosher salt
1 tsp black pepper (for the lime-pepper dip)

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 tbsp lime juice
- 1 tsp coarsely cracked black pepper
- Pinch of kosher salt
Steps:
1. Beef marinated 20-30 minutes: cubes in the oyster sauce, fish sauce, soy, sugar, half the garlic and the pepper. Rice cooked day-old style (or fresh, tray-chilled). Eggs beaten. Watercress and tomatoes ready as the plate's cool side.
2. Tomato fried rice: 1 tbsp avocado oil and 1 tbsp butter in a wok over high heat, the remaining garlic 20 seconds; tomato paste fried 1 minute until dark red; the cold rice in, tossed hard 2-3 minutes until every grain is stained orange-red; fish sauce and bouillon through. Eggs scrambled in at the end (or fried separately and laid over).
3. Shake the beef: the wok wiped, the remaining oil until smoking, beef in one layer — then SHAKE the wok and toss so the cubes char on all faces, 3-4 minutes total, medium-rare inside. The remaining butter in at the end, tossed until glossy. Onion wedges in for the last minute, charred at the edges.
4. Serve: the red rice, beef and onions over, watercress and tomato wedges alongside, the lime-pepper-salt dip in a small dish for the beef.

Common mistakes:
- Stirring the beef constantly in a cool wok: it steams. Smoking wok, one layer, shake and toss.
- Fresh warm rice: clumps instead of grains. Cold rice for frying, always.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Lime-Pepper Butter — in a small pan, melt 2 tbsp butter over medium heat; off the heat, stir in 1 tbsp lime juice, 1 tsp cracked black pepper and a pinch of salt. Spoon over the beef — the lime-pepper dip, buttered and warm.

Title: Shrimp & Broccoli Couscous
Ingredients:
2 lb large shrimp (21/25), peeled and deveined, tails removed
2 cups dry instant couscous
2.25 cups low-sodium chicken broth
6 cups broccoli florets (about 1.5 lb), cut into bite-size pieces
2 tsp ground cumin
1.5 tsp ground coriander
1 tsp ground turmeric
1 tsp sweet paprika
0.5 tsp ground cinnamon
0.5 tsp cayenne pepper (optional; start with 0.25 tsp for gentle heat)
4 tbsp olive oil, divided
3 tbsp unsalted butter, divided
1 large yellow onion, diced (cut into small even cubes about 1/2 inch)
4 garlic cloves, minced (chopped very fine)
1.5 tsp kosher salt, divided
0.5 cup golden raisins
0.33 cup sliced almonds, toasted
0.5 cup chopped fresh cilantro
0.25 cup chopped fresh mint
1 lemon, cut into wedges

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1/2 tsp ground cumin
- 1/2 tsp sweet paprika
Steps:
1. Couscous: broth to a boil, couscous in, off the heat covered 5 minutes, fluffed with the butter and a fork. Spice mix in one bowl (cumin, coriander, turmeric, paprika, cinnamon, cayenne). Onion diced, garlic minced, broccoli in small florets, almonds toasted, herbs chopped.
2. Char the broccoli: 2 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high, broccoli in one layer, untouched 2-3 minutes until charred at the edges; onion in for 3 minutes until golden; garlic and the spice mix 1 minute until fragrant. Raisins through.
3. Couscous folded into the skillet (or the vegetables over the couscous) with the remaining butter.
4. Sear the shrimp separately: remaining olive oil in a skillet over high heat, shrimp seasoned, one layer, 90 seconds a side until pink with charred edges.
5. Shrimp over the couscous, almonds and herbs scattered, lemon wedges at the table.

Common mistakes:
- Shrimp cooked in the couscous: they steam and overcook while the grains set. Sear separately, lay over.
- Raw-tasting spices: they need their minute in the hot oil with the onion.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Spiced Butter — in a small pan, melt 2 tbsp butter over medium heat; add 1/2 tsp ground cumin and 1/2 tsp sweet paprika, sizzle 20 seconds until brick red and fragrant. Spoon over the shrimp and couscous — the spice mix, finished in butter.

Title: Shrimp & Tomato Orzo
Ingredients:
1 lb dry orzo
2 lb large shrimp (21/25), peeled and deveined
2 cans (14.5 oz each) crushed tomatoes
0.5 cup extra-virgin olive oil, divided
1 large red onion, diced (cut into small even cubes about 1/2 inch)
4 garlic cloves, minced (chopped very fine)
1 tbsp dried oregano
0.5 tsp crushed red pepper flakes (start with 0.25 tsp for gentle heat)
6 oz feta cheese, crumbled
0.5 cup pitted Kalamata olives, halved (slice = cut into thin flat pieces)
0.5 cup chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley
1 lemon, cut into wedges
1.5 tsp kosher salt, divided
0.75 tsp black pepper

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 2 tbsp crumbled feta cheese
- 1 tsp lemon juice
Steps:
1. Broiler on high, rack 6 inches below. Orzo boiled in salted water 1 minute shy of done; drained. Shrimp patted very dry and seasoned. Onion diced, garlic minced, olives halved, parsley chopped, feta crumbled.
2. Tomato base: half the olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium heat, onion 6-8 minutes until golden; garlic, oregano and chile flakes 30 seconds; crushed tomatoes in, simmered 8-10 minutes until thick and sweet.
3. Orzo folded through the sauce.
4. Shrimp pressed into the top in one layer; the remaining olive oil drizzled over; feta scattered.
5. Broil 4-6 minutes until the shrimp are just pink and curled and the feta browns in spots — watch it; broilers go from golden to gone in a minute.
6. Parsley over, lemon wedges alongside. Serve from the skillet.

Common mistakes:
- Shrimp boiled in the sauce from raw for 15 minutes: rubber. They broil on top, briefly.
- Thin tomato sauce: it must reduce before the orzo goes in, or the dish is soup.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Lemon-Feta Butter — in a small pan, melt 2 tbsp butter over medium heat; off the heat, whisk in 2 tbsp crumbled feta and 1 tsp lemon juice until the feta softens into the butter. Spoon over the shrimp — a warm, tangy butter over the broiled feta's edges.

Title: Shrimp Enchilada Rice Bake
Ingredients:
2 lb large shrimp (21/25), peeled, deveined, and cut into thirds
4 cups cooked long-grain white rice (from about 1.25 cups dry)
2 cans (10 oz each) red enchilada sauce
2 cups shredded Monterey Jack cheese, divided
1 cup shredded sharp cheddar cheese
1 can (15 oz) black beans, drained and rinsed
1 can (4.25 oz) diced green chiles
1 large yellow onion, diced (cut into small even cubes about 1/2 inch)
2 garlic cloves, minced (chopped very fine)
2 tbsp olive oil
1 tsp ground cumin
1 tsp chili powder
1.25 tsp kosher salt, divided
0.5 cup sour cream, for serving
0.5 cup chopped fresh cilantro
1 fresh jalapeno, thinly sliced (optional, for serving)

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1/3 cup sour cream
- Juice of 1 lime
- 1/2 tsp ground cumin
- Pinch of kosher salt
Steps:
1. Oven at 375 F. Rice cooked. Onion diced, garlic minced, shrimp in thirds (small pieces distribute through the bake instead of hiding in chunks), beans rinsed.
