2. Sear the shrimp quickly: olive oil in a skillet over high heat, shrimp 60-90 seconds until just pink at the edges — they finish in the oven, and baked shrimp overcook if you give them a head start.
3. Onion in the drippings 5 minutes until golden; garlic, cumin and chili powder 30 seconds.
4. Fold together in a 9x13: rice, shrimp, onion mix, beans, green chiles and one can of enchilada sauce. The second can poured over the top; both cheeses scattered in a full blanket.
5. Bake 18-22 minutes until bubbling at the edges and the cheese browns in spots. Rest 5 minutes.
6. Sour cream dolloped, cilantro and jalapeño slices over.

Common mistakes:
- Fully cooked shrimp before the bake: rubber in rice. Sixty seconds of sear, no more.
- One can of sauce: the rice drinks it and the bake dries. Two cans, one in and one over.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Lime Crema Pan Sauce — in a small pan, melt 1 tbsp butter over low heat; whisk in 1/3 cup sour cream, the juice of 1 lime, 1/2 tsp ground cumin and a pinch of salt until just warm and pourable — never boil. Drizzle over the bake at serving.

Title: Shrimp Jalapeño Tacos
Ingredients:
2 lb large shrimp (21/25), peeled and deveined
3 fresh jalapenos, thinly sliced into rounds (slice = cut into thin flat pieces)
1 cup sour cream
1 fresh jalapeno, minced (mince = chop very fine)
2 tbsp fresh lime juice, plus lime wedges for serving
2 tbsp unsalted butter
1 tbsp olive oil
3 garlic cloves, minced (chopped very fine)
1 tsp ground cumin
1 tsp chili powder
0.75 tsp kosher salt
18 small corn tortillas (6-inch)
3 cups shredded green cabbage
1 ripe avocado, sliced
0.5 cup chopped fresh cilantro

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- Juice of 1 lime
Steps:
1. Jalapeño crema first: sour cream, the minced jalapeño, lime juice and a pinch of salt whisked and refrigerated. Shrimp patted very dry, seasoned with cumin, chili powder and salt. Cabbage shredded, avocado sliced last, tortillas ready.
2. Sear the shrimp: olive oil in a large skillet over high heat, shrimp in one layer, untouched 90 seconds until charred at the edges; flip 30-60 seconds. Out.
3. Garlic butter finish: heat down, butter in, garlic 30 seconds until fragrant; shrimp back for 15 seconds, tossed in the garlic butter with the sliced jalapeños.
4. Tortillas warmed directly over a flame or in a dry skillet until pliable and blistered.
5. Tacos: cabbage, shrimp, avocado, crema in lines, cilantro over, lime at the table.

Common mistakes:
- Wet shrimp: pale and steaming. Towels, then a hot pan.
- Garlic in from the start: it burns while the shrimp sear. Butter and garlic at the end.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Extra Garlic-Lime Butter — in a small pan, melt 2 tbsp butter over medium heat with 1 minced garlic clove for 30 seconds; off the heat, the juice of 1 lime. Spoon over the tacos — a second pour of the pan's best idea.

Title: Shrimp Pomodoro Risotto
Ingredients:
1.5 cups arborio rice
2 lb large shrimp (21/25), peeled and deveined
1 can (28 oz) crushed tomatoes
6 cups low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth, kept warm
1 large yellow onion, diced (cut into small even cubes about 1/2 inch)
4 garlic cloves, minced (chopped very fine)
0.5 cup dry white wine
4 tbsp unsalted butter, divided
3 tbsp olive oil, divided
0.75 cup finely grated Parmesan cheese
0.5 cup torn fresh basil leaves
0.5 tsp crushed red pepper flakes (optional; start with 0.25 tsp for gentle heat)
1 tbsp fresh lemon juice
1.5 tsp kosher salt, divided
0.75 tsp black pepper

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 clove garlic, thinly sliced
- 1 tbsp torn fresh basil
Steps:
1. Broth at a bare simmer. Onion diced, garlic minced, Parmesan grated, basil torn, lemon juiced. Shrimp patted very dry and seasoned.
2. Sear the shrimp: olive oil in a skillet over medium-high, shrimp in one layer, 90 seconds untouched until pink with seared edges; flip 30 seconds. Out — they return at the end for seconds.
3. Risotto: remaining oil and half the butter in a wide pot, onion 5-6 minutes until soft and sweet; garlic and chile flakes 30 seconds; rice stirred 2 minutes until translucent at the edges. Wine in, absorbed.
4. Crushed tomatoes in; then the broth a ladle at a time, stirring often, 18-20 minutes to al dente and flowing.
5. Off the heat: remaining butter and the Parmesan beaten in until glossy; lemon juice folded through.
6. Shrimp laid over each bowl, basil scattered across.

Common mistakes:
- Shrimp simmered in the risotto: rubber. Sear, rest, lay over.
- A dry risotto: it should flow like lava and ripple. More broth, then more stirring.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Basil-Garlic Butter — in a small pan, melt 2 tbsp butter over medium heat with 1 sliced garlic clove for 30 seconds; off the heat, stir in 1 tbsp torn basil. Spoon over the shrimp — the pomodoro's herbs, finished in butter.

Title: Soy Garlic Chicken & Edamame
Ingredients:
3 lb boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1.5-inch pieces
0.5 cup low-sodium soy sauce
0.25 cup packed brown sugar (or 3 tbsp honey)
6 garlic cloves, minced (chopped very fine)
1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
2 tbsp rice vinegar
1 tbsp toasted sesame oil
3 tbsp avocado oil (or another neutral oil), divided
2 cups frozen shelled edamame, thawed
4 green onions, thinly sliced (slice = cut into thin flat pieces)
1 tbsp sesame seeds (optional, for garnish)
4 cups cooked white rice, for serving
0.5 tsp black pepper

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp brown sugar
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
Steps:
1. Sauce whisked: soy, brown sugar, garlic, ginger, vinegar, sesame oil. Chicken in 1 1/2-inch pieces. Edamame thawed and drained dry, green onions sliced. Rice cooked and ready.
2. Sear the chicken in two batches: 1 1/2 tbsp avocado oil in a large skillet over medium-high, chicken in one layer, untouched 3-4 minutes until deeply golden and caramelized at the edges; toss to finish. Batches — this sauce sugars fast and a crowded pan steams instead of caramelizing.
3. Sauce in, simmered 1-2 minutes until it thickens and lacquers the chicken.
4. Edamame through for 1 minute to heat. Black pepper over.
5. Over the rice; green onions and sesame scattered.

Common mistakes:
- Sauce reduced past glossy: it turns to tar and salt. One to two minutes.
- One giant batch: pale, boiled chicken. Two batches, real caramelization.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Extra Soy-Garlic Glaze — in a small pan, simmer 3 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp brown sugar and 1 tsp grated ginger for 2-3 minutes until syrupy. Spoon over the chicken for a second lacquer.

Title: Soy Garlic Pork & Zucchini
Ingredients:
1.5 lb pork tenderloin, trimmed of silverskin and sliced into 1/4-inch medallions
3 medium zucchini (about 1.5 lb), halved lengthwise and sliced into 1/4-inch half-moons
6 tbsp soy sauce
3 tbsp honey
6 cloves garlic, minced
1 tbsp rice vinegar
1 tsp red pepper flakes (start here; add more at the end if you want more heat)
2 tbsp toasted sesame oil
2 tbsp avocado oil, divided
4 green onions, sliced thin on a diagonal
1 tbsp sesame seeds

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp honey
- 1 clove garlic, minced
Steps:
1. Sauce whisked: soy, honey, garlic, vinegar, chile flakes, sesame oil. Pork in dry 1/4-inch medallions, seasoned. Zucchini in half-moons. Rice cooked and ready.
2. Sear the pork in two batches: 1 tbsp avocado oil in a large skillet over medium-high, medallions in one layer, untouched 2 minutes per side until deeply golden. Out.
3. Zucchini in the drippings in one layer, untouched 2 minutes until charred at the edges; toss 1 minute to just tender — zucchini cooked past snappy turns to mush in the sauce.
4. Pork back; the sauce in; toss 1 minute until everything is lacquered and glossy.
5. Green onions and sesame over; rice under.

Common mistakes:
- Wet pork: it steams gray. Towels, thoroughly, before the pan.
- Zucchini first and held: it weeps. Cook it last, serve it now.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Extra Soy-Honey Glaze — in a small pan, simmer 3 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp honey and 1 minced garlic clove for 2 minutes until syrupy. Spoon over the pork and zucchini for anyone who likes theirs extra glazed.

Title: Spanish Pork & Crispy Potatoes
Ingredients:
2.5 lb Yukon Gold potatoes, scrubbed and cut into 3/4-inch cubes
1.75 lb boneless pork loin, cut into 1-inch-thick chops (about 6 pieces)
5 tbsp olive oil, divided
2 tsp smoked paprika (pimenton), divided
1 tsp dried oregano
5 cloves garlic, minced
1 tbsp sherry vinegar (or red wine vinegar)
1.5 tsp kosher salt, divided
1 tsp black pepper
1/4 cup fresh parsley, chopped

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/3 cup dry sherry (or low-sodium chicken broth)
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
Steps:
1. Oven at 425 F. Potatoes in 3/4-inch cubes on a sheet pan. Pork chops patted very dry, rubbed with the salt, pepper, oregano and half the smoked paprika. Garlic minced, parsley chopped.
2. Potatoes: tossed with 3 tbsp olive oil and salt, one layer, roast 30-35 minutes, flipping once, until crisp and deep golden.
3. Sear the chops: remaining olive oil in a skillet over medium-high until shimmering; chops down untouched 4-5 minutes until a deep crust forms; flip, 3-4 minutes to 145 F, the garlic and remaining paprika in for the last minute so the garlic toasts without burning.
4. Sherry vinegar splashed in at the end, sizzling and reducing 30 seconds around the chops.
5. Rest the chops 5 minutes. Serve over or beside the crispy potatoes, parsley over, pan juices spooned around.

Common mistakes:
- Garlic in from the start: burnt and bitter. The last minute only.
- Potatoes crowded: they steam. One layer on the biggest pan.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Sherry Pan Sauce — in the chop skillet over medium heat, add 1/3 cup dry sherry (or chicken broth); scrape up the paprika-dark fond and reduce by half. Off the heat, whisk in 2 tbsp cold butter. Spoon over the chops and potatoes — Spain in a spoonful.

Title: Spicy Beef & Zucchini Rice
Ingredients:
2.5 cups jasmine rice, rinsed
1.5 lb ground beef (85/15)
2 medium zucchini (about 1 lb), cut into 1/2-inch dice
3 tbsp gochujang (Korean fermented chili paste; start with 2 tbsp if you are heat-shy)
3 tbsp soy sauce
1 tbsp brown sugar (start here; add 1 tsp more at the end if you want it sweeter)
2 tbsp toasted sesame oil
4 cloves garlic, minced
1 tbsp fresh ginger, minced
1 tbsp avocado oil
4 green onions, sliced
1 tbsp sesame seeds

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp gochujang (Korean chili paste)
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp sugar
- 1 tsp toasted sesame oil
Steps:
1. Rice on (rinsed jasmine; boil, cover, lowest heat 15, rest 10). Sauce whisked: gochujang, soy, brown sugar, sesame oil. Zucchini in 1/2-inch dice, garlic and ginger minced, green onions sliced.
2. Brown the beef hard: the avocado oil in a large skillet over medium-high, beef in one layer, untouched 4 minutes until a dark crust forms; break into crumbles and finish crisp at the edges. Drain the fat.
3. Garlic and ginger 30 seconds. Zucchini in, 3-4 minutes until golden at the edges and just tender — it should keep its bite.
4. Sauce in, tossed 1-2 minutes until everything is lacquered.
5. Over the rice; green onions and sesame over.

Common mistakes:
- Zucchini cooked to mush: it goes in after the beef and comes out snappy. Watch it.
- Steamed beef: one layer, untouched, dark crust first.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Sesame-Gochujang Glaze — in a small pan, simmer 2 tbsp gochujang, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sugar and 1 tsp toasted sesame oil for 1-2 minutes until glossy. Spoon over the bowls for a second, hotter lacquer.

Title: Spicy Pork Bulgogi Bowls
Ingredients:
2 lb pork shoulder, placed in the freezer 30 minutes before slicing
1/3 cup gochujang (Korean fermented chili paste)
3 tbsp soy sauce
2 tbsp sugar (start here; add 1 tsp more at the end if you want it sweeter)
2 tbsp toasted sesame oil
5 cloves garlic, minced
1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
1/2 yellow onion, grated on a box grater
2 tbsp mirin (or 1 tbsp rice vinegar mixed with 1 tbsp water)
1 tsp gochugaru or red pepper flakes (optional, for extra heat)
2.5 cups jasmine rice, rinsed
2 large carrots, peeled and cut into thin matchsticks
1 English cucumber, sliced into thin half-moons
1 tbsp avocado oil, plus more between batches if the pan looks dry
4 green onions, sliced
1 tbsp sesame seeds

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp sugar
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 tsp toasted sesame oil
Steps:
1. Pork frozen 30 minutes, then sliced paper-thin against the grain. Marinade whisked: gochujang, soy, sugar, sesame oil, garlic, ginger, grated onion, mirin, gochugaru. Pork in for 30 minutes minimum. Rice on. Carrots in matchsticks, cucumber in half-moons (quick-pickled in a pinch of salt and sugar if you like).
2. Sear in batches — the rule of bulgogi: a skillet or griddle over high heat with a film of avocado oil, pork in one layer, untouched 2-3 minutes until the marinade chars into dark, sticky edges; toss to finish. Three batches is normal. A crowded pan boils the pork in its marinade and the char never comes.
3. All the pork back for 30 seconds to marry. Green onions and sesame over.
4. Bowls: rice, pork, carrots, cucumber. The pan's charred scrapings spooned over — that is liquid gold, not a mess to wash.

Common mistakes:
- One batch: stewed pork. The char IS bulgogi.
- Thick slices: they chew like chops. Paper-thin, against the grain.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Extra Bulgogi Glaze — in a small pan, simmer 3 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tsp grated ginger and 1 tsp toasted sesame oil for 2-3 minutes until syrupy. Spoon over the pork bowls.

Title: Steak au Poivre with Parmesan Mash
Ingredients:
3 lb Yukon Gold or russet potatoes, peeled and cut into 1.5-inch chunks
4 tbsp unsalted butter, divided
1 cup whole milk, warmed
1 cup Parmesan cheese, finely grated (about 3 oz), plus extra for serving
6 sirloin steaks, 8 oz each and 1 to 1.25 inches thick
3 tbsp whole black peppercorns, coarsely crushed
2 tbsp avocado oil
1 large shallot, minced
1/3 cup brandy or cognac
1 cup beef stock
1 cup heavy cream
1 tsp Dijon mustard
2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1/4 cup brandy (or cognac)
- 1/2 cup heavy cream
- 1/2 tsp coarsely cracked black pepper
- Pinch of kosher salt
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
Steps:
1. Potatoes into cold salted water; simmer 15-18 minutes until completely tender; drained, steamed dry, mashed with the butter, warm milk and Parmesan — fluffy, never whipped. Steaks out 30 minutes ahead; peppercorns coarsely crushed (a bag and a heavy pan — cracked, not powder).
2. Press the pepper crust onto both sides of the steaks with the salt. Avocado oil in a cast iron over high heat until smoking; steaks down untouched 4-5 minutes until the crust sets dark; flip, 3-4 minutes to medium-rare (130 F).
3. Rest the steaks 10 minutes. The pan sauce in the same skillet: shallot in the drippings 1 minute; brandy in (stand back — it may flame; that is correct and brief), reduced by half; stock in, reduced 2 minutes; cream and Dijon in, simmered 2-3 minutes until it coats a spoon. A knob of the remaining butter whisked in at the end.
4. Steaks sliced or whole over the Parmesan mash, the au poivre sauce spooned generously across.

Common mistakes:
- Pepper powder instead of cracked: it burns bitter and vanishes. Coarse cracks, pressed on.
- Sauce boiled hard after the cream: it can split. A simmer, then off.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Extra Au Poivre Sauce — in a small pan, simmer 1/4 cup brandy until reduced by half; add 1/2 cup heavy cream, 1/2 tsp cracked black pepper and a pinch of salt; simmer 2-3 minutes until it coats a spoon; off the heat, 1 tbsp cold butter whisked in. Served in a small jug at the table — because with steak au poivre, there is never quite enough sauce.

Title: Tomato Beef Rice Bowls
Ingredients:
2.5 cups jasmine rice, rinsed
1.5 lb flank steak, sliced 1/4-inch thin against the grain
2 tbsp soy sauce, plus 2 tbsp more for the sauce
1 tbsp Shaoxing wine (or dry sherry)
1 tbsp cornstarch, plus 2 tsp more for the slurry
1 tsp toasted sesame oil
1 tsp sugar, plus 2 tbsp more for the sauce
1/2 tsp baking soda (tenderizer - no need to rinse at this small amount)
1/3 cup ketchup
1 tbsp tomato paste
1/2 cup water or beef stock
2 tbsp cold water (for the slurry)
3 large ripe tomatoes, cut into wedges
1 large onion, cut into wedges
3 cloves garlic, minced
1 tbsp fresh ginger, minced
3 tbsp avocado oil, divided
1/2 tsp white pepper
2 green onions, sliced

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp ketchup
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp sugar
- 2 tbsp water
- 1 tsp unsalted butter
Steps:
1. Rice on (rinsed jasmine; boil, cover, lowest heat 15, rest 10). Beef sliced thin against the grain, tossed with 2 tbsp soy, the Shaoxing, 1 tbsp cornstarch, the sesame oil, 1 tsp sugar and the baking soda (the Cantonese tenderizing trick — 15 minutes).
2. Sauce whisked: remaining soy, ketchup, tomato paste, stock or water, 2 tbsp sugar, white pepper, and the cornstarch slurry held separate. Tomatoes and onion in wedges, garlic and ginger minced.
3. Sear the beef in two batches: 1 1/2 tbsp avocado oil in a wok over high heat, beef in one layer, untouched 90 seconds until dark at the edges; toss 1 minute. Out.
4. Onion in for 2 minutes until charred at the edges; garlic and ginger 20 seconds; tomatoes in for 2-3 minutes until they slump and juice.
5. Sauce in, simmered 1 minute; the slurry in to gloss; beef back for 30 seconds. Green onions over; rice under.

Common mistakes:
- Tomatoes cooked to sauce: they should slump, not dissolve — wedges with presence.
- Skipping the baking soda: chewier beef. A half teaspoon is the takeout tenderness secret.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Extra Tomato-Soy Glaze — in a small pan, simmer 3 tbsp ketchup, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sugar and 2 tbsp water for 2 minutes until glossy; off the heat, 1 tsp butter whisked in. Spoon over the beef for a second, sweeter lacquer.

Title: Tomato Braised Pork with Rice
Ingredients:
2.5 lb boneless pork shoulder, cut into 2-inch chunks
2 tbsp olive oil
1 large onion, diced
2 carrots, peeled and diced
2 celery stalks, diced
5 cloves garlic, minced
2 tbsp tomato paste
1 cup dry red wine (Chianti or similar - cook with one you would drink)
1 (28 oz) can San Marzano tomatoes, crushed by hand
1 cup chicken stock
2 sprigs fresh rosemary
2 bay leaves
1 tsp dried oregano
1/2 tsp red pepper flakes (start here for gentle heat; add more at the end if you want it spicier)
2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
1 tsp black pepper
3 cups long-grain rice, rinsed

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1 cup pork braising liquid (from the recipe)
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter, cold
Steps:
1. Oven at 325 F. Pork in 2-inch chunks, patted very dry and seasoned. Soffritto (onion, carrot, celery) diced, garlic minced. Rice rinsed, cooked near serving.
2. Sear the pork in batches: olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high, pork in one layer, 3-4 minutes untouched per batch until deeply crusted. Out.
3. Soffritto into the drippings 8-10 minutes until soft, sweet and golden; garlic 30 seconds; tomato paste 2 minutes until darkened. Wine in, scraping, reduced by half.
4. Hand-crushed tomatoes, stock, rosemary, bay, oregano and chile flakes in; pork back. Into the oven, partially covered, 2 to 2 1/2 hours until the pork shreds at a touch and the sauce has turned rich and dark.
5. Pork pulled into coarse shreds in its sauce (or left in chunks, both are done). Salt checked.
6. Over the rice, with more sauce than seems polite — it is the right amount.

Common mistakes:
- A pale sear: the braise cannot invent the crust later. Batches and patience.
- Shredding to mush: coarse shreds keep their texture in the sauce.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Rosemary and Red Wine Pan Sauce — ladle 1 cup of the braising liquid into a small saucepan; boil 4-5 minutes until reduced by a third and glossy. Off the heat, whisk in 1 tbsp cold butter. Spoon over the pork and rice — the braise, concentrated.

Title: Tomato Coconut Cod Stew
Ingredients:
2.5 lb cod fillets, cut into 2-inch chunks
Juice of 2 limes
2 tsp kosher salt, divided
1 tsp black pepper
2 tbsp dende (Brazilian red palm oil) - or substitute 2 tbsp olive oil plus 1 tsp sweet paprika for the golden color
2 tbsp olive oil
1 large onion, thinly sliced
4 cloves garlic, minced
1 red bell pepper, thinly sliced
1 yellow bell pepper, thinly sliced
3 large ripe tomatoes, sliced into rounds
1 (13.5 oz) can full-fat coconut milk, shaken well
1 cup fish or chicken stock
1/2 cup fresh cilantro, chopped, plus more for serving
Lime wedges, for serving
3 cups long-grain rice, rinsed

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1/2 tsp sweet paprika
- Squeeze of lime juice
Steps:
1. Cod in 2-inch chunks, tossed with the lime juice, salt and pepper; refrigerated 15 minutes (the lime firms it so it holds together in the stew). Onion and the peppers sliced thin (poblanos swap in for the peppers if you want warmth), tomatoes in rounds. Rice rinsed and on.
2. Base: olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat, onion and the peppers 8-10 minutes until soft and sweet; garlic 1 minute. Tomato rounds laid over; bare simmer 5 minutes until they begin to melt.
3. Coconut milk and stock in; bare simmer 5 minutes — never a hard boil, which splits coconut milk.
4. Cod slid in gently; lid on; bare simmer 6-8 minutes until it just flakes. Spoon sauce over rather than stirring.
5. The dendê (or the olive oil and paprika substitute) drizzled over at serving — its sunset color is the moqueca's signature. Cilantro over, lime wedges alongside; rice under.

Common mistakes:
- Boiling the coconut milk: it splits greasy. Bare simmer from the moment it lands.
- Stirring the cod: it breaks. Slide in, lid on, spoon sauce over.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Achiote-Lime Butter — in a small pan, melt 2 tbsp butter over medium heat with 1/2 tsp sweet paprika until deep orange; off the heat, a squeeze of lime. Spoon over the cod — the dendê color and richness, finished with butter and lime.

Title: Tomato Saffron Cod with Rice
Ingredients:
2.5 lb cod fillets, cut into 2-inch chunks
1/2 tsp saffron threads
1/2 cup dry white wine, warmed
4 tbsp olive oil, divided
1 large onion, diced
1 red bell pepper, diced
5 cloves garlic, minced
1 tsp smoked paprika
1 (28 oz) can crushed tomatoes
1 cup fish or vegetable stock
2 bay leaves
1/2 cup fresh parsley, chopped
1 lemon, cut into wedges
1.5 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
1/2 tsp black pepper
2.5 cups long-grain rice, rinsed

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- 2 tbsp saffron-steeped white wine (from the recipe's bloom)
- Squeeze of lemon juice
Steps:
1. Saffron bloomed in the warmed wine 15 minutes until deep gold (cold liquid will not bloom saffron — this is the recipe's first law). Cod in 2-inch chunks, patted dry and seasoned. Onion and the pepper diced (a poblano stands in), garlic minced. Rice rinsed and on.
2. Sofrito: 2 tbsp olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat, onion and the pepper 8-10 minutes until soft, sweet and golden; garlic and smoked paprika 30 seconds.
3. Crushed tomatoes in; bare simmer 10 minutes until thick and darkened.
4. The saffron wine and stock in; bare simmer 5 minutes. Cod slid in; lid on; 6-8 minutes until it just flakes.
5. Remaining olive oil drizzled over, parsley scattered, lemon wedges alongside; rice under or beside.

Common mistakes:
- Saffron into the pot dry: half its perfume stays locked. Bloom it in the warm wine.
- Boiling the cod: bare simmer, lid on, patience.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Saffron-Lemon Butter — in a small pan, melt 3 tbsp butter over medium heat until foaming; add 2 tbsp of the saffron wine (steeped as in the recipe) and simmer 30 seconds; off the heat, a squeeze of lemon. Spoon over the cod — golden butter for a golden stew.

Title: Turkey-Free Beef Moussaka Bowls
Ingredients:
2 large eggplants (about 2.5 lb), cut into 1-inch cubes
3 tbsp olive oil, divided
1.5 lb ground beef (85/15)
1 large onion, diced
4 cloves garlic, minced
2 tbsp tomato paste
1 (14.5 oz) can diced tomatoes
1/2 cup dry red wine (or beef stock)
1.5 tsp dried oregano
1/2 tsp ground cinnamon
1/4 tsp ground nutmeg, plus 1/4 tsp more for the bechamel
1 bay leaf
2 tsp kosher salt, divided, plus more to taste
3 tbsp unsalted butter
3 tbsp all-purpose flour
2 cups whole milk, warmed
1/2 cup Parmesan cheese, grated
1 large egg yolk
1/4 tsp white pepper
2 cups long-grain rice, rinsed
1/4 cup fresh parsley, chopped, for serving

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter, plus 1 tbsp more (cold) to finish
- 1/2 cup crushed tomatoes
- 1/2 tsp dried oregano
Steps:
1. Oven at 425 F. Eggplant in 1-inch cubes on a sheet pan with 2 tbsp olive oil and salt, one layer; roast 20-25 minutes, flipping once, until deeply golden and supple. (The bowls skip the casserole dish — everything lands over rice.) Rice rinsed and on. Milk warmed for the béchamel.
2. Brown the beef hard: remaining olive oil in a skillet over medium-high, beef in one layer, untouched 4-5 minutes for a dark crust; break up and finish. Onion in 5 minutes until golden; garlic 30 seconds; tomato paste 1 minute.
3. Wine in, scraping, reduced by half; diced tomatoes, oregano, cinnamon, nutmeg and bay in; bare simmer 12-15 minutes until thick. Eggplant folded through.
4. Béchamel: butter melted, flour whisked 2 minutes (pale), warm milk in a stream whisking constantly; simmer 3 minutes to a thick nappe. Off the heat: the egg yolk whisked in fast, Parmesan, nutmeg, white pepper.
5. Bowls: rice, the eggplant-beef mixture, béchamel spooned generously over the top (the bowl's moussaka lid). Parsley over.

Common mistakes:
- Raw eggplant in the sauce: it drinks oil and stays spongy. Roasted first, it turns silky.
- Thin meat sauce: simmer it thick or the bowls slump.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Tomato-Oregano Butter — in a small pan, melt 1 tbsp butter; add 1/2 cup crushed tomatoes and 1/2 tsp dried oregano; simmer 4 minutes until glossy; off the heat, 1 tbsp cold butter whisked in. Spoon alongside the béchamel on each bowl — a bright red counterpoint to the white sauce.

Title: Turmeric Fish with Dill Rice
Ingredients:
2.5 lb cod fillets (or halibut), cut into 1.5-inch chunks
2 tbsp ground turmeric
3 tbsp fish sauce
2 tbsp sugar
1/2 cup plain whole-milk yogurt
4 cloves garlic, minced
2 tbsp fresh galangal, grated (traditional; or substitute fresh ginger)
2 tbsp avocado oil, plus 4 tbsp more for frying
1 tsp kosher salt
1/2 tsp black pepper
2 tbsp cornstarch
2 large bunches fresh dill (about 4 oz), cut into 2-inch lengths
8 green onions, cut into 2-inch lengths
1/2 cup roasted peanuts, roughly chopped
3 cups jasmine rice, rinsed
1/4 cup fish sauce (for the dipping sauce)
1/4 cup warm water (for the dipping sauce)
2 tbsp sugar (for the dipping sauce)
Juice of 2 limes
2 cloves garlic, minced (for the dipping sauce)
1 Thai chili, minced (start with half if you are heat-shy)

For the pan sauce (optional):
- 3 tbsp avocado oil
- 1 clove garlic, thinly sliced
- 1/4 cup chopped fresh dill
Steps:
1. Marinate the fish (30 minutes to 2 hours, in glass or steel — turmeric stains plastic permanently): chunks in the turmeric, fish sauce, sugar, yogurt, garlic and galangal (or ginger), with the avocado oil and cornstarch. Rice rinsed and on. The dipping sauce whisked (fish sauce, warm water, sugar, lime, garlic, chile) — sweet-sour-hot.
2. Dill and green onions in 2-inch lengths — a mountain of them; in cha ca they are a vegetable, not a garnish.
3. Fry the fish: the 4 tbsp avocado oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high until shimmering; fish lifted from the marinade, in one layer, untouched 3 minutes until a turmeric-gold crust forms; flip gently, 2-3 minutes until just cooked. Out.
4. Dill and green onions into the hot turmeric oil in the pan, tossed 30-60 seconds until wilted and fragrant — serve the fish and herbs straight from the sizzling pan if you can; cha ca is a tableside dish.
5. Over the jasmine rice, peanuts scattered, the dipping sauce spooned over at the table.

Common mistakes:
- A timid amount of dill: two bunches is the recipe, not a garnish suggestion. It wilts to a fraction.
- Fish flipped early: the turmeric crust sticks and tears. It releases when the crust sets.

PAN SAUCE (optional, worth it): Dill and Garlic Oil — in a small pan, heat 3 tbsp avocado oil until shimmering; add 1 sliced garlic clove and 1/4 cup chopped dill; sizzle 30 seconds. Spoon the hot oil over the fish and rice at the table — cha ca's sizzle, on demand.
